title: Rams waive returner Xavier Smith
summary: Earlier this week, Rams special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone told reporters that the team was not considering making a change at punt returner.
full_text: Earlier this week, Rams special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone told reporters that the team was not considering making a change at punt returner. That plan has apparently changed. Los Angeles announced on Friday that the team has waived receiver/returner Xavier Smith. Smith had served as the team’s primary punt returner for each of the last two seasons. But he also has made some critical mistakes, including fielding a punt deep in L.A. territory that looked like it would be a touchback in the third quarter of last week’s eventual loss to Denver. Smith averaged 9.9 yards per punt return and 20.6 yards per kick return over the first three weeks this season. While he had not caught a pass in 2026, he recorded 18 catches for 303 yards in 2025. The Rams’ unofficial depth chart listed Konata Mumpfield as the team’s backup punt returner. We’ll see if he in fact does get the nod at the position when L.A. takes on Philadelphia on Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Christian Parker expresses regret at play call at end of loss to Ravens
summary: Christian Parker is a first-time defensive coordinator who was charged with fixing a unit that allowed the most points in the NFL last season.
full_text: '' Christian Parker is a first-time defensive coordinator who was charged with fixing a unit that allowed the most points in the NFL last season. The Cowboys currently rank 30th in yards allowed and 25th in points. It's better but not much better. Parker has taken some heat for his decision to play man defense with seven seconds left against Lamar Jackson, who completed a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers that set up Tyler Loop's game-winning, 56-yard field goal. Parker admitted this week he erred with the play call. "Oh, for sure," Parker said, via Schuyler Dixon of the Associated Press. "You know, I had an original call in mind, but overthought the situation, relative to what their mindset was going to be going to overtime, trying to get something quick, Hail Mary, all those things. So, I definitely would make a different call if that the situation came up again." Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, now an analyst for NBC Sports, called Parker's decision to play man coverage "somewhat negligent" during a halftime segment on Sunday Night Football. Tomlin said Parker should have called for zone coverage in that situation to protect against what happened. Parker said he does not listen to "outside noise." "To be honest with you, I don't pay it any mind," he said. "We have more than enough on our plate in here to worry about what the outside noise is, whether it's good or bad. I think that regardless of how that outside noise creeps in the building, it can affect you in multiple ways. So we've just been focusing on trying to get this next one."
author: Charean Williams

title: Dan Campbell: We were "very much in on" Joey Porter Jr.
summary: Prior to Wednesday's trade sending cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Steelers to the Cowboys, there were reports of interest in Porter from other teams as well.
full_text: '' Prior to Wednesday's trade sending cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Steelers to the Cowboys, there were reports of interest in Porter from other teams as well. The Lions were one of the teams mentioned in those reports and head coach Dan Campbell confirmed them during a Friday press conference. Campbell said, via multiple reporters, that the Lions were "very much in on" Porter prior to Pittsburgh's deal with Dallas. He said everything has to "align" for a deal to reach the finish line, however, and the Cowboys were able to get there first by sending a pair of draft picks to the Steelers. The Lions' interest in cornerback help is easy to understand. The release of Terrion Arnold left them without an expected starter in the defensive backfield and it stands to reason that they'll continue looking at possible ways to bolster the group ahead of the trade deadline.
author: Josh Alper

title: Packers DT Warren Brinson to miss "significant time" with groin injury
summary: Packers defensive tackle Warren Brinson missed the first three games of the season with a calf injury and he's set to miss a lot more action with a new ailment.
full_text: '' Packers defensive tackle Warren Brinson missed the first three games of the season with a calf injury and he's set to miss a lot more action with a new ailment. Brinson appeared on this week's injury report with a groin issue in addition to the calf and head coach Matt LaFleur said that it will be the reason for an extended absence from the field. "Unfortunately I think he's gonna miss a significant amount of time," LaFleur said, via Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's website. "All he did was slip and injuries occur and a lot of times it's non-contract." Brinson was a sixth-round pick last year. He had 13 tackles and a half-sack in 11 appearances as a rookie.
author: Josh Alper

title: Todd Monken: Week 1 was tough, our guys trusted the process
summary: The Browns moved to 3-1 when Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers's final, desperate heave was picked off by safety Grant Delpit on Thursday night and head coach Todd Monken reflected on how improbable that record would have felt not so long ago.
full_text: ' The Browns moved to 3-1 when Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers's final, desperate heave was picked off by safety Grant Delpit on Thursday night and head coach Todd Monken reflected on how improbable that record would have felt not so long ago. Week 1 saw the Jaguars pummel Monken's team in his head coaching debut and much of the conversation was about whether they would bench quarterback Deshaun Watson before their Week 3 home opener. Those discussions all centered around the incessant boos Watson heard from Browns fans in an August preseason game against the Bills, but it turned out to be a lot of wasted words. Watson has led game-winning drives in the fourth quarter each of the last three weeks and the entire Browns team has had little resemblance to the one that got blown out in Jacksonville. "It’s a credit, I’ll go back to Deshaun, but to our team. I mean, that was a complete, maybe disaster is a little bit strong, but that’s a tough opening game in every phase, other than maybe kickoff return, maybe, other than that," Monken said, via a transcript from the team. "But the guys trusted the process. We got stung a little bit, and our guys responded to that. And, man, that locker room is fun, right there celebrating those guys. Big, big, big divisional win. And so, but Deshaun, before the game, I got a chance to, I was in the coach’s office, and I was going over the call sheet with him again, and I said, 'Isn’t this really cool? Like, you’re going to be introduced last, isn’t that really freaking cool?' It was only seven weeks earlier, and, right, it’s, 'Where are we going to go from here, right? The Bills game at home, right? Where are we going from here, where are you going, where are we going?' So cool." Monken noted later in his press conference that its only three wins and there is certainly a lot of football left to be played, but that's a promising prospect for Cleveland rather than a distressing one for the first time in a long time.
author: Josh Alper

title: Travis Kelce set to surpass Tim Brown, move into No. 7 on NFL's all-time receptions list
summary: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's next catch will be a significant one for his place in NFL history.
full_text: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's next catch will be a significant one for his place in NFL history. Kelce has 1,094 receptions in his NFL career, tying him with Tim Brown on the all-time list. With his next catch, Kelce will move ahead of Brown and be No. 7 in NFL history for career catches. In first place on the all-time catch list is Jerry Rice, whose record of 1,549 receptions may never be broken. Kelce won't catch Rice even if he plays until he's 40. After Rice on the career catch list are Larry Fitzgerald (1,432 catches), Tony Gonzalez (1,325), Marvin Harrison (1,102), Cris Carter (1,101) and Jason Witten (1,228). Then comes Kelce, who is climbing up the ranks of the most productive pass catchers ever to play the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Todd Monken on Mason Graham: Hopefully we get good news
summary: Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham had to exit Thursday’s victory over the Steelers with a knee injury.
full_text: Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham had to exit Thursday’s victory over the Steelers with a knee injury. Graham was spotted postgame on crutches and wearing a brace on his knee postgame. In his Friday news conference, Monken noted he did not have an update on Graham, who is still undergoing tests. But Graham, the No. 5 overall pick of the 2025 draft, has been one of the team’s best players over the first few weeks of the season. “He’s a tremendously talented young player, that you could see early in the season it all coming together ,” Monken said. “Like I said last week, we want all of our young players to be great right away and we need them to be great right away. That’s the nature [of] the business we’ve chosen. But I just think he’s worked awfully hard. He’s not only active and quick, he’s a highly intelligent player — which I think helps him in terms of reading sets, in terms of communication up front, and he plays with an unbelievable effort. “So, it’s a shame for him. But, hopefully we get good news.” Graham has recorded 4.0 sacks with six tackles for loss and five QB hits so far in 2026. He finished last year with 0.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, and four QB hits.
author: Myles Simmons

title: NFLPA names Mack Hollins their Community MVP for Week 4
summary: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has been named their Community MVP for Week 4 of the 2026 season.
full_text: '' The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has been named their Community MVP for Week 4 of the 2026 season. Hollins recently hosted a Special Olympics Family Field Day for 125 athletes along with their families. The event featured eight different stations staffed by 25 coaches and several other Patriots players took part in the celebration,. “It is such an honor to be named this week’s NFLPA Community MVP,” Hollins said. “I am grateful to have been able to experience it with the Special Olympics community and continue building a relationship that means so much to me. None of this would have been possible without the help of so many outstanding volunteers and passionate people.” The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to Hollins's Free the Feet Foundation. He will also join the other weekly MVPs as candidates for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns and Steelers mismanaged the final seconds of the game
summary: On Sunday, the Ravens and the Cowboys provided stark examples on how to handle, and how not to handle, the final seconds of a close game in light of the current kickoff rules.
full_text: On Sunday, the Ravens and the Cowboys provided stark examples on how to handle, and how not to handle, the final seconds of a close game in light of the current kickoff rules. The Steelers and the Browns apparently learned nothing from it. After the Browns failed to work the clock down to the final few seconds before what became the game-winning field goal, 10 seconds remained. Like the Cowboys in Rio, the Browns kicked into the end zone, giving the Steelers the ball at the 35. (A cutaway to Browns coach Todd Monken seemed to reveal his dismay.) It opened the door for the Steelers, who had a timeout in hand, to try to gain just enough yardage to allow for a field goal that would have forced overtime. From the TV copy, it appeared that the Browns were playing the same kind of outside leverage that the Cowboys deployed when the Ravens, who had only seven seconds to work with, gained 27 yards and kicked the walk-off field goal. That gave the Steelers a shot at completing a pass in the middle of the field. But the Steelers didn't call a play that would have entailed a quick throw for a moderate gain and a shot at a field goal. Instead, quarterback Aaron Rodgers rolled to his right, looking to uncork a long throw. The pass, which came back to earth just inside the Cleveland 20, was intercepted. Game over. Why not try for a 20- to 30-yard gain? Quick decision, quick throw. If it works, take the time out and try the field goal. If it doesn't, let Rodgers try to connect on another Thursday night miracle . Coach Mike McCarthy (or Rodgers himself) inexplicably opted for a middle ground, with a long throw that, if it had connected, possibly would have allowed for a time out and a short field goal. The decision made no sense. The Steelers could have had two shots — a shorter attempt to put them in field goal range for overtime and, if that failed (without an interception), a Hail Mary to win it. The 2025 shift of the touchback point from the 30 to the 35 has significantly altered the available strategies for the final 10-15 seconds of a game. The Browns repeated the Cowboys' mistake by conceding the 35, and the Steelers failed to try to seize upon the very real possibility of using the final 10 seconds to gain enough ground to send it into overtime.
author: Mike Florio

title: T.J. Watt: Steelers made it too easy for Browns to go downfield at the end of the game
summary: Steelers linebacker T.J.
full_text: '' Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt had a sack, two tackles for loss, a pass deflection and two quarterback hits on Thursday night, but he was not happy with the defensive effort in the 27-24 loss to the Browns. After the Steelers tied the game 24-24 with 1:42 remaining in the fourth quarter, the Browns went 36 yards on seven plays to move into range for the game-winning field goal. Watt said that led to the Steelers losing a game they should have won. "To sit here and not be 3-1 isn't acceptable," Watt said, via Steelers.com. "Obviously, it's a long season, a lot left to go, but we just have to put it together. Even at the end of the game, it was way too easy [for the Browns] getting down the field and getting in [field goal] range. Just have to look at everything and move forward." The Steelers' next three games are against teams with losing records -- the Colts, Buccaneers and Saints -- and then they have a rematch with the Browns. The schedule sets up for Pittsburgh to go on a run, but Watt knows the defense needs to play better.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell among Jets ruled out for Week 4 vs. Bears
summary: The Jets will be shorthanded when they play the Bears on Sunday.
full_text: The Jets will be shorthanded when they play the Bears on Sunday. Head coach Aaron Glenn announced in his Friday press conference that Breece Hall (quad), tight end Mason Taylor (thumb), receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), left guard Dylan Parham (knee), and linebacker Kiko Mauioga have all been ruled out. It sounds like edge rusher Kingsley Enagbare also could end up being questionable, as Glenn said Enagbare will be a limited participant in Friday’s practice. He was limited on Wednesday but did not practice on Thursday. Minkah Fitzpatrick appears on track to return from a groin injury, as he was upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice. New York’s full injury report with the rest of the club’s game statuses will be released later on Friday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jayden Daniels out this week, Marcus Mariota starts again
summary: Daniels returned to practice this week, but he won't play against the Colts.
full_text: '' Quarterback Jayden Daniels will have to wait at least one more week to return to the Commanders lineup. Daniels was able to practice this week with a brace on his dislocated left elbow, but head coach Dan Quinn ruled him out for Sunday's game against the Colts during a Friday press conference. Marcus Mariota will get the start in London. It's Mariota's second straight start and he was able to help the Commanders beat the Seahawks in Week 3. He was 19-of-31 for 183 yards and three touchdowns in Washington's 33-31 win. Daniels was limited in practice this week, but a return to full participation next week would bode well for his chances of playing against the Giants in Week 5. While Daniels will remain out, Quinn said linebacker Frankie Luvu and tight end Chig Okonkwo will play against Indianapolis. Both players missed the last two games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Roger Goodell met with Gov. JB Pritzker, Illinois lawmakers about Bears stadium on Thursday
summary: Publicly, the Bears have said their "sole focus" for the site of their new stadium site is Hammond, Ind.
full_text: Publicly, the Bears have said their " sole focus " for the site of their new stadium site is Hammond, Ind. But the storied franchise playing its home games in a different state is not a done deal — potentially far from it. After there was reporting in August that commissioner Roger Goodell had met with select state lawmakers , Illinois Governor JB Pritzker issued a statement on Thursday saying he had met with Goodell. "The Governor's Office has remained in conversation with the Bears about their plans in Illinois throughout the summer,” the statement reads. "Today, Governor Pritzker was grateful to meet in Illinois with NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell , Pat Ryan, Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch, Rep. Kam Buckner, and Sen. Bill Cunningham. "The Governor and General Assembly leadership were glad to participate in a productive meeting focused on keeping the Bears in Illinois and protecting taxpayers." Ryan is a Bears minority owner, and the namesake of Northwestern University’s Ryan Field, which was recently rebuilt and is set to open on Friday when the Wildcats play Penn State. Interestingly, none of speaker Welch, Rep. Buckner, or Sen. Cunningham represent Arlington Heights — which is the suburb of Chicago where the Bears purchased a 326-acre property for a new stadium and development. But all three do represent districts in and around Chicago. The league also issued a statement on the meeting, via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network: “The NFL appreciated the opportunity to meet with Governor Pritzker and legislative leaders today,” the statement reads. “Timely action is essential as the Bears work to find a long-term stadium solution for the club and their fans.” It’s unclear what the solution will be for the Bears and their stadium going forward. But it does appear that at least the league is working to keep the club playing its home games in its home state.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike McCarthy doesn't know whether the Joey Porter Jr. trade affected the team
summary: The Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys less than 24 hours before their Week 4 game at Cleveland.
full_text: '' The Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys less than 24 hours before their Week 4 game at Cleveland. After the 27-24 loss, coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether the timing of the move had a negative impact on the team. "You know, I mean, that's really, you know, a question that's really specific to individuals, and I can't really speak on every individual," McCarthy said. "You know, the timing was, you know, was the night before a game, and, you know, I'm sure that's what the guys woke up to but, yeah, I mean, it's part of our business." Earlier in the press conference, McCarthy revisited the intersection between business and football, as it played out throughout the Porter saga. "You never hope business, you know, gets in the way of your preparation and playing, but, you know, it's the modern NFL," McCarthy said. "You know, it was a situation where, you know, it's been going on for some time. As an organization, we felt like this was the best thing for us and, you know, we wish Joey well, and, you know, I never really got a chance to coach Joey, but, you know, obviously, did some, you know, did some great things here, and we wish him the best in Dallas." McCarthy added that there "was definitely a point" where he "definitely thought it was a possibility" that Porter would play for the Steelers against the Browns. "We had a rep count in mind," McCarthy said, "so that's what we were working towards." Quarterback Aaron Rodgers also got a question about the timing of the Porter trade and the potential impact on the team. "You gotta ask the defensive guys," Rodgers said. "They're probably around him more often but, you know, I thought Joey might play this week, based on his practice stuff but, you know, we wish Joey well." One defensive player wasn't surprised by the move. At the outset of the Thursday night broadcast, Kaylee Hartung said linebacker Patrick Queen knew that, when Porter didn't get on the bus with the team to Cleveland, "he wouldn't be in Pittsburgh when they came back." Porter is now in Dallas. And it appears that he will indeed make his 2026 debut on Sunday, when the Cowboys face the Texans.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen Ramsey on Joey Porter Jr.: Unfortunate it didn't work out, but I'm happy for him
summary: After a long, drawn out negotiation, the Steelers dealt cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys on Wednesday night.
full_text: '' After a long, drawn out negotiation, the Steelers dealt cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys on Wednesday night. Porter's now-former teammate Jalen Ramsey went through a similar situation with the Jaguars back in 2019, which ended with him being traded to the Rams. After Thursday night's loss to the Rams, Ramsey told reporters that he felt like a big brother to Porter and wanted him to be a valued, important part of the Steelers going forward. “It is very unfortunate that it didn’t work out, ” Ramsey said, via Mark Kaboly of the Pat McAfee Show. “But at the same time, I am happy for him. I am happy that he is getting a fresh start. I wish him all the success in his NFL future. I think he is a stud, I really do. I think he is a top-five guy. People argue that he’s top 10, but I really think Joey is a good player, I really do.” Ramsey also referenced his own story and compared it to Porter. “It happens, and everybody moves on,” Ramsey said. “For me, I’ve been through it before. I was Joey before at one point. When I was 24, I was Joey. A little different; our situations were a little bit different. The exit was similar, potentially. It is what it is. I treat it as part of the NFL business. We held hope as long as we could that things would get done, but that’s part of it. That’s business. Guys have to do what’s best for them because the NFL is not for long. You have to do what is best for you, and you can’t be mad at a man wanting to do that.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike McDaniel: I'm not living in hope, I'm living in reality about our offense
summary: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel got a vote of confidence from head coach Jim Harbaugh on Wednesday, but he knows that the status quo on offense isn't going to work.
full_text: '' Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel got a vote of confidence from head coach Jim Harbaugh on Wednesday, but he knows that the status quo on offense isn't going to work. The Chargers lost to the Bills last Sunday despite being plus-four in the turnover column and McDaniel said at a Thursday press conference that "we were the reason we lost a football game." They had five turnovers over the first two games, so the unit had a big hand in those losses as well. McDaniel said he hasn't lost faith in the offense and thinks he has "a much better understanding" of what can bring out better play in quarterback Justin Herbert, but he acknowledged that results on the field are the only thing that matter. "There has been improvement , but does anyone care? No, but we better improve. . . . I’m not trying to have moral victories or anything like that," McDaniel said. "It’s steadfast that there’s things that we’ve done in the past three games that is active participation in losing the game. Flat out, our jobs are to improve everything. I’m not living in hope, I’m living in reality." It won't be the easiest week to get on track as the Chargers will be in Seattle to face the Seahawks they try to bounce back from the end of their 12-game losing streak. McDaniel and the Chargers need to find a way, however, or the next vote of confidence may never come.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: "Final straw" for Steelers was Joey Porter Jr.'s Wednesday claim of back pain
summary: The Steelers thought the dance was over.
full_text: '' The Steelers thought the dance was over. When the music started up again, they decided they'd had enough. As explained by Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , the " final straw " for the Steelers in their relationship with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. came when Porter, after two days of fully participating in practice, claimed that he had back pain on Wednesday. That's when the Steelers decided to make a trade. Ultimately, it was a win for Porter. He got what he wanted — a one-way ticket out of town. Former Cowboys linebacker Micah Parsons achieved the same result last year. Once the Cowboys realized he was serious about not playing unless and until he got a new deal, they traded him to the Packers. For the Steelers, who seemed to think Porter eventually would blink, the fourth game became the moment they accepted that Porter was committed to the bit. And, yes, it was a bit. He wasn't too injured to play, if he was injured at all. Amazingly, he's not even listed on the Cowboys' injury report, one day after being limited on Pittsburgh's final report of the week, and in turn ruled out for Thursday night's game. For players who can't hold out due to the financial consequences under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, a hold in that lingers until they get what they want is the best, and only, alternative. Was it a real injury? If the team has no way to challenge it without creating an ugly legal fight and/or a P.R. shitstorm, it doesn't matter. For most players, a lifetime of football has caused some condition from the top of their head to the tips of their toes that would justify not playing. Unless the team is willing to stage a confrontation that would instantly ruin an already tenuous relationship, the only viable option is to trade the player.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joey Porter Jr.'s back is "feeling better," and he hopes to play Sunday
summary: The Steelers had ruled out the cornerback for Thursday Night Football.
full_text: '' The Cowboys' injury report did not change Thursday. The only thing that changed was the trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was not listed on the report. That was news in and of itself from the report as Porter practiced after passing his physical. The Steelers had ruled out Porter for Thursday night's game against the Browns, adding his on-again, off-again back issue on Wednesday's injury report. In no surprise, Porter said his back was "feeling better" after the trade to the Cowboys. He hopes to make his 2026 debut on Sunday when the Cowboys play the Texans. "We're just trying to take things day by day ," Porter said after his first practice in Dallas, via Todd Archer of ESPN, "and if everything looks good, then we should be out there." Porter's addition gives the team depth at the position, with cornerbacks Shavon Revel (right knee/right ankle) and Cobie Durant (hamstring) still not practicing. Porter did not get the contract extension he wanted in Pittsburgh and was holding in, an inactive for the first three games. He will play in Dallas on the final year of his deal, because, he said, the Cowboys have shown him " value " that the Steelers didn't. “I think he’s excited about the opportunity to maybe play, but we’ll see how the rest of the week goes," Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News . "This was a good start today.” Porter said he got what he wanted in going to the Cowboys and now he would like to finish his career in Dallas. "I'm down with it if they are. I want to finish my career here," Porter said. "So hopefully I just perform like how I know how to perform and do what I do, and I'm going to let everything take care of the rest." Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) also did not practice a second consecutive day, and safety Malik Hooker (fractured forearm) was limited again after returning to practice Wednesday. Outside linebacker James Houston (shoulder) remained a full participant.
author: Charean Williams

title: Deshaun Watson: Momentum shifts are part of the NFL, you have to ride the waves
summary: When Thursday night's game got to halftime, it looked like the Browns might roll over the Steelers for an easy win.
full_text: '' When Thursday night's game got to halftime, it looked like the Browns might roll over the Steelers for an easy win. After going scoreless in the first quarter, Cleveland found the end zone on three straight possessions in the second quarter and carried a 21-10 win into halftime. Things went south again after the break, however, and a Deshaun Watson interception helped spark a 14-3 Steelers run in the fourth quarter that put overtime on the table. Watson and the Browns had been in similar straits in their last two games and they came through for the third straight week. Watson completed four passes for 45 yards and the Browns survived a late sack and incompletion when Andre Szymt hit a 56-yard field goal for a 27-24 win. “That’s part of the NFL. You have to ride the waves," Watson said, via a transcript from the team. "So many momentum shifts, they are the best in the world, just like us. They are a really good team. They are going to make plays, and they made a couple of plays that went their way. We made a couple of plays that went our way. We just have to ride the wave until our opportunities came and at the end of the day, whenever those moments come, especially at the end, we found a way to get the W. That’s what ultimately matters.” Watson's feelings about riding the waves was about Thursday night, but it's something that can be applied to his entire run in Cleveland. For much of that time, it looked like a shipwreck was the only possible outcome, but the last few weeks have offered long-awaited reasons to believe otherwise.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Rodgers' second TD draws Steelers to within 21-16
summary: The Steelers had minus-6 yards passing in the third quarter as the Browns had two sacks of Aaron Rodgers.
full_text: The Steelers had minus-6 yards passing in the third quarter as the Browns had two sacks of Aaron Rodgers. The fourth quarter has gotten off to a better start for the visitors. On the second play of the final quarter, the Steelers had a pass interference penalty overturned on replay. Robert Spears-Jennings intercepted Deshaun Waston's deep pass intended for Denzel Boston. Steelers defensive back Daylen Everette was called for defensive pass interference, though, and the 42-yard penalty had the Browns at the Pittsburgh 23. The Steelers challenged the play, and it was reversed on replay because Jack Sawyer tipped the pass at the line of scrimmage, negating the penalty. Rodgers took advantage with a six-play, 77-yard touchdown drive. He rolled to his right to avoid another sack and threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to tight end Darnell Washington. The Browns stopped the 2-point conversion, leaving the Steelers trailing 21-16. Rodgers is 16-of-29 for 222 yards with two touchdowns and an interception.
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Deshaun Watson leads Browns to 27-24 win over Steelers
summary: Watson drove the Browns 36 yards in seven plays to set up Andre Szmyt's 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left.
full_text: The Browns is the Browns? Forget that. Cleveland upset Pittsburgh 27-24 on Thursday Night Football, moving into sole possession of first place in the AFC North if only briefly. The Browns are 3-1, a half-game better than the Bengals and Ravens, while the Steelers are 2-2. Browns kicker Andre Szmyt kicked a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left for the game-winner in an entertaining game. Aaron Rodgers had the ball at the 35 after the Browns kicked it into the end zone, but safety Grant Delpit intercepted Rodgers at the Cleveland 18. Deshaun Watson played a flawless first half, with 181 yards and a touchdown, before the Steelers adjusted in the second half. The Browns quarterback finished 24-of-33 for 268 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Both of his turnovers came in the second half, with his interception changing the momentum. On the second play of the final quarter, the Steelers had a pass interference penalty overturned on replay and reversed to an interception. Robert Spears-Jennings intercepted Watson’s deep pass intended for Denzel Boston. Steelers defensive back Daylen Everette was called for defensive pass interference, though, and the 42-yard penalty had the Browns at the Pittsburgh 23. The Steelers challenged the play, and it was reversed on replay because Jack Sawyer tipped the pass at the line of scrimmage, negating the penalty. It led to Rodgers' second touchdown pass, a 21-yarder to tight end Darnell Washington, that drew the Steelers to within 21-16 after a failed 2-point conversion. After Szmyt's 44-yard field goal, Rodgers drove the Steelers to a late tie. The Steelers faced a fourth-and-10 at the Cleveland 11 with 1:51 remaining. Rodgers targeted Washington for a third consecutive play, and safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was penalized for pass interference. Rodgers then hit Pat Freiermuth for a 3-yard touchdown on the next play, with 1:42 left. Rodgers tied it with a quarterback sneak on the 2-point conversion from the 1-yard line after Jared Verse jumped offsides. The Steelers, though, couldn't stop the Browns, who drove 36 yards in seven plays for the winning field goal. Cleveland finished with 372 yards and the Steelers 361. Rodgers went 22-of-40 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. Jaylen Warren rushed for 93 yards on 17 carries, and DK Metcalf caught five passes for 115 yards. Roman Wilson added three catches for 74 yards. The Browns sacked Rodgers five times, but they had to overcome 14 penalties for 88 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Signs point to Tyson Bagent for the Bears on Sunday
summary: As Bears coach Ben Johnson prepares for a reunion with fellow former Lions coordinator Aaron Glenn, Johnson is doing his best to keep Glenn and the Jets in the dark about who the starting quarterback will be.
full_text: As Bears coach Ben Johnson prepares for a reunion with fellow former Lions coordinator Aaron Glenn, Johnson is doing his best to keep Glenn and the Jets in the dark about who the starting quarterback will be. It's one of the benefits of having injury issues complicate the most important position in pro football. The uncertainty can be weaponized, in the hopes of preventing the next opponent from knowing who they'll face. Johnson is trying his damnedest to keep the plans for Week 4 secret. Through two full practice days in advance of the game against the Jets, he has largely succeeded. That said, it's hard to keep the many people who are present for practice from saying something to someone who is trying to find out who's getting the work. As we hear it, Tyson Bagent (not Case Keenum) has gotten the first-team reps so far this week. This obviously points to Bagent as the starter in place of Caleb Williams, who continues to recover from a hamstring injury. It makes sense. Bagent earned the backup role. He entered the Week 2 game against the Vikings in the fourth quarter and nearly pulled off a last-second win. Keenum got the Monday night start because he was available to prepare for the game against the Eagles at a time when Bagent was in the concussion protocol. By the time Bagent was cleared, the hay was in the barn with Keenum. The question of whether a coach can keep the identity of his starting quarterback a secret is separate from whether the league should allow it. It creates another chunk of inside information that could be mishandled by those who know the truth. Presumably, the Bears will make an announcement today. Or maybe they won't. The rules don't require it. And if it's Bagent, the Bears can say they necessarily made the announcement by not updating their depth chart . Bagent is No. 2, Keenum is No. 3. Both are healthy. Common sense points to Bagent. If he's indeed getting all of the practice reps, that only reinforces it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike McCarthy on exchange with Aaron Rodgers: "I wish I wouldn't use those words"
summary: In the first quarter of Thursday night's game between the Steelers and the Browns, Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers became upset.
full_text: In the first quarter of Thursday night's game between the Steelers and the Browns, Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers became upset. Given that he's often upset during games, that doesn't really narrow it down. He was particularly perturbed that the play was coming in too slowly. And a microphone caught his words. " What the fuck? " Rodgers angrily said to the sideline. "Call it." The Prime Video cameras then cut to coach Mike McCarthy, who seemed to say, "Fucking asshole." After the game, McCarthy initially feigned confusion when asked about communication issues. When the questioning became more specific, he said that Steelers P.R. director Burt Lauten had told McCarthy about the exchange that made its way to TV. "Communication sometimes is not the best choice of words, but everybody's competing on the field," McCarthy said. "I think, you know, what's said on the field, the way I grew up in this game, you know, usually stays on the field. That's not the case today. I understand that. But, yeah, any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn't use those words." For Rodgers's part, he wasn't asked about the specific exchange. Either way, the Steelers fell to 2-2. They're currently in last place in the AFC North, as the only team with two losses. If the Bengals and Ravens win on Sunday, the Steelers will be all alone in the basement of the division.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers DE Derrick Harmon carted with foot injury

It is unknown how or when Harmon was injured. Harman has no stats on Thursday night, but he has 12 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble this season. title: Jared Verse after beating Steelers: I don't have respect for anybody who plays dirty
summary: Browns defensive end Jared Verse picked up an unnecessary roughness flag in Thursday night's win over the Steelers, but he says it was Pittsburgh that played dirty.
full_text: Browns defensive end Jared Verse picked up an unnecessary roughness flag in Thursday night's win over the Steelers, but he says it was Pittsburgh that played dirty. Verse said after the game that he and the Steelers went back and forth with a lot of trash talk, and also said the Steelers were playing dirty in addition to their talk. “ They were talking crazy . I was telling them, ‘You’re double-teaming, y’all sliding, y’all garbage.’ I was talking crazy to them. I don’t have any respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra shit after the game, excuse my French. So, I can't wait to see them again. It's going to be a good time when I see them again," Verse said. author: Michael David Smith

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Great start for Joey Porter Jr., we'll see about Sunday
summary: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was traded to the Cowboys late on Wednesday night and went through his first practice with the team on Thursday.
full_text: '' Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was traded to the Cowboys late on Wednesday night and went through his first practice with the team on Thursday. Porter did not practice all summer because of what was called a back injury and had been on the injury report in Pittsburgh during the season due to that injury or conditioning needs related to his long absence. He was not on the Cowboys' injury report for any reason, which has led to thoughts that he will be on the field for Dallas when they face the Texans on Sunday. During a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the team is still working out whether Porter will make his debut this weekend. “We’ll see how he moves around today, see if he’s sore today," Schottenheimer said, via Jon Machota of TheAthletic.com. "But I thought it was a great start yesterday. Really, really pleased with not just what I saw on the field, but really just the way he attacked his preparation and in learning the system. The big thing that will drive this is his ability to communicate with Caleb Downs and some of the safeties and things like that as we get ready to finish the prep.” Schottenheimer called the deal for Porter a sign the Cowboys are in "win-now mode" and that suggests we'll be seeing the newest Cowboy on the field sooner rather than later.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons announce death of Ring of Honor member Jeff Van Note
summary: The Falcons announced on Friday that their longtime center Jeff Van Note has died at the age of 80.
full_text: The Falcons announced on Friday that their longtime center Jeff Van Note has died at the age of 80. Van Note was selected by the Falcons in the 11th round of the 1969 draft and he remained with the team through the 1986 season. Van Note was added to the franchise Ring of Honor in 2006 Van Note played linebacker at Alabama, but was moved to center by then-Falcons head coach Norm Van Brocklin. He became a starter in 1970 and was named a second-team All-Pro twice while making six Pro Bowls. "Today, we mourn the loss of a true Falcons legend," Falcons owner Arthur Blank said in a statement. "Jeff Van Note dedicated 18 seasons to this franchise and became one of the most respected and beloved players in our history. He embodied toughness, resilience, humility, and an unwavering commitment to his team, qualities that earned him the admiration of generations of Falcons fans." Van Note played in 246 games during his time with the Falcons, which is second only to his former teammate Mike Kenn in franchise history.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mason Graham left Thursday's game on crutches and wearing a knee brace
summary: One of the only negative developments for the Browns on Thursday night was the left knee injury that knocked defensive tackle Mason Graham out of the game.
full_text: One of the only negative developments for the Browns on Thursday night was the left knee injury that knocked defensive tackle Mason Graham out of the game. Graham was injured in the first half of the 27-24 win over the Steelers and did not return to the game. Head coach Todd Monken said he had no update on Graham's condition during a postgame press conference, but Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported that Graham left the stadium on crutches while wearing a brace on his knee. There will likely be further testing of the injury on Friday and the Browns will be hoping for good news about a player who had four sacks in the first three weeks of the season. Graham's absence did not stop the Browns from finishing the night with five sacks of Aaron Rodgers. Mike Hall and Maliek Collins each had one of them and that duo will be crucial to the Browns defense if Graham is out of the lineup moving forward.
author: Josh Alper

title: Darren Rizzi: Special teams coaches want NFL to change rule for holders on kickoffs
summary: Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi says his colleagues around the league almost all agree that holders should be allowed on kickoffs only if the wind is blowing the ball off the tee, and not to give the kicking team an advantage by placing the ball at an unusual angle.
full_text: ' Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi says his colleagues around the league almost all agree that holders should be allowed on kickoffs only if the wind is blowing the ball off the tee, and not to give the kicking team an advantage by placing the ball at an unusual angle. Under the NFL's dynamic kickoff rule, a 12th player can take the field as a holder on kickoffs, with our without the use of a tee, as long as the holder runs off the field immediately after the ball is kicked. Rizzi says the intent of the rule was to allow the kicking team to ensure the ball would stay in the tee on windy days, but the Eagles gained attention in Week 2 for using a holder just to hold the ball on the ground at an odd angle, which changes the trajectory of the kick and makes it harder to return. Rizzi helped organize a conference call of special teams coordinators and said almost everyone agreed that the NFL should change the way the rule is officiated so that kickoffs are on a tee and holders are for weather conditions, not creating an advantage for the kicker. “We don’t want the ball on the edge, we don’t want the ball on the ground, we don’t want the ball held sideways. We want just a regular kickoff,” Rizzi said. “That's kind of what was discussed amongst the coordinators. If we’re not unanimous, we’re darn close to it, the way we feel about it. That's why you saw some holders come out to start the game. And that's really not the intent. It's a work in progress. It hasn't been remedied yet." Rizzi said there's no question the kicking team benefits from using the holder. "There's definitely an advantage from the kicker's standpoint because the different angles you can create with the ball," Rizzi said. "That's fine if you want to kick one of those knuckleballs or dirty balls with the ball in a tee, have at it. Adding the 12th player to create an advantage is something we want to stay away from." The rules allow for the holder, but Rizzi would like to see an administrative change similar to the one the NFL made during the 2022 season , when the Raiders were told they had to stop using a holder to place the football on top of the tee, rather than in the tee. Rizzi said he believes the NFL will do that. "It's a small little thing that created a big problem." Rizzi said. "I think we're gonna get it resolved."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Todd Monken is working his greatest magic yet with Browns, Deshaun Watson
summary: After helping Lamar Jackson reach historic heights and winning two national championships at Georgia, Monken may be delivering his most impressive coaching performance yet
full_text:
The Kyle Shanahan-Sean McVay trees have blossomed a number of notable "offensive guru" NFL coaches.
That group obviously includes Shanahan and McVay themselves, and names like Matt LaFleur, Mike LaFleur, Kevin O'Connell, Liam Coen, Zac Taylor, Mike McDaniel and Klint Kubiak.
Todd Monken isn't one of them, but the first-year Cleveland Browns coach should have the same acclaim as that group after the latest and perhaps greatest masterpiece of his coaching career: leading the Deshaun Watson-quarterbacked Cleveland Browns to a 3-1 start and first place in the AFC North.
Monken has flashed many flourishes of brilliance. As Oklahoma State's offensive coordinator, he helped quarterback Brandon Weeden (22nd overall pick in 2012 NFL Draft ) and receiver Justin Blackmon (5th overall pick in 2012 NFL Draft) power their squad to a 23-3 record as college football's most electrifying passing tandem.
In 2018, Monken worked as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive coordinator. The Buccaneers went 5-11, but it wasn't because of his offense -- Tampa Bay's defense surrendered 29 points per game, the second-most in the NFL that season. Monken cobbled together the league's No. 12 scoring offense (24.8 points per game) with a quarterback platoon of Jameis Winston and Ryan Fitzpatrick . Collectively, Monken squeezed a combined 5,125 yards passing and 36 passing touchdowns out of the two of them.
As the Georgia Bulldogs offensive coordinator from 2020 to 2022, he helped quarterback Stetson Bennett go from a walk-on to a two-time national championship-winning passer across the 2021 and 2022 seasons. Yes, those Bulldogs squads had an embarrassment of NFL first-round draft picks among their defensive players in those years, but Monken's Bennett-led offenses put up the ninth-most points in college football in 2021 (38.6 points per game) and the fifth-most in 2022 (41.1 points per game).
Monken's magic helped lift Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson to new heights. Jackson won the 2023 NFL MVP under Monken, but the peak came the following year in 2024 when he earned first-team All-Pro honors despite finishing as the MVP runner-up to Josh Allen . Jackson completed the 2024 regular season with the following all-time production: 4,172 yards passing, a 41-4 passing-touchdown-to-interception ratio, 915 yards rushing and a 119.6 passer rating. That means Jackson finished the 2024 regular season with the following firsts, per CBS Sports Research:
Jackson's 119.6 passer rating ranked as the fourth-most all-time in a season, trailing only three occurrences that resulted in NFL MVP accolades: Rodgers in 2011 (122.5) and 2020 (121.5) and Manning (121.1) in 2004.
All of those feats of coaching acumen are strong, but none is as incredible as what Monken is doing as a first-time NFL head coach in Cleveland. The Browns are 3-1 and in sole possession of first place in the AFC North for the first time with Deshaun Watson as their quarterback.
The last time they were in first place in the division was Sept. 22, 2022, when Watson was still suspended by the NFL for his off-field legal issues . How miraculous has their 3-1 start been this season? They have won three consecutive games, all as an underdog for the first time since 2001, per CBS Sports Research, and Watson is now only the second Browns quarterback with a game-winning drive in three straight weeks since 1950. Only he and Brian Sipe in 1979 have done so as Cleveland quarterbacks in that span.
Watson entered the 2026 season a broken man, on and off the football field. Watson sat out the entire 2021 season while dealing with the fallout from demanding a contract/trade and being sued over 20 times in civil court for sexual misconduct. Cleveland still traded a package of draft picks, highlighted by three first-round selections, and then extended him on a five-year, $230 million deal that was fully guaranteed. Watson only played 19 games across his first four seasons in Cleveland because of a season-ending shoulder injury and two Achilles tears. In those 19 games, he profiled as statistically one of the NFL's worst passers, ranking in the bottom five in the NFL in multiple efficiency statistics among the 50 quarterbacks who had thrown 500-plus passes from 2022 to 2025.
Expected points added (EPA) per dropback
* Only Zach Wilson ranked worse than Watson among 50 QBs with 500-plus passes from 2022 to 2025
So, how is Monken getting Watson to play like a league-average starter at the age of 31 off of two Achilles tears? He is doing a great job highlighting Watson's strengths and coaching the hell out of his young, revamped supporting cast. Monken simplified Cleveland's offense for Watson with a couple of key elements. No quarterback has a higher rate of lining up in shotgun than Watson's 71.9% rate, and he is maximizing the remaining mobility Watson still possesses, utilizing run-pass option plays for his quarterback at the fourth-highest rate in the league, 11.8%.
Essentially, Monken is drawing on his years as a collegiate offensive coordinator to create a simplified, college-style offense to get Watson back to the basics as a quarterback. Pairing that scheme with a completely revamped offensive line with five new full-time starters and a trio of young pass catchers -- 2026 first-round pick wide receiver KC Concepcion , 2026 second-round pick Denzel Boston and 2025 third-round pick tight end Harold Fannin Jr. -- also helps, and Monken also deserves plenty of credit for successfully pairing his offensive youth movement with a quarterback who looked like his football career was on its last legs entering the season.
Expected points added (EPA) per dropback
As the three consecutive wins and the overall 3-1 record this season show, Monken's game plan is working. Watson looks like a capable NFL quarterback again, which is truly Monken's greatest football magic trick yet.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL Week 4 picks: Our experts face off on Cowboys vs. Texans, Rams at Eagles and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season has plenty of storylines to watch. Derrick Henry is looking to run wild against his former team in the Tennessee Titans; the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders battle from London; and Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams look to get back on track vs. the Philadelphia Eagles .
This season has been pretty unpredictable so far. Four teams enter Week 4 tied for the best record in their division after last-place finishes in 2025: The Las Vegas Raiders , Cleveland Browns , New York Giants and the New Orleans Saints . Which one of these teams could be a legitimate sleeper? And when could we see J.J. McCarthy take over at quarterback in New York?
Below, CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Sept. 29 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Advanced data courtesy of CBS Sports Research
Dajani (Colts -3.5): I think this matchup is about which defense stinks less. The Colts rank worst in total defense (417.3) and third-worst in scoring defense (30.3). The Commanders rank second-worst in scoring defense (30.7) and have allowed the highest opponent passer rating (124.4) and most passing touchdowns (11) this year. Marcus Mariota has definitely brought some magic to the lineup, as evidenced by last week's upset of the Seattle Seahawks , but I would argue the Colts are the better team.
Do you remember the last time the Colts played overseas? They defeated the Atlanta Falcons in overtime thanks to a ridiculous performance from Jonathan Taylor . The star running back rushed 32 times for 244 yards and three touchdowns, while also adding 42 yards as a receiver. He's already up to 325 total yards and four touchdowns through three weeks. I expect him to show out on Sunday for our friends across the pond.  … Prediction: Colts 27, Commanders 21
Dubin (Commanders +3.5): Marcus Mariota is a competent enough backup quarterback to keep this game close. He just went and beat the Seahawks, after all, and the Colts have a much friendlier defense. He should be able to keep the chains moving. I'm just not sure that'll be enough for the Commanders to actually win the game this time around. I think this is a big Jonathan Taylor game, even if Washington has been good on the ground so far and allowed just 44 rushing yards last week against Seattle. Plus. Washington's pass defense should give Daniel Jones and Co. a chance for their best game to date. … Prediction: Colts 23, Commanders 20
Dajani (Bengals -2.5): The Jacksonville Jaguars have been red-hot and just defeated the New England Patriots by a whopping 29 points. As for the Bengals, they just lost to Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers in a thrilling game. We thought the Cincy defense was reborn, only for Rodgers and Co. to drop 30 points on them. This is going to be a popular "upset" pick this week, but I'm actually going to take the Bengals. They are back at home after two road games and have covered the spread in six straight non-divisional contests. This Jaguars team isn't perfect, and you saw some issues during their Week 2 loss to the Denver Broncos . The offensive line could struggle with Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen , while this secondary will have their hands full with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . Don't overlook the fact that Joe Burrow is 3-0 vs. Trevor Lawrence dating back to the 2019 College Football Playoff Title game. … Prediction: Bengals 24, Jaguars 20
Dubin (Jaguars +2.5): I hate to be the guy that takes what Dajani described as the popular upset pick right after he called people out for it, but I'm going to do just that. The Jaguars should be 3-0 right now, but they fell apart in the second half against the Broncos in Week 2. The offense is firing on all cylinders. The defense has forced six turnovers in three games. Cincinnati's defensive improvement looked like a mirage in Week 3 against the Steelers and may have just been a function of playing dysfunctional offenses in the Buccaneers and the Nico Collins-less Texans . I think Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can put up some points here, but I like the Jags to score even more.  … Prediction: Jaguars 30, Bengals 27
Dajani (Rams -3): The Eagles' loss to the Chicago Bears may stay with me forever. We had a 38-year-old quarterback dicing up a Super Bowl-caliber defense, as Ben Johnson put Vic Fangio in a proverbial chokehold on national television. Then, we had a former Super Bowl MVP quarterback looking completely lost. All that to say, how am I supposed to back Philly in this spot against an angry team that just lost in primetime?
If we are being honest with ourselves, the Eagles haven't looked very good at all this year. They were hardly dominant in the Week 1 victory over the Commanders or Week 2 win against the Titans. Philly is the only team that hasn't scored in the first quarter this season, and the defense is still waiting to force that first takeaway. The Eagles haven't even covered the spread this season, so I'll take the visiting Rams to get back on track.  … Prediction: Rams 26, Eagles 20
Dubin (Rams -3): The Rams have looked like the Rams we expected for six quarters this season, and very much like a different team for the other six quarters. Meanwhile, the Eagles have looked exactly like the Eagles we expected for eight quarters and like a disaster for four. How does that all net out? I think it nets out with Matthew Stafford having some success through the air against a somewhat surprisingly friendly Eagles pass defense that isn't getting as much pressure as you'd expect, and with Jalen Hurts and Co. continuing their stilted start to the season.  … Prediction: Rams 24, Eagles 20
Dajani (Texans -2.5): I've given the Texans the benefit of the doubt for an entire month with nothing to show for it. I can no longer wait for C.J. Stroud to get the offense off the ground or for the defense to become good again. With that said, there is one big reason why the Texans will get their first win this season, and that's Nico Collins . He's missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, but should return this week to face one of the worst defenses in the NFL. C.J. Stroud averages 10.7 yards per attempt when targeting Collins. That number drops to 7.7 when he targets any other receiver. In the one game Collins played in this season, he caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown while Houston came one play away from defeating the Buffalo Bills … Prediction: Texans 30, Cowboys 26
Dubin (Texans -2.5): The Cowboys need their offense to be perfect in order to win games. Their defense once again seems like it's that bad, and it is also hemorrhaging players at linebacker and in the secondary. Offenses, generally, cannot be perfect against the Texans' defense. Houston should also be getting Nico Collins back here, so I think the Texans can actually move the ball for a change. … Prediction: Texans 24, Cowboys 21
Dajani (Broncos +3): Maybe I'm the Broncos expert? When Denver was down 16-0 to the Rams last Sunday night, I was telling everyone not to go to bed because the game was not over. Sure enough, the Broncos bucked back. Denver has the most comeback wins (14), second-half comebacks (11), fourth-quarter comebacks (7) and 14-point comebacks (3) over the past two seasons.
I'm leaning toward the Broncos again in this spot because of the San Francisco 49ers ' injuries. Nick Bosa is going to miss some time with knee/calf issues, wide receiver Mike Evans injured his rib, linebacker Dre Greenlaw sat out of practice Wednesday with a quad injury and we'll see what the status of left tackle Trent Williams is later in the week. Denver is 5-1 straight up in its last six games as an underdog, and Bo Nix is 10-0 in his past 10 games vs. NFC opponents.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, 49ers 23
Dubin (49ers -3): San Francisco is merrily rolling right along with the best offense in the NFL through the first three weeks despite…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL Week 4 schedule: Why Rams vs. Eagles is make or break for both teams
summary: A look at some under-the-radar games you should be tuning into, including a battle of unbeatens no one saw coming
full_text:
With three weeks behind us, we're starting to see who is the real deal and who may need to wait for next season. Going into Week 4, there are five undefeated teams remaining: the Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs , Las Vegas Raiders , Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers .
Some teams are meeting expectations, while others are falling far short of preseason hopes (ahem, Los Angeles Chargers , ahem). Plus, there are some major surprises this year, including one that I will highlight below.
Each week, I take a look at some of the more underrated games, and all three I picked last week turned out to be worth watching. Let's dive into this week's games that may not be on everyone's radar, or at least weren't when the season started, and why you should tune in:
Sunday, Oct. 4 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo , try for free)
The Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles are both NFC teams that need to shape up. Both are coming off losses, with the Rams entering the contest 1-2 and the Eagles at 2-1.
Philly is coming off an ugly 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears and backup quarterback Case Keenum , who, before last week, hadn't played a game in 1,009 days . Losing to a 38-year-old third-string QB isn't exactly something to brag about. The Eagles' other two wins, against the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans , were by a combined six points.
The Eagles' offense looks uninspiring, and their defense has allowed 20-plus points each week. Things need to change this week if you're Philly. The Rams have not had a smooth start to the year, and the Eagles can take advantage of those early-season growing pains to regain their own confidence.
Now to the Rams, who need to take advantage of Philly's own growing pains. This is a big game for L.A., as it attempts to shake off the dust and show that it can be a contender in the conference. The Rams need to expose the weaknesses of the Eagles' pass rush, offensive line and safeties. If they can do that, they'll have a chance at earning their own confidence back.
The Rams fell to 1-3 most recently in 2024 and did make it to the playoffs at 10-7, but lost in the wild-card round. Any Sean McVay team is going to have high expectations, and 1-3 is not meeting that mark. Throw in a difficult division, with the 3-0 49ers and defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks , and each win's value only increases.
There is a lot on the line for both teams, and I think that pressure and an even matchup in terms of struggles will make this a game to watch.
Sunday, Oct. 4 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, Paramount+
This game may not be underrated anymore, but if you asked most people this offseason if they thought a Week 4 matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders would be a must-watch between undefeated teams, they'd probably say "no." They'd probably wonder why you'd even ask such a question.
Well, that question is not so silly anymore. The Raiders are ... good?
This game has everything. It's a divisional matchup, includes the surprise team of the year so far and will result in one team getting their first loss (and it happens to be on CBS and streaming on Paramount+).
I think this will have the energy of Chiefs-Raiders games from back when they were in Oakland.
Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins is tied atop the NFL for most passing touchdowns with nine, and having top weapon Brock Bowers back is no doubt helping his numbers. The Raiders can shock everyone by defeating Patrick Mahomes and Co., and if they do, it may be time to consider the Raiders the real deal.
I like this game a lot and think it will be one we'll be watching highlights of on Monday.
Sunday, Oct. 4 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Paramount+
The New York Giants are a team I can't quite predict yet. Losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury significantly changed the identity of the team. They managed to win their first game without him, but it wasn't pretty. New starter Jameis Winston went 14-of-22 for 118 yards and no touchdowns in the 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans. Losing linebacker Brian Burns to an ACL and meniscus injury is also a big hit.
The Giants may be able to squeak out a few more wins, and with the Eagles not playing their top football and the Cowboys and Commanders at 1-2, New York could make it to the top of the NFC East standings this week.
If Winston continues to struggle, the Giants now have a new backup as an option. Nine Eighteen, aka J.J. McCarthy , was added this week in a trade that left some scratching their heads and others praising the move . Head coach John Harbaugh said Winston is the starter for the rest of the season, but that will only hold if he can be in the "up" phase of his up-and-down career.
The Arizona Cardinals are also an interesting team that still has the potential to go either way this season. Like the Giants, they have a veteran at the helm in Jacoby Brissett . One of Arizona's two losses this season was a blowout to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, but their other defeat was a close battle against the San Francisco 49ers, one of the best teams in the conference. They aren't the worst 1-2 team out there and are one I'll be keeping an eye on.
I'm interested to see whether these teams can be considered a tough (or even slightly tough) opponent going forward this season. It's a battle of veteran quarterbacks at a time when each team needs to build an identity beyond their passer, because neither is the long-term answer for their team.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Road warriors: One NFL team won't play a single game at home during the month of October
summary: Half of the team's month will actually be spent outside of the United States
full_text:
The month of October should be an interesting one for the Jacksonville Jaguars , and that's because they won't get to play a single game at home. That's right, the Jags will not be playing any games in Jacksonville during October.
The Jags' month-long road trip will start this week with a game in Cincinnati, and after that, they'll be leaving the country for two weeks. Here's their full October schedule:
Week 4 (Oct. 4): at Cincinnati Week 5 (Oct. 11): vs. Eagles (in London) Week 6 (Oct. 18): vs. Texans (in London) Week 7 (Oct. 25): Bye
The Jaguars are the first team in some time to go an entire calendar month without playing a game in their home city. Seven years ago, the Jags and Cards both found themselves in the same situation in November. The Cards played three games on the road and lost them all (they also had a bye during the month). The Cardinals went into November with a 3-5-1 record and ended the month 3-8-1; by then, their season was basically over.
As for the Jaguars, they also went 0-3 during their November away from home in 2019. They played one game in London and two road games, losing them all. They were 4-4 going into the month, but ended November at 4-7, and like the Cardinals, their season was essentially over at that point. The 2026 Jaguars will be hoping to avoid a similar fate.
The Jaguars will be playing two straight games in London this year for the third time in franchise history, but this season, their setup is slightly different from it has been in the past. The Jags will be the HOME team in BOTH games, marking the first time in league history that a team has played as the home team in back-to-back international games.
Although most teams would prefer to avoid a road trip like this, the Jaguars actually requested it . With their new stadium currently undergoing a $1.4 billion renovation, the team wanted an extra-long road trip so the construction crews would have a full month to get some work done without worrying about an NFL game.
The final phase of construction at the stadium will take place in 2027, and during that period, the Jaguars will be leaving town for the entire season. Next year, the Jags will be playing their home games in Orlando . The Jags also have a deal in place that allows them to play up to three games in London next year, so they could end up taking one of the longest road trips in NFL history at some point in 2027.
For this year's road trip, the Jaguars will be going 35 days between home games, a stretch that could potentially make or break their season. After the long road trip, the Jags will return home on Nov. 1 for a game against the Colts .

title: Cowboys' Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb have been nearly perfect this season. Why it's still not enough
summary: Both Prescott and Lamb profile as top-five players at their positions while leading a top 10 scoring offense, but Dallas is 1-2
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Do the Dallas Cowboys (1-2) need literal perfection out of four-time Pro Bowl quarterback Dak Prescott and five-time Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb to win games in 2026?
Yes, the question sounds facetious, but the stark contrast in their play versus their defense makes it worth asking. This season, Dallas possesses the No. 7 scoring offense (29.3 points per game) and the No. 25 scoring defense (27.3 points per game). Since Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones traded away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers a week before the start of the 2025 season, Dallas' defense has allowed an NFL-worst 29.7 points per game.
This season, Prescott and Lamb are connecting at a near-perfect rate while both performing like top-five players at their respective positions. Prescott ranks eighth in the NFL in completion percentage (69.5%), tied fifth in passing touchdowns (7), ninth in passer rating (107.2) and fifth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.28). Lamb stands sixth in the league in catches (20), fourth in receiving yards (309) and tied for fourth in receiving touchdowns (3). Lamb had just three receiving touchdowns in the entirety of the 2025 season after suffering a high ankle sprain in a Week 3 loss at the Chicago Bears , but feeling healthy once again, No. 88 is back to full strength.
"He is just playing lights out. He is playing really, really confident," Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams said of Lamb on Thursday. "I love what we're getting right now. He's been outstanding."
However, it's still not nearly enough. The Cowboys are 1-2, thanks in large part to their crumbling defense. But they may have found a way to fix it.
Prescott and Lamb have regained the form they lost over the last few seasons. At their 2023 peak, Lamb led the league in catches (135) and receiving first downs (87), and Prescott led the NFL in passing touchdowns (36). This season, Pro Football Focus charts Dallas' dynamic duo as connecting on 20 of their 25 targets for 309 yards (the third-most between a duo in 2026), three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for an NFL-best 157.8 passer rating. A perfect passer rating is 158.3.
The Prescott-to-Lamb connection is within a point of being perfect. Blitz or no blitz, that hasn't mattered with 13 of the targets coming without a blitz and 12 coming when the defense blitzes. This is what seven seasons (2020-2026) of high-level chemistry looks like.
"CeeDee is a hell of a player. I don't need a lot of credit for him getting open and making those guys miss," Prescott said Thursday. "I think the best thing that's happened, and it'll continue to grow, is just our communication. We've played a lot of ball together, but the more that we're exactly on the same page, the harder it is for whoever and anybody that's trying to cover that guy. So he's thinking the way that I'm thinking, and it's fun."
What does the subtle communication look like this season? A little look here, a lean of the head there and being able to decipher each other's movements and what they're setting in a fraction of a second.
"The longer you're throwing to a guy, there are just little things. Body language, the way he comes out of a route," Adams said. "They can communicate to you with their head turned, and I think these guys have been around each other so long now that Dak knows the speed in which he'll come out of a punch and plant versus a punch and pivot. There's nonverbal communication that goes with the amount of experience that these guys have playing together."
Some people may think seven years together would have made the Prescott-to-Lamb connection old hat, but Lamb claims it's quite the opposite.
"We've been cooking," Lamb said. "I don't think this is our first time really connecting at this rate, but I do hope to continue and continue to build, continue to be better...Like I said in camp, I was learning a lot of things, just finding new ways of getting open."

Brock Purdy to Mike Evans (SF)
Trevor Lawrence to Jakobi Meyers (JAX)
Patrick Mahomes to Travis Kelce (KC)
So what's new for Lamb? He's consistently been one of the NFL's top playmakers out of the slot, but this year, the middle of the field has been open for business for him at perhaps a greater rate than it ever has been. Adams said Dallas has figured out that defenses are trying to attack the line of scrimmage with blitzes from the second level while playing soft, zone coverage behind the blitz. The result? The ability to feast over the middle. Just look at PFF's target maps for the duo:
So do Prescott and Lamb need to maintain this perfection going forward if Dallas is to return to the playoffs for the first time since 2023? Lamb doesn't think so.
"I just feel like we just got to continue to be who we are," Lamb said. "We think so highly of ourselves to where it's almost as if we think of ourselves as playing perfect, playing a perfect game. [It's about] just continuing to stay above the sticks, stay within third and manageable, converting on first downs, getting in the red zone, converting in those [chances]."
This season, the 2026 Cowboys defense made Dallas the third team since 1963 (when team sacks became an officially tracked stat) to allow 375-plus total yards per game (387.0, third-worst in the NFL), have two or fewer sacks (2, third-fewest in the NFL) and no interceptions (tied for last in the NFL) through a season's first three games.
Per CBS Sports Research, the other two teams were the 1976 New York Jets and the 2022 Arizona Cardinals . Neither of those teams hit the five-win mark when their defenses started off this worrisome through the first three games.
* Team sacks became an officially tracked statistic in 1963
That's why Dallas made an early-season blockbuster deal late Wednesday night in an effort to course-correct the defense before the first quarter of the 2026 season comes to a close. They shipped a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for a true No. 1 cornerback in Joey Porter Jr . He led the NFL in passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage in 2025 (among 128 players with at least 60 pass attempts thrown their way) with a 49.1 passer rating allowed. No other corner allowed a sub-50 passer rating against.
Porter Jr.'s 48.1% career completion percentage allowed ranks as the fourth-lowest in the NFL since he entered the league in 2023 among those with at least 150 passes thrown their way, per CBS Sports Research.
The Cowboys are in win-now mode with Jones set to turn 84 years old and desperate for a fourth Super Bowl ring while he is still around to chase them.
"Jerry and I have talked from the very beginning. We're in a win-now mindset," said Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer on Thursday. "Why? Well, Jerry's 84. That's one reason. Dak Prescott's still playing at elite level. We've got some elite weapons on offense, and the defense is getting better. And again, you add a player like this that I've just had a ton of respect for the way he plays."
Prescott is ready to win, too. He saw the Cowboys fumble away his age-31 season in 2024 and his age-32 season in 2025 following three consecutive 12-win campaigns from 2021 to 2023. That's why excitement and gratitude were two of his top emotions when he saw the news that Porter Jr. is now his teammate. Roughly 83% of Dallas' defensive snaps this season are going toward players in either their first or second year with the Cowboys. That's the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the New York Jets (85%) per CBS Sports Research — two teams that are trying everything they can to rebuild their defenses ASAP.
