title: Falcons legend Jeff Van Note has died
summary: Atlanta Falcons fans who endured the first two decades of this franchise’s existence were only occasionally rewarded with winning seasons, much less greatness. As has been the case for the Falcons throughout their 60 year history, it was up to individual stars to make this franchise feel special when the wins and losses didn’t feel […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO - NOVEMBER 23: Jeff Van Note #54 of the Atlanta Falcons sits on the sidelines during a National Football League game against the San Francisco 49ers played on November 23, 1986 at Candlestick Park in San Francisco, California. (Photo by David Madison/Getty Images) | Getty Images Atlanta Falcons fans who endured the first two decades of this franchise’s existence were only occasionally rewarded with winning seasons, much less greatness. As has been the case for the Falcons throughout their 60 year history, it was up to individual stars to make this franchise feel special when the wins and losses didn’t feel special at all. So you watched Tommy Nobis, an underrated great who had the undying respect of his peers. You rooted hard for Claude Humphrey, who put together the first leg of a Hall of Fame career in Atlanta. You winced as Steve Bartkowski took big hits and cheered as he still delivered some of the franchise’s biggest passes. Later on, you watched William Andrews glide and dance through defenders and mourned the career he might have had if not for injury. But if you were a fan of this team all the way back to the 60s, mostly you watched Jeff Van Note. Maybe he didn’t jump out to you on a play-by-play basis, but you saw him every single game mauling some hapless defensive tackle, paving the way for a rotating cast of runners, and keeping everyone from Bob Berry to David Archer upright. You watched him suit up in rain and sunshine, for the worst and best squads the Falcons had to offer, surrounded by players and coaching staffs who continually turned over and changed. The constant was Van Note, with a bloody nose and an injured knee, with that mustache and his 57 jersey crouched over the ball for thousands upon thousands of snaps. He did it for 18 years, missing only four games with that aforementioned knee injury, and along the way Van Note became the greatest center in Falcons history and one of the finest centers the NFL produced in his era. The most remarkable part of that was that he was actually drafted as a linebacker in the 11th round and barely played his rookie season, but Norm Van Brocklin saw Van Note as a center and the rest is history. What made Jeff Van Note great—inspiring, even—was that consistency. He did something he loved and was good at tenaciously, professionally, and with little complaint, no matter how dark and dumb everything around him might have been or felt. He gave so much to this franchise as a player, a legend, and later a broadcaster that it was a no-brainer to make the six-time Pro Bowler a Ring of Honor inductee. The very best players and people the Falcons have offered us over these many years, from Van Note to Mike Kenn to Julio Jones to Grady Jarrett to Matt Ryan, have followed in his footsteps by coming to play, by leading in word and deed, and showing up on Sundays to try to drag this impossible franchise to greatness with everything they could give. It’s a wonder, and the work and the dignity and the consistency are something we can all admire and emulate in our own lives. Jeff Van Note has died , as the headline says, and we mourn the passing of a Falcons legend. But we also remember Jeff Van Note as a good man and a great player who gave so much to our favorite team, and we can and should kindle that memory for many, many years to come.

title: AFC North Preview, Week 4: Steelers and Browns face off in primetime at 2-1
summary: After three weeks, all four teams in the AFC North have the same record, sitting at 2-1 each. The Steelers, Browns and Ravens were each victorious in Week 2, while the Bengals lost to Pittsburgh in the first divisional contest of the season. Let’s take a look at the updated standings and break down each […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers fumbles as he is sacked by Grant Delpit #9 of the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images After three weeks, all four teams in the AFC North have the same record, sitting at 2-1 each. The Steelers, Browns and Ravens were each victorious in Week 2, while the Bengals lost to Pittsburgh in the first divisional contest of the season. Let’s take a look at the updated standings and break down each team’s upcoming matchup in Week 4. Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers 2-1 Baltimore Ravens 2-1 Cleveland Browns 2-1 Cincinnati Bengals 2-1 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ Cleveland Browns, 8:15pm EST (Thursday Night) The Steelers are coming off a nail-biting win over the Bengals last week, where they squeezed out a 30-27 victory in a surprisingly high-scoring affair. In doing so, Pittsburgh jumped out to an early 1-0 record in the division, which places them atop the standings despite all teams having the same record. The Steelers had their best offensive performance of the season thus far in Week 3, gaining over 400 total yards with 22 first downs. They’ll look to replicate this success as road favorites against the Browns on Thursday Night Football. The biggest revelation for the Steelers from last game is they found success on the ground. Without Rico Dowdle (toe) in the lineup, Jaylen Warren totaled 127 rushing yards on just 17 carries — while also adding another 49 yards as a receiver. Expect Warren to be featured heavily again versus Cleveland’s defense, whose front seven has been strong so far this year. Pittsburgh was also able to get complimentary pass-catchers like Roman Wilson and Broderick Washington involved in the passing game. Aaron Rodgers should continue spreading the ball around to keep the Browns’ defense honest. On the other side of the ball, the Steelers had their worst performance of the early season last week, but there’s reason for optimism in this matchup. While they’ve won their last two games, the Browns still rank bottom-five in both passing yards and rushing yards per game. If the Steelers can get pressure on Deshaun Watson and prevent the Browns from unlocking any explosive plays, they should be able to keep points to a minimum. Cleveland Browns Matchup: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers, 8:15pm EST (Thursday Night) The aforementioned Browns are coming off a second straight win after looking lifeless in the regular season opener. Cleveland narrowly defeated the Carolina Panthers at home, 21-18, and won both recent games by a combined seven points. Nevertheless, the Browns defense has been playing well, and they’re getting more complimentary play on the offensive side of the ball. This week’s divisional matchup against the Steelers at home will be a big test for head coach Todd Monken’s team. Much has been made about Deshaun Watson’s sudden turnaround and while his play has improved, the Browns’ passing attack has still been limited to mostly short-yardage throws. The biggest factor for Watson is avoiding turnovers, which he’s done much better with no interceptions since Week 1. Watson’s scrambling ability has also been a weapon for the Browns, as he’s rushed for 105 yards overall with a 21-yard run last week. The Steelers will likely try to heat up Watson under center. If the Browns can connect on a couple of explosive plays, that could be a huge lift for them. On defense, look for the Browns to make a concerted effort to keep Warren contained. If the Steelers struggle to run the ball, they are much less potent offensively. Mason Graham has been a force in the middle of the defensive front with four sacks in three games. He could be big X-factor against Zach Frazier, one of the top centers in the league. The Browns’ defensive backs match up well against Pittsburgh’s pass-catchers on paper, so they may feel comfortable playing a lot of man coverage to cause more havoc at the line of scrimmage. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: vs. Tennessee Titans, 1:00pm EST The Ravens came out of their trip to Brazil as winners of a thrilling game against the Dallas Cowboys. A back-and-forth, high-scoring affair saw the Ravens escape with a 34-31 victory following late-game heroics from Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers and Tyler Loop, who kicked the game-winning 56-yard field goal. It was far from a perfect win but much-needed, as they staved off another potential blown double-digit lead defeat. Now, the Ravens will look to secure their first win at home this year in a favorable matchup against the Titans. The Titans rank second-to-last in yards per game and have scored the third fewest points, averaging 12.3 through three weeks. They’ve had two chances to win close games over the past two weeks but came up short, losing by a combined nine points. This is a prime chance for Jesse Minter’s defense to have a breakout performance, which has been up-and-down so far. Expect Minter to dial up blitzes often against second-year quarterback Cam Ward and create exotic defensive looks. The former No. 1 overall pick has thrown for 168 yards per game so far. Tennessee’s defense has been much more formidable, ranking No. 10 in yards and points allowed per game. The biggest challenge for the Ravens’ offensively will be blocking up front, particularly limiting the damage of All-Pro defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons. The onus will be on Vega Ioane, who is set to start at center for the first time, John Simpson and Andrew Vorhees/Emery Jones Jr. to hold up. The Ravens have been a bottom-tier pass protection team so far this season. Derrick Henry will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Tennessee, so expect him to be extra motivated to have another productive afternoon. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, 1:00pm EST As mentioned previously, the Bengals dropped a close game to the Steelers last week on the road, giving them their first loss of the season. They took a big step back defensively in that matchup, allowing over 400 yards and 22 first downs, and will look to bounce back in a difficult Week 4 matchup. The Bengals are hosting a talented Jaguars team that is also 2-1 and has a point differential of +46 this season, which ranks No. 2 narrowly behind the San Francisco 49ers. In slowing down the Jaguars’ offense, the Bengals will need to key in on Parker Washington, who is an emerging star at wide receiver. Washington has 15 catches for 221 receiving yards and three touchdowns through three games, establishing himself as Trevor Lawrence’s go-to target. The Bengals are allowing 260 passing yards per game, which ranks fifth-worst in the league. Their ability to force turnovers against Lawrence and limit explosive plays will be key for pulling out a win. On offense, the Bengals will try again to unlock more explosive plays in the run game. Chase Brown’s longest rush of the season so far has gone for only 12 yards. Joe Burrow has started to build some momentum with five touchdowns and no turnovers over the past two games. The Jaguars’ is Top 10 against the run but allows the ninth-most passing yards per game, so this may be another Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins-centric game.

title: Buffalo Bills are about to have an abundance of defensive line depth
summary: The strength of the Buffalo Bills defense through two games has been its play in the trenches and on the edge, and the team’s frontline is on the verge of becoming incredibly deep. Let’s not take anything away from the inside linebacker group — Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard have played quality football. But Greg […]
full_text: The strength of the Buffalo Bills defense through two games has been its play in the trenches and on the edge, and the team’s frontline is on the verge of becoming incredibly deep. Let’s not take anything away from the inside linebacker group — Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard have played quality football. But Greg Rousseau just won AFC Defensive Player of the Month , Deone Walker has been unblockable in the middle, and DeWayne Carter is emerging as one of the better run-stopping rotational defensive tackles in the NFL, out of nowhere. August acquisition Greg Gaines has filled-in admirably too with 55 snaps through three contests. He only has one pressure yet has made four tackles with two stops and done the dirty work on stunts and when asked to eat double teams against the run. Ed Oliver missed Week 2 against the Lions but has five pressures on 64 pass-rush snaps and made plenty of impact disrupting the Texans backfield in Week 1 that couldn’t be found on the stat sheet. Landon Jackson has been the least-effective of Buffalo’s defensive linemen to date, yet he has seven tackles without a miss on 83 snaps through three games in a mostly non-sexy, two-gapping role. Entering Week 4’s clash with the Patriots, the Bills those five defensive linemen have played between 25% and 67% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps. And now likely adding to that group — 2025 second-round pick T.J. Sanders. Sure, his rookie season was underwhelming, and he dealt with a knee injury. He’s yet to appear in 2026 thanks to another knee ailment and an appendectomy. He went from DNP on Wednesday to limited on Thursday, so he’s trending in the right direction for Sunday. I know there’s essentially zero buzz for Sanders right now. I absolutely still believe in him. He’s super talented. In August, I called him the biggest X-factor on Buffalo’s defense . For a team that, on paper, wants to deploy two or three defensive linemen on any given play, Sanders’ return — along with veteran Phidarian Mathis on the practice squad — makes for significant depth. The edge group isn’t as deep, but Jim Leonhard suddenly has plenty of horses on the interior of his defense that offer a variety of differing skill sets to opposing offensive lines.

title: Bills Week 4 rooting interests: Who Buffalo fans should root for
summary: Three weeks down, and so far our rooting interests have been pretty easy to figure out.  The Buffalo Bills should win. The rest of the AFC East should lose. Teams Buffalo has beaten should win, because strength of victory is our friend. Teams still waiting on the Bills’ schedule can win, too, because strength of schedule may eventually matter.  And, when […]
full_text: Football: Buffalo Bills fans display a sign that reads Lets Go Buffalo vs Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium. Orchard Park, NY 11/2/2025 CREDIT: Erick W. Rasco (Photo by Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X164794 TK1) Three weeks down, and so far our rooting interests have been pretty easy to figure out. The Buffalo Bills should win. The rest of the AFC East should lose. Teams Buffalo has beaten should win, because strength of victory is our friend. Teams still waiting on the Bills’ schedule can win, too, because strength of schedule may eventually matter. And, when none of that applies, we can always fall back on one of my favorite rules: Bad AFC teams should win enough games to stay away from the really good draft picks, while bad NFC teams are welcome to lose as often as they would like and collect them instead. But we’re getting close to the point where things change. After this weekend, four games will be in the books. That’s still early, but it’s also roughly a quarter of the regular season. Beginning next week, we’re going to have to start paying a little more attention to the top of the AFC standings. Strength of schedule is nice. Making the road to the No. 1 seed a little less crowded is nicer. For one more week, though, we’ll mostly stick with the rules that got us here. _____________________________________________________________________________- AFC East New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills Root for: Buffalo Bills This one needs no explanation. But the win will mean more than a much more pleasant Monday for Bills Mafia. It’s Buffalo’s first AFC East game of the season. New England is 1-2. Not going to lie – watching the Patriots return to reality has been fun. Let’s remind them who the real “Beast of the East” is. Go Bills! New York Jets at Chicago Bears Root for: Chicago Bears This one checks two boxes. The Jets are the Jets, which means we want them to lose. The Bears are also on Buffalo’s schedule later this season, which means a Chicago win helps the strength-of-schedule side of things. No overthinking required. Miami Dolphins at Minnesota Vikings Root for: Minnesota Vikings Miami loses? Good. A future Buffalo opponent wins? Also good. The Vikings are 3-0, but they’re safely tucked away in the NFC, so their undefeated record isn’t standing between Buffalo and anything we want. Let Minnesota keep winning while Miami keeps doing the opposite. _____________________________________________________________________________ Rest of the AFC Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns Root for: Cleveland Browns This is a weird place to start because the entire AFC North is 2-1. There isn’t a bottom-feeder available for us to adopt, and there isn’t a clear division leader for us to knock down. So, we’ll take Cleveland. If the Browns eventually turn into a legitimate AFC threat, we’ll adjust. For now, putting another loss on Pittsburgh works just fine, and we don’t have a strength-of-schedule reason to prefer either one. Indianapolis Colts at Washington Commanders Root for: Washington Commanders Here’s an easy one. Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule, and Indianapolis is in the AFC. Give the AFC team another loss and let Washington take the win. It doesn’t do much for Buffalo, but not every game has to. Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans Root for: Houston Texans Houston is 0-3, which isn’t exactly helping Buffalo’s strength of victory after the Bills beat the Texans in Week 1. A Texans win gives Buffalo’s strength of victory a boost and gets Houston away from the bottom of the standings and, eventually, the very top of the draft. That’s two reasons to temporarily become Texans fans. So, come on, Houston. Do something useful. Tennessee Titans at Baltimore Ravens Root for: Baltimore Ravens Enjoy this one, because I suspect this answer might be different pretty soon.Baltimore is on Buffalo’s schedule and Tennessee isn’t, so under our early-season rules, we’re rooting for the Ravens and the strength-of-schedule bump. But Baltimore is already 2-1 and very much part of the AFC conversation. Once we get through this week, teams hanging around the top of the conference aren’t going to keep getting our support just because Buffalo plays them eventually. Jacksonville Jaguars at Cincinnati Bengals Root for: Cincinnati Bengals There isn’t much direct Buffalo benefit available here. Both teams are 2-1, neither is on Buffalo’s schedule, and they’re both in the AFC. So, this is mostly a pick-your-poison game. Jacksonville currently leads the AFC South, while Cincinnati is stuck in that ridiculous four-way 2-1 tie in the AFC North. We’ll take Cincinnati and put a loss on a division leader. We’re getting close enough to the point where that starts mattering. Kansas City Chiefs at Las Vegas Raiders Root for: Las Vegas Raiders And here is where our rules collide headfirst. Kansas City is 3-0. Las Vegas is 3-0. Both are sitting right beside Buffalo at the top of the AFC, and the Raiders are also on Buffalo’s schedule in Week 6 – a full six weeks before the Bills can handle their own business with the Chiefs. So we’re taking Las Vegas and handing Kansas City its first loss. Los Angeles Chargers at Seattle Seahawks Root for: Los Angeles Chargers Please win a football game, Chargers. Buffalo just beat Los Angeles, but that put the Chargers at 0-3. That’s not particularly helpful for the strength-of-victory column. A Chargers win gives that number a boost and, as a bonus, moves an AFC team away from the premium draft picks. Seattle can take the loss and move a little closer to them instead. This is exactly what our weird little rule system was built for. Denver Broncos at San Francisco 49ers Root for: Denver Broncos This one is mostly about strength of schedule. Denver is a future Buffalo opponent, so every Broncos win makes the Bills’ schedule a little stronger. They’re 2-1, which is worth keeping an eye on in the AFC, but we’re not quite ready to start rooting against every AFC team with a winning record. Plus, a Denver win coupled with our hopeful Kansas City loss keeps the AFC West crowded at the top. Let them spend all their time and energy fighting with each other. Maybe by the time they remember Buffalo is over here, they won’t have much fight left for us. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants Root for: Arizona Cardinals Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule, so we’re heading to the draft-pick portion of the program. The Giants are 2-1. Arizona is 1-2. Let the Cardinals get back toward the middle while the Giants take the loss. We’re not trying to hand premium draft capital to NFC teams that don’t need our help getting better. Los Angeles Rams at Philadelphia Eagles Root for: Los Angeles Rams Meet next week’s opponent. Buffalo heads to Los Angeles in Week 5, so we’d like the Rams to look a little better before the Bills get there. A Rams win improves Buffalo’s strength of schedule now and could become a strength-of-victory boost later if Buffalo handles its own business. Besides, at 1-2, Los Angeles could use the help. Green Bay Packers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers Root for: Green Bay Packers The Packers are on Buffalo’s schedule. The Buccaneers aren’t. That’s enough for now. Green Bay doesn’t show up until December but wins count the same whether we collect them for the strength-of-schedule pile before or after we meet. Detroit Lions at Carolina Panthers Root for: Detroit Lions Buffalo already beat Detroit, so we know the drill. Every Lions win from here makes that Week 2 victory look a little better. Carolina doesn’t appear on Buffalo’s schedule and can happily absorb the loss. Strength of victory wins this one. Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints Root for: Whoever you want We’ve found it. The game where I can’t come up with a particularly convincing reason to care. Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule. Both are in the NFC. Both are 1-2. If we’re…

title: Buffalo Bills Record Book Watch: Josh Allen one TD from history
summary: Three weeks into the season, the Buffalo Bills’ record book is already getting a little crowded.  Josh Allen keeps running his way past some of the biggest names in NFL history. Greg Rousseau has apparently decided two sacks per game is a perfectly reasonable pace. And James Cook took one look at the absurd number we gave him in […]
full_text: Three weeks into the season, the Buffalo Bills’ record book is already getting a little crowded. Josh Allen keeps running his way past some of the biggest names in NFL history. Greg Rousseau has apparently decided two sacks per game is a perfectly reasonable pace. And James Cook took one look at the absurd number we gave him in last week’s Superhuman chapter and knocked a rather large chunk off it anyway. Now the New England Patriots are coming to Orchard Park, and the numbers are starting to get interesting. Some records need only a nudge. Others require another afternoon of doing something that really shouldn’t have become routine. Let’s open the book and get started. Grab the pencil pouch — we’ll need a pencil, an eraser, and, if things go according to plan, plenty of permanent ink. ____________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1: Sure Things • Dawson Knox receptions: Knox caught one pass against Los Angeles, bringing his career total to 233 and pulling him even with Cole Beasley on Buffalo’s all-time receptions list. One catch Sunday gives Knox 234 and moves him past Beasley into 15th place all by himself. Considering Knox has caught at least one pass in every game this season, we’re comfortable putting this one in permanent ink territory. Of course, we were comfortable with Shakir here last week, too, and immediately blamed ourselves for whatever happened next. Apparently, Sure Things comes with some responsibility. ____________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2: A Good Bet • Josh Allen rushing touchdowns: Allen ran for two more touchdowns against the Chargers, bringing his career total to 85 and pulling him even with former Bill Marshawn Lynch for 17th on the NFL’s all-time list. One rushing touchdown against New England does quite a bit of housekeeping. No. 86 moves Allen past Beast Mode, ties Priest Holmes for 16th in NFL history, and gives Allen the 88th touchdown he has scored as a Bill, breaking the franchise record he currently shares with Andre Reed and Thurman Thomas. Of course, Allen could make a mess of our carefully organized record book by catching a touchdown instead. That would still break the Bills’ franchise touchdown record, while leaving Lynch and Holmes exactly where they are. And, considering Allen already has four career receiving touchdowns, we probably shouldn’t give him any ideas. One trip to the end zone. Three changes to two different record books — assuming Allen gets there the conventional quarterback-who-doesn’t-play-conventionally way. We probably should have grabbed more permanent ink. ____________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3: Not Impossible Apparently, we have a theme. • Josh Allen rushing touchdowns: Allen has rushed for two touchdowns in each of Buffalo’s first three games, becoming just the fourth player in NFL history to open a season with multiple rushing touchdowns in three straight games. Two more against New England would extend that streak to four. It would also bring Allen to 87 career rushing touchdowns, moving him past both Marshawn Lynch and Priest Holmes on the NFL’s all-time list. And, yes, it would make everything we just wrote in Chapter 2 permanent-ink official. • Greg Rousseau sacks: Rousseau has been working in twos, too. He has exactly two sacks in each of the Bills’ first three games, giving him six on the season — the most ever by a Buffalo player through three games. He’s also just the third NFL player to begin a season with at least two sacks in each of his first three games. And apparently we aren’t the only ones who noticed. Rousseau was just named the AFC Defensive Player of the Month for September. So what are we asking for Sunday? Two rushing touchdowns from Allen. Two sacks from the newly minted AFC Defensive Player of the Month. Apparently, Not Impossible now means just keep doing the ridiculous thing you’ve done every single week. ____________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4: Superhuman • James Cook rushing yards: Look who refuses to leave. Last week, Cook needed 363 yards to catch Josh Allen for fourth place on the Bills’ all-time rushing list. We pointed out that would require him to break Adrian Peterson’s NFL single-game record by 67 yards. Cook responded by running for 154 yards against the Chargers while Allen added 22. So, fine. We’ll do the math again. Allen now sits at 4,835 career rushing yards, with Cook at 4,605. That leaves 230 yards between them, meaning Cook needs to outgain his quarterback by 231 yards Sunday to take over fourth place. Is that still Superhuman? Absolutely. Is it considerably less Superhuman than it was seven days ago? Also yes. Apparently, Cook has decided this chapter is less a category and more a weekly challenge. Welcome back, Chef. ____________________________________________________________________ We’ve sharpened the pencils, found the eraser, and uncapped the permanent ink. Now we wait to see which one we’ll need most on Sunday. Somewhere between one Dawson Knox catch and James Cook casually outrushing his quarterback by 231 yards, there should be something worth adding to the record book.

title: DeWayne Carter emerging as one of NFL’s better run-stopping DTs
summary: The DeWayne Carter emergence is so surprising, I can’t help myself but to write about the third-year pro again ahead of the Buffalo Bills matchup with the New England Patriots in Week 4. On September 22, I wrote about Carter making the most of his opportunity in the first two contests of the season. Then, […]
full_text: The DeWayne Carter emergence is so surprising, I can’t help myself but to write about the third-year pro again ahead of the Buffalo Bills matchup with the New England Patriots in Week 4. On September 22, I wrote about Carter making the most of his opportunity in the first two contests of the season. Then, he rocked against the Chargers in Week 3. His best performance as a member of the Bills, in my opinion. Because there are now three games of 2026 in Carter’s third season to pull from — let’s call it a mini-breakout for now — he’s due for a film session. Carter has four pressures on 42 pass-rush snaps entering Week 4, good for a respectable pressure rate of 9.5% (particularly for a 320-plus pounder). But Carter has made the most sizable impact against the run, and of course, Buffalo clearly needed to improve its porous ground-game defense from a season ago. Seth has yet to describe the methodology behind his new run-defense metric, but we can safely assume Carter’s place in the Top 10 can serve as another indication of the sturdiness of his run-stopping performance to date. Let’s dive into those run-stopping efforts. Here against the Texans, watch how Carter, aligned at 1T to the right of the ball on the screen, bench presses the center at the point of attack before quickly reacting to the play direction to help secure the tackle near the line of scrimmage. pic.twitter.com/GfhvQME2Dw — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) October 1, 2026 That is A+ awareness and wherewithal to find the ball-carrier and take him down in a very short period of time after the snap. The following week against the Lions, Carter demonstrated his nimble feet and balance when avoiding a wham block from tight end Sam LaPorta, who’s a damn good in-line blocker. pic.twitter.com/usHOVOVodz — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) October 1, 2026 Not only did Carter impressively avoid LaPorta altogether, he closed on Jahmyr Gibbs, probably the most purely explosive running back in football, before he could flip on the jets through the line of scrimmage. Then against the Chargers, aligned at 2i on the inside shoulder of the left guard, Carter effortlessly worked through the down block from the center to stop this Omarion Hampton run before it could materialize. pic.twitter.com/OTI8awP67p — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) October 1, 2026 Another run lane closed quickly. Back to Week 1 against the Texans, this was probably the most shining example of Carter’s potential against the run. On this play, he was aligned at 2i again, on the inside shoulder of the right guard. At the snap, watch how Carter crossed the face of No. 69 Ed Ingram, ripped to keep the blocker off him, planted his outside foot in the ground to launch to stop Woody Marks in his tracks. pic.twitter.com/ZEz9MrIzgU — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) October 1, 2026 And how about Carter’s tackling radius there? Serious lower-body explosion to wrap up the second-year running back in a flash. Heck, that’s the real-life, on-field usage of the broad jump at the combine right there. Those were all high-caliber run-stopping reps from Carter. And he’s making those kind of impact plays after adding 20-30 pounds this offseason to play closer to the football along the defensive line. From likely cut to run-defense cog who has provided pass-rush juice at a reasonable clip, Carter has been, quite easily, the most pleasant surprise on Buffalo’s defense in the first three games of the 2026 campaign.

title: Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns, Week 4 ‘TNF’ fan discussion
summary: Thursday Night Football is back, Rumblers! While there’s no Buffalo Bills game until Sunday, there is a hard-nosed AFC North divisional matchup to enjoy this evening. We’ve finally hit October on the world’s most popular calendar, and, with that, the hitting gets all the more intense the deeper into fall we go. Tonight, the Cleveland […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers fumbles the ball defended by Grant Delpit #9 of the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thursday Night Football is back, Rumblers! While there’s no Buffalo Bills game until Sunday, there is a hard-nosed AFC North divisional matchup to enjoy this evening. We’ve finally hit October on the world’s most popular calendar, and, with that, the hitting gets all the more intense the deeper into fall we go. Tonight, the Cleveland Browns host the Pittsburgh Steelers in a battle of two 2-1 teams. The entire AFC North is log-jammed at 2-1, but the Steelers have a tenuous hold on first place, while the Browns are currently in the third slot. This is an important early season game, and one plenty that should hold your interest most of the evening. Are we in for a low-scoring slugfest, or will quarterbacks Aaron Rodgers and Deshaun Watson light it up in primetime? It’s worth wondering who actually enjoys watching either guy throw the football these day, but here we are. In terms of rooting interests, there’s not a lot of drama regarding Bills story lines. It’s a “choose your own adventure” evening. If history holds, then Pittsburgh is the more “dangerous” team as a playoff hopeful. However, it really doesn’t matter since Buffalo doesn’t play either team in the regular season. It’s really difficult finding a good reason to cheer on Rodgers or Watson. Impossible? That’s for you to decide. If you care about such things, Rodgers has said he’s retiring at the end of the 2026 NFL season, so tonight would be the final ‘TNF’ game for him. Remember, the Browns traded away Myles Garrett, and just today the Steelers traded away Joey Porter Jr. In terms of drawing power, these teams look a bit different than they did last December. There’s an interesting fact for uniform connoisseurs: Pittsburgh and Cleveland have a combined one logo between the right and left “sides” of their helmets. Plus, the Browns have this little elf guy they called Brownie, but most people forget about him, and he’s never been used by the team as their helmet logo. Maybe the NFL needs elf logos? With that, here’s your open thread for Week 4 of Thursday Night Football on Prime ! As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Patriots: Josh Allen rivalry history
summary: There are a lot of places we could set the dial on the Time Capsule this week.  The Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots have been sharing the AFC East for decades, leaving us with more than enough games, moments, and grudges to fill this space several times over. New England holds an 80-52-1 advantage […]
full_text: There are a lot of places we could set the dial on the Time Capsule this week. The Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots have been sharing the AFC East for decades, leaving us with more than enough games, moments, and grudges to fill this space several times over. New England holds an 80-52-1 advantage in the all-time series. But that record comes with a pretty significant Tom Brady/Bill Belichick-sized asterisk. During that era, the Patriots went 34-4 against Buffalo. Take those games away, and the Bills actually lead the rest of the series, 48-46-1. We remember. We don’t particularly need to relive all of it. So, instead of traveling through the entire history of Bills-Patriots football, we’re setting the Time Capsule for 2018 — the year Josh Allen arrived in Buffalo. Allen entered the rivalry while New England still owned it. Since then, the balance has shifted, the Patriots dynasty has ended, and some of the most memorable games of the Allen era have come against the team that spent so many years standing in Buffalo’s way. Before the Bills and Patriots meet again Sunday in Orchard Park, let’s go back to where the Josh Allen chapter of this rivalry began. ________________________________________ 2018-19: Some things hadn’t changed yet Josh Allen’s first chance at the Patriots came late in his rookie season, although it wasn’t his first chance to watch them from the Buffalo sideline. He was injured when New England came to Orchard Park in October 2018, then got the start when the Bills traveled to Foxborough two days before Christmas. It went about the way Bills-Patriots games had been going for most of the previous two decades. New England won 24-12, Allen threw for 217 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, and the Patriots continued on their way to another AFC East title — and, eventually, another Super Bowl. A year later, Buffalo was much closer to becoming the team we recognize now. The Bills started the 2019 season 3-0 before the defending Super Bowl champions came to Orchard Park. Buffalo’s defense held Tom Brady to 150 passing yards and no touchdowns, but Allen threw three interceptions before leaving the game, and New England escaped with a 16-10 win. By the time the teams met again in December, the Bills were 10-4 and had already secured a playoff spot. This time Allen threw for 208 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, and Buffalo carried a 17-13 lead into the fourth quarter. New England still found a way to win, 24-17. Allen’s record against the Patriots was 0-3. Buffalo was getting closer, but close still counted the same way it always had against New England. _____________________________________________ 2020: The first turn Tom Brady was gone when New England arrived in Orchard Park on Nov. 1, 2020, but beating the Patriots still mattered. Buffalo hadn’t beaten New England at home since 2011. Sean McDermott had never beaten Bill Belichick as a head coach. And Allen, after three tries, was still looking for his first win against the Patriots. The Bills finally got it, 24-21, but even that one came with a little late-game drama. New England was driving in Buffalo territory in the final minute when Justin Zimmer knocked the ball loose from Cam Newton and Dean Marlowe recovered it. If that win cracked the door, the rematch kicked it open. Buffalo went to Foxborough for Monday Night Football in December with the AFC East title already secured and handed New England a 38-9 loss. Allen threw four touchdown passes, three to Stefon Diggs, as the Bills completed their first season sweep of the Patriots since 1999. A rivalry that had spent years feeling impossibly one-sided suddenly looked very different. _________________________________________ 2021: The wind, the rematch, and the Perfect Game Of course, New England wasn’t going to disappear quietly. The Patriots came to Orchard Park for Monday Night Football in December with first place in the AFC East at stake and weather conditions that turned the game into one of the strangest chapters in the teams’ entwined history. With wind gusts whipping through the stadium, New England attempted just three passes. The Patriots ran the ball 46 times, Buffalo couldn’t finish its late opportunities, and New England left with a 14-10 win and control of the division. Three weeks later, the Bills went to Foxborough and took it back. Allen threw for 314 yards and three touchdowns in a 33-21 Buffalo win that put the Bills back atop the AFC East. Buffalo went on to win the division, and the reward was another meeting with New England — this time in Orchard Park in the Wild Card round. That one didn’t require much late-game drama. Buffalo scored touchdowns on each of its first seven possessions. The Bills didn’t punt. They didn’t attempt a field goal. They didn’t turn the ball over. Allen threw for 308 yards and five touchdowns, and Buffalo eliminated New England with a 47-17 win in a game that became known simply as the Perfect Game. For a generation of Bills fans who had spent most of the Brady era waiting for New England to deliver the next miserable chapter, this was something entirely different. Buffalo didn’t just beat the Patriots. For one freezing January night in Orchard Park, the Bills owned them. _________________________________________ 2022-25: Buffalo has the upper hand, but New England still gets its shots The Perfect Game didn’t end the rivalry. It did, however, change what Bills fans expected from it. Buffalo swept New England again during the 2022 season, including an emotional 35-23 win in Orchard Park in the regular-season finale. But the Patriots have provided enough reminders since then that division games rarely cooperate with expectations. New England stunned Buffalo 29-25 in Foxborough in October 2023 before the Bills answered with a 27-21 win at home later that season. Buffalo won the first meeting of 2024 as well, 24-21 in Orchard Park. The Patriots won the season finale in Foxborough, 23-16, although that game came after Buffalo had already locked up the AFC’s No. 2 seed and Allen played only one snap before Mitch Trubisky took over. Then came 2025, and a Patriots team that was suddenly much more difficult to dismiss. New England came into Orchard Park in October and handed Buffalo a 23-20 loss. When the teams met again in December, the Bills found themselves down 21-0 in Foxborough before Allen and the offense flipped the game. Buffalo scored touchdowns on five consecutive possessions, Allen threw three touchdown passes, and the Bills came all the way back for a 35-31 win. __________________________________________________________________________ Which brings the Time Capsule back to Orchard Park, where the two will meet Sunday afternoon to write the next chapter of this long-running sag Allen’s chapter against New England started with three straight losses, at a time when the Patriots were still the team Buffalo was trying to catch. Eight years later, Brady is long gone, the AFC East has changed hands more than once, and the Bills no longer enter Patriots week wondering whether they can finally get past New England. But if the last few seasons have taught us anything, it’s that New England may no longer own this rivalry, but they haven’t exactly made a habit of going quietly.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Greg Rousseau named AFC Defensive Player of the Month after historic September for the Bills
summary: The NFL calendar has officially flipped to October, but Greg Rousseau has one more piece of business to collect from September. Rousseau has been named AFC Defensive Player of the Month, the first monthly award of his NFL career and the first for a Buffalo Bills defensive player since Jordan Poyer earned the honor in […]
full_text: The NFL calendar has officially flipped to October, but Greg Rousseau has one more piece of business to collect from September. Rousseau has been named AFC Defensive Player of the Month, the first monthly award of his NFL career and the first for a Buffalo Bills defensive player since Jordan Poyer earned the honor in December 2017. And considering what Rousseau did during the Bills’ 3-0 start, this one shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. GROOOOOOT‼️ @gregrousseau is the AFC Defensive Player of the Month: https://t.co/qcavvvXdBZ pic.twitter.com/3FQtJeqPwM — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) October 1, 2026 Three games. Six sacks. Rousseau opened the season with two sacks in each of Buffalo’s first three games, giving him an NFL-leading six sacks in September. He also forced three fumbles, tying for the league lead. NFL statistics confirm Rousseau finished the month with 15 total tackles, 12 solo tackles, six sacks, three forced fumbles and a pass defended. But the numbers become even more impressive when you start attaching some history to them. Rousseau became just the third player in NFL history to record at least two sacks in each of his first three games of a season, joining Mark Gastineau in 1984 and Kevin Greene in 1998. He also joined some pretty exclusive company in Buffalo. Rousseau became only the third Bills player to record three consecutive games with at least two sacks, joining Bruce Smith in 1990 and Bryce Paup in 1995. That is not a bad pair of names for Groot to find himself standing beside. Consistency was the story There wasn’t one game doing the heavy lifting, either. Rousseau recorded two sacks against the Houston Texans in Week 1, two more against the Detroit Lions in Week 2 and another two against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3. He added two forced fumbles against Houston and another against Detroit. His six sacks are already within one of the seven sacks he recorded during the entire 2025 season. Rousseau’s career high is eight, which he recorded in both 2022 and 2024. Yes, we are only three games into the season, but I think Rousseau might be a fan of the new defensive scheme. From weekly recognition to a monthly honor Rousseau’s start has been one of the biggest stories of Buffalo’s undefeated September, and we’ve been watching the streak build each week. Now the NFL has acknowledged his success in September. Three games. Three consecutive two-sack performances. And now, AFC Defensive Player of the Month. Not a bad opening month for Groot.
author: Sara Larson

title: Buffalo Bills vs. New England Patriots; Movable object vs. stoppable force
summary: After allowing 31 points in their first two games, the Buffalo Bills finally had a respectable outing on defense against the Los Angeles Chargers by allowing 6.9 points less than the league average of 22.9. That said, questions still abound regarding the Bills’ D because, well… it’s very well possible the Chargers just. kinda. suck. […]
full_text: After allowing 31 points in their first two games, the Buffalo Bills finally had a respectable outing on defense against the Los Angeles Chargers by allowing 6.9 points less than the league average of 22.9. That said, questions still abound regarding the Bills’ D because, well… it’s very well possible the Chargers just. kinda. suck. Sure, allowing 16 points is a good thing, but it’s also the highest total anyone has allowed Los Angeles so far this year. If Buffalo’s defense then is a movable object, it should come as no small comfort then that so far their next opponent has been a very stoppable force on offense. The New England Patriots are tied with the Miami Dolphins as the worst offense in the league at 12 points per game scored. That’s juuuuuuuuust over half the league average. Speaking of average offense, the Patriots offense has gotten within a field goal of it with their 20 point effort in Week 2 vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers (their only win so far). Buffalo managed 24 points in a game where they handed over the ball faster and more often than Halloween candy. This intro is already too long; in this matchup of potential futility, who has the edge? Weakness vs. Weakness: Analyzed Before we begin with the stats, let’s take a trip down memory lane. Remember when I used to do math videos each week? HA! That was weird. Let’s do a call back to one, to explain my “rule of four.” If you’re too stubborn to give me clicks on the ol’ YouTube here’s a very brief breakdown. Top ten lists for NFL teams can take a hike. The top ten of a 32 team distribution is over 30% of the sample size. Guess what? The bottom part of your top ten is thoroughly average and should be treated like it. The rule of four is based around a Bell Curve distribution and, while not absolute, provides a good rule of thumb to separate teams into groups. Groups of fours, hence the name. In the 32 team distribution for a stat my rule of thumb says the top four are the “elite” teams. The next four can be considered “good” or more accurately “better than average.” Average is a bit tricky as “average” should never be considered a single point. In fact, in most groupings the “average” cluster is the largest group by far. If you multiply four by four, you get sixteen. The middle sixteen teams are average. The next group of four are the “bad” or “worse than average” team, and the final group of four are the “terrible” teams. Or to visualize… 1 – 4 = Elite 5 – 8 = Good 9 – 24 = Average 25 – 28 = Bad 29- 32 = Terrible Got it? OK, let’s begin then… The Buffalo Bills’ Defense We’ll start with my favorite stat, points per drive. The Bills allow 2.52 points per drive, which ranks 25th. That squeaks into the “bad” grouping. They allow a scoring drive about 45% of the time and are 23rd in the league so “average.” To clarify, I don’t mean to insinuate there’s no difference between a rank of 23 vs. a rank of 10; but on gamedays you shouldn’t expect a lot of predictive validity in that stat. The 23 can likely be expected to hang against the 10. The Bills have an average takeaway rate with a rank of 17 and narrowly hit average with a rank of 24 in yards allowed per drive. There’s not a single major stat I can find where the Bills reach the “good” level. The closest is sack rate where their 8.18% lands at ten. On the flip side, there’s a few more “bad” stats and even some dabbling into “terrible.” Their interception rate is 26th, they’re 30th in first downs allowed per game; and the 27th ranked passing yards per game shows that their decent sack rate hasn’t precisely resulted in stopping the passing game of their opponents. Is there any signs of life from this group? Why yes! Let’s check out play direction charts courtesy of the NFL. If you’re new to these charts, they show play direction-based rankings and stats and are almost as high up the information I love to look at as per drive metrics. What do they show for Buffalo? In the rushing game, they’re actually good at limiting the overall gain when runs are to the left guard or right end. This comes with the sample size caveats as we’re only three weeks in, but it does suggest that opponents will have varying success depending on where they try to fit a run in. In the passing game it looks like attacking the short middle of the field and short right is gonna get you some yards with abysmal rankings of 30 in completion percentage in both. Now that does offer a bit of a confounding variable. They’re 28th and 32nd in yards allowed in those zones, but higher completion percentages eliminate “zeros” from the stats and naturally lead to higher per gain averages. In other words, you still expect big gains there, but a lot of it is due to the ball not hitting the turf in those areas. All of that makes it shocking that the Bills (so far) have been one of the best teams (fourth) defending the short left side of the field. Now the chart ranks them similarly in the deep middle part of the field, but I hesitate to call that real with only six attempts in that direction so far. The Patriots’ Offense In what is essentially a “woe is me” contest, are the Patriots’ numbers on offense any better than the Bills on defense? Remember how I said the Patriots were tied in points per game with the Dolphins as worst in the league? Let’s use points per drive as the tiebreaker. On a per opportunity basis, who is more futile? That would be the Patriots. At 0.97 points per drive, they comfortably trail Miami at 1.29 which is a huge gap. That 0.32 difference is tied for the largest gap between two teams in the league. And that tie is with the gap between the first and second place teams (49ers and Cowboys). For reference, league average is 2.10 points per drive. The Patriots are also in last place in percentage of drives ending with a score at 23.3% (average is 39%). No one has turned the ball over more either with over 1/4 of their drives ending with a turnover. Which helps explain how they’re 16th in yards gained per drive. They move the ball, then hand it over. With turnovers potentially normalizing, this does suggest that perhaps the Patriots will improve at some point as a heads up. Back to trashing them though… They’re 28th in sacks allowed, 28th converting 3rd downs, and worst in touchdown rate in the red zone. Put in very candid terms, they’d need a big jump just to reach average. What do the play direction charts say though? Is there a spot of the field that’s their bread and butter? I’ll repeat the disclaimer of low sample sizes, but New England has been shockingly successful in running off the left tackle (7th) and guard (1st). They’re also fine right up the middle. A single outlier here can skew things at this point in the season but an outlier in that direction still means they did something well. In the passing game the data so far shows a wealth of mediocre. When you’re not truly all that good anywhere, you don’t necessarily need to be all that terrible either to put yourself in a bad place. That said, the hit “good” on completion percentage for deep middle passes and flirt with “good” on passes short right. Interestingly, on those short right passes the average gain is 30th in the league. With such a high completion rate and such a **** average gain, that translation means that the short right passes are veeeeeery short. The deep middle passes to some extent are the same story; pairing the 8th best completion rate with the 19th best average gain. The Final Straw What does this all mean? First and foremost I don’t think it’s remotely a stretch to say that if we really are making this a game of who can throw the bigger pity party, it’s the Patriots. The data has them in the bottom four or eight in many areas. The Bills are more consistently dabbling in the realm of average despite some weaknesses. If there’s one potential concern it’s hinted at above. The Pats’ incredibad stats are likely a major function of their turnover rate. They could literally gameplan to be…

title: Our first month with an app broke our commenting records
summary: A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it.  The goal with this app was to make it easier to join […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it. The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center. The results so far are encouraging. In fact, it’s helped us set a new all-time record for comments this month across all of SB Nation’s communities, and I want to thank you for that. One of the most exciting new features is the game chat. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you’re not going to find anywhere else. We also wanted to elevate the community’s contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we’ve set single-day commenting records three different times since the season started. And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there’s an option at the top to do that. So, one month in, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven’t checked it out, you can get it for iOs or Android . And if you’re not an app user, that’s OK! We’re glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.

title: Brian Answers: Injuries, play call balance, practice squad rules, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re coming off a rough Sunday, but its a new week, the Panthers are playing in prime time, and they have a ton of injuries to figure out. Let’s dive in to all your questions! Brazilian Panther: Okay Brian, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - AUGUST 28: Corey Thornton #31 of the Carolina Panthers reacts during the first half of a preseason game against the Houston Texans at Bank of America Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re coming off a rough Sunday, but its a new week, the Panthers are playing in prime time, and they have a ton of injuries to figure out. Let’s dive in to all your questions! Brazilian Panther: Okay Brian, with almost a month of football so far, tell us two players on the Panthers that disappointed you the most so far and two others that surprised you on the positive side of things. I find it hard to get into early grades on players only 3 games in, but I will give it a try. I’ve been most surprised by Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller at the tight end position. This position was considered to be a need all throughout the off-season, but these two have been showing out so far as reliable pass catching targets which I really did not expect going into the season. Obviously Waller has shown more touchdown production, but they both have carved out reliable roles in the passing game in a tight end room that I think many considered one of the worst in the NFL on paper. As far as disappointments, I think its hard not to point to Derrick Brown as one of them. I think he’ll find his way once again, but he’s definitely played below expectation in these first 3 games. I’d also say Robert Hunt at right guard, for the money they are paying him he hasn’t been a top tier guard so far. Brice Guild: We have had to call on a lot of depth players already this season. Give me your take on the the performance and quality of play we have seen from them. Lee Hunter is certainly playing well enough to justify having a 4th round pick play significant snaps at corner. I would also give Zakee Wheatley props as he’s been graded pretty highly at safety. I mentioned the tight ends already so I won’t rehash that, but on offense Brycen Tremayne is still continuing to show he can play as a wide receiver when called upon. Coach_K: which cornerback are you looking forward to step up or perhaps sign? I don’t know if Carolina will sign a cornerback in the next couple of days, I think they just end up sticking with what they have. This is a great opportunity for Corey Thornton to step up from the practice squad after playing some really meaningful snaps as a UDFA last season before being knocked out due to injury. I think he makes a lot of sense to take some snaps when they need to pull Will Lee off the field or rotate at the nickel position. Thornton showed he can play wherever they need him to, and Sunday would really allow him to build on his rookie season. DBelt: What have you noticed about the difference in the offense with Brad Idzik calling plays, for better or worse? The aggression on offense is definitely up a notch from last season. I like them taking more deep shots down the field, but it really shot them in the foot going for it on 4th down against the Browns and trying to get intermediate completions instead of just getting the sticks. We’ll see if they can level it out, but I do enjoy the idea behind the aggression. CasualFanAlso: What impact, if any, has the performance of the OL had on the timeline for the return of Moton and Ekwonu? I know the team will want to be “cautious”. I don’t expect them to move the timelines up at all, as sad as that may be to read. Taylor Moton’s blood clots aren’t something you can rush and Ikem Ekwonu is still going to be lucky if he plays at all this season. Both will return when it makes sense. schrodingersblackcat: You’re Brad Idzik. How do you address the offense’s struggling ground game? How do you distribute the workload between Chuba and Dillon and whoever else we have in the backfield? What is an acceptable YPC? How do you improve the O Line’s ability to establish a credible run threat early in the game? I don’t really know to be honest. They might be missing their starting left guard and right tackle this week, so that’s already going to be a handicap. My best guess is one cut rushes that don’t take long to develop, and have the back just hit the hole fast. Maybe mix in some presnap motion to get the linebackers moving prior to the snap. More RPOs could also work as an extension of the run game since Bryce Young is so comfortable with those. carolinajerry: Brain, Panthers Nation is panicking. Fans are spiraling. Please instill some good ol’ Panthers optimistic delusion into us and save our sanity. Will we be ok? The optimist in me says that the Panthers probably should have won that football game on Sunday, they just missed some easy turnovers and made mental mistakes, combined with some questionable 4th down decisions in a game where defense was ruling. These are all correctable mistakes, and they aren’t facing a mobile quartertback this week which ultimately cost them a lot of points on defense in weeks 1 and 3. There’s actually a strong chance they can rebound against the Lions if they clean up their own mistakes and force Detroit into a few of their own. And being 2-2 going into a much needed bye week wouldn’t be a bad position to be in at all. Dcangio09: What happened to Derrick Browns strength, anchor and power. I haven’t seen him get repeatedly blown off the line this consistently since his 1st couple years. This is one of those few questions where I don’t really know what to say. Its been quite concerning how much of a drop off we’ve seen, both on the field and as far as dumb penalties and mental mistakes. I’m sure the offenses have schemed around him because he’s one of the best in the game, maybe they will play Cam Jackson more to try and take some of those double teams off of him. DannyLimes: How surprised will you be on a scale of 1 to 43.25 (where 1 is not surprised and 43.25 is a surprised as you could possibly be about something) when we beat the Detroit Lions? What is the main reason for this surprise or lack there of? I actually wouldn’t be all that surprised if the Panthers pulled out a win, so maybe a 28? The Panthers actually match up fairly well against the Lions offensively, if they can control the pass rush a bit. Defensively, the biggest killer for them has been quarterbacks escaping the pocket and extending plays and I don’t see that happening with Jared Goff. This could be a game where Ejiro Evero breaks out some new looks to throw off the offensive gameplan with new personnel due to injury. And its at home. Being unpredictable could really work to their benefit. celticgreen86: With Damien Lewis not out a few weeks, what changes do you anticipate to the OL which will now lose its best player to date? The Panthers clearly liked Corey Bullock quite a bit when they claimed him on waivers during roster cutdowns. So I think he’s just going to step right in and play, which will be interesting to watch. What they do at tackle should Monroe Freeling be unable to play might be more interesting. sgtx: What questions should we be asking that we haven’t ? I miss the food questions. Aggressively_avg2: Based off games played, and the fact we literally could have had Pat Surtain, Jaycee Horn has to go down as a bust, right? Nope. Jaycee Horn has been one of the best at his position, and these same injuries could have befallen Surtain if he were put in the same position. Horn didn’t enter the league with injury concerns. Players getting hurt just happens. Chef: Hey, Brian! Lots and lots of doom and gloom after the Browns debacle. Give me something that no one is talking about that should age well as the season progresses. Position groups, individual players, coaches, ect are all on the table. I need some silver linings, thanks. The Panthers special teams unit is one of the best in the league, and that’s building on what the unit did last season.…
author: Brian Beversluis

title: Panthers vs Lions: Matchups to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers are very, very banged up. Fortunately, they have an early bye, and this is one of the few times where they’ll probably be happy to see it. But before they get there, they have to host the Detroit Lions in front of a national audience on Sunday Night Football. These kinds of […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 24: Shaq Thompson #7 of the Carolina Panthers tackles Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions during the fourth quarter of the game at Bank of America Stadium on December 24, 2022 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are very, very banged up. Fortunately, they have an early bye, and this is one of the few times where they’ll probably be happy to see it. But before they get there, they have to host the Detroit Lions in front of a national audience on Sunday Night Football. These kinds of games are always scary given some of the eggs we’ve seen laid by Panthers in this spot, and it’s even scarier given the team’s health. Let’s dive into the key matchups that the Panthers need to win or at least be competitive to give themselves a chance to improve to 2-2. Will Lee and Akayleb Evans vs. Amon-Ra St. Brown Everyone who keeps up with the Panthers knows we have to start here. Amon-Ra St. Brown is one of the best wide receivers in the NFL, and the Panthers aren’t going to have their star cornerback duo to try to stop him. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are both out for the next several weeks at least, leaving rookie Will Lee and Akayleb Evans to handle him outsid. Chau Smith-Wade will have to give it his best shot in the slot, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Lions put St. Brown out wide more to test the Panthers’ corner depth. Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke can muddy up some throwing lanes in the middle to help when St. Brown works in that area, but I don’t know if the outside corners are going to stand a chance if left out on an island. Monroe Freeling or Stone Forsythe vs. Aidan Hutchinson Rookie tackle Monroe Freeling is currently in the concussion protocol, so his status for Sunday’s game is very much up in the air. If he can’t go, Stone Forsythe is poised to fill in. In either case, the Panthers will be at a severe disadvantage against superstar edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson. The offensive line struggled against the Browns, and Hutchinson is arguably better than anyone on that Browns front. He already has 3.5 sacks this season and is liable to wreck the Panthers’ offensive game plan. They badly need whoever suits up at right tackle to at least put up a fight against Hutchinson. Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke vs. Jahmyr Gibbs Jahmyr Gibbs is one of the best players in the NFL regardless of position, so the Lions have elected to build most of their offense out of Gibbs. He’s averaging over 27 touches per game so far this season and converting those into 154.3 yards from scrimmage per game and six total touchdowns. He’s explosive if he gets out into space, and over a third of his carries and over half of his catches go for first downs. The Panthers linebacker duo is going to have their hands full getting Gibbs to the ground and keeping him from generating explosive plays, especially if the weather limits the Lions’ downfield passing game. Football players vs. the rain Current forecasts say it’s going to be cool and very wet on Sunday night. This game is widely expected to be a shootout, but the rain might put a significant damper on that. We’ll see what happens when two good offenses and two depleted defenses go against one another in a game where the weather is playing most of the defense.
author: Jonathan DeLong

title: Panthers vs Lions: Round table predictions, odds, and what’s left of Carolina’s two-deep.
summary: Let’s take a look at where I started this prediction piece last week: Things seem to be looking up for the Carolina Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young. One dominant defensive performance and two excellent offensives ones have given us more good football to start a season than we have seen in years. Welp. Nothing feels […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Devin Lloyd #55 and Jean Phillips #5 of the Carolina Panthers react to a sack during an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s take a look at where I started this prediction piece last week : Things seem to be looking up for the Carolina Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young. One dominant defensive performance and two excellent offensives ones have given us more good football to start a season than we have seen in years. Welp. Nothing feels like it is trending upward after how thoroughly the Panthers fell apart against the Cleveland Browns. Yeah, Bryce Young didn’t play amazing football and had more than a few plays that failed the eye test he was otherwise acing this season. Yeah, Ejiro Evero’s defense couldn’t get a stop at the end of the game. Those are both valid complaints. The early aggressiveness on fourth down and the inability to establish a consistent running game are what cost us that game more so than anything else that was under the Panthers control. The real story, however, continues to be the injuries that the Panthers have suffered. I’m still wary of Young’s future, but I can’t really judge anything when the team can barely field half of the starters they entered the offseason with. This week’s injury news started rough and has only gotten moreso with the release of the injury reports. To put it all in perspective, Pride of Detroit asked us five questions this week and four were related to the Panthers injuries. Here are our predictions for the week, but reader beware: there isn’t a lot of optimism to be found right now. Staff predictions for Week 4 Walker Clement Panthers 17, Lions 21 – A fourth quarter touchdown makes the score look closer than it feels, but still not close enough to cover the spread . The only thing that slows the Lions down is the rain. Jonathan DeLong Panthers 28, Lions 35 – The offense gets their mojo back against a bad Lions defense but they can’t overcome all the injuries in the secondary. Brian Beversluis Panthers 24, Lions 35 – Jahmyr Gibbs gets 200 scrimmage yards. Daniel Belton Panthers 73, Lions 84 – The Lions offense against the banged up Panthers defense is the immortal clash between the Unstoppable Force and the Quite Easily Movable Object. Amon-Ra lights up the Panthers secondary, Bryce Young continues playing well but can’t keep up. Eric Buchanan Panthers 27, Lions 34 – Panthers attempt to slow the game down early, but a couple big plays from the Lions open the floodgates to a shoot-out. Andrew Sweat Panthers 34, Lions 10 – Since the Panthers seem to always do the opposite of what I think they’ll do, Carolina wins as Bryce Young throws for 400+ yards
author: Walker Clement

title: Panthers vs Lions: Storylines
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to week 4, where the Panthers look to shake off an away loss to the Cleveland Browns as they welcome the Detroit Lions to Charlotte. Its a prime time matchup, which I know sends shivers down many of your spines if you are familiar with the Panthers history in the 2000s/2010s during […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Tommy Tremble #82 of the Carolina Panthers is tripped by Xavier Watts #31 of the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Butch Dill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to week 4, where the Panthers look to shake off an away loss to the Cleveland Browns as they welcome the Detroit Lions to Charlotte. Its a prime time matchup, which I know sends shivers down many of your spines if you are familiar with the Panthers history in the 2000s/2010s during early regular season night matchups. The Lions have an explosive offense, a very good defensive line, but a weakened secondary. We could see a shootout Sunday night. Let’s dive into the storylines to watch. Offense: Keep up with the Lions The Lions offense is definitely scary going into this game. They have averaged 31 points per game, 368.3 yards per game, and 5.6 yards per play in 2026 so far. Those are all in the top 10 as far as offense is concerned (per Teamrankings.com). The Panthers offense has been very good at times, but Bryce Young is both the most productive passer in the NFL from a yardage standpoint and also the most pressured QB right now. The Panthers offense cannot afford to get behind too far on the Lions, as letting them pin their ears back and get after Bryce is going to cause problems as the game goes on. The formula for winning this game very much mirrors the formula they used to beat the Rams the first time around in 2025, which is to keep pace and score points. Jalen Coker playing would very much help here, but if he can’t, the Panthers will need to target the Lions depleted secondary while also keeping somewhat of a balance with the rushing attack. The Lions haven’t been all that amazing against the rush, averaging 4.4 yards per rush surrendered which is 20th in the NFL. Their pass defense is towards the bottom in most categories , so having some balance should help keep the offense on schedule. Defense: So… who is playing cornerback? To add injury to injury following the loss to the Browns, the Panthers announced this week that both CBs Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson will likely miss around 8 weeks due to the injuries they sustained against the Browns. As you may know, those two form one of the best CB duos in the NFL, so their absence will hurt. The Panthers currently have 3 CBs on the active roster, and 4 on their practice squad. I would expect them to give Corey Thornton a promotion along with one of their other PS guys, and what this cornerback unit looks like will be interesting. I’d imagine Will Lee steps into the CB1 role, but their strategy of moving CB1 around the formation is likely out the window now. How Ejiro Evero responds to what is likely a bloodbath matchup for this beat up secondary is going to be huge. I think they’ll factor in guys like Tre’Von Moehrig, Lathan Ransom, and Zakee Wheatley into how they deploy their nickel defenses, so its certainly something to pay attention to during the game Sunday. Even if it causes great pain. Bonus storyline: Continue leaning on the tight ends The Panthers tight end room has quietly been quite helpful for this offense. Tommy Tremble is playing his best football, free agent signing Darren Waller has proved to be a matchup nightmare that I did not expect at this stage in his career, and Mitch Evans continues to factor in as a reliable player who can do a bit of everything well. They may choose to go back to the 2025 strategy of trying to play more ball control centric football against an explosive offense, so how these guys are deployed and perform could be the huge difference maker in how this offense operates on Sunday. What are you looking for on Sunday night, Panthers fans?

title: Reviewing the Bears’ PFN grades from Week 3 vs. Eagles
summary: The Chicago Bears bounced back in a major way on Monday night, picking up the decisive 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles to improve to 2-1 for the season. It was about as thorough a beating as one could imagine. The Bears’ passing attack proved to be too much for the Eagles to overcome, while […]
full_text: Sep 28, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Case Keenum (11) celebrates after the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears bounced back in a major way on Monday night, picking up the decisive 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles to improve to 2-1 for the season. It was about as thorough a beating as one could imagine. The Bears’ passing attack proved to be too much for the Eagles to overcome, while Chicago’s heavy blitz helped them generate pressure on passing downs and keep Jalen Hurts guessing all evening. These efforts are reflected in the analytics, where several key contributors on the Bears finished with favorable production. Each week, I’ll review how Chicago’s eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network’s Impact Scoring model. Here’s how Week 3 looked. Offense Case Keenum: 79.1 (12th of 32 QBs) D’Andre Swift: 75.1 (29th of 44 RBs) Kyle Monangai: 70.7 (37th of 44 RBs) Kalif Raymond: 80.2 (11th of 67 WRs) Luther Burden III: 76.1 (28th of 67 WRs) Rome Odunze: 70.0 (53rd of 67 WRs) Colston Loveland: 77.0 (11th of 37 TEs) Braxton Jones: 76.3 (35th of 71 OTs) Joe Thuney: 74.3 (34th of 60 OGs) Garrett Bradbury: 83.5 (3rd of 32 Cs) Jonah Jackson: 77.3 (21st of 60 OGs) Darnell Wright: 85.7 (1st of 71 OTs) Week 3 marked the second week in a row that Darnell Wright finished with the highest PFN OL Impact grade of any offensive tackle in the NFL. He remains the top-graded lineman in the league, regardless of position. Keenum was quite efficient with his workload, ranking No. 12 in the NFL with 0.18 EPA per dropback. Though he finished the game with a strong 70.6% completion percentage, his completion percentage over expected (CPOE) was just +2.8. That generally suggests Ben Johnson did a good job making life easier with assignments to manage. Defense Montez Sweat: 74.1 (31st of 92 EDGEs) Neville Gallimore: 53.9 (94th of 97 DTs) Austin Booker: 75.2 (29th of 92 EDGEs) Dayo Odeyingbo: 76.8 (21st of 92 EDGEs) Devin Bush: 74.0 (40th of 66 LBs) T.J. Edwards: 85.3 (7th of 66 LBs) Malik Muhammad: 72.4 (62th of 92 CBs) Jaylon Johnson: 67.5 (81st of 92 CBs) Dillon Thieneman: 96.1 (2nd of 73 SAFs) Cam Lewis: 72.1 (51st of 73 SAFs) After a stellar outing in Week 3, Dillon Thieneman now ranks as the second-best safety in the NFL by PFN SAF Impact grading to start the year. Against Philadelphia, he allowed a targeted passer rating of just 2.8 in coverage, with his key interception of Andy Dalton in the end zone playing a major factor in the Bears’ win. Elsewhere in the secondary, Jaylon Johnson remains an analytical liability. However, both Devin Bush and T.J. Edwards have graded above average in coverage at the linebacker position. Special teams (for the sickos) Cairo Santos: 80.6 (15th of 29 Ks) Tory Taylor: 74.0 (23rd of 32 Ps) There’s not a lot flashy to break down from Chicago’s special teams performance this week. Cairo Santos made both of his field goals and didn’t miss an extra point, but since his field goals only came from 29 yards and 48 yards out, respectively, he didn’t get much love analytically from a difficulty perspective.
