title: Who on the Bears will keep up with the Jets’ Kenyon Sadiq?
summary: After a notably poor Week 1 performance, the Bears defense has suddenly shown some life. Since the start of the 3rd quarter in Week 1, the Bears have allowed a very respectable 29 points across 10 total quarters. Meanwhile, they have proven that the turnover trend from last year was not a fluke, as they […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: tight end Kenyon Sadiq #16 of the New York Jets runs the ball against cornerback D.J. Reed #4 of the Detroit Lions during the second half of an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images After a notably poor Week 1 performance, the Bears defense has suddenly shown some life. Since the start of the 3rd quarter in Week 1, the Bears have allowed a very respectable 29 points across 10 total quarters. Meanwhile, they have proven that the turnover trend from last year was not a fluke, as they currently have 3 fumble recoveries to go along with 3 INTs, giving them a +4 turnover differential. Still, the defense has remained imperfect. Saquon Barkley ran for 5.5 yards per carry on Monday night. Cornerbacks Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson are still giving up big plays too often (though rookie Malik Muhammad appears to be trending towards a full-time starter across from JJ). The defense is trending up, but remains a work in progress. Enter the Jets in week 4. While the Jets still aren’t contenders, they have some legitimate studs who need to get the attention of Ben Johnson and co. The one guy that has me most nervous is rookie tight end, Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq, the 16th overall pick in the 2026 draft, is an undersized TE that plays more like a bulked-up WR. Standing at 6’-3” and 241 lbs, Sadiq ran a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at the combine and has already shown that his speed translates to the field. Last week, Sadiq torched the Lions to the tune of 7 receptions for 105 and a TD. Most impressive was his contested TD reception, shown in the second clip of this tweet: Kenyon Sadiq showed EVERYONE why he was the TE1 in the 2026 NFL Draft today: • 8 targets (2nd on team) • 7 receptions (2nd on team) • 105 yards (most by Jets TE since 2019) • 1 receiving TD (T-1st on team) The Jets haven’t seen an elite TE talent like this in MULTIPLE… pic.twitter.com/dAkExnPVTq — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) September 27, 2026 As you can see, Sadiq plays like his hair is on fire and can beat you with speed or run straight through you. For a team that might be without Breece Hall, you can expect a heavy dose of Kenyon Sadiq to keep the short and intermediate game going for Geno Smith. Who might be lined up against him? My guess is that Devin Bush will find himself in zone coverage and in the same area as Sadiq often. Bush, a significant offseason signing by Ryan Poles, has been relatively quiet through three games with 8 solo tackles, 2 TFLs, and 1 PD. He’s not invisible, but he hasn’t gotten in on many impact plays either. Bush was signed to be a replacement for the departed Tremaine Edmunds to bring additional speed (4.42 40 time) and coverage chops at the position, and with a player like Sadiq ascending, and the loss of a versatile piece in Cam Lewis, the Bears will rely on Bush to make an impact in coverage and keep up with Sadiq. If the Bears shut down Sadiq, and with Breece Hall sidelined, I’d expect Geno Smith to struggle to find consistency against the Bears’ defense.

title: NFL Week 4 Game Preview: Chicago Bears vs. New York Jets
summary: Coming off a short week, the Chicago Bears will have to decide which backup quarterback they want to start against the New York Jets. Whoever it is, Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum, they will have a tough act to follow. And a tough defense to play against. The Jets are 1-2, but are much more […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: Quarterback Geno Smith (7) of the New York Jets calls a play at the line of scrimmage during an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Coming off a short week, the Chicago Bears will have to decide which backup quarterback they want to start against the New York Jets. Whoever it is, Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum, they will have a tough act to follow. And a tough defense to play against. The Jets are 1-2, but are much more competitive than they were a season ago. Their two losses have been by a combined 10 points. On the other side, the Bears need to prove their victories against the Panthers and Eagles weren’t flukes and the outlier on the young season was the Vikings game in the rain. Taking care of a team still on its rebuild will go a long way in showing the Bears are indeed not going to regress this year. Let’s meet the Jets. New York Jets SB Nation site: Gang Green Nation Record: 1-2, second in AFC East Last week: 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions Game day, time, TV: Sunday, noon CT, FOX Spread: Chicago -3.5 Bears all-time record against: 9-4 Historical meetings: The highest-scoring meeting between these teams was back in 2010, when the teams met the day after Christmas in week 16. The 10-4 Jets came to Chicago to face the 10-4 Bears. A 10-0 Chicago lead evaporated in the second quarter as Shonn Greene ran for a 3-yard touchdown, Dwight Lowery picked off Jay Cutler and returned it 20 yards for a touchdown and LaDainian Tomlinson rushed for a 3-yard score. But the Bears answered back as Cutler scrambled for a 2-yard score himself. In the third quarter, Cutler hit Johnny Knox for a 40-yard score. It was the first of three third-quarter TDs. Cutler also connected with Devin Hester for a 25-yard TD and Knox again for a 26-yard score. In the meantime, Mark Sanchez found Santonio Holmes for a 23-yard score, but it wasn’t enough. The Bears won 38-34. Last meeting: Week 12 of 2022. Who could forget the matchup of Mike White against Trevor Siemian? White carved up Matt Eberflus’s defense for 315 passing yards and three TDs. Garrett Wilson scored twice and Elijah Moore scored once. Byron Pringle scored Chicago’s only touchdown as they got smoked 31-10 by the Jets. Injury report: The Jets had nine players on their injury report Wednesday. Limited participation EDGE Kindgley Enagbare S Minkah Fitzpatrick TE Jeremy Ruckert TE Kenyon Sadiq Did not participate RB Breece Hall LB Francisco Mauigoa WR Adonai Mitchell OL Dylan Parham TE Mason Taylor Offense: The Jets come to Chicago ranked 17th in points and 13th in yards. Their passing offense ranks 11th and their rushing offense ranks 26th. Geno Smith (75.5 pct cmp/783 yds./4 TD/0 INT) has recaptured the strong play he showed in Seattle a few years ago. He also has a bit more to work with than he did last year in Las Vegas. With Garrett Wilson (21 rec./243 yds./2 TD), rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq (12/143/1) and Adonai Mitchell (9/123/0), they’re able to move the ball and score. Breece Hall (10 rec./102/0 and 51 car./163 yds./1 TD) plays a big role for their offense as a rusher and checkdown. If he can’t go, Braelon Allen (19 att./61/1) will fill in for him. Defense: The Jets defense comes in ranked 12th in points allowed and second in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks third and their rushing defense ranks seventh. No. 2 overall draft pick David Bailey (2 sk/12 tkls/3 TFL/1 FF/3 QB hits) is playing up to his draft position. Kingsley Enagbare (2 sk/2 TFL/2 QB hits/1 FF), Demario Davis (22 tkl/1 sk/2 TFL/1 QB hit) and Jamien Sherwood (18 tkl/1 PD/2 TFL) are other statistical leaders on the defense. In the secondary, Azareye’h Thomas (13 tkl/2 PD/2 TFL), Andre Cisco (16 tkl/2 TFL/1 PD) and Dane Belton (16 tkl/1 PD) are patrolling. Key matchups: The Jets can be run on. They’re allowing 4.2 yards per attempt, which ranks 18th. Their offense ranks third in average offensive drive length. Winning the time of possession and getting them off the field are big keys here. Their passing defense ranks high early in the season, so with a backup QB playing, the Bears will have to pick their spots. And establish the run early. On defense, slowing down the Jets’ running game will be important. If they can get to Geno Smith, he will make some bad throws and turn it over. But if he’s in rhythm, he’s still a good quarterback. Containing Garrett Wilson and Kenyon Sadiq will be big, too. Key stats The Jets have yet to have a defensive interception this year. The Jets defense is allowing 4.8 yards per play, which is tied for 29th with the Patriots, 49ers and VIkings. New York blitzes 33.6 percent of the time, 25th in the league. The Bears rank second in blitz percentage after Minnesota. Opposing QBs have a 98.6 rating against the Jets, which ranks 23rd. New York’s third down defense ranks fifth, allowing just 32.3 percent of opponents’ third downs to be converted. A question to encourage discussion? What will it take for the Bears to get a win this week?

title: Case Keenum Week 3 QB Grade: Eagles @ Bears Film Breakdown
summary: Note: You may notice another new name included in my QB grades/metrics. This may explain why… Well, when I said last week that whoever started against the Philadelphia Eagles would get the same treatment here, I partially didn’t expect that quarterback to be Case Keenum. The Bears entered Week 3 with about as much uncertainty […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears throws during the first quarter of the NFL game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Note: You may notice another new name included in my QB grades/metrics. This may explain why… Well, when I said last week that whoever started against the Philadelphia Eagles would get the same treatment here, I partially didn’t expect that quarterback to be Case Keenum. The Bears entered Week 3 with about as much uncertainty at quarterback as you could ask for. Caleb Williams was ruled out with the hamstring injury he suffered against Minnesota, while Tyson Bagent spent most of the week in concussion protocol. Bagent ultimately cleared on Sunday, but with Keenum receiving the full week of preparation, Ben Johnson stuck with the 38-year-old veteran for Monday Night Football. It would be Keenum’s first NFL start in 1,009 days. Against an undefeated Philadelphia Eagles team. What could possibly go wrong? Apparently, not much. Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns, added another score on the ground and finished with a 110.8 passer rating, and a very solid 122.0 True Passer Rating as Chicago cruised to a 27-7 win. The Bears finished with 375 yards of offense, controlled the ball for nearly 37 minutes and, maybe most importantly, didn’t turn it over once. But what stood out to me most wasn’t necessarily the production. It was how different the offense looked getting there. Keenum obviously isn’t Caleb Williams, and Ben Johnson didn’t ask him to be. With Williams, there is always an element of controlled chaos available to the offense. His arm talent allows Chicago to attack areas of the field that most quarterbacks simply can’t, while his mobility and creativity can turn a broken play into something completely different. We’ve already seen plenty of that through the first two years with Williams under center. Keenum’s game was almost the opposite. The ball came out quickly. owning just a 2.19s time to throw Monday night, as the Bears opted to (mostly) work the underneath, with just 7 aimed passing attempts traveling more than 10 yards downfield and a 6.1 ADoT overall for the outing. And when the Eagles did Blitz, Keenum made the Eagles pay. Johnson summed it up pretty well during the post game presser, praising Keenum for getting the ball to “the right guy in time,” taking care of the football and making good decisions. And against Vic Fangio’s defense, that approach made a lot of sense. Before the game, Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor talked about how Philadelphia’s defensive structure forces quarterbacks to remain patient. Fangio wants to limit explosive plays, keep everything in front of the defense and force an offense to methodically work its way down the field. Keenum was perfectly content doing exactly that. Chicago ran 35 times and threw it 34, despite averaging just 3.7 yards a carry, staying almost perfectly balanced while Keenum played point guard. He took the available completions, kept the offense on schedule and allowed Ben Johnson’s scheme to manufacture opportunities rather than trying to create them himself. And despite some of the early issues with the run, Keenum was sharp on play action passing, throwing just 1 incompletion from play action. But all that’s not necessarily a criticism of Caleb Williams, either. In fact, there are things Williams can do within this offense that Keenum simply cannot. The ability to create outside structure, attack vertically and turn pressure into explosive plays is a massive part of what makes Williams special. But Keenum’s performance was a great example of what the other end of the spectrum looks like. Sometimes the answer doesn’t need to be spectacular. Sometimes it’s identifying the coverage, trusting the concept and getting the football out. And when Philadelphia finally gave Chicago an opportunity for an explosive play, Keenum took it, hitting Kalif Raymond for a 41-yard touchdown in the third quarter that helped turn a 13-7 game into a comfortable Bears lead. Keenum did an excellent job on the play identifying busted coverage and getting the ball to Raymond. There are certainly lessons Williams can take from that performance when he returns. Not because the Bears suddenly discovered they are better off with Case Keenum, but because Keenum showed just how efficient Ben Johnson’s offense can be when the quarterback consistently operates within its timing and structure. For one night, that was more than enough. Now let’s see how Keenum’s performance actually graded. Benchmarks Stat Formatting Key: This week we will be comparing Keenum’s week 3 start against Williams’ Season Totals and Averages. (Season totals are underlined , Season Averages in Italics , and this week’s stats appear in regular text.) C/A: 36/55 (65.5%) | 18/27.5 (65.5%) | 24/34 70.6% Yards: 407 | 203.5 | 247 Touchdowns: 4 | 2 | 3 Turnovers: 1 | 0.5 | 0 QB at Fault Sacks: 0 | 0 | 0 aDOT: 7.7 | 6.1 Passer Rating: 92.0 | 110.8 True Passer Rating : 113.4 | 122.0 Time to Throw: 3.34s | 2.19s Time to Pressure: 2.75s | 2.27s Pressure Rate: 41.57% | 23.68% On-Target Rate: 83.3% | 63.6% Poor Play Rate / Big Play Rate: 7.5 % PPR / 5.0% BRP | 0.0% PPR / 7.3% BRP EPA per dropback: +0.31 | +0.18 ANY/A : 6.2 | 8.4 Game Scorecard The full grading sheet for each play can be found here. Game Notes Note: Last year, I included PFF grades in these breakdowns. With PFF continuing to expand its use of AI across its platform, and with my confidence in how accurately its grades reflect quarterback performance declining, I’ve decided to move away from them this season. In their place, I’ll be using PFN’s Impact Score , which will be notated as PFN on grading sheets moving forward. NFL Passer Rating / True Passer Rating / PFN Impact Score: 110.8 / 122.0 / 79.1 The NFL’s average passer rating through Week 2 sat at 93.5, making Keenum’s 110.8 against the Eagles a very good start, especially considering the circumstances. A 122.0 TPR represents an upper-level “Good” game in my model, where 100 serves as the baseline for “Average.” For comparison’s sake, that would have put Keenum around 11th in the league in average TPR during the 2025 season, one spot ahead of Joe Burrow and one behind Jared Goff. On the PFN scale, where 75 represents an average qualifying starter and 90 is elite territory, Keenum finished Week 3 with a 79.1 Impact Score , ranking 12th of 31 qualifying quarterbacks. Not bad for a QB who had not made an NFL start in over 1000 days! On-Target Throws: 2026 Average: 83.3% | Week 3: 63.6% Reminder: Completion percentage ≠ On-Target Percentage. I only chart aimed passes, meaning throwaways, spikes and passes deflected at the line are excluded. Drops can still be credited as on-target. Short-Level Passing (Behind LOS–9 yards): 17/26 | 69.2% On-Target Deep-Level Passing (10–20+ yards): 4/7 | 57.1% On-Target There was perhaps a little live-game rust despite an otherwise solid performance. Keenum notably misfired on a handful of Out routes, with several misses coming behind his intended receiver, about the last place you want to miss on an Out. More on those in the play review. Poor Play Rate / Big Play Rate: 0.0 % PPR / 5.7% BPR Keenum played a clean game essentially from start to finish. And while he did miss on some Out route throws that can lead to dangerous turnovers, none of them were egregious enough to warrant grading them Poor or Turnover Worthy. He did make three “Great” graded plays on the night, all three coming on the Bears’ final drive of the first half. We’ll break down two of them further: 1.) A fantastic throw with pressure in his face, dropping the ball over the mid-level defenders for a 25-yard gain to Luther Burden. 2.) A great anticipation throw into a hole in the zone to Rome Odunze for 22 yards. 3.) Finally, a 12-yard completion to…

title: Chicago Bears Big Play Breakdowns from Week 3
summary: I think we can all agree that Ben Johnson’s game plan for Week 3 was perfect for Case Keenum. It wasn’t a particularly explosive game plan, but it was perfect for the spot start on Monday Night Football. Only four explosives from the primetime tilt to discuss this week. Explosive Play 3.1 – Q2 6:14, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Kalif Raymond #14 of the Chicago Bears catches a pass to score a touchdown during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images I think we can all agree that Ben Johnson’s game plan for Week 3 was perfect for Case Keenum. It wasn’t a particularly explosive game plan, but it was perfect for the spot start on Monday Night Football. Only four explosives from the primetime tilt to discuss this week. Explosive Play 3.1 – Q2 6:14, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 20. Case Keenum completes pass short left to Luther Burden for 25 yards. This one is just kind of a crazy play all around. The Bears come out in 11 personnel with Kalif Raymond and Luther Burden lined up tight next to Colston Loveland on the right side with Rome Odunze split out left. Keenum motions Burden and snaps quickly, allowing Burden to release up the C-gap (between tackle and tight end). Raymond follows Burden’s release through the C-gap out into his route. Keenum fakes to Monangai and then, feeling immediate pressure, flicks a ball over the top of two defenders to Burden who is dragging right to left. It’s an incredible play by Keenum to find the open guy in space quickly before getting hit and a nice play by Burden to make it an explosive play after securing the catch. Explosive Play 3.2 – Q2 5:39, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 45. Case Keenum completes pass deep right to Rome Odunze for 22 yards. The very next play, a perfect ball thrown with maximum anticipation. The Bears use 12 personnel here (one running back, two tight ends) but line up Cole Kmet as a full back. Kmet motions laterally a couple steps to the right and peels back left to block the blitzing corner. This is a max protect look here as only two are out on a route here as both tight ends and the back are in to protect Keenum. Still, there’s pressure after the play fake to Kyle Monangai but Keenum fires the ball to Rome two full steps before he reaches the top of his route to find the hole in the coverage, making an easy catch. Contrast this with a similar pitch and catch from last week where Bagent held for an extra second, allowing the defender to recover and making it a more difficult play for Rome. This is teach tape from Keenum and simply doesn’t get much better. Case Keenum throws a DIME to Odunze 🎯 @PHIvsCHI on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Q5bYFcZtIK — NFL (@NFL) September 29, 2026 Explosive Play 3.3 – Q3 5:55, 1st and 10 from the Philly 41. Case Keenum completes over the middle to Kalif Raymond for 41 yard touchdown. Bears come out in a standard 11 personnel here with Sam Roush as the lone tight end lined up to the left with Luther Burden stacked behind Rome Odunze and Kalif Raymond on the right side. Keenum motions Burden to the left and at the snap, Burden has just cleared the right tackle. It’s enough to confuse the assignment for the Eagles defense as Raymond runs free in the middle. Keenum delivers the ball a bit behind Raymond, who makes a great spinning catch and races to the end zone, topping 20 miles per hour. I’m not sure if the 38-year old Keenum finding the 32-year old Raymond for a TD is the oldest TD connection in Bears history or not, but it’s got to be up there. KEENUM FINDS RAYMOND FOR A 41-YARD TD 🐻 @PHIvsCHI on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Q3YWUsEgp1 — NFL (@NFL) September 29, 2026 Explosive Play 3.4 – Q4 2:00, 4th and 1 from the Philly 34. D’Andre Swift off left tackle for 15 yard gain. The Bears come out of the two minute warning with a 4th and 1 and decide to end the game on offense (love it). The break the huddle and rush to the line in a super jumbo package with three tight ends and an extra offensive lineman and Darnell Wright shifted over on on the left side. So the look right to left is Roush, Thuney, Bradbury, Jackson, Benedet, Wright, and Kmet on the line with Loveland and Luke Newman lined up in the backfield to the left. Swift takes the snap and runs behind the beef on the left side, breaking an arm tackle at the line of scrimmage before breaking a second tackle at the second level before a third arm tackle probably does enough to stop him before fourth Eagle ends the play. 15 yards on a 4th and 1 to clinch it seems pretty good to me. Bonus clip — The Sucker Sneak! This is very much not an explosive but I love Ben Johnson calling the “sucker sneak” against the Eagles, essentially the exact opposite of the “Tush Push.” Essentially, the left guard pulls left, the right guard pulls right and that action suckers the defensive tackles enough to open up the middle. The center climbs to the second level to take on the linebacker and before you know it, the QB has a rushing touchdown. Deception and cleverness against the team that has perfected the brute force sneak. Keenum became the oldest player in Chicago Bears franchise history to rush for a score on this play. CASE KEENUM TAKES IT HIMSELF FOR 6️⃣ @PHIvsCHI on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wzuJYvhELQ — NFL (@NFL) September 29, 2026 2026 Explosive Play Count: D’Andre Swift 5, Kyle Monangai 4, Caleb Williams 4, Rome Odunze 3, Kalif Raymond 2, Luther Burden 2, and one for Cole Kmet. What was your favorite explosive play from this one? The TD to Raymond is the easy answer because, well, it’s a score, but that throw to Burden for 25 yards is the one I’ve been thinking about the most since Monday.

title: Bengals vs. Jaguars: Odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 4 matchup
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars are putting all the chips on the table in this battle of the cats. The Bengals are coming off a disappointing road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that showed some holes in their new-look defense. That could be a problem as the Jaguars offense has been humming mostly through […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals and Jacksonville Jaguars are putting all the chips on the table in this battle of the cats. The Bengals are coming off a disappointing road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that showed some holes in their new-look defense. That could be a problem as the Jaguars offense has been humming mostly through three weeks. How do the oddsmakers and experts see this one playing out? Odds Cincinnati is currently a 2.5-point favorite at home, according to FanDuel Sportsbook. The usual spread based on even teams meeting is the home team getting 3.5 points of favorability, so clearly Jacksonville is eating into the home-field advantage there. The over/under is set at 51.5 points. Cincinnati has gone over that mark twice in their season so far, but the Jaguars have never reached that height. However, they have scored 35 and 34 points so far. That is more than the Bengals’ 33 points against the Tampa Bay Bucs, their highest output of the season. Expert picks ESPN has seven of their 11 experts still going with Cincinnati Four of CBS Sports’ seven experts are taking Cincinnati Three of NFL.com’s five experts are going with the Jaguars NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from experts around the web — has the Bengals being picked 52 percent of the time. Cincy Jungle Prediction Clearly, this is expected to be a close game between two very good AFC teams with good quarterbacks leading them. Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence also met in the 2019 National Championship when Burrow and the LSU Tigers defeated Trevor Lawrence and the Clemson Tigers (another game between big cats). Jacksonville boasts the top-scoring defense, only allowing 12 points per game, but when you have played the Cleveland Browns, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots, it really doesn’t compare to an offense like Cincinnati’s. However, you can say the same about Cincinnati’s defense, as none of the offenses they have faced have exactly lit the world on fire either. This game likely comes down to turnovers and the little things like penalties. That second one has plagued this team so far. However, returning home after a humbling loss could do this team good. The Bengals defense gets to Lawrence just enough to edge out a win over the Jaguars Final Score : Bengals 38, Jaguars 34 Now, send us your game predictions in the comments section! Who Dey! title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Jaguars
summary: As the Cincinnati Bengals get set to host the Jacksonville Jaguars, here are four key matchups to watch for on Sunday at Paycor Stadium. Parker Washington vs. Dax Hill Parker Washington has been the top receiver for the Jaguars through the first few weeks of the season. He comes into this game with 221 receiving […]
full_text: Sep 14, 2025; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (1) runs with the ball against Jacksonville Jaguars defensive back Travis Hunter (12) in the second half at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As the Cincinnati Bengals get set to host the Jacksonville Jaguars, here are four key matchups to watch for on Sunday at Paycor Stadium. Parker Washington vs. Dax Hill Parker Washington has been the top receiver for the Jaguars through the first few weeks of the season. He comes into this game with 221 receiving yards and 2 touchdowns. Bengals starting nickel corner Jalen Davis was placed on IR Tuesday afternoon. The Bengals have officially moved Dax Hill into the slot corner role on their depth chart. That doesn’t necessarily mean he will play there all the time, but until Ja’Sir Taylor comes off of short-term IR sometime in the next few weeks, we are likely to see him playing there a lot. Hill will be tasked with slowing down Washington this Sunday as the Bengals host the Jacksonville Jaguars. Emmanuel Pregnon and Robert Hainsey vs. Dexter Lawrence Emmanuel Pregnon is the Jaguars rookie left guard. He has had some inconsistent performances to start the season, as should be expected from any rookie offensive lineman. In week 2 against Denver, Pregnon allowed four pressures during the game. However, during week 3 he didn’t allow a single pressure against a very talented Patriots defensive line. Center Robert Hainsey, on the other hand, did allow a couple of pressures and a couple of quarterback hits against New England. Hainsey finished that game with a 36.2 pass block grade. Meanwhile, Dexter Lawrence was able to record 2 more sacks against the Steelers this past week. Lawrence has been an absolute force in the middle of the Cincinnati defense. It wouldn’t be surprising to see a lot of Trevor Lawrence (no relation to Dexter) scrambling all game long on Sunday. Dexter Lawrence vs. Pittsburgh Steelers pic.twitter.com/gOiD8ycO6r — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Orlando Brown Jr. vs. Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker Brown is likely to face off against Hines-Allen more often, but should see both of the Jaguars’ talented pass rushers at times on Sunday. Brown had a rough performance against the Texans during Week 2, giving up three sacks on the day. He was able to bounce back against the Pittsburgh Steelers for the most part. He allowed just two pressures all game, and he did not surrender a sack. Hines-Allen has six pressures, 1.5 sacks, and a forced fumble during the season so far. He has 62.5 career sacks. Opposite of him is typically Travon Walker. The former No. 1 overall pick has 13 pressures so far this season. He has 29 career sacks of his own coming into this one. Amarius Mims has yet to surrender a pressure through three games, so the Jaguars defense will be looking to attack Orlando Brown Jr. If he can hold up as he did against the Steelers, the Bengals should be able to put up a lot of points again in this one. Ja’Marr Chase vs. Travis Hunter The Jacksonville Jaguars traded up to select Travis Hunter with the second overall selection during the 2025 draft. The second-year player is now focused more on being a full-time corner, which was always the most logical spot to play him. While he will occasionally get in for some offensive plays, he has been allowed to really focus on the defensive side of the ball this season. He recorded his first interception of the year in Week 3 against the New England Patriots. He will likely face off a lot against Ja’Marr Chase. After the first week when Chase recorded just two catches for 12 yards, he has been seeing a lot more targets come his way over the last two weeks. Chase has 173 receiving yards with three receiving touchdowns over the past two weeks. He and fellow receiver Tee Higgins are playing at a high level right now. I would expect that to continue on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Ja'Marr Chase puts 6️⃣ on the board @CINvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yeZQQAjlTQ — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026

title: Joe Burrow pushes back on ‘not clutch’ narrative
summary: Remember that famous clip of Joe Burrow bouncing up and down the sidelines and him saying, “Put it in my hands! Put it in my hands, it’s over!” That was in Week 4 of the 2021 season against the Jacksonville Jaguars, when Joe Burrow led a 10-play, 73-yard drive that took the last 5:33 off […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Quarterback Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images Remember that famous clip of Joe Burrow bouncing up and down the sidelines and him saying, “Put it in my hands! Put it in my hands, it’s over!” That was in Week 4 of the 2021 season against the Jacksonville Jaguars, when Joe Burrow led a 10-play, 73-yard drive that took the last 5:33 off the clock in a 24-21 comeback victory. Not to mention, the Bengals trailed 14-0 at halftime of that game. Burrow was 17/20 for 253 yards and two touchdowns in the second half of that game. Three touchdown drives and the game-winning drive for the game-winning field goal. Some might say that’s clutch. It’s because it is. Joe Burrow is clutch. Period. Whatever false national narratives that are being floated around are fruitless . Just go back and watch any clutch moment from Burrow in 2021 and 2022. He proved time and time again in those two seasons that he is clutch. It is not at all his fault the Bengals have lost games over the last two seasons. Those national narratives clearly forget why the Bengals lost those games. But just for the record, Joe Burrow reiterated that he wants the ball in his hands when the game is on the line. “I feel like I’m pretty good in those moments,” Burrow said Wednesday, via Bengals.com . “There’s no place I’d rather be. I want it in my hands when you put the game on the line. I trust myself in those spots. I trust our guys in those spots. We feel confident that we’re going to get it done.” Boom. Debate over. Joe Burrow is clutch. He knows he’s good in those situations, and Bengals fans and those who cover the Bengals know he is good when the game is on the line. Carry on.

title: Bengals News: Why Andrew Whitworth is irritated with the Bengals
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have long had an issue of seemingly calling off any sort of aggression despite having Joe Burrow and this offense at its disposal. There are examples of it working out. One was even in this game where Burrow tossed a touchdown to Mike Gesicki on 4th-and-1 just outside of the red zone. […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Thursday Night Football analyst Andrew Whitworth looks on prior to a preseason game between the New England Patriots and the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals have long had an issue of seemingly calling off any sort of aggression despite having Joe Burrow and this offense at its disposal. There are examples of it working out. One was even in this game where Burrow tossed a touchdown to Mike Gesicki on 4th-and-1 just outside of the red zone. Yet they are unwilling to let an offense that has been cooking go and win the game. Instead they opt to try to pin the opponent deep. This frustration was echoed by former Bengals tackle Andrew Whitworth on his podcast FITZ and WHITZ: “Here’s my philosophy: Give the ball back to Joe Burrow,” Whitworth said . “I don’t care if it’s on the 40. I don’t care if we’re on our own 10. Okay, Joe Burrow, get that offense on the field. I feel pretty good with a lead. Like they’re going to find a way to get some points. That moment there drove me crazy. Trying to do too much. We don’t need to steal a possession, we don’t need to block the punt and get short field. We drove up and down the field all day. Just get the ball back to Burrow and get off the grass. Get off the grass, get the possession, let’s go play.” This all rings a bit true. Of course we are playing with hindsight here, but they let the defense really go out and win against the Houston Texans, why not let the offense win when it was on fire Sunday? Bengals News Quick Hits | Record-Holder Shayne Graham Pulling For Money Mac; Dex Eyes Jax Dexter Lawrence talks about cutting down on penalties and mistakes that cost them Sunday. They allowed a few big runs on the game, but a bigger issue was getting guys down on contact. Too many times we saw runners shedding tackles or falling forward. All of that adds up as well. Some of the guys behind the defensive line need to toughen up. ‘You’ve Got To Try Something To Slow Me Down’ – Bengals DT Dexter Lawrence Weighs in on Steelers’ Leg Holds There is always some shenanigans with the Steelers when they play the Bengals. At least one of the plays could have qualified as him being engaged with a blocker and another going low. Can’t wait for the Dexter Lawrence rule this offseason. And those dweebs had the audacity to mock his dance like they did something. Bengals’ leaders agree on the fix: Move on, finish drives and trust the depth The message is pretty simple. You aren’t the lowly Bengals trying to claw into the playoffs. People were talking up the defense after Week 2 around the league. You are going to get everyone’s best shot. You have to treat every opponent like it is do or die. You can’t waltz into Pittsburgh even when the Steelers are having an off year. NFL News Steelers-Browns on ‘Thursday Night Football’: What We Learned from Cleveland’s 27-24 win The Browns are 3-1, and the offense is looking competent. They found a way to close out a close game against the Steelers. It really feels like this Week 3 loss is one we will come back to look on and wonder how it happened. Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker, 49ers QB Brock Purdy highlight September Players of the Month Evan McPherson wins AFC Special Teams player of the month. He leads the league with five field goals from 50 yards or more. He has been a very underrated weapon this year fans might take for granted. NFL Week 4 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game Two experts took the Bengals out of five. This is a game could be a precursor to a possible playoff game down the line. Getting to 3-1 certainly would be nice as the schedule starts to open up with some easier opponents on the horizon. Two high powered offenses going at it. Look for turnovers and penalties to decide this one.

title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars
summary: After suffering their first setback of the 2026 season, the Cincinnati Bengals will look to get back into the win column on Sunday when they host the Jacksonville Jaguars. Both teams enter this crucial matchup as two of the top teams in the AFC and prime playoff contenders. The Jaguars are coming off a 35-6 […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown (30) completes a pass on fourth down to extended the drive in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 2 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium in downtown Cincinnati on Sunday, Sept. 14, 2025. The Bengals came back from a halftime deficit to win 31-27. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After suffering their first setback of the 2026 season, the Cincinnati Bengals will look to get back into the win column on Sunday when they host the Jacksonville Jaguars . Both teams enter this crucial matchup as two of the top teams in the AFC and prime playoff contenders. The Jaguars are coming off a 35-6 beatdown of the New England Patriots, the very team that won the AFC a season ago. If the Bengals are going to get back on track, here are three keys to getting a win Sunday vs. Jacksonville. Limit Explosive Plays Cincinnati struggled all game long to limit the Pittsburgh Steelers from making explosive plays. The Steelers were able to gash the Bengals on the ground and through the air for several big plays this past Sunday. The Steelers finished the game with seven explosive plays against the Bengals. SEVEN explosive plays for the Steelers offense against the Bengals in Week 3 #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/4BJNyu4Sda — Steelers Depot 7⃣ (@Steelersdepot) September 28, 2026 Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars moved to 2-1 on the season after defeating the reigning AFC Champion Patriots by 29(!) points. In the passing game, the Jaguars have a trio of talented receivers in Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and Brian Thomas Jr. who can hit big plays downfield. Bhayshul Tuten has been the leading rusher in Jacksonville. He is averaging 4.7 yards per carry so far this season. Avoid self-imploding The Bengals had 12 penalties in Week 2 at Houston but still won 20-6. They cut that number to just six penalties in Week 3 at Pittsburgh, but some were costly and came at inopportune times. Amarius Mims was flagged for lining up too far in the backfield on the Bengals’ second possession of the game. That penalty wiped out what would have been a Tee Higgins first down reception. Ultimately, it led to the Bengals having to settle for a field goal. Penalties were not even the worst part of the game against the Steelers. Multiple special teams miscues led directly to 10 points by the Steelers. Darrin Simmons called for a punt block with the Bengals up three points in the second half. Cedric Johnson roughed the punter, and the Steelers kept possession of the football. They went on to score a touchdown just a couple of plays later. First time you force the Steelers to punt, and you do this. Still not sure the logic of trying to block this was when your offense had been putting up points all game. pic.twitter.com/UpXbs5Ik15 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 After the Bengals regained the lead, returner Ke’Shawn Williams muffed the punt. PJ Jules inexplicably tried to bend down and pick the ball up instead of diving on it. The Steelers were able to recover the ball and went on to add another three points. Up 27-24 and just forced a punt… Ke’Shawn Williams takes his eyes off the ball and doesn’t catch the punt, PJ Jules tries to bend down and pick the ball up instead of diving on it. Game changer. pic.twitter.com/Q4LIHC5dXH — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Even after those miscues, the Bengals offense was back on the field with a little over two minutes remaining and a chance to tie or take the lead. They were able to get down in field goal range, but Dalton Risner was blown up by Derrick Harmon, leading to a Joe Burrow sack fumble. The Steelers recovered, and the Bengals dropped to 2-1 on the season. Dalton Risner gets beat by Derrick Harmon and Burrow with piss poor ball security ends it. Bengals drop to 2-1 in a game they had multiple chances to win. On to Jacksonville.. pic.twitter.com/k393lToQUw — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 On the other side this week, the Jaguars come in riding high after crushing New England in one of the best performances any team has had so far this season. They were able to force two Drake Maye interceptions, along with two more Maye fumbles on the day. You can say this every week, but the Bengals cannot afford to turn the ball over against the Jaguars. That Liam Coen-led offense is too explosive to give extra possessions to. Take care of the football, and you will give yourself a chance to win this game. Run The Ball Effectively From Shotgun I don’t see the Bengals running the ball a ton against Jacksonville this week, but when they do run it, they need to be effective. Jacksonville comes into this game with the eighth-best rushing defense in the NFL this season. They are allowing just 91 total rushing yards per game. The Bengals have been too predictable that they are running the ball from under center. Joe Burrow doesn’t look comfortable when using play action from under center either. Meanwhile, they have had some effective runs from out of shotgun. This feels like a game that the Bengals might decide to stick with what has worked in the past. Let Joe Burrow see what is in front of him from shotgun, and pick your spots to hit some big rushing plays out of that formation.

summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will look to bounce back this Sunday, when the Jacksonville Jaguars make their way to Paycor Stadium in Week 4. After coming out of Week 3 banged up, Bengals fans have been watching the practice status of several players. Right guard uard Dalton Risner (knee) missed Wednesday’s practice and was listed as […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will look to bounce back this Sunday, when the Jacksonville Jaguars make their way to Paycor Stadium in Week 4. After coming out of Week 3 banged up, Bengals fans have been watching the practice status of several players. Right guard uard Dalton Risner (knee) missed Wednesday’s practice and was listed as a nonparticipant on Thursday, as he worked on the rehab field with a brace on his right knee. As a veteran with a year in the offensive system, Risner has a chance to play Sunday with limited practice reps if he and the team agree he can play. title: Ken Anderson sees a different Bengals organization in 2026
summary: There’s a pretty deeply ingrained belief among Bengals fans when it comes to the Brown and Blackburn families. You know the one. They’re cheap. They’ll never spend enough. They’ll never make the big move. They’ll always find a reason not to push the chips into the middle of the table. For years, there was plenty […]
full_text: There’s a pretty deeply ingrained belief among Bengals fans when it comes to the Brown and Blackburn families. You know the one. They’re cheap. They’ll never spend enough. They’ll never make the big move. They’ll always find a reason not to push the chips into the middle of the table. For years, there was plenty of evidence to support that frustration. But then came the 2026 offseason. And according to Bengals legend Ken Anderson in an exclusive chat with The Orange and Black Insider, perhaps it’s time to reconsider some of those preconceived notions. Anderson, who spent his entire 16-year playing career in Cincinnati and quarterbacked the Bengals to Super Bowl XVI, spent some time with us to discuss the current team and reminisce on his great career. His perspective on the organization and its ownership is particularly interesting because he has seen just about every version of the Bengals there has been. Anderson isn’t looking at the Browns and Blackburns from the outside. He lived through the Paul Brown years. He played for the franchise when Mike Brown was taking on an increasingly significant role. He has watched the organization evolve for decades, including being a coach at one point. And what he’s seeing now is different. That’s not to say Bengals fans should suddenly forget every frustration they’ve had with ownership. They shouldn’t. But there’s a difference between giving the Brown family a lifetime achievement award for spending money and acknowledging when the organization actually does something that fans have been demanding for years. The Bengals went all-in this offseason. At least, by barometers they have previously set for themselves. Not “all-in” in the NFL buzzword sense where a team restructures a couple of contracts and signs a mid-level free agent. They went out and got Dexter Lawrence. They went out and got Jonathan Allen, Bryan Cook, and others. Anderson, a guy who has been linked to the Bengals for over 50 years, took notice. We initially asked Anderson about what he thought about these moves. “At the end of last year, Joe Burrow said: ‘We’ve got to do things differently’, and it was encouraging to see the Bengals do things differently,” Anderson said. “Nobody in their right mind thought they would give up the 10th pick in the draft to make a trade for a guy like Dexter Lawrence. And that was, maybe, the best trade in the history of the Bengals; I don’t know how that’s going to turn out.” He also noted the amount of money devoted to the defense this offseason, including Cook’s Super Bowl background upon his return to Cincinnati. They made major investments in the defensive line and dramatically changed the personality of a defense that had been one of the biggest problems on the roster. Anderson’s comments essentially challenge the idea that the Bengals’ ownership group has never been willing to make those kinds of moves. That’s worth considering. Because sometimes Bengals fans — myself included — have allowed the reputation of the franchise to become so entrenched that we automatically view every move through the lens of what the Bengals used to do. This offseason wasn’t what the Bengals used to do. It was aggressive and expensive. And, most importantly, it was exactly the kind of offseason that people had been demanding from the organization. That’s easy to dismiss as front-office speak. And, frankly, Bengals fans have heard plenty of talk over the years. Later in the interview, we asked Anderson about preconceived notions about the Brown/Blackburn family. “Well, number one, they really do want to win. I mean, that’s the whole goal of Mike Brown,” Anderson said. “But also, he’s thinking two or three years down the road. You know, making sure that they can field good teams then, as well.” This lines up with the Bengals previously rolling over cap space in recent years, as well as never being in salary cap hell. They also often draft in a way that does supply the roster with players who may not be pegged as immediate starters, but ones who could supplant incumbents once their contracts expire. The Bengals’ own reporting later highlighted just how involved Mike Brown remained in the process, with Tobin saying Brown was “instrumental in getting a lot of things done” during the offseason. Tobin also emphasized that the personnel department’s work was collaborative and that he wasn’t making it happen without the rest of the organization. That’s a pretty different picture from the cartoon version of Bengals ownership that has existed in the minds of many fans for decades. Does that mean the Browns and Blackburns should suddenly be immune from criticism? Absolutely not. The Bengals haven’t won a Super Bowl in their existence as a franchise. They haven’t even gotten back to one since Super Bowl LVI. And ultimately, the only thing that will make this offseason truly meaningful is what happens when the games matter most. But give credit where credit is due. The Bengals identified a problem in a year of urgency, and they attacked it. They spent the money. They made the trades, while simultaneously trying to bring continuity to other areas on the team. They added established players rather than simply hoping the draft would solve everything. And now, with Anderson offering his perspective, there’s an interesting question for Bengals fans to consider: What if the biggest change isn’t that the Browns suddenly became a different ownership family? What if the biggest change is that the circumstances finally convinced them to operate differently? Joe Burrow changes the equation. A franchise quarterback entering his prime changes the equation. Maybe they learned a hard lesson 15 years ago with Carson Palmer. And, perhaps most importantly, the pressure to capitalize on that window changes the equation. Anderson knows what a Super Bowl team looks like. He was the quarterback of the Bengals’ first one. So when someone with his history and perspective pushes back against some of the long-standing assumptions surrounding the organization, they’re saying, “I’m willing to listen.” That doesn’t mean blindly trusting ownership. It means acknowledging what actually happened. The Bengals talked about going all-in — and then they actually went all-in. Now it’s up to the players, coaches, and front office to prove that those moves were worth it. And if they do? Maybe Bengals fans will finally have to retire a few of those old assumptions about the people running this franchise. We were pleased to chat with the Bengals’ legend, courtesy of Heartflow . The former Cincinnati quarterback recently learned that up to 1 in 3 retired football players die from cardiovascular disease, yet much remains unknown about their risk. Wanting to be proactive with his health in new ways, he enrolled in Heartflow’s GAMEFILM Registry, a program designed to analyze the heart health of former professional athletes with the goal of improving the standard of care for everyone. Just as coaches study game film to anticipate what’s coming next, Heartflow’s first-of-its-kind AI technology helps predict what’s coming for your heart. From former professional athletes like Ken, whose bodies endured years of elite physical demands, to the everyday person with a family history of heart disease and beyond, these kinds of advanced insights can be life-changing. Be sure to be proactive about your health, and check out our amazing chat with one of the best Bengals players to ever suit up!

title: Evan McPherson named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month
summary: Cincinnati Bengals kicker Evan McPherson has been named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September, the NFL announced Thursday. McPherson, now in his sixth season, converted all eight field-goal attempts and eight extra points in Cincinnati’s three September games. His 32 points scored tied for the most by any NFL kicker, while his […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals place kicker Evan McPherson (2) celebrates a field goal in the first quarter of the NFL Preseason game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Detroit Lions at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Thursday, Aug. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Cincinnati Bengals kicker Evan McPherson has been named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September, the NFL announced Thursday. McPherson, now in his sixth season, converted all eight field-goal attempts and eight extra points in Cincinnati’s three September games. His 32 points scored tied for the most by any NFL kicker, while his total field goals tied for the most by an AFC kicker. He also led all kickers in field goals made from 50+ yards with five. The 27-year-old McPherson opened the season vs. Tampa Bay in Week 1 by going 4/4 on his field-goal attempts, including makes of 55 and 58 yards. He became the first kicker in Bengals history and is the only NFL kicker this season to make multiple kicks from 55 yards or beyond in a game. McPherson followed that up with another pair of field goals from 50+ yards in Week 2 at Houston. He then hit from 50 yards and 38 yards in the Bengals’ Week 3 game at Pittsburgh. His five field goals from 50+ yards are the most in a single month in Bengals history. He’s made his last 20 field-goal attempts overall dating back to Week 11 of last season, which is the second-longest streak in team history behind 21 consecutive field goals by Shayne Graham in 2007. This is McPherson’s second AFC Special Teams Player of the Month award of his career. title: Browns winning games because of the “And” needed in football
summary: After the Cleveland Browns beat the Carolina Panthers in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, we asked our readers to share why they believed the team was winning games. The answers were a little all over the place, which is not only to be expected but maybe the point for a young team with […]
full_text: After the Cleveland Browns beat the Carolina Panthers in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season, we asked our readers to share why they believed the team was winning games . The answers were a little all over the place, which is not only to be expected but maybe the point for a young team with a lot of moving parts. After the Browns’ victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football to kick off Week 4, the answer might just be the word “And.” Simple but confusing, right? A few years ago, there was a trend involving the ampersand (&) sign. It ended up on T-shirts, social media posts, and found its way into conversations about a variety of things. In sports, it was used to highlight a group of players from your favorite team. For this year’s Cleveland team, the problem is that the list of reasons they are being successful would be too big for a T-shirt (and we will probably miss one). Yet, the reason the Browns are 3-1 and will enter Week 5 with at least a share of the AFC North lead is the “and” of it all. Each game has heroes, not a hero. Each game has had big plays, not just a big play. Each win saw multiple coaching decisions and scheme adjustments, not just one key one. Players, not player. & Coaches, not coach. & Efforts, not effort. & Decisions, not decision. & Sacrifices, not sacrifice The list goes on and on and on. The difference between this positive start to Cleveland’s season and the few others that they have had seems to be in the collective. The Browns are not winning games just because their opponents make mistakes. Cleveland isn’t winning games because of some heroic effort by an individual or two. The Browns didn’t pull off an upset because of terrible weather, a trick play, or some fluke injury. It is “the we and the us and the we-n-us” like the fictional character Zava from “Ted Lasso” said: That is also why these three straight wins have come down to the wire, left us breathless and shaking at times, and left us wondering how easily things could have gone sideways. And thankful that they did not. The Cleveland Browns are 3-1 AND leading the AFC North AND have a chance to build on the wins AND have extra draft picks AND have the greatest fanbase supporting them AND, at least for one day, are the talk of the NFL. Bask in it Browns fans; enjoy the team-oriented wins. Welcome to Victory Friday, Victory Saturday, Victory Sunday, and Victory Monday. They are so, so sweet.

title: Browns vs Steelers: Winners, losers as Cleveland uses defense, key plays to secure win
summary: The young NFL season has the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers at 2-1-0 and tied for the AFC North Division lead. Well, actually, all four teams in the division have the same record. New head coach Todd Monken has transformed every offensive team that he has been hired to coach. Cleveland is simply his next […]
full_text: The young NFL season has the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers at 2-1-0 and tied for the AFC North Division lead. Well, actually, all four teams in the division have the same record. New head coach Todd Monken has transformed every offensive team that he has been hired to coach. Cleveland is simply his next stop. RELATED: NFL POWER RANKINGS The Browns have had good luck against Pittsburgh in the past five years, going 4-1-0 at home. Could they continue that success on Thursday Night Football and find themselves still on top of the division? Nobody believes that this year’s Browns roster will do anything. QB Deshaun Watson is playing better, kicker Andre Szmyt still hasn’t missed a field goal attempt, and the defense is keeping the production of Jim Schwartz while putting Mike Rutenberg’s spin to things. In the end, Cleveland saw their big lead disappear in the fourth quarter with several turnovers and a ton of untimely penalties. It took a Szmyt 56-yard field goal to win it 27-24 . So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? BROWNIES – Week 4 Winners CB Denzel Ward – What a wonderful pick early in the second quarter as the Steelers were driving. Ward had totally covered up WR Michael Pittman. This set the tone for the game’s defensive effort. Finished with four total tackles, one QB hit, an interception, and one batted pass. Jaleel movin' and groovin' for the score! #PITvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/b2xqYWjjGJ — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 2, 2026 RB Jaleel McLaughlin – If you had to reach for the Browns depth chart to see who #38 was after he scored Cleveland’s first points in the second quarter, so did we. McLaughlin completely juked out two Steeler defenders and got an excellent downfield block from TE Harold Fannin and WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who remained engaged on his man. Stunning run. Defense – DC Mike Rutenberg wanted to make sure that WR D.K. Metcalf was not going to beat his defense, so he devised some double coverage that eliminated him from the Steelers’ offense and forced QB Aaron Rodgers to look elsewhere. That worked well until late in the fourth quarter when Metcalf came alive with several big gains. Twice in the first half, the Steelers drove inside the Red Zone and yet only scored three points. Several third downs became sacks as the defensive backfield had great coverage. After the Deshaun Watson fumble, each pass play was well-covered as Pittsburgh was maneuvering for the field goal until DT Mike Hall returned to the game and got the sack. The Steelers got back into the game with the ball back with just over six minutes to play, yet it was a three-and-out. 60 YARDS DOWN THE FIELD FOR DB! #PITvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/9rrJl5NINH — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 2, 2026 WR Denzel Boston – How did Boston get so open in the second quarter, he made a slight wiggle to affect CB Daylen Everette, then took off deep with his speed. QB Deshaun Watson laid a perfect throw and the Browns were in business inside the 20. With 1:39 left in the first half, Boston recognized that Watson was in trouble and moved towards his QB with a great grab, but the offense accepted a holding call instead. How reliable was Boston when Cleveland was on the one-yard line late in the fourth quarter with a first-down pass when the Browns wanted to work the clock? Led all receivers with 89 yards. QB Deshaun Watson – Terrific flip pass to RB Quinshon Judkins after the Boston huge gain. Watson looked off the safety, who drifted away from the center, and found Q out of the backfield. Down on the one-yard line with the second touchdown on the next play. Getting the safety to move out of the center made this play. Nice toss to Boston for the first down at midfield with 3:22 left before the half. Then two plays later, Steelers DT Yahya Black had gotten past RG Austin Barber and was bearing down when Watson threw a strike to Concepcion that gained 25 yards. How did Watson not get sacked by two defenders with 1:29 left in the first half, and instead find Judkins, who took it to the one-yard line? I LOVE HAROLD FANNIN #PITvsCLE on @NFLonPrime pic.twitter.com/UH4gsEGues — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 2, 2026 Great recognition for the TD toss to Fannin right before the half, with great coverage by LB Patrick Queen. The Clemson rendition of Watson would have taken off numerous times, but this version left the pocket several times, only to toss some short passes. The lost fumble in the third quarter, the interception in Quarter 4, and the other fumble that he was able to recover with 6:38 remaining in the game are concerning. Each one killed great drives and gave the Steelers hope for a comeback. With 8:34 left in the game, facing a third-and-four and the pocket collapsing, Watson was able to run for 21 yards and a needed first down. View this post on Instagram Missed a wide-open Fannin on the third-down play with just over four minutes to go, which also stopped the clock, and then had the untimely sack on the final drive, already in good field goal range. Finished going 24 for 33 for 268 yards, one touchdown, one pick, sacked twice, with a QB rating of 94.0. LB Carson Schwesinger – How about that tackle on 6’-7”, 265-pound TE Darnell Washington early in the second quarter? Went low, hung on until help arrived, and the result was a one-yard gain instead of running over a bunch of guys. Had the delayed blitz that became the McGuire sack with 6:06 left before the half. Nailed RB Jaylen Warren early in the third quarter for no gain. Led all Cleveland defenders with nine total tackles. Play calling – The first half was on full display as Cleveland’s offense went down and finished drives with touchdowns instead of field goals. Head coach Todd Monken got the message that the Browns could not get the run game going, so he began calling short-to-intermediate passing plays that worked over and over in the first half. Monken then began to call run plays in the third quarter to milk the clock and control the time of possession. The third-and-seven for the short pass to WR Jerry Jeudy for the first down showed Monken’s ability to alter the game plan. Monken also kept up with whether DE T.J. Watt was on the field or not, and ran when he went to the sidelines and passed when he was on the field. Special teams – P Corey Bojorquez boomed his first kick 68 yards; the pooched a punt that got an advantageous bounce, to which WR Malachi Corley was able to down the punt at the one-foot line. Great field awareness for Corley. A whopping punt late in the game was recorded as an 81-yard kick. Is this right? A 62.75-yard final average? The punt and kickoff coverage team had suffocating coverage and gang tackling from Donovan McMillan, Winston Reid, Toriano Pride Jr., and Sam Williams. K Andre Szmyt nailed his first field goal attempt from 44 yards and every PAT, then kicked the 56-yard game-winner with 10 seconds left like it was nothing. FROWNIES – Week 4 losers Penalties – Ahhhh!!! In the first quarter alone, the Browns had five penalties accepted, including on the opening kickoff. Another two were declined: holding – Mekhi Blackmon; illegal contact – Denzel Ward; offsides – Mike Hall; roughing the passer – Maliek Collins; and then Jared Verse’s encroachment gaffe on the one-foot line that gave the Steelers offense some breathing room. The Adin Huntington sack right before the half was wiped out by the hands-to-the-face call on Sam Williams. Nine penalties in the first half. A third-and-eight during the first drive of the second half becomes a third-and-13. The pass interference call against the rookie S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was a fourth-down play that eventually became a touchdown. The nice strike to Jeudy with 1:11 left in the game was negated on a false start by LG Zion Johnson. 14 total penalties in this game. T.J. title: Browns vs Steelers: 19 takeaways from big Week 4 AFC North win for Cleveland
summary: In a surprising matchup that would decide who was leading the AFC North coming out, the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers faced off on the shores of Lake Erie in Week 4’s Thursday Night Football. Injuries and big plays highlighted the game, with the Browns holding the lead from the middle of the second quarter, […]
full_text: In a surprising matchup that would decide who was leading the AFC North coming out, the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers faced off on the shores of Lake Erie in Week 4’s Thursday Night Football . Injuries and big plays highlighted the game, with the Browns holding the lead from the middle of the second quarter, but the veteran Steelers keeping the game close in the second half. A stressful back-and-forth game that the Browns pulled out the victory late in the game , running their record to 3-1 and sitting atop the AFC North as Week 4 gets started with a huge Cleveland victory. Andre Szmyt crushed the 56-yarder and has made 22 in a row Just an impressive clutch kick late in the game by the young kicker. A kick to, basically, win the game against a division rival in primetime, and Szmyt’s kick would have been good from about 65 yards or so. Mason Graham injury Graham had a great start to the season, but his early injury took away the defense’s best player . The Browns defense was still competitive during the game, but the loss of Graham was problematic and limited Mike Rutenberg’s unit. Crowd was a huge benefit The stadium was clearly rocking, even after Graham’s injury and the Browns starting with a three-and-out and then giving up a 17-play touchdown drive. The camera was shaking at times, caused multiple penalties, and frustrated the Steelers offense a lot. Boswell’s missed FG A generally consistent kicker, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell pulled his field goal attempt left in the second quarter, keeping the score a 14-7 Cleveland lead. Mike Hall’s return – Sack plus touchback combo Joining Graham in the locker room, Hall was actually carted off the field with an ankle injury. No one expected him to return, but there he was back on the field in the third quarter. All of a sudden, Hall shot through the offensive line and sacked Aaron Rodgers . The play pushed the Steelers out of field goal range, and the ensuing punt went out of the end zone, so the Browns were not pinned deep. Using KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston to strengths There are times that it is a good idea to get “cute” by using players in different ways than the opponent might expect. Right now, HC Todd Monken isn’t doing that with the two Cleveland rookies. Use deep balls, out routes, and slants to take advantage of Boston’s size. Using quick routes and screens to get Concepcion the ball in space, exactly what his skill set calls for. Getting everyone involved on offense Seven different Browns players catching the ball and four different players getting runs, Cleveland’s offense wasn’t a one- or two-person show, and it kept the Steelers from focusing on only a few. WR Jerry Jeudy made some huge plays late in the game, for example. Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell coverage key The Browns defense wasn’t perfect, but CBs Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell made things difficult for the Steelers for most of the game. Late, Rodgers forced some very good throws toward his guys, but Ward and Campbell forced him to look elsewhere, leading to a ton of pressure on the oldest player in the NFL. Huge to have two lockdown cornerbacks. Creative blitzing is fun Just really fun to get to enjoy the Browns defense bringing pressure in a variety of ways. Not only that, but the pressures made sense as they were paired with the right coverage behind them. Deshaun Watson doing enough and not enough Watson continues to be inconsistent. A really good second quarter, followed by not a lot of success in the second half until the last drive. Still concerns about his arm strength and ball security when running with it. A win is a win, but there are some weaknesses, including the inconsistencies, that are concerning. Running game got going in the 2nd half While the team only had 112 yards rushing, they had more than the Steelers and really got things going in the second half, when they were milking the big lead. Monken went a bit away from it as Pittsburgh made their comeback, but it was good to see some pressure being placed on the defense from Cleveland’s rushing attack. Tipped pass to INT instead of DPI A good play by former Ohio State Buckeyes LB Jack Sawyer to get his fingertip on it. Instead of a big defensive pass interference penalty, Pittsburgh gets the interception. Goes from Cleveland being in scoring position to giving the ball away. “Find Myles Harden” plan goes well much of the game Harden looked terrible in Week 1, better the last two weeks, but Week 4 was “find CB Myles Harden ” and throw the ball to whoever he is guarding. The PFF grades and data will be negative, and Harden’s spot on the roster could be in jeopardy. Sacks, hits on QB impacted Aaron Rodgers The veteran closed the 4th quarter very well, but throughout the game it was clear how the pressures, sacks and hits on the quarterback were impacting Rodgers. Quincy Williams all over the field, quick Nice to see LB Quincy Williams making big plays, especially in coverage and on a few blitzes, complementing LB Carson Schwesinger . LB Devin Bush played well for Cleveland, but Williams’ speed is just at a different level. Big 4th-quarter miss by Watson to Fannin A tough throw, running left trying to hit a player in front of you, but Watson had to make that throw and could have potentially ended the game. TE Harold Fannin Jr. was wide open with no defender around him. As Watson noted after the game, he made things harder on his team than he had to. Tight games are rough on the stress level Some of us are too old for these kinds of stressful games. I was shaking, buzzing for most of the 4th quarter. Would love a few easy wins after this. Jared Verse’s penalty leads to an easy 2-pointer, tying the game While Graham’s absence was huge on Rodgers’ QB sneak for the two-point conversion, that isn’t the play call if DE Jared Verse doesn’t go offsides on the first attempt, moving the ball to where it could have snuck in. Winning games is so much fun The Cleveland Browns are 3-1 heading into some extra rest for Week 5. Leading the AFC North through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season is surprising to almost everyone. And so much fun for fans. What were your takeaways from the Week 4 victory for the Browns over the Steelers? Join the conversation!
