title: Will the Chiefs’ pass rush return to form this week against the Raiders?
summary: Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. It’s a quote made famous by Mike Tyson, and it applies in all aspects of life. Especially football. Imagine you’re standing in your backyard playing catch with your 7-year-old son. It’s easy to throw a pass 10 yards away. No pressure, right? But what […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. It’s a quote made famous by Mike Tyson, and it applies in all aspects of life. Especially football. Imagine you’re standing in your backyard playing catch with your 7-year-old son. It’s easy to throw a pass 10 yards away. No pressure, right? But what if there’s someone in front of your child? Suddenly the throw becomes more difficult. Now imagine a 290-pound grown man sprinting toward you at full speed as you’re attempting to make the throw. Yeah, good luck. That’s the life of an NFL quarterback. Every. Single. Week. It sounds miserable. It’s no wonder fewer than 20 people in the world can do this job at a high level at any given time. Applying that pressure on opposing quarterbacks is the goal of every defensive coordinator in the league. Don’t let the opposing quarterback get comfortable. Get him off his spot. Throw him off of his rhythm. We hear this every single week. It’s easier said than done. But when you do it, it’s special. It’s what made the Seattle Seahawks ’ defense stand out a year ago. It felt like a new player was getting after the quarterback on every single play. That defensive line came at opposing offenses in waves. It was constant, relentless pressure. It’s the kind of thing every team in the league hopes to replicate. The Kansas City Chiefs are no different. After the first week of the season, it felt like Kansas City might be on its way to a better year in that regard. The defensive line made Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix look uncomfortable from the very first snap. Steve Spagnuolo was in his bag. The results were hard to argue. Chiefs defenders had three sacks and five quarterback hits in that season-opener against Nix and the Broncos. This same defense has zero sacks and five quarterback hits over the past two weeks… combined. Wait, what? Why? How? Didn’t this team just spend millions on a new nose tackle and multiple top-50 selections on defensive linemen? And aren’t they spending $50 million against the cap on two other defensive linemen? Yupp. They are. The results should be better. But they aren’t. Not yet, at least. What’s gone wrong? Let’s dive into the numbers, shall we? Team: Time to Throw: Average Depth of Target Pressure Rate Sacks Blitz Rate Broncos: 2.48 sec 4.1 yards 21% 3 45% Colts: 2.65 sec 5.7 yards 24% 0 24% Dolphins: 2.9 sec 9.2 yards 26% 0 31% *Stats courtesy of Dynatize & Pro Football Reference So, yeah, it’s a bit all over the place. The Chiefs blitzed the Broncos, and Denver responded by getting the ball out of Nix’s hands as quickly as possible. It resulted in a ton of dump-offs and a lower pressure rate, but the Chiefs’ blitzes paid off with a few sacks. The blitz rate dropped over the past couple of weeks. The pressure rate did increase ever so slightly, but the Chiefs’ ability to finish plays in the backfield all but disappeared. It’s strange. It’s hard to explain. It needs to change. This is a good week to get things back on track. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins is the first true pocket passer the Chiefs have faced all season. He’s been sacked five times and hit 10 times over the past two weeks against the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Chargers , and he could be without starting right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson this week. Powers-Johnson has missed practice each of the past two days with a groin issue. His replacement would seem to be Caleb Rogers, a player with six career starts. That sound you hear is defensive tackles Chris Jones and Peter Woods licking their chops. This was already a relatively advantageous matchup for the Chiefs’ defensive line, and it looks like it’s getting better. Brandon Thorn of Establish The Run ranked the Chiefs’ defensive line vs. the Raiders’ offensive line as the fifth-biggest mismatch in the league this week. He has the Raiders rated as the 21st “best” offensive line in the league. The Chiefs rate as the fifth-best defensive line. That’s a lot of faith in a group that hasn’t produced. There are reasons why smart individuals like Thron still have so much belief in a group that’s failed to produce a sack over the past two weeks. It’s entirely possible the Chiefs’ defensive game plan focused on stopping the run against the Indianapolis Colts . At times, it looked like they played more of a contain rush against quarterback Malik Willis to force him to win from the pocket. It’s also possible safety Chamarri Conner’s absence has forced Steve Spagnuolo to run a more vanilla game plan on the back end of the defense in recent weeks. Throw in a nagging calf injury for Jones, and you’ve got a formula for limited pass-rush production. That’s all fine and dandy. But eventually this unit has to start putting pressure on the opposing quarterback again. This would be a good week for it to start.

title: Steve Spagnuolo sees accountability among Chiefs’ defense
summary: Although the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 3-0 start, fans have found the last two defensive performances stressful. After a dominant Week 1 showing against the Denver Broncos, the Indianapolis Colts took the unit to overtime and nearly won after advancing to the Kansas City 17-yard line in the extra period. In Week […]
full_text: (Photo by Alie Skowronski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Although the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 3-0 start, fans have found the last two defensive performances stressful. After a dominant Week 1 showing against the Denver Broncos , the Indianapolis Colts took the unit to overtime and nearly won after advancing to the Kansas City 17-yard line in the extra period. In Week 3, the lowly Miami Dolphins posted their highest yardage total (and their lowest-scoring performance) of the season against Kansas City’s defense. Per Next Gen Stats , the Chiefs are actually fourth in expected points added (EPA) per defensive play at -0.16. Still, the unit is not passing the eye test for many observers, including their leader. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo explained before Thursday’s practice that everyone is well aware of the recent deficiencies. “By the time Tuesday rolls around when I first see them, they’re chewed out,” remarked the coach. “I’ve already chewed myself out for a whole day. So, we like to have constructive criticism. The good thing about this group is they’re all pretty accountable. Even if I’m standing in there and pointing something out, I see a lot of heads shaking, ‘Yeah, you’re right,’ so that part I don’t even worry about.” Spagnuolo shares frustrations that opponents seem to get out of trouble in third-down situations that should favor the defense. He is happy with how his squad has come through multiple times in key fourth-down moments. “You look at third down percentage, and it looks crappy,” he acknowledged, “but I kind of dissect the whole thing. That’s a run play I think [Miami] had — there was one third and 10 there that they had a really good design route concept that beat what we had out there. So, I’m going to give them that, but all of a sudden, if you take three [plays] out of there, it’s a whole different ballgame. What was good was when we were able to stop them and get it to fourth down. We had the three fourth-down stops that were key. Now, we don’t want to always be banking on that because those are pretty difficult. But would I like to be better in third down? Yeah, and we’ll dissect it and hopefully come up with something a little bit better this week.” The team’s pass rush has underwhelmed, going two weeks without a sack and giving teams extra time to get out of difficult situations. While the team’s pass rushers have knocked down some key passes, they aren’t getting to the quarterback quickly enough. “I think we’d all like to see it better on first and second down,” said Spagnuolo. “That’s where some of those plays got long. We’ve got to do better on the back end with those explosive passes, but when the down gets extended, guys have a tendency to kind of get open at some point. So, first and second down is one thing that we’ve looked at. I was happy that we got our hands up and knocked some balls down. That play [defensive tackle Chris Jones] made with [defensive end George Karlaftis] was really important. “I thought we could have had five turnovers. I thought we had three missed opportunities. We’ve got to get those…Third down was something we’d like to get better at. Pass rush on first and second down. We’ve talked about all those things.” Sunday’s road matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders will show whether those discussions are proving fruitful. Spagnuolo does not expect an easy day against veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Raiders are currently second in the league with 0.56 EPA per third-down pass play. “Big challenge,” Spagnuolo said of Cousins. “I’ve been down this road before. Kirk’s one of these quarterbacks that I’ve got a tremendous amount of respect for. He’s been doing it for a long time. I think he’s a quality guy. Every time I see him, I tell him how much I respect his character. That part is great, but on the football field, he gets the ball out so quick that he makes it really difficult. I think the knocking down of passes will be really important. The sticky coverage and making him throw it into tight windows will be really big. When we do that, we need a couple of knockdowns by a corner or a safety to get him in a longer down the distance or get us off the field. We’ll have to mix it up, but I think you’ve got to be a little bit careful with a guy that’s as smart as Kirk is.”

title: Kingdom Keys: 3 keys to a Chiefs victory over the Raiders in Week 4
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders will renew their longstanding rivalry Sunday afternoon, but this meeting carries more early-season significance than most expected. Both teams enter the matchup undefeated at 3-0, marking the first time they have simultaneously opened a season with three consecutive victories. The winner will take sole possession of first […]
full_text: (Photo by Kirby Lee/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders will renew their longstanding rivalry Sunday afternoon, but this meeting carries more early-season significance than most expected. Both teams enter the matchup undefeated at 3-0, marking the first time they have simultaneously opened a season with three consecutive victories. The winner will take sole possession of first place in the AFC West. Kansas City was expected to return to contention after last season’s disappointment. Las Vegas has been the surprise. The Raiders have already matched their win total from 2025, defeating the Miami Dolphins , Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints behind a rebuilt roster and first-year head coach Klint Kubiak. Here are three keys to a Chiefs victory in Week 4: Offensive key: Control Maxx Crosby Kansas City’s first responsibility will be preventing defensive end Maxx Crosby from taking over the game. A proposed offseason trade that would have sent Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens fell through after the Ravens reportedly had concerns about his surgically repaired knee. Crosby remained in Las Vegas and appears motivated to prove those concerns were misplaced. Through three games, he has generated 17 pressures, including two sacks, four quarterback hits and 11 hurries. The Raiders’ pass rush extends beyond Crosby. Las Vegas ranks second in the NFL in pressure rate at 36%, according to Pro Football Reference , and has the fourth-most sacks in the NFL with 10, despite rarely needing to blitz. Edge rusher Malcolm Koonce recorded six pressures and a pivotal strip-sack against New Orleans, while Kwity Paye has also been productive opposite Crosby. That creates a significant challenge for Kansas City’s offensive line, particularly rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson, the NFL’s Offensive Rookie of the Month for September; he has allowed just three pressures in each of his first three games without surrendering a sack. This will be his most difficult assignment yet. Crosby moves around the defensive front, so the Chiefs cannot expect one blocker to handle him throughout the game. They must identify his location before every snap and provide help when necessary through tight ends, running backs, and protection slides. Kansas City can also neutralize the Raiders’ rush by continuing to run the football and use play action. A credible rushing threat can make Crosby hesitate before attacking upfield, even if only for a moment. The Chiefs should mix in quick throws, screens, moving pockets and misdirection rather than repeatedly asking Mahomes to operate from obvious passing situations. If Kansas City protects him long enough to attack downfield, it can challenge a Raiders secondary that has occasionally surrendered opportunities despite the defense’s impressive start. The Chiefs do not have to eliminate Crosby. They simply cannot allow him to wreck the game. Defensive key: Keep Brock Bowers under 75 yards Las Vegas has a talented backfield featuring Ashton Jeanty and rookie Mike Washington Jr., but Kansas City’s primary defensive concern must be tight end Brock Bowers. Bowers missed the Raiders’ first two games after undergoing a meniscus procedure. He returned against New Orleans and immediately reminded the NFL why he is one of its most dangerous tight ends, catching 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. That performance earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors. What makes Bowers especially difficult to defend is how Las Vegas deploys him. He can line up as a traditional tight end, in the slot or outside like a wide receiver. That versatility allows the Raiders to identify favorable matchups. This presents a challenge for a Chiefs defense that has occasionally struggled when linebackers and safeties are isolated in space. Indianapolis slot receiver Josh Downs caught seven passes for 72 yards in Week 2, and Miami repeatedly used quick passes and motion to extend drives last week. Kansas City cannot depend on one defender to cover Bowers all afternoon. Steve Spagnuolo should vary his approach by using bracket coverage, safety help and physical contact near the line of scrimmage. Changing the coverage picture could also prevent Kirk Cousins from immediately recognizing where Bowers will be available. Completely stopping Bowers is unrealistic. Keeping him below 75 receiving yards is a more reasonable goal. If the Chiefs prevent him from dominating the middle of the field and producing explosive gains, Cousins will have to rely more heavily on the rest of the Raiders’ receiving corps to sustain drives. X-factor: Win on third down Third down could decide which undefeated team leaves Allegiant Stadium in control of the division. Kansas City’s offense has converted 17 of 37 third downs this season — a 45.9% success rate. The Raiders are slightly behind at 16 of 39, or 41%. The Chiefs converted three of seven opportunities against Miami, but several stalled possessions prevented them from taking complete control earlier. Against a Raiders defense that generates pressure without blitzing, staying in manageable third-down situations will be essential. Kansas City cannot consistently face third-and-8 or longer and allow Crosby, Koonce and Paye to rush without respecting the run. Success on first and second down will give the Chiefs access to their entire playbook and allow Mahomes to use play action, quick passes, or the running game to move the chains. Defensively, the Chiefs must improve upon what happened against the Dolphins. Miami converted eight of 16 third downs, including several during an early 17-play drive. The Chiefs entered the game holding opponents below 30% on third down, but quick throws and coverage breakdowns repeatedly kept Miami’s offense on the field. Allowing Bowers and Cousins to duplicate that success would enable Las Vegas to control possession while keeping Mahomes on the sideline. Kansas City must communicate through motion, tackle immediately after the catch, and find ways to pressure Cousins without leaving Bowers isolated against a linebacker. The bottom line Offensively, Kansas City needs to control Crosby by helping its tackles, maintaining its commitment to the running game and using play action to create opportunities downfield. Defensively, the Chiefs must limit Bowers’ favorable matchups and keep him below 75 receiving yards. On both sides of the football, they must consistently win on third down. If Kansas City accomplishes those three things, it will have an excellent opportunity to improve to 4-0, take sole possession of first place in the AFC West, and remind Las Vegas that the division still runs through the Chiefs.

full_text: (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are off to a strong start this season, and so are two players in particular: running back Kenneth Walker and left tackle Kahlil Benson. Walker was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month and Benson was named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month. Shoutout to Arrowhead Pride user Cherbonek for sharing the news and some good notes on each player. Running back Jerick McKinnon was the last Chiefs player to be named AFC Offensive Player of the Month, earning it in December 2022, the month after quarterback Patrick Mahomes took the award for November. The season before, Mahomes won the award in December of 2021. He also won the award in November 2020, September 2019, and 2018. While with the Seattle Seahawks , Walker won the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month award, but the last Chiefs player to earn it before Benson was running back Kareem Hunt in 2017; he won in September and December that year.

A road game against the 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders will decide the AFC West leader through the first four games of the season. The Raiders have matched Kansas City’s hot start with first-year head coach Klint Kubiak […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s reason to believe the Kansas City Chiefs ’ toughest test of the season will be in Week 4. A road game against the 3-0 Las Vegas Raiders will decide the AFC West leader through the first four games of the season. The Raiders have matched Kansas City’s hot start with first-year head coach Klint Kubiak leading a young team laced with the right veterans. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid praised Kubiak’s work during his press conference on Wednesday. “He’s a good football coach, he’s got good assistant coaches, guys that have been in the business for a while, and they’ve got good schemes,” Reid said. “The guys are executing it and executing it fast and accurate.” “They’ve got a ton of turnovers, and batted balls and everything else,” Reid pointed out. “So they’re playing aggressive football.” Las Vegas has forced nine turnovers this year, two more than any other team has. The newcomers the Raiders acquired this offseason are driving that number: former Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Nakobe Dean leads the league with three forced fumbles, and rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses leads the NFL in interceptions. The new-look Raiders look sharp, but even when the team hasn’t had success in recent seasons, it has topped Kansas City. Last year, Las Vegas squeaked out a 13-12 win in the season finale; on Christmas Day 2023, the 6-8 Raiders upset the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium and nearly cost the team its chance at eventually winning Super Bowl LVIII. “Yeah, they’ve always played us tough over the years,” Reid acknowledged. “I mean, it’s still Raiders and Chiefs, and the records really didn’t matter going into it. Both teams played hard against each other. They’ve got a good group of guys right now and good leadership, and they’re doing well. A lot of turnovers.” Up front, everybody knows defensive end Maxx Crosby is the main threat — but edge rushers Malcolm Koonce (2.5) and Kwity Paye (2) each have more sacks than the five-time Pro Bowler does to start this season. It’s a pass-rush group that quarterback Patrick Mahomes knows will test the offensive line, including rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson. “I have all the trust in the world in those guys,” Mahomes said. “It’s not just Maxx. (Koonce)’s doing a great job. Kwity Paye’s doing a great job of rushing the passer, all those guys, and so it’ll be another challenge for them, and I’m excited for them to go out there and accept it.” On the other side of the ball, the Raiders have been captained by quarterback Kirk Cousins; last week, his top target made his season debut: tight end Brock Bowers, after missing the first two games of the season due to a last-minute surgery to trim his meniscus, caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton knows it will take the entire defense’s attention to keep Bowers in check. He talked about Las Vegas’ offense on Wednesday. “We only got one game on him this year, and how they’re going to use him,” Bolton said. “But obviously, he’s versatile with the ball. They find different ways to get him involved in the offense, spread him out, put him in location, screen game, so we’ve got to be aware of where he’s at. Just kind of have 22 eyes on him… that’s the game plan.” Running back Ashton Jeanty will also need attention in the run game — but also as a receiver. This year, the 2025 first-round pick has caught 13 passes for 97 yards and two touchdowns. The Chiefs’ linebackers will need to keep Jeanty in check, putting Kansas City’s defense in position to get off the field. “They’re running the ball well, playing good up front,” Bolton acknowledged. “Kirk Cousins staying clean, throwing the ball on time and on target, so definitely a challenge for us to get them off the spot, stop the running game, get some penetration, and get some third-and-longs.”

title: Chiefs Injuries: Analyzing Josh Simmons’ bulging disc injury
summary: Head coach Andy Reid finally clarified one of the biggest question marks surrounding the Kansas City Chiefs’ 2026 season. In his Wednesday media availability, Reid revealed Simmons has a bulging disc in his lower back, which is why he has not made his 2026 season debut. Simmons initially injured his back during training camp and […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Head coach Andy Reid finally clarified one of the biggest question marks surrounding the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season. In his Wednesday media availability, Reid revealed Simmons has a bulging disc in his lower back, which is why he has not made his 2026 season debut. Simmons initially injured his back during training camp and has not practiced since mid-August. Let’s examine the injury affecting quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ blind-side protector. Analyzing the injury The low back, the lumbar spine , consists of five large vertebrae. Between each vertebra lies an intervertebral disc. Each disc acts as a shock absorber for the spine, as well as a cushion between each vertebral level. The disc serves to prevent nerve compression, shearing, and accelerated degenerative conditions of the spine. When a disc bulges, the outer protective layer weakens and stretches outward, but the inner gel-like portion stays intact. A more significant injury is a herniated disc, where the disc protrudes outward because of a tear or crack in the outer protective layer. A bulging disc can cause many problems. These include, most notably, pain, loss of range of motion, radicular symptoms (lower extremity pain or abnormal sensation), and loss of strength. Nerves originate from each level of the spine and branch outward to the rest of the body and the extremities. The nerve roots from the lumbar spine innervate the lower extremities. Bulging discs that compress nerves can cause lower extremity pain, numbness, tingling, and/or loss of strength. Unfortunately, there is no set timeline for how long a bulging disc takes to resolve. Many factors affect the healing process. Decompression and rest are key early in rehab, along with restoring any lost mobility. With any lower extremity symptoms, the goal is to centralize symptoms to the lumbar spine. Once symptoms decrease, the focus can shift more toward strengthening and returning to higher-level activity. The bottom line Reid said it himself in his press conference, “backs can be kind of tricky.” They can flare up easily, and when lower-extremity symptoms are present, they can take time to resolve entirely. It’s already apparent this is a significant injury, as Simmons has not practiced in a month and a half. Based on the information reported, however, the extent of the bulging disc (mild, moderate, or severe) and whether multiple spinal levels are involved are unknown. Obviously, if there are multiple impaired discs or the severity of protrusion is greater, the symptoms will be more pronounced, and his return to play will take longer. Offensive tackle is a position which requires speed, power, strength, and body control. All these attributes can be affected by a back injury, making it vital Simmons is healthy before returning to the field. Nerve compression is almost certainly at play here, given the lower-extremity weakness. The focus should shift from a timeline for Simmons’s return to ensuring he is healthy for the long run. The Chiefs are in for a marathon of a season—currently in position for a postseason run. All reports from the team indicate Simmons is progressing well, and so trust should be given to the rehab professionals to give Simmons every opportunity to return to the field in 2026.

title: Patrick Mahomes values ‘bragging rights’ over Maxx Crosby
summary: NFL analysis frequently focuses on quarterback matchups — ironically, players who never actually share the field during a game. One of the best current rivalries between a quarterback and a defender set on thwarting him will reignite Sunday when the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Las Vegas Raiders. For the 14th time, starting […]
full_text: (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images NFL analysis frequently focuses on quarterback matchups — ironically, players who never actually share the field during a game. One of the best current rivalries between a quarterback and a defender set on thwarting him will reignite Sunday when the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Las Vegas Raiders . For the 14th time, starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes will face off against one of the league’s best pass rushers, the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby. Crosby has six career sacks and is credited with 16 quarterback hits when facing Kansas City. Speaking before Wednesday’s practice, Mahomes left no doubt the respect he has for the man who will spend Sunday trying to bring him down. “He’s one of the best competitors in the league,” observed Mahomes. “I think that’s where the respect comes from is that we kind of have that mutual want to be the best on the field when we’re out there. So, when you go against those guys, it brings out the best in you, but there’s a ton of respect for how he plays the game of football, how he competes, and the man that he is. For me, I just know when I step on that football field, I’m going to need my best because he’s going to bring his best, and I think that’s when you get the best games out there.” Some may be surprised to see the Chiefs among the final five undefeated squads, but no one expected a 3-0 start for the Raiders, who held the first overall selection in April’s NFL Draft. Mahomes believes the talent added around Crosby has aided the Las Vegas turnaround. “They’ve brought in a lot of guys that are really good football players,” Mahomes noted, “and they’ve added young, talented guys in there as well. Obviously, it starts with Maxx and their defensive line and being able to protect and be able to run the ball and do stuff like that. But they have great players everywhere, and they fly to the football…We’ll have to execute at a high level, but it’ll be a great challenge for us, and we’re excited for it.” The Raiders appeared to have traded Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens early last offseason. Ultimately, Baltimore pulled out of the trade citing injury concerns following Crosby’s physical. Mahomes is surprised any concerns would cause a team to pass on adding Crosby’s talent, but he expects the veteran to use the situation as motivation. “He was going to be on the Ravens, so, either way, I would’ve saw him at some point,” Mahomes remarked. “It was a weird offseason. It was surprising to me just knowing who he is and the way he competes and they trade for him, and they end up not taking him and wanting to send him back. Because of the player that he is, I know he’ll use that as motivation. He’s coming off injury as well, and I know he’ll use that as motivation as well. So, it’s always great to have the great players in the league and get up to go up against them and compete. So, I’m excited for it.” As both players advance in their NFL careers, Mahomes sees something special in the familiarity with Crosby. “It’s almost like whenever you’re young, and you’re competing with one of your friends,” he explained. “You want to win because you kind of have those bragging rights. You kind of go into the offseason, and if you see the guy, you can kind of give him a little something here and there. It’s something about that. It’s just what the pure football is, is having the best competitors compete against each other and that’s what I think you really get whenever you go out there and it’s Raiders versus Chiefs.”

title: Chargers draft elite DT in new 2027 NFL mock draft
summary: Through three games this season, you would think that draft analysts would all agree that the Chargers would be looking at offensive players in next year’s draft. Surprisingly though, it’s been defensive linemen more so than anything else, both tackles and edges. The Chargers have done a good job of building and establishing a room […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 6: Will Echoles #52 of the Ole Miss Rebels during a game between the Ole Miss Rebels and the Louisville Cardinals at Nissan Stadium on September 6, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Through three games this season, you would think that draft analysts would all agree that the Chargers would be looking at offensive players in next year’s draft. Surprisingly though, it’s been defensive linemen more so than anything else, both tackles and edges. The Chargers have done a good job of building and establishing a room that offers both top-tier play, young potential, and tried-and-true veteran leadership. At the same time, that room is missing a dynamic pass rusher who can help push pockets and get from point A to point B as fast as possible. In this new 2027 mock draft from CBS Sports, analyst Mike Renner has the Chargers selecting Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles with the 14th overall pick. That spot in the draft would also mean Renner foresees the Chargers actually winning some games this year, putting them around six to eight Ws in the column. Here’s what Renner had to say about the pairing: “ Echoles is the kind of interior penetrator the Chargers’ defensive line has been missing. They have a lot of guys who are great at eating space in the run game, but not many who can create havoc in the backfield. That’s what Echoles has been doing since the start of last year. ” At 6’3 and 310 pounds, Echoles has both the mass to hold up in the middle and explosiveness off the line to make quarterbacks nervous on passing downs. Through four games this season, Echoles has three tackles for loss and a half sack, but his film shows a guy that does a lot of influencing on each play without ending it in the stat sheet. Will Echoles was DOMINANT vs. LSU (7 pressures, 3 TFL, 1 sack) He was my clear DT1 over the summer (No. 13 overall) and hasn't disappointed so far in 2026. Equally disruptive vs. pass/run. pic.twitter.com/vLRmXF2u4r — Dane Brugler (@dpbrugler) September 20, 2026 Defensive tackle is a hard position to foresee the Chargers selecting that early due to several other positions of need that seem much more prominent right now, but elite interior players are also hard to come by and play just as big of a role in stopping offenses as anyone else. Hard to get off a pass when someone is in your face in an instant. Hard to establish the run when your interior can’t get movement. These are all things Echoles will bring to a team in 2027.

summary: The Los Angeles Rams are gearing up for Week 4 against the Philadelphia Eagles, and they may have Puka Nacua back, but they may be without Aaron Donald and others. full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are gearing up for Week 4 against the Philadelphia Eagles, and they may have Puka Nacua back , but they may be without Aaron Donald and others. The start to the season has been shaky for Los Angeles with flat performances, injuries and some unlucky calls . At times, the Rams have looked good too, so there’s that. The question for this Rams team is how good will they be? They have the talent; they are still competing the last two weeks despite some real injuries (Myles Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1). The Rams will see if Donald can suit up for them on Sunday and or they’ll see if they can withstand some more bad luck. Rams’ Aaron Donald Update Teases A Possible Break For Eagles (sports.yahoo) “When the head coach Sean McVay met with reporters, he revealed that Donald is dealing with a sore back. Currently, the superstar’s game status is up in the air. “I wouldn’t want to say anything of that nature yet,” McVay said regarding Donald’s status for Sunday’s action, according to Rams reporter Zach Edwards . “But (his) back’s a little bit sore, and he’s as tough as it gets, we’ll continue to have updates as the week goes.” Rams OC expects Nacua (groin) to practice in full (nbcsports) “Scheelhaase also said that Nacua “twisted” to catch a pass thrown behind him yesterday, which the offensive coordinator took as a good sign. Nacua is on track to face the Eagles in Week 4. As long as he gets through the practice week without suffering a setback, Nacua is an elite WR1 this week.“ Sean McVay addresses speculation that Puka Nacua’s absence was contract-related (ramswire) “During Nacua’s absence, some speculated that he wasn’t injured at all and that it was all contract-related. Nacua, of course, has not yet signed an extension with the Rams despite being in the final year of his contract, causing some to spread the rumor that he was quietly holding out. During an interview on ESPN Los Angeles Wednesday, McVay addressed that speculation and denied its plausibility. “Yeah, it’s not true,” McVay said. “He just did a great job with our walkthrough. He’s been working, chomping at the bit to get back out there with his teammates and this week, we expect him to be out there.” What Is Jalen Hurts’ Career Record Against Los Angeles Rams? (athlonsports) “Heading into Week 4, Hurts has played against the Rams four times as a starter for Philadelphia and he boasts a 4-0 record in those games. Hurts won his first start against the Rams in October of 2023 in a 23-13 Eagles victory. He threw for 303 yards, 1 TD and 1 interception in that game, while also adding 72 rushing yards and another TD with his legs.“ Rams special teams coach backs Xavier Smith but admits he must improve (ramswire) “Ventrone’s group brought in a new long snapper, Joe Cardona, and added linebacker Grant Stuard to assist with their punt and kick coverage. The Rams chose to stick with Xavier Smith at returner, despite his muffed punts in the NFC Championship Game. In 2026, results have varied, and on Thursday, Ventrone spoke about Smith’s work. Calling it for what it was, Ventrone said Smith has been inconsistent and needs to do a better job of tracking and fielding punts. However, Ventrone also made it clear that Smith is still the guy moving forward.“ Sportsbook Insiders: Examining the Latest Super Bowl Odds Movement; Why Rams Remain Highly Rated (si.com) “After all, they’ve lost to two contenders in San Francisco and Denver and have fallen to third in the odds to win their own division. Going to the Super Bowl – never mind winning it – out of a wild card spot won’t be easy, but that’s the path the Rams may have to take in 2026. Sports Illustrated recently spoke to several oddsmakers about the Rams’ outlook – and their latest Super Bowl odds – to see if they’re still viewed as the best team in the NFL. “The Rams are currently still our highest power rated team, but the gap has narrowed significantly since preseason,” a FanDuel Trader told Sports Illustrated. “Once they get Puka and Myles Garrett back, they should regain a healthy lead as our highest rated team.” Rams’ Week 4 clash vs. Eagles could have pivotal playoff implications later (ramblinfan) “While still early, LA’s division odds are shrinking fast. 3-0 San Francisco and 2-1 Seattle lead the NFC West. Both have easier schedules. Further complicating the climb, the Horns have dealt with constant injuries in the first three games, including many to key starters. Judging where things stand now, they will most likely need to navigate the Wild Card route through the playoffs. Knowing this, games against NFC opponents grow in importance. A Week 2 victory over the Giants was a step in the right direction. Beating the Eagles would be even better.“ Evan Silva’s Matchups: Rams at Eagles (establishthefun) “The Rams’ unprecedented early-season travel schedule rolls on, following up a Sunday night road game in Denver with a cross-country trip to Philadelphia. Matthew Stafford more than made things work sans top WR Puka Nacua (hip) in each of the last two games, notching Weeks 2-3 fantasy finishes of QB5 (vs. NYG) and QB6 (@ DEN). Nacua’s expected return heightens Stafford’s ceiling, while Bears third-stringer Case Keenum ’s picking apart of Philly last Monday night further inspires confidence in the NFL’s reigning MVP. … Blake Corum isn’t going away as a change-of-pace back, but Kyren Williams distanced himself in a high-efficiency Week 3 performance at Denver, out-snapping Corum 61 to 25 and out-touching him 21 to 8. Sean McVay is understandably more willing to lean on Williams in hostile environments, which Philadelphia obviously presents. Williams’ every-week RB1 value is set in stone. Corum remains a mere bench stash, albeit a still-exciting one.“ Los Angeles Rams vs. Philadelphia Eagles NFL Pro Week 4 Preview (nfl.com) “Brett Kollmann and Trevor Sikkema deep dive into the Rams vs. Eagles matchup with key Next Gen Stats insights from NFL Pro.” Rams’ Puka Nacua listed as limited at practice, but his update is better than that (sports.yahoo) “”Rams-Eagles injury report for Thursday. Puka Nacua said he was a full participant today, but he’s officially listed as ‘limited,'” Grosbard posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter. Los Angeles has looked efficient on offense under coach Sean McVay . Davante Adams expectedly handled the air attack slack in Nacua’s absence. But fans know this system is at its most explosive best with Nacua inside the huddle. Yet this offense became turnover prone against the Broncos. Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga stepped in front of two errant Matthew Stafford passes: One that handed Denver a 23-19 lead on a pick six, then the second to seal the win at Empower Field.“ Comment of the Day: “Honest conversations about AD and Garrett would probably suggest that we won’t get a lot from either. Garrett could still pay off down the line, but this is looking like a very sad return for the Ram legend. Things can change, but it doesn’t look good. That said, if the O can stay healthy and peak, we can at least get back to last year with a leaky defense and a high powered offense. No reason that can’t happen. Adams seems MUCH MORE locked in w/ Stafford, and if Puka is getting right, that’s dynamic. TEs when healthy are a solid committee, and our backfield is productive.” -Dr.Ram Feedpost of the Day:
author: Danny Stone

title: Rams Week 4 injury report: Terrance Ferguson expected to miss Sunday’s game
summary: Terrance Ferguson sustained a medial ankle sprain during Week 3 against the Denver Broncos and is expected to miss the upcoming game against the Philadelphia Eagles, according to Sean McVay. While it is a setback for the second-year tight end, it opens the door for rookie Max Klare. With injuries at the position, does it […]
full_text: Terrance Ferguson sustained a medial ankle sprain during Week 3 against the Denver Broncos and is expected to miss the upcoming game against the Philadelphia Eagles , according to Sean McVay. While it is a setback for the second-year tight end, it opens the door for rookie Max Klare. With injuries at the position, does it mean Klare is in for a bigger role? Acording to McVay, it does. Per Blaine Grisak of SI: “It certainly does,” said Sean McVay. “This week will represent an opportunity for him to be able to get some reps and maybe get some good game-time action for us.” Week 4 Injury Designations: Puka Nacua, listed as limited on Thursday, is expected to play: “I do, yeah,” McVay said. “Had a good workout on uh on Sunday and um you know good walkthrough just now and so um excited to be able to have him back.” Nacua was initially injured during training camp, as he suffered a groin injury or psoas injury. This turned into a hip ailment, that has now kept him out of both Week 2 and Week 3. Kamren Kinchens will miss another week with his hamstring issue. This will be his third game in a row since injuring the hamstring in Week 1. Jaylen Watson dislocated his shoulder against Denver on Sunday an d is expected to be out. His absence in the second half of that game illustrated just how little depth the Rams have in the defensive backfield. The Broncos put up 30 points in the half after being shut out in the first. Colby Parkinson suffered an AC joint sprain in his shoulder in the Denver game. Parkinson did not practice today and may be a game-time decision. Josh Wallace was limited due to a shoulder injury. His game status should be released Friday, but it should be noted that he played last week until the end of the game. Aaron Donald did not practice for the second day in a row with a sore back and is listed as questionable. McVay offered more updates on Donald, stating that he is dealing with a back injury. When pressed further, the Rams head coach said he did not want to say whether or not the defensive end would miss the game . “I wouldn’t want to say anything, you know, of that nature yet, but uh I think um you know, the back’s a little bit sore,” McVay said of Donald. Nate Landman did not practice and is listed as questionable with a shoulder injury. Injury Timeline Week 1 (Sept. 10): Suffered the shoulder and thumb injury late in the season-opener against the San Francisco 49ers. Weeks 2 & 3: Listed as limited in practice leading up to matchups against the Giants and Broncos, though he successfully played through the pain in both contests. Week 4 (Current): Continues to be listed as limited on practice reports, though head coach Sean McVay has not indicated any threat to his availability for Sunday. Davante Adams and Poona Ford had a designated rest days, and Myles Garrett must remain on the IR for at least another week after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

title: Rams-Eagles: Trent McDuffie showing his worth
summary: The Los Angeles Rams (1-2) will travel to the east coast for the first time in the 2026 Regular Season for a Week 4 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles (2-1). The Rams are coming off of a disappointing finish in Week 3 Sunday Night Football where they lost 30-26 to the Denver Broncos. The Rams […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD,CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Trent McDuffie #22 of the Los Angeles Rams defends in coverage during an NFL football game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams (1-2) will travel to the east coast for the first time in the 2026 Regular Season for a Week 4 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles (2-1). The Rams are coming off of a disappointing finish in Week 3 Sunday Night Football where they lost 30-26 to the Denver Broncos. The Rams controlled the majority of the contest until collapsing in the 3rd quarter due to questionable officiating and special teams woes. The Rams will look to right their course in Week 4; relying on key pieces as they try to work their way back to .500 on the season. What strengths do they have going into their matchup with Philly? Here’s a look at the two teams… QUARTERBACK Matthew Stafford is one of the best pure passers of all time. Jalen Hurts is anything but comfortable working as a drop back passer. Look no further than Hurts last 32 games… 🚨 #Eagles Jalen Hurts has thrown for 300+ passing yards ONE TIME in his last 32 games. pic.twitter.com/qApj8E7Ms0 — NFL Rumors (@nflrums) September 30, 2026 SKILL PLAYERS With the expected return of Puka Nacua, the Rams get a huge boost to their offense which allows Davante Adams to play a #2 role. With Kyren Williams and Blake Corum working as a tandem, the Rams skill players outweigh Saquon Barkley, Devonta Smith, and Makai Lemon. OFFENSIVE LINE The Rams offensive line has been really good through three weeks. Coleman Shelton is graded as the No. 1 center in all of football, 73.3, according to Pro Football Focus (PFF) . Jackson and Avila both grade in the 70.0s. The Eagles line has allowed 8 sacks in 3 games; having played the Commanders, Titans, and Bears. They are without Landon Dickerson leaving their interior susceptible. DEFENSIVE LINE Both the Rams and Eagles defensive lines have underachieved through three weeks. Aaron Donald, Kobie Turner, and Braden Fiske combine for 0 sacks, while Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Jonathan Greenard combine for 1 sack. The Rams defensive line has been pretty stout against the run outside of the 2nd half of football in Australia. The Eagles paid Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, & Jonathan Greenard a combined $328 million this offseason They have totaled 1 sack through 3 weeks pic.twitter.com/MCS5BOfouN — Underdog (@Underdog) September 29, 2026 SECONDARY Originally, I had given the Eagles the upperhand but after digging deeper the Rams have the better defensive backs. Trent McDuffie and Quentin Lake have been two of the best secondary players in all of football. The only CBs to be targeted multiple times in man coverage and have a 0.0 passer rating allowed this season Trent McDuffie Travis Hunter pic.twitter.com/rQlgHKWMjq — PFF (@PFF) September 29, 2026 Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean, and Tariq Woolen are a strong trio of cornerbacks but they haven’t had the strongest start to the 2026 season. SPECIAL TEAMS The Rams will probably never be favored in this category except for maybe when they play the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. COACHING This game isn’t between Sean McVay and Nick Sirianni. It’s between Sean McVay and Vic Fangio. And then whether Chris Shula can keep Sean Mannion’s offense inconsistent. If Sean McVay sticks to running the ball enough, Rams will walk away with a win.
author: Steven Ridings

title: 5Qs, 5As with Bleeding Green Nation: How is Jalen Hurts faring with yet another new OC?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams take on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 for the fourth straight season. Los Angeles is searching not only for its first win over the Eagles since the 2020 campaign, but also for its first win over Philly with Nick Sirianni at the helm. Ahead of an important matchup between NFC […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams take on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 for the fourth straight season. Los Angeles is searching not only for its first win over the Eagles since the 2020 campaign, but also for its first win over Philly with Nick Sirianni at the helm. Ahead of an important matchup between NFC contenders who suffered bad losses last week, I spoke with Brandon Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation to get the inside scoop on Jalen Hurts working with yet another new offensive coordinator, Vic Fangio’s defense and more. Q – The Eagles were dreadful on offense against the Bears on Monday night, getting shut out in the second half of the 27-7 loss. Philadelphia has been inconsistent offensively since last year. With new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion in tow, what potential signs of life are you seeing from the unit, and where must they improve? A – The Eagles are the only NFL team yet to score points in the first quarter. A season after leading the league in three-and-out percentage, no offense has a worse mark in that category in the second halves of games this season. And, yet, it’s clearly not ALL bad. The Eagles wouldn’t have been able to win two games if that was the case. Jalen Hurts carried the offense in the Eagles’ first two games. He also had a good first half against the Bears before falling off the rest of the night. While it’s always encouraging to see the quarterback play well, the problem is that they were relying on him too much. And by that I mean they were consistently getting into third-and-longs and then asking Hurts to bail them out by making high-leverage plays over and over. Again, it’s good that Hurts was able to do that, but it’s just not a sustainable way to go about playing offense. The Eagles’ run game did show some promise in the first half against Chicago before also falling off as the team fell behind the Bears on the scoreboard. Saquon Barkley still looks pretty spry, so, maybe there’s hope this unit can get back on track. Or maybe the lack of schematic cohesion continues to be a problem. BGN film guru Jonny Page noted that it looks like the Eagles are running two separate offenses. Q – Quarterback Jalen Hurts received a ton of criticism this offseason for his leadership approach. Despite winning a Super Bowl, he still cannot shake the negativity. Mannion is Hurts’ sixth OC in the NFL, so how are those two clicking three games into their partnership? A – As noted above, Hurts carried the offense over the first two weeks. He was especially crucial in the Eagles’ win over the Titans, leading a game-winning 65-yard touchdown drive. He finished with a pretty rough box score against the Bears. But look at his first half numbers from that game: 10/13, 111 yards (8.5 average), 0 TD, 0 INT, 101.8 passer rating … two carries, two yards, one rushing touchdown. Also, Hurts was robbed of the opportunity for another touchdown when the concussion spotter pulled him off the field and took a long time to clear him (Nick Sirianni calling a timeout could’ve been nice). Before Hurts could return to the game, Andy Dalton threw an interception directly to a safety in the end zone. So, he’s been good more often than not this season. Not sure exactly how to divvy up the credit here, I typically lean towards the player deserving most of it. But Mannion probably deserves some as well; he’s been very hands-on with Hurts since joining the Eagles. The offense still has much to figure out. For now, the quarterback playing well is a reason for optimism. Q – Vic Fangio’s defense had a rough showing in primetime as Bears backup QB Case Keenum completed over 70% of his passes with three total touchdowns in his first start since 2023. How do Matthew Stafford and company follow Chicago’s blueprint and come away with a much-needed win in Week 4? A – Nice try! I refuse to answer since Sean McVay is going to read this. OK, probably not. I don’t know if there’s a blueprint as much as Ben Johnson is just a really great offensive mind and he was clearly one step ahead of Fangio all night long, just like he was when the Eagles hosted the Bears last year. I’m guessing Rams fans are well aware that McVay is 0-4 against Fangio. But it’s not like the Rams haven’t had any success against him. They produced 402 yards of offense against him in their playoff loss in January 2025. They put up 356 yards against his defense last season. If I’m the Rams, I’m looking to get rid of the ball quick (which Case Keenum did) and try to exploit the Eagles’ safeties. That’s a weak point on this defense. I would not be throwing towards Quinyon Mitchell, who’s very much a lockdown corner. Q – Philly didn’t come close to defending their Super Bowl crown in 2025, given they lost in the Wild Card Round. Despite fielding one of the league’s top rosters, there’s still a lot of uncertainty about this team. How do you anticipate the rest of their season will play out? A – The Eagles are 2-1 but they’re not exactly inspiring a ton of confidence right now. They’re not as strong in the trenches as they’ve been in the past, despite big investments in the lines. Their offense is overly reliant on the quarterback making plays instead of being a well-oiled machine. The defense is struggling to live up to lofty expectations. Their winning record is disguising a team that’s looking like a below average group at this point in time: Entering Week 4, the Eagles rank 20th in point differential 20th in offensive EPA/play 20th in defensive success rate 22nd in DVOA 24th in defensive EPA/play 28th in offensive success rate — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 30, 2026 How the Eagles compare to other teams in terms of EPA through 3 games (via RBDSM) pic.twitter.com/sF400ohVPG — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 30, 2026 Are they hopeless? Of course not. This team has earned some level of benefit of the doubt. They’ve never not made the playoffs since the Jalen Hurts/Nick Sirianni era began in 2021. They’re coming off back-to-back NFC East title wins, which previously hadn’t been accomplished by any team in this division since 2004. In 2024, things were looking bleak for the Eagles after a 2-2 start. They got absolutely dominated by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 4 of that season … before then going on a massive run to win Super Bowl LIX. Just because it happened then doesn’t mean they’re definitely going to be OK this year. It’s entirely possible they’re just not a very good team. I’m not yet ready to move off my preseason prediction that they’ll win around 11 games. Q – Last week, Mile High Report asked Rams fans what they thought about the “super team” moniker. What is a separate question you have for the fanbase? A – Hey, I like the framing you used here. Here’s my question for Turf Show Times readers, who are hopefully using the SB Nation app … * Let’s say Nick Sirianni and Sean McVay swapped places. What would your expectations be for the Eagles and the Rams this season? Bonus: You didn’t ask for a game prediction but I’d like to share one anyway. The Eagles are underdogs in this game. They’re 0-5 straight up and 1-4 against the spread as home dogs since 2021. The Eagles will make this game more competitive than they did against the Bears on Monday night. But the Rams will finally get a win at The Linc. Final score: Eagles 24, Rams 28.
author: Evan Craig

title: The Rams have a right-side problem
summary: It’s a good thing that Matthew Stafford isn’t left-handed, because the right side of the L.A. Rams offensive line has had the worst pass protection duo in the league through three weeks. Kevin Dotson’s name has been the first one proposed as having a pass protection issue this season, and by some accounts he had […]
full_text: It’s a good thing that Matthew Stafford isn’t left-handed, because the right side of the L.A. Rams offensive line has had the worst pass protection duo in the league through three weeks. Kevin Dotson’s name has been the first one proposed as having a pass protection issue this season , and by some accounts he had the worst performance of any Rams offensive player against the Broncos. On this play against Denver’s elite defensive tackle Zach Allen, you can see that Dotson may as well not exist: Zach Allen's hand technique is so fun to watch. pic.twitter.com/RcXHfqvqlZ — Lance Sanderson (@LanceS_MHH) September 28, 2026 Allen practically waves him away like a cloud of smoke and is immediately barreling down on Stafford. Dotson has allowed a pressure on over 8% of his pass blocking reps this season, according to PFF. One play doesn’t make a player bad, and certainly I think clips like the one get overblown and taken out of context. But if I’m Dotson or Dotson’s agent, knowing that free agency is on the horizon in 2027, I know that what teams are going to be looking at is whatever data and film that they have readily available. The data hasn’t been in Dotson’s favor yet this season, including this chart: According to this, Dotson has the sixth-worst successful pass block rate among all guards in the NFL. How often Guards have been 1-on-1 in pass blocking and how their percentile grade fulfilling their assignment pic.twitter.com/mRT7NDFcCm — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) October 1, 2026 PFF has him ranked 66th out of 72 in pass protection. No matter how good the opponents are that Dotson has had to deal with, like Allen who could be an All-Pro, it would be good for the Rams guard to start stacking positive games in the future. Especially given that he may not be getting as much help from his right as he would like to have. #Rams Week 3 Bottom 5 offense PFF scores Colby Parkinson – 54.1 Xavier Smith – 52.8 Jordan Whittington – 52.2 Blake Corum – 49.8 Kevin Dotson – 37.9 — East Coast Rams Pod (@EastCoastRams) September 28, 2026 Warren McClendon is ranked 57th out of 70 tackles in pass protection. Here in the tackles chart, he is ranked in the bottom-third for successful pass block reps: Offensive line is a weak link system where one mistake in pass blocking can create pressure to blow up a play. A look at how often Offensive Tackles are left on islands and their percentile Successful Block rate when left on an island pic.twitter.com/BZCWtNF2cy — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) September 30, 2026 According to PFF, McClendon has allowed six QB hits, which is the most by any tackle in the NFL through three games. McClendon was blamed for seven pressures and two penalties against Denver . Between McClendon and Dotson, just those two have allowed 38-year-old Stafford to be hit nine times in three games. Stafford was sacked four times by the Broncos, and the only reason he’s probably not sacked at a higher rate generally is thanks to his experience of sensing pressure and getting the ball out quickly. Stafford may be doing more work to keep himself healthy than the right side of his offensive line. Zach Allen was on fire down the stretch. This was on three consecutive plays! pic.twitter.com/L0vsGEaGUp — Lance Sanderson (@LanceS_MHH) September 28, 2026 So what are the Rams going to do about it? Rookie Keagen Trost is the most interesting name to keep an eye on this season, but he is on short-term IR right now. He is eligible to return in Week 5, although it isn’t likely that Trost is going to be on the active gameday roster any time soon unless a player gets injured. Trost may go the entire season without playing, but his main objective by the team has always been to be ready for 2027. Dotson, McClendon, Coleman Shelton, and Steve Avila are all free agents. Re-signing all four is a longshot, and at this rate re-signing Dotson for the amount of money he probably wants to command is unlikely. Dotson had been one of the highest-paid guards in the NFL but that doesn’t seem fair anymore. Avila is also younger, and since he’s performing better seems to be a better bet for where some of L.A.‘s offensive line budget will go next. McClendon is a tougher choice because right tackles are harder to find. Plus, it’s not as though A.J. Jackson is great on the field or totally reliable as a person. There’s just only so many resources that the Rams can throw at the offensive line, between trade assets and money, and they already spent a lot of next year’s on acquiring Myles Garrett. There won’t be a first-round pick spent on an offensive lineman in 2027 since L.A. doesn’t have one. They spent a lot of their money this year on Aaron Donald and Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson and Garrett. So Dotson and McClendon will need to step up. Perhaps this is just a minor blip on the radar . It could be just that . However, one thing about radar blips: You’d be stupid to not keep track of where they end up.

title: Our first month with an app broke our commenting records
summary: A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it.  The goal with this app was to make it easier to join […]
full_text: (Photo by Rob Carr/Getty Images) | Getty Images A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it. The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center. The results so far are encouraging. In fact, it’s helped us set a new all-time record for comments this month across all of SB Nation’s communities, and I want to thank you for that. One of the most exciting new features is the game chat. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you’re not going to find anywhere else. We also wanted to elevate the community’s contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we’ve set single-day commenting records three different times since the season started. And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there’s an option at the top to do that. So, one month in, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven’t checked it out, you can get it for iOs or Android . And if you’re not an app user, that’s OK! We’re glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: NFL says DPI call against Rams in Week 3 was unnecessary
summary: Sean McVay reports the NFL told him that the pass interference call against Josh Wallace on Sunday night football against the Denver Broncos shouldn’t have been called. Simple as that. Except it was called, and the Rams basically sit at 1-2 instead of 2-1 because of it. Well, that call, a blown 16-point lead and […]
full_text: Sean McVay reports the NFL told him that the pass interference call against Josh Wallace on Sunday night football against the Denver Broncos shouldn’t have been called. Simple as that. Except it was called, and the Rams basically sit at 1-2 instead of 2-1 because of it. Well, that call, a blown 16-point lead and some other mistakes so to speak caused the 1-2 mark, but don’t get hung up on the details. What matters is trying to win the next game. That’s the NFL. Whatever your record is, just win the next game. The Rams didn’t do that last Sunday. Everyone will see how they do this Sunday. NFL Delivers Unfortunate Reality Check for Los Angeles Rams (heavy.com) “It is a call that Denver Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant, with whom Wallace was accused of interfering, said certainly occurred, but also admitted that he sold “just enough” to give his side the best opportunity to secure a flag. It worked, but it should not have, according to the league and Rams head coach Sean McVay. “McVay said the NFL told him that Josh Wallace should not have been flagged for pass interference,” The Athletic’s Nate Atkins posted on X on September 30.“ NFL admits Rams shouldn’t have been called for DPI vs. Broncos (ramswire) “McVay was visibly upset on the broadcast, seemingly saying, “You can’t call that.” NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay sided with the defense , saying he didn’t think Wallace’s contact warranted a flag. Bryant later admitted he helped the call along . “I did sell it just enough,” he said, though he added that Wallace gave him “a little nudge.” No one’s coming to rescue the Rams, so they’ll have to help themselves (starting now) (ramblifan) “Some well-meaning folks are trying to prop up fans’ hopes. But it could just have the opposite effect. Rather than rally Rams fans, it motivates future foes to stop the hype. And at 1-2, the Horns do not need already tough opponents circling their calendars. Losses need not be glossed over , nor should they be. NFL athletes are not fans of being anointed. True competitors want to earn their success, respect, and accompanying accolades. So no, neither players nor coaches need to soften the blow. Losing should hurt. It’s that pain that drives elite players to higher heights. Finding groove will take time, but Rams must begin trending in right direction The Rams have no choice but to focus on their next opponent on a week-by-week basis. Their record now won’t matter if they finish at 15-2.“ Rams star Puka Nacua expected to return vs Eagles (byucougarwire) “That is back-to-back games that Nacua has missed. He also sat out the game against the New York Giants. Fantasy football owners and Rams fans have a reason to rejoice. Head coach Sean McVay has good news about Nacua’s status for this week’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Nacua returned to practice on Wednesday with an injury designation of “limited,” but McVay expects his star wide receiver to play against the Eagles this week.“ Film Room: How Zach Allen Turned the Tide vs. Rams (si.com) “Allen has been on the outside of the discussion among Denver’s defensive playmakers for a few seasons now, despite his production and accolades. Pat Surtain II has already won Defensive Player of the Year, and Nik Bonitto is one of the best edge rushers in the league. They get a lot of attention, and understandably so. What doesn’t make sense is how little attention Allen gets on a national stage as one of the best interior defensive linemen in the game. He was a one-man wrecking crew against the Rams. Despite a nondescript start, Allen led the team with seven total pressures, three quarterback hits, and a sack. What he did in the second half should be plastered across the media landscape, as he spearheaded a pressure package that got to and rattled Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford at will.“ Puka Nacua’s Rams Return Comes Just in Time for Eagles Showdown (sports.yahoo) “Nacua was still listed as limited in practice Wednesday, September 30th, though head coach Sean McVay said Nacua is expected to play. Why the Rams are bringing Nacua back Rather than play him through some discomfort, the Rams opted to sit Nacua and give him time to heal, since the season is still very young.“ Rams Need More From Linebacker Nate Landman Amid Concerning Decline (sports.yahoo) “Landman on a one-year deal for $11 million was great value. Since signing his extension, Landman’s level of play has dropped off significantly and has been much closer to what it was throughout his career with the Atlanta Falcons . Landman Hasn’t Sustained His Early Success From Week 1 to Week 11 last year, Landman was PFF’s 20th-ranked linebacker and forced four fumbles. He had four games with 10 or more tackles and a missed tackle rate of just 10.2 percent. From Week 12 until the end of the season, he was PFF’s 33rd-ranked linebacker and did not force a single fumble. He had three games with 10 or more tackles, two of which came in the playoffs, and had a 19.1 percent missed tackle rate.“ NFL Week 4 Betting Report: Books Being Flooded With Rams Money (foxsports) “Here’s how you know that the NFL drives the American sports betting bus: Steelers vs. Browns, which is not exactly a marquee matchup, will still draw plenty of eyeballs and action from the public betting masses. “The NFL is still king,” Caesars Sports head of football trading Joey Feazel said. “Even as much as we complain about some of these Thursday night games, it’s still the NFL. We’re still all watching, and it’ll still be bet on.” Los Angeles Rams at Philadelphia Eagles: How to watch, listen to and live stream Sunday Night Football Week 4 (therams.com) “The Rams and Eagles last met in Week 3 last season on Sept. 21, 2025, a narrow 33-26 win for the Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 196 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. Running back Kyren Williams had 94 rushing yards on 20 carries, and 18 receiving yards with a receiving touchdown. Wide receiver Puka Nacua led the team with 11 receptions for 112 yards while Davante Adams added 56 yards and a touchdown. Defensively, four different players recorded a sack, including outside linebacker Byron Young who had six total tackles and three for loss. Safety Kam Curl led the team with nine total tackles and safety Quentin Lake had six total tackles with four passes defended. Kickoff for Sunday’s game at Lincoln Financial Field is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. pacific time on FOX.“ Brian Allen reflects on his draft call, winning Super Bowl LVI, blocking Aaron Donald & more | Rams Iconic (rams.com) “D’Marco Farr sits down with former Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Brian Allen on this live episode of Rams Iconic. Watch him reflect on the 2018 NFL Draft, winning Super Bowl LVI, trying to block defensive end Aaron Donald & more.” Comment of the Day: “OBJ? Let’s see… he’s been a non-factor/cut for the last five years. Why in God’s name does anyone think he’d move the needle for the Rams? Still pissed about that PI call… the soft-ass “hands to the face” call as well. Wallace made a great defensive play and the Rams had a 3rd down stop taken away. title: Resilience powering the Raiders’ renaissance thus far in 2026 campaign
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-0 to start the 2026 campaign and, as one of the — if not biggest — surprise teams in the league, the memes popping up are hilarious. Like this one regarding the unbeaten AFC teams that include: The Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, and the Silver & Black. But Klint […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-0 to start the 2026 campaign and, as one of the — if not biggest — surprise teams in the league, the memes popping up are hilarious. Like this one regarding the unbeaten AFC teams that include: The Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, and the Silver & Black . But Klint Kubiak’s surging football team is indeed, no laughing matter. Las Vegas entered the new year with severely low expectations coming off a 3-14 season that gave the team the No. 1 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft, which ended up being Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza. General manager John Spytek was flush with coin and spent the cap space wisely by landing high-priced free agents like center Tyler Linderbaum and linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker, to name a few. But despite the influx in talent in both free agency and the draft, expectations remained tempered with analytics models giving the Raiders a 6.7 percent chance of starting 3-0. After topping the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers to start the season, caveats popped up immediately. Such as the lowly Dolphins and listless Chargers were cupcakes and of course the Raiders beating them was going to happen — dismissive in nature. Week 3, however, provided a more sound litmus test against the equally surging Saints and things did look dire as Las Vegas fell very much behind against New Orleans — all of which was their own doing. And the biggest reason why this rendition of the Raiders came back to drop the Saints: Complementary football. “We don’t win the game without those four turnovers in the fourth quarter,” Kubiak said during his Monday media session. “That was impressive how they kept getting the ball back for us on offense, and it just really changed the whole game. And again, that’s a big part of winning and losing, is protecting the ball and taking the ball away. So, three games into it, long season to go, and every week’s a new challenge. We’re starting from scratch now back for Kansas City.” The comeback road win was the latest example of Kubiak and Co. delivering a resounding double-fisted middle finger to said projections and naysayers, alike. Resilience on display. #LVvsNO | #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/UiBCFfcvJk — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) September 28, 2026 Complementary football — a fleeting thing for previous Raiders regimes — is the standout item that’s giving Las Vegas the resilience. And that’s something Kubiak was keen to learn about his football team. “Well, I think that the number one thing is you don’t really get to find out about somebody until the chips are down and their back’s against the wall. So, our backs were against the wall yesterday, down two scores,” Kubiak said. “So, we found out a lot about guys’ resilience and toughness because everything’s fine if you’re up two scores at the end of the game. But what do you do when you’re down two scores?” Rising to the occasion was a foreign concept for the Raiders variants of year’s past and the rookie head coach alongside his coaching staff are flipping that narrative. As Kubiak highlighted immediately after the victory against the Saints, the four fourth-quarter takeaways was the catalyst to the turn around. With his offense getting the ball back after a trio of fumbles and an interception, Kubiak wasn’t going to let that go to waste. He dialed up plays that resulted in four-yard touchdown passes from veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins to wide receiver Cody White and Brock Bowers, in respective drives which vaulted Las Vegas ahead 35-27. And the final forced fumble — by Dean — helped the Silver & Black slam the door shut on the Saints. The outstanding fourth-quarter performance by defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s defense boosts the team’s takeaway total to nine — which leads the league, by the way. The Carolina Panthers are second with seven takeaways on the young season. (For reference: The Raiders had 16 total takeaways in 2025, good for 24th in the league). Leonard — a rookie coach himself as defensive boss — is proving the “attacking defense” he spoke about this offseason wasn’t just talk. Remarkably, the Raiders defense is aggressive and putting opposing offenses on its heels without being a blitz-heavy unit. Las Vegas has the eighth lowest blitz rate in the league at 19.5 percent (22 blitzes called), according to Pro Football Reference. The Minnesota Vikings, who are atop the league and on a different spectrum altogether, pace the NFL with a 66.4 percent rate on 89 total blitzes called. “I think just the whole staff — the whole defensive staff — are doing a great job getting on the same page with each other. And nothing was perfect yesterday but found a way to get it done,” Kubiak said when asked about Leonard’s defense. “Great communication on the sideline, and just a credit to the players for finishing the game four turnovers, that was the game right there.” Autumn has been kind to the @Raiders 🏴‍☠️ pic.twitter.com/wFgrkuj21n — Inside the NFL (@insidetheNFL) September 29, 2026 But as Kubiak noted above, Week 4 brings the Chiefs to town. And the battle of the 3-0 AFC West teams is set be one of the best matchups this Sunday. That contest is the first of nine grueling games for Las Vegas before the team’s bye week after a November 29 road game against the Cleveland Browns. There’s no looking ahead for Kubiak and Co., but following the Chiefs, the Raiders go on the road to face the New England Patriots, return home to face the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams in back-to-back weeks, to close out the month of October. So it was only natural Kubiak was asked about the importance of momentum as the team gets ready for tough opponents. “Yeah, they all are important. Every game, it’s a every week you’re just focused on that one opponent,” Kubiak responded. “When it’s a division opponent, you know there’s even more on the line.” There’s indeed a Raiders renaissance happening and it’s being led by two rookie coaches: Kubiak at 39 years old and Leonard at 41 years old. It’s a long season ahead and we’ll learn even more about these particular Raiders come this Sunday against the Chiefs and beyond. There will surely be the lows this season as the highs have been both impressive and surprising. Defeat will come at some point. And how Kubiak and Co. responds to that will be intriguing. If it’s like anything we’ve seen from the in-game response to adversity, word to the wise: Be prepared to be impressed — again.
author: Ray Aspuria

full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders head into a Week 4 showdown at home against the Kansas City Chiefs with unbeaten records and the top spot in the division on the line. In an unheralded primetime matchup in the NFL’s late window, many fans will be upset because this game won’t be nationally televised. Despite the Raiders surprising hot start and quest to go from worst to first in 2026. The Chiefs open as -4.5 favorites but even they realize they are in for a dogfight against the Raiders. This matchup has actually been far more exciting in recent years than it has been. With the Chiefs finishing the 2025 season with a loss to the then-league-worst Raiders. However, this group isn’t those Raiders. As challenges and measuring-stick games go, this week is gargantuan. Calling it huge doesn’t do it justice. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak may not be into accepting anyone’s flowers but everything is different about the 2026 Raiders. Even though the majority of the roster remains the same. These guys are tough and have answered every challenge to this point. Displaying signs of growth that indicate they aren’t anywhere near the ceiling of their own potential. On paper, these teams are evenly matched. One might even surmise the Raiders are the better team. The Chiefs have the bigger star power at certain positions, but the Raiders have taken them to the woodshed and put belts to ass before. It’s got all the makings of a barn-burning, slobber-knocking heavyweight fight. At the end of it we will have an even better idea of just how for real the Raiders really are.
