title: Raider killer Travis Kelce looks reborn
summary: When Travis Kelce walked off the Allegiant Stadium field after the final game of the 2025 season last January, many people thought that would be the end of his eventual Pro Football Hall of Fame career. It was a fitting ending because Kelce has dominated against the Raiders over the years. In the end, though, […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Travis Kelce walked off the Allegiant Stadium field after the final game of the 2025 season last January, many people thought that would be the end of his eventual Pro Football Hall of Fame career. It was a fitting ending because Kelce has dominated against the Raiders over the years. In the end, though, Kelce decided to come back for the 2026 season. And, bad news for the Raiders. He looks like vintage Kelce through three games. After showing sign of decline past couple of seasons, Kelce, who turns 37 Monday, looks refreshed and he and Chiefs’ quarterback Patrick Mahomes are performing at a high level together again. Through three games, Kelce has 14 catches on 18 targets for 231 yards and two touchdowns for the 3-0 Chiefs. Stopping Kelce will be crucial for the Raiders Sunday. And we all know Kelce loves playing against the Raiders and in Las Vegas. The Raiders beat the Chiefs in Las Vegas last season without Mahomes. It was the Chiefs’ first loss in Allegiant Stadium. According to Statsmuse.com , Kelce has 133 receptions for 1,648 yards and 12 touchdowns in 24 games against the Raiders. Stopping Kelce from adding big numbers to his Raiders total will be a key to the game.

title: Miami Dolphins vs. Minnesota Vikings: Three reasons the Dolphins can win, lose in Week 4
summary: The Miami Dolphins show signs of life.  They hung with the Kansas City Chiefs for most of the game and could have been in contention for a win without penalties, mistakes, and other issues young teams need to clean up.  This week, the Dolphins face the 3-0 Vikings, making Miami the 2nd team in NFL […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the Kansas City Chiefs during the first quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Alie Skowronski/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins show signs of life. They hung with the Kansas City Chiefs for most of the game and could have been in contention for a win without penalties, mistakes, and other issues young teams need to clean up. This week, the Dolphins face the 3-0 Vikings, making Miami the 2nd team in NFL history and the 1st since 1986 to have their first 4 opponents go undefeated (hat tip to Urthling). Talk about a brutal schedule. Maybe we could have foreseen the Chiefs and Niners, but the Raiders and Vikings are a surprising 3-0. Anyway, this game is not without its own glimmers of hope. Reasons for hope Miami’s offense is showing some potential The Chiefs’ defense generally doesn’t get much media attention because all the focus is on quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the offense. But their defense is top 5 or top 10 in total yards allowed (4th), passing yards allowed (6th), rushing yards allowed (10th), and in scoring defense (3rd). Miami was expected to struggle offensively, despite being at home. It was supposed to be even worse when they lost Achane to injury. However, the Dolphins managed 329 yards of offense, including some explosive plays, and for the first time this season, they didn’t have a single 3-and-out… unless you wanna count the 3-play drive to end the game when it didn’t matter. They moved the ball without Douglas and Achane for all or most of the game. Now, it wasn’t all sunshine and rainbows. The Dolphins had 2 drives that ended in a turnover on downs. They also fumbled in scoring territory where at least a field goal was likely. The offense committed several penalties that set them back, and this team isn’t capable of consistently overcoming that. But they made progress and should keep developing as the season moves forward. Minnesota’s offense is bad Despite everything I just wrote, the Dolphins’ offense is still bad. At least in terms of scoring. They are averaging 12 PPG and haven’t gotten over 13 points in any game. But in terms of yardage, they aren’t the worst. Their opponent this week IS the worst offense in this regard. The Vikings are dead last in total yards at 715, passing yards at 411, and are just above the Dolphins in rushing yards at 304 (tied for 16th; Miami is 20th at 295). The Vikings score more than the Dolphins, averaging 23.7 PPG. But they have faced the Bears (7th in scoring defense), Bucs (23rd in scoring defense), and the Packers (30th in scoring defense). The Dolphins have faced the Chiefs (3rd), 49ers (5th), and Raiders (8th). The Dolphins have faced the 6th, 10th, and 14th best passing defenses. The Vikings have faced the 11th-, 12th-, and 13th-best passing defenses. The Dolphins have faced the 10th, 15th, and 20th best run defenses. The Vikings have faced the 2nd, 21st, and 28th best run defenses. I could make other comparisons, like opponents’ pressure percentages and so on, but I think you can smell what The Earl is cooking here. As bad as the Dolphins offense has been, the Vikings have been similarly bad. If there was ever a game for a struggling secondary to have a chance… Miami’s defense is also showing some potential So far, the Dolphins have faced some tough offenses. They got their feet wet against the Raiders and Ashton Jeanty. They faced the juggernaut 49ers and their arsenal of weapons, then came home to face off against Mahomes and the league’s leading rusher. The Dolphins have faced the 2nd- and 3rd-ranked teams in scoring offenses this season. The Niners are averaging 32.7 PPG while the two AFCW teams are tied at 29.3. That is a LOT of scoring. Yet in Week 3, they held the Chiefs to 17 points until a late drive pushed them to 24. The Chiefs and Niners are tied for 6th in passing yards. I discussed the issues with the total number of incompletions Miami allowed, but they have faced tough opponents. In the last two games, the Dolphins have allowed less than 100 yards rushing, including just 88 total yards to the Chiefs, who have the league’s top rusher. They limited him to 70 yards on 18 carries – 3.9 YPC – including a 22-yard run. Meaning they held him to 48 yards on the other 17 carries – 2.8 YPC. That’s solid work against a guy who went over 100 yards in the previous 2 games. The Chiefs said they wanted to lighten his workload, but the other RB went 6 for 17. The passing defense still needs work, but instead of Purdy or Mahomes, they get the Murray/Wentz combo that is averaging 137 passing yards per game. Something will have to give here. The rookies are also stepping up. Miami also saw rookie CB Chris Johnson go untargeted by Mahomes all game. Rookie LB Jacob Rodriguez is tied for 7th in the league in combined tackles at 28 and has 3 TFLs, which is tied for 17th with several players. That is solid considering he doesn’t get sacks added to that total. He also generated a turnover this week with the INT and is now the leading favorite to win defensive rookie of the year. The Dolphins still haven’t recorded a sack but did manage to generate 8 pressures in this game (per PFR). Miami’s 3 previous opponents have lower-end pressure percentages, but now face Murray, who is pressured about as much as we have seen Willis get pressured. Could this be the game for the defense to get things right, build some confidence, and start to turn this ship around? Reasons for Concern Vikings still have weapons As fun as it is to discuss the Vikings’ potential offensive ineptitude, they still have a dynamic WR duo in Justin Jefferson (who may not play) and Jordan Addison, plus a good receiving TE in TJ Hockenson. They have Aaron Jones at RB, who is currently 12th in the league with 203 yards. Despite the emerging potential from the pass defense, they have still not forced more than 6 incompletions in the last 2 games. Part of that is a lack of pressure, and part of that is softer coverage. If either or both of those issues show up, the Vikings have more than enough talent on offense to make the Dolphins pay. The Vikings have also faced circumstances that could explain a lack of offensive production. They scored 39 points at home in week 1 but lost their starting QB in the 1st quarter. That generally puts a damper on the offense, even if the backup is good. That backup then had to travel to face a good Chicago team in week 2, the one top-ten scoring defense they have faced. Then they had to travel to Tampa Bay to face the 6th-ranked defense in yards allowed. One home game with injury issues and 2 road games. Now the Vikings have their starter back and will be playing at home against a defense that allows 80.3% of opponents’ passes to be completed and allows 28.7 PPG. Maybe the Vikings offense is the one that can help the Dolphins defense turn their ship around. Or maybe the Dolphins defense is the one for the Vikings offense to turn their ship around. On the road again The Dolphins are singing like Willie because they travel to face an opponent for the 3rd time in 4 games. Road games in the NFL are tough for anyone and even more so for a struggling team. The Vikings are more than a TD favorite, and ESPN’s matchup predictor gives Minnesota an 83.1% chance to win . For an offense that has struggled with pre-snap issues, they now have to go play in a raucous environment where noise will be a factor. Miami committed 8 penalties in week 1 and 7 penalties in week 2. In each game, 6 of those penalties were offensive. This issue can rear its ugly head again this week, and this offense cannot afford to get behind the sticks and in unfavorable down-and-distance situations because… Vikings defense and the Brian Flores factor I saved the worst for last because this has the potential to unravel any of the hope I mentioned. We’ll start with Flores. Everyone is…

title: Miami Dolphins offensive line review: Tracking the guards in Week 3
summary: The Miami Dolphins fell to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, dropping to 0-3 as they continue navigating a significant roster rebuild. While wins and losses matter, much of the focus in 2026 remains on the development of Miami’s young talent. That is especially true along the offensive line, where rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor […]
full_text: The Miami Dolphins fell to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, dropping to 0-3 as they continue navigating a significant roster rebuild. While wins and losses matter, much of the focus in 2026 remains on the development of Miami’s young talent. That is especially true along the offensive line, where rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor and second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea are important pieces of the team’s future. How are they performing this season? Each week, we take a closer look at the guards and what is being said about their most recent performance. Kadyn Proctor Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 1 71.2 79.0 63.4 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 2 62.0 72.4 39.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 57.5 51.1 71.3 Jonah Savaiinaea Game Snap Counts Penalties PFF Overall Grade PFF Run Blocking PFF Pass Protection 9/13, @ Raiders 59 (100%) 0 47.6 50.9 38.2 9/20, @ 49ers 56 (100%) 0 65.9 68.5 46.1 9/27, vs. Chiefs 73 (100%) 0 56.6 58.4 47.5 What We Learned The grades paint a mixed picture of Miami’s performance against Kansas City, but there were still encouraging signs from the Dolphins’ young guards. For the first time this season, Miami did not allow a sack, and on Ollie Gordon’s touchdown run , Kadyn Proctor executed an impressive pull to the left, sealing off Chiefs safety Jaden Hicks before helping escort (forcefully) Gordon into the end zone. While that play was a highlight, there is still room for growth in pass protection. Proctor and Jonah Savaiinaea were each charged with two pressures, while the offensive line surrendered nine hurries overall. Even so, Proctor showed improvement as a pass protector, earning a 71.3 pass-blocking grade from PFF after posting a 39.1 mark the previous week. The tracker will be updated each week throughout the season. For a more in-depth breakdown of Proctor’s and Savaiinaea’s performance, check out offensive line Coach Eric Smith’s film analysis of the game, which you can find on his YouTube channel, Focused on Fins .

summary: The Miami Dolphins visit the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday and will see plenty of familiar faces on the opposing sidelines. full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 13: Minnesota Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel (43) gets up to run with the ball after recovering a fumble he helped cause during the fourth quarter of a NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers on September 13, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis MN. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins visit the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday and will see plenty of familiar faces on the opposing sidelines. Vikings practice squad linebacker Kyle Van Noy played in Miami in 2020 while Minnesota’s coaching staff includes defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander, who played safety for the Dolphins in 2011 and was Miami’s defensive backs coach in 2020 and 2021; defensive assistant Charlie Frye was Miami’s quarterbacks coach in 2021; passing game coordinator Josh McCown was a training camp quarterback in 2008; assistant head coach Frank Smith was Miami’s offensive coordinator from 2022 through 2025; and Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell was a training camp quarterback for the Dolphins in 2011. Of course, Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores was the head coach for the Dolphins from 2019 through 2021. And perhaps the most recognizable person on the field for Dolphins fans, with his hair flowing out from under his helmet, will be linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel. AVG played for the Dolphins from 2019 through 2023, appearing in 73 games, including 42 starts, recording 2019 tackles, 17 sacks, two interceptions, seven passes defensed, three forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries, and two touchdowns. A 2019 fifth-round pick for Miami out of Wisconsin, Van Ginkel signed as a free agent with the Vikings in 2024, taking a fan favorite out of the Miami defense and reuniting him with Flores. Miami Dolphins on SI writer Alain Poupart took a look at the one who got away as Miami prepares to face the Vikings: Former Miami Dolphins safety Jevon Holland is off to a great start in his second season with the New York Giants and he was recognized Thursday as the NFC Defensive Player of the Month. He’s not, however, somebody the Dolphins should regret not having retained as a free agent two offseasons ago. Andrew Van Ginkel, who the Dolphins will face for the first time since he left when they take on the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, is an entirely different story… It was one thing to debate whether the Dolphins should have done whatever it took to keep former draft picks like Christian Wilkins, Robert Hunt and/or Holland instead of having them leave as free agents instead of spending big money on outsiders like Tyreek Hill and Jalen Ramsey, but the conversation should have been much simpler with Van Ginkel. summary: Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had a debut for the ages — nabbing five passes for 94 yards against the Las Vegas Raiders in week one. Unfortunately, the young player suffered an ankle injury in the fourth-quarter of Miami’s week two loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He was seen in a walking […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas (7) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had a debut for the ages — nabbing five passes for 94 yards against the Las Vegas Raiders in week one. Unfortunately, the young player suffered an ankle injury in the fourth-quarter of Miami’s week two loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He was seen in a walking boot following the game and eventually missed the team’s tilt against the Kansas City Chiefs at home in week three. According to David Furones of the Sun Sentinel, Douglas was not seen practicing for the Dolphins on Thursday — continuing the recent trend of missed practices for the rookie while he recovers from his ankle ailment. That puts his availability for Miami’s week four contest on the road against the Minnesota Vikings in serious jeopardy despite head coach Jeff Hafley’s early week optimism while labeling Douglas as “day-to-day.” Still no Caleb Douglas, Rob Beal practicing during media viewing at Thursday drills. Chris Bell appears to still be limited. Storm Duck again out there. Tucker Addington still wearing red. https://t.co/IhgNbrJE4r — David Furones (@DavidFurones_) October 1, 2026 In his absence last week, fellow rookie receiver Chris Bell led all Dolphins’ receivers in receiving yards — tallying 67 yards on four receptions. Malik Washington added five receptions for 56 yards. Going against a Brian Flores led Vikings defense, quarterback Malik Willis could benefit greatly from Douglas’s separation skills. After all, Douglas led the NFL in separation yards per route run after his week one showing — averaging 5.3 yards of separation each time he ran a route. Unfortunately, it looks like Willis, and all Miami Dolphins’ fans, will likely have to wait at least one more week to see Douglas back in action.

title: Can Malik Washington step up among Dolphins injury issues?
summary: When a talented player suffers a season-ending injury, you’ll often hear coaches talk about adopting a “next-man-up mentality” and the opportunities available to the others in the position room. We saw that when the Dolphins’ All-Pro running back De’Von Achane tore his ACL against the Chiefs in Week 3, and everyone’s attention went to Ollie […]
full_text: When a talented player suffers a season-ending injury, you’ll often hear coaches talk about adopting a “next-man-up mentality” and the opportunities available to the others in the position room. We saw that when the Dolphins’ All-Pro running back De’Von Achane tore his ACL against the Chiefs in Week 3, and everyone’s attention went to Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright. For the Dolphins, though, replacing Achane isn’t simply about replacing carries – it’s also about replacing explosiveness from arguably the most talented player on the team. And no player on Miami’s roster may be better suited for that challenge than Malik Washington. The Challenge Isn’t Just Replacing Carries When people think about Achane, they naturally think about his rushing production. But that’s only part of the story. Achane created problems for defenses because he could line up anywhere and threaten a defense in multiple ways. He could run between the tackles, catch passes out of the backfield, motion across the formation, or turn a simple touch into a chunk play. He forced defenses to account for him before and after the snap. Replacing him won’t be as simple as handing the ball to another running back. The Dolphins need someone who can create offense in space, be moved around the formation and force defensive coordinators to adjust. That’s where Washington enters the conversation. More Than a Gadget Player One of the biggest misconceptions about Washington is that he is simply a gadget receiver. Under Mike McDaniel, much of his role fit that description. Screens, jet sweeps, reverses and return opportunities were often the easiest ways to get the ball in his hands. But that role never fully reflected the player he was coming out of college. At Virginia in 2023, Washington set single-season school records with 110 receptions and 1,426 receiving yards. He wasn’t a possession receiver whose job was simply catching short passes and moving the chains. He was a volume playmaker whose game was built on creating yards after the catch and making defenders miss in space. Entering this season, one of the biggest questions surrounding Washington was whether he would have an opportunity to show more of his complete skill set . Through three games, he has already caught 12 passes for 152 yards, averaging 12.7 yards per reception. Just as importantly, coaches have spent months praising his development as a complete receiver. Back in August, when head coach Jeff Hafley was asked what had impressed him most about Washington’s development , he pointed to growth that went beyond manufactured touches: “Just his overall route running. … I think a lot of people might think of him as a bubble guy, a catch and run guy, a quick screen guy, a get him the ball on a hitch and let him run. Just him at the top of the routes and I think him really trying to master the route tree and the techniques that are being asked to do, and just his overall consistency of how he approaches every day.” Washington’s Versatility Makes Him Unique What makes Washington uniquely suited for an expanded role is less about elite speed or production, but his versatility. The Dolphins can line him up at all three receiver spots. They can motion him into the backfield. They can hand him the football, as they did twice against the Chiefs. They can use him as a returner. They can manufacture touches in space. Few players on Miami’s roster offer that kind of flexibility. And Washington himself seems to understand that. When asked this week how many positions he can play , he responded, “I think I could play a lot, man. I still throw the ball. I still keep my arm warm just in case, so I’m prepared for whatever.” The more ways a coaching staff can deploy a player, the harder he becomes to defend. The Opportunity Is Already There The coaching staff has acknowledged Washington’s ability to contribute in multiple roles. Speaking after Sunday’s game, Jeff Hafley noted that Washington stepped into a role the offense already had available for him. “Malik Washington, I told you guys yesterday that’s a role that Bobby’s had plays in for him and he did a nice job stepping up.” Washington wasn’t viewed as an emergency option when injuries hit the backfield. The offense already had concepts available for him in those situations. Now, with Achane out for the season, Miami has an opportunity to explore that versatility even further. Replacing Impact, Not Carries The Dolphins remain committed to being a run-first football team, and Jeff Hafley made it clear this week that philosophy is not changing. Washington is not likely going to line up as running back for 20 carries a game. Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon will have important roles to play moving forward. But as much as the Dolphins will need backs to absorb carries, they will also need someone capable of providing the creativity, unpredictability and explosiveness that disappeared when Achane went down. Malik Washington may not replace Achane, but he might be the player best equipped to help Miami replace what Achane brought to it.

title: Our first month with an app broke our commenting records
summary: A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it.  The goal with this app was to make it easier to join […]
full_text: (Photo by Joel Auerbach/Getty Images) | Getty Images A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it. The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center. The results so far are encouraging. In fact, it’s helped us set a new all-time record for comments this month across all of SB Nation’s communities, and I want to thank you for that. One of the most exciting new features is the game chat. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you’re not going to find anywhere else. We also wanted to elevate the community’s contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we’ve set single-day commenting records three different times since the season started. And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there’s an option at the top to do that. So, one month in, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven’t checked it out, you can get it for iOs or Android . And if you’re not an app user, that’s OK! We’re glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.

title: Can Kevin O’Connell’s 3-0 Vikings Survive the Dolphins Trap? Week 4 Preview
summary: The 3-0 Minnesota Vikings face a Miami Dolphins team in full rebuild mode, but as The Real Forno Show warns, this Week 4 matchup has trap game written all over it. — Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano sat down with Dolphins guy Kevin Fielder for the Week 4 preview, and this one is messier than […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 3-0 Minnesota Vikings face a Miami Dolphins team in full rebuild mode , but as The Real Forno Show warns, this Week 4 matchup has trap game written all over it. — Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano sat down with Dolphins guy Kevin Fielder for the Week 4 preview, and this one is messier than a 7-point spread and actually it being double-digits. Miami, under Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley, is in an evaluation year. Not a tank. Fielder put it on Sullivan: “This is not going to be a rebuild in the sense that we’re gonna tear this down.” They brought in Malik Willis to reunite him with two people who already coached him in Green Bay. Early returns are mixed. Fielder was honest about it: “I think we’ll be talking about the Miami Dolphins needing a quarterback at some point in the next few years.” De’Von Achane tore his ACL in Week 3, so Bobby Slowik has to rebuild the run game around Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright. The Vikings have their own questions. Kyler Murray has one full game in purple. Justin Jefferson had not practiced all week when we recorded. Tyler watched that debut and said, “I think he saw too much flash of color and decided not to” throw it into those windows. Fielder pushed back: “He’s just missing things down the field… there were explosive plays to be had.” Brian Flores’ defense is going to test that Miami line. Fielder likes the interior: “Kadyn Proctor at left guard, Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard, Aaron Brewer at center, has played incredibly well.” The Vikings’ run game is still a work in progress with Josh Oliver out for the year and Aaron Jones always nicked up. Spread says comfortable. The tape says do not overlook them. Key Points from the Episode: The Dolphins are the NFL’s youngest roster but have been “oddly competitive” — pushing the Chiefs, 49ers, and Raiders De’Von Achane’s ACL injury forces a schematic shift toward power-gap running Chop Robinson, drafted to be a pass rusher, has struggled in year three — “he just has to figure something out” Miami’s defense is 30th in EPA per play and 32nd in EPA per dropback, but 9th against the run Brian Flores’ “blitz” numbers are inflated — his base is five rushers, which the NFL counts as a blitz complains Fielder Kyler Murray’s misses against Tampa were reads, not accuracy: “He’s missing things that he should be taking” If Justin Jefferson sits, Jordan Addison and Tai Felton take on larger roles Donovan Jackson has been a revelation at left guard: “That guy is a baller. I was wrong,” Fielder conceded Fielder called this the “quintessential trap game” — closer than fans expect Dave Stefano invoked the 2018 Bills upset: “We were so much favored and we got our [back sides] handed to us” Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: The Real Forno Show is your go-to Minnesota Vikings podcast for film-room analysis, draft talk, and unfiltered takes — and this Week 4 preview is essential listening before kickoff. Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano leave no angle uncovered, from Brian Flores’ defensive wizardry to the Kyler Murray chemistry clock ticking toward a Week 6 bye. Whether the Vikings roll or the Dolphins shock the world, this is the conversation that frames your Sunday. Fan with Us!!! Guest Kevin Fielder @TheKevinFielder joins Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . So here’s a question for you: Will the Vikings prove they can dominate a team they should beat, or is this the week Miami steals one nobody saw coming?

LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, Justin Jefferson did not practice again, which suggests things are trending toward his not playing on Sunday. My guess is that is this were a playoff game, Jefferson would be playing. But this being the Dolphins week four at home, the Vikings may be cautious with Jefferson and not rush him back. It’s also possible that he is active on Sunday but on a pitch count if he’s feeling pretty good and is able to practice on Friday. Other than that, Aaron Jones returned to practice but Blake Cashman was still limited with an elbow. I don’t think that’ll keep him from playing on Sunday, however. Punter Brett Thorson still hasn’t practiced and I think it’s a good bet that the Vikings call up Johnny Hekker again from the practice squad to take on the punter/holder duties for another week. For the Dolphins, starting center Aaron Brewer was downgraded to limited with a hand injury on Thursday. Not sure if that is something that’ll keep him out or not, but the downgrade makes his status on Friday of more interest. Other than that, it looks like backups Beal and Douglas are trending toward being out. Stay tuned. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Myles Price Named NFC Special Teams Player of the Month
summary: Apparently the NFL naming Myles Price the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 3 just wasn’t enough to emphasize how good he’s been so far this year, so the league took it a step further on Thursday. The NFL has named Price the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Month for the […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings returns a kick for a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Apparently the NFL naming Myles Price the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 3 just wasn’t enough to emphasize how good he’s been so far this year, so the league took it a step further on Thursday. The NFL has named Price the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Month for the month of September for what he’s done over the first three weeks of the season so far. We went through Price’s accomplishments in the story we ran yesterday about his weekly award, but let’s go ahead and do them again here anyway because. . .well, he deserves it. In addition to being the only player in the league to return a punt for a touchdown so far this season, Price leads the National Football League in punt return yardage (130), punt return average (21.7 yards), kickoff return yardage (353), and all-purpose yardage (483). Price is now the eighth member of the Vikings to be named Special Teams Player of the Month and, technically, gives the Minnesota Vikings the award in back-to-back months. Will Reichard won the award for December 2025/January 2026. Here is a full list of Vikings Special Teams Player of the Month recipients: Fuad Reveiz (December 1994) Mitch Berger (November 1998) Mitch Berger (September 1999) Mitch Berger (September 2000) Chris Kluwe (September 2005) Percy Harvin (September 2012) Blair Walsh (December 2012) Cordarrelle Patterson (September 2013) Will Reichard (December 2025/January 2026) Myles Price (September 2026) So, to clarify, it’s ten different awards for eight different players, given that Berger won the award three different times. Congratulations to Myles Price on being named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Month for September!

Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we’ve set single-day commenting records three different times since the season started. If you haven’t checked it out, you can get it for iOs or Android . And if you’re not an app user, that’s OK! We’re glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.

title: NFL predictions: Will the Patriots upset the Bills in Week 4?
summary: Arguably the most impactful win of the New England Patriots’ 2025 season came against their biggest rivals. In Week 5, they managed to upset the Buffalo Bills 23-20 in primetime — a win that ended up setting the tone for the rest of the season, and for the AFC East title returning to Foxborough for […]
full_text: Arguably the most impactful win of the New England Patriots’ 2025 season came against their biggest rivals. In Week 5, they managed to upset the Buffalo Bills 23-20 in primetime — a win that ended up setting the tone for the rest of the season, and for the AFC East title returning to Foxborough for the first time in six years. Fast forward to 2026, and the Bills and their 3-0 record again look like a serious contender for the division title. The Patriots, on the other hand, are facing an uphill battle: not only did they start the season 1-2, their offense around MVP runner-up Drake Maye has struggled playing consistent football and holding onto the ball. If there ever was a get-right game for the team, this week’s might be it. The Patriots, after all, are headed to Buffalo for a rematch of that Week 5 battle last season. Will the outcome be the same this time around, and the 6.5-point underdogs according to FanDuel Sportsbook manage another upset in Orchard Park? Let’s find out what Pats Pulpit’s staff and community think. Patriots vs. Bills score predictions Bernd Buchmasser: The Patriots have had their fair share of struggles and will be heading into a hostile environment on Sunday. An upset would be monumental and, just like last year, might have a lasting effect on the team and it’s confidence. However, unlike in 2025, the gap between them and the Bills feels very much too big to be overcome at this point in time. While the game should be more competitive than last week’s shellacking in Jacksonville, New England’s issues and injury woes will be too much to overcome versus one of the best teams in the NFL. | Patriots 17, Bills 21 Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! Follow every snap and discuss every decision with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Connect through our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Matt St. Jean: Drake Maye looks broken, as does the Patriots offense as a whole. The Bills have been rolling and just won easily despite losing the turnover differential badly. It’s hard to imagine this being competitive with the version of Drake Maye we’ve seen this season. | Patriots 10, Bills 27 Dylan Klayman: The Bills, as they often do, look unbeatable to start off the year. Drake Maye is completely flustered and lost right now. The defense also did not perform last week, and got very little pressure on the quarterback. Penalties have also been racking up. Based off what we have seen from the Patriots this season, this game won’t be very close. | Bills 34, Patriots 17 Pat Lane: I’m doing this based solely on hope, because, if the Patriots get blown out, I will consider the season essentially over. They have to show some fight, and being able to score 20+ on offense would be huge. The Bills are a wagon, so I’m expecting this to most likely be a loss, but how they play is incredibly important to me. A close loss like this could be a springboard for them moving forward. Based on what we’ve seen so far this year, this outcome might be a surprise, but I’m hoping to see some growth from Maye this week. We’ll see how far that hope takes me. | Bills 24, Patriots 21 What do you think? Do you agree with our assessment? Or do you feel differently one way or the other? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts with the rest of the community .

title: Ben Brown ‘ready to roll’ should Patriots call upon him against Bills
summary: Entering 2026, right guard was supposed to be a position of strength for the New England Patriots. Mike Onwenu had been their best offensive linemen for several years now, and even with plenty of football under his belt has remained a top-tier if somewhat underrated blocker in the run and pass game. However, three games […]
full_text: Entering 2026, right guard was supposed to be a position of strength for the New England Patriots. Mike Onwenu had been their best offensive linemen for several years now, and even with plenty of football under his belt has remained a top-tier if somewhat underrated blocker in the run and pass game. However, three games into the season the outlook has changed dramatically. Onwenu suffered a fractured ankle in Week 2 against Pittsburgh, with his replacement — training camp free agency pickup Greg Van Roten — going down with an ankle injury one week later. With both now on injured reserve, the Patriots are scrambling for answers at the spot. Looking at the roster, there are three candidates to fill Onwenu’s shoes now that Van Roten is out of the equation for at least four weeks: Ben Brown, Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor. Brown entered training camp as the No. 4 interior lineman but was hampered by an ankle injury in preseason; Rouse was acquired in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings ahead of late-August’s roster cutdowns; Pryor was signed just this week to provide additional depth and experience. Who among them will emerge as the starter remains to be seen, but based on past performance in the system, Brown looks like a realistic candidate. If indeed called upon, he vows to be ready. “Physically, I feel great. I’m ready to roll however that might look,” he said earlier this week. “It’s just like Coach [Mike Vrabel] always says, ‘Prepare every week as a starter regardless of if you’re actually out there or not.’ That’s what we are intending, to be ready. And so, whatever is asked upon me, I’ll be ready for whatever.” A rookie free agent in 2022, Brown made his way to New England via the Raiders practice squad in 2024. Since then, he has played 33 games with 14 starts — all of them at either left guard or center. In fact, only 11 of his 1,007 offensive snaps with the team have come at right guard. And yet, Brown feels confident in his ability to play that role, in part because he did so during his college career at Ole Miss. Ultimately, though, his goal is to just help the team regardless of the role he is asked to play on game days. “I want to do whatever I can to contribute, however that might look,” he said. “I just want to be ready for whenever my number’s called upon. Whenever that might be, because you never know in the NFL. It’s long seasons and a lot goes on in it. Best thing I can do for this football team is just be ready whenever my number’s called.”

title: Patriots mailbag: What’s wrong with the run game?
summary: The New England Patriots are looking to put a blowout loss behind them as they get ready for a big divisional battle against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. I know it is early but I thought we would see improvements in the run game with the […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are looking to put a blowout loss behind them as they get ready for a big divisional battle against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. I know it is early but I thought we would see improvements in the run game with the addition of Gilliam. An improved run game would certainly be a big plus while Maye figures things out. Why do you think we haven’t seen the positive impact yet of having a proven FB? The OL injuries? – sqpondme Why no outside runs utilizing Henderson’s speed? – Davel The Patriots’ run game has been poor for the second straight season, currently ranking last in the league in success rate and 24th in Rush EPA. While the running backs and offensive line are not free of blame, the scheme has not helped by stressing defenses pre-snap with motion or other creativity. Instead, the Patriots have largely leaned on duo this season, hoping to move defenders off the line of scrimmage, but have repeatedly run into bodies as defensive fronts use line games up front to create disruption. McDaniels, however, believes there is still value in staying the course early in the season. “I think last year we went through a very similar stage where sticking with certain things was helpful for us,” Josh McDaniels said Thursday. “I’ve talked about this a lot in a running game, in training camp, you have X amount of practices in pads. If you do or don’t play in the preseason games, that is what it is, right? So, you have opportunities to work together in a physical environment. And I think sometimes, what I’ve seen in the last so many years is September and October end up being an extension of that for the run game especially, because double teams and pads on a 330 lb. human being, when you don’t do it over and over and over again daily sometimes it takes a few more repetitions to get good at it. “And so, whether it’s outside zones or toss cracks or double seam schemes or draws, whatever the scheme is, I think fitting runs and doing it with the proper technique and fundamentals takes some time in pads.” It’s not realistic for the Patriots to completely scrap their run-game scheme, meaning more time on task will need to produce better results. But there are ways New England could add more variety, including getting TreVeyon Henderson outside more often. Henderson has seen 37% of his carries outside the tackles this season, compared to 49% last season, albeit in a small sample size. There should be opportunities for him and Rhamondre Stevenson to hit the edges this week against the Bills defense. When it comes to Gilliam, the fullback is clearly hobbled which is affecting his playing time and impact. His workload was managed the entire offseason before he finally was listed on the injury report this week with a knee injury. What is going on with Hunter Henry and why has he disappeared? I said I think Eli Raridon could be TE #1 by season’s end. That might be sooner than even I thought. When should we expect Eli Raridon to return fully healthy? – For Pats Sake The lack of a true blocking tight end has also worked against them in the run game. As for Henry, the 31-year old certainly has appeared to lose a step early on, while teams are also sitting on his underneath routes in quick game concepts to take his production away. Raridon was back to being a limited participant this week so should be ready to go Sunday. The Patriots need him back on the field for his explosiveness in the passing game and blocking ability. What is the formula to restore Maye confidence – 7i165 Correcting Maye’s confidence, decisiveness and decision-making are the biggest things that need to improve for him to get back on track. As for how to do that, I’m not in Maye’s mind or a psychologist. That’s something for the coaching staff to figure out, which raises an interesting question: Should they rein him in and try to prevent him from beating himself? That brings risk in itself, as Maye could lose the aggressiveness that typically makes him so dangerous. If take away Maye’s turnovers, how would you rate him this year as a Quarterback? – sumeetw Analytically, Maye has been around league average when removing the six interceptions and one fumble. I’d say that passes the eye test as there are still encouraging signs on film such as him generating explosives against Pittsburgh, stepping up through the pocket in Jacksonville or working a scramble drill to Kyle Williams in the fourth quarter. He is also moving the football as the Patriots are 12th in the league in yards per drive. The turnovers and penalties are just not allowing them to finish, as they rank last in points per drive (0.97). Mike Onwenu, our starting Right Guard, goes onto to IR. A week later, Greg Van Roten, the top backup, joins him on IR. Walter Rouse replaced GVR, and he struggled in this new position for him. Is Rouse the answer going forward? Or would Ben Brown be a better option? – PatsFanFromNH I would go with Ben Brown. He’s proven to be their best interior backup and right guard is his natural position dating back to college. Whether that is a season-long fix or not is TBD, and I also wouldn’t rule out newly signed Matt Pryor factoring into the mix in some fashion. Is it too early to start thinking about who we should be looking at in next year’s draft? – poindexterregan It’s never too early to start thinking about next year’s draft. It should be a loaded class and I’d imagine the front seven will be an area of emphasis for the Patriots. I’m not ready to start thinking about some of the edge rushers projected in the top-five, but Georgia linebacker Chris Cole has been a favorite of mine as a mid-to-late first-round pick. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

title: Bills TE Dalton Kincaid a focal point for Patriots defense this week
summary: The Buffalo Bills offense has been one of the best in the NFL so far this season, and a big reason why is the play of its top tight end. Dalton Kincaid has been fantastic lately. And don’t just take our word for it: that is exactly how New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills offense has been one of the best in the NFL so far this season, and a big reason why is the play of its top tight end. Dalton Kincaid has been fantastic lately. And don’t just take our word for it: that is exactly how New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel described him ahead of the two teams’ Week 4 matchup. “Kincaid has been fantastic lately, averaging almost 19 yards a catch,” Vrabel said earlier this week. Vrabel’s description of the 26-year-old makes sense. He has, indeed, been a productive player for the Bills and one of quarterback Josh Allen’s most trusted targets this season. Kincaid ranks first on the team with 14 receptions — including one for a touchdown — and trails only wide receiver D.J. Moore in total targets through three games. His 263 receiving yards and 18.8-yard average per catch, meanwhile, are not just the most on the Bills, but also lead all NFL tight ends heading into the fourth week of the season. How the Patriots plan to keep him in check will be seen, but they have so far been quite successful going against tight ends. In their first three games, the position group has gained just 84 yards on 10 catches against defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr’s unit. That being said, as Patriots safety Kevin Byard explained, the “tight end” label might actually not be the best way to describe what Kincaid provides. “I see him as a wide receiver. The things they do with him are as a wide receiver,” Byard said. “He’s going to be split out wide, when they have two tight ends out there, he runs receiver routes. I mean, shoot, he’s their top target right now. When you look at his stats, it’s not normal tight end stats. Josh Allen trusts him. He’s going up with great body control, going up attacking the football. He’s a dynamic player and we’re going to have to contain him.”

title: Patriots vs. Bills weather forecast for NFL Week 4
summary: Fresh off a blowout loss in the Florida heat, the New England Patriots will return to more friendly playing conditions in Week 4. A trip to Buffalo for an AFC East showdown with the Bills awaits head coach Mike Vrabel’s team this weekend. While the weather in Western New York can be a challenging, especially […]
full_text: Fresh off a blowout loss in the Florida heat, the New England Patriots will return to more friendly playing conditions in Week 4. A trip to Buffalo for an AFC East showdown with the Bills awaits head coach Mike Vrabel’s team this weekend. While the weather in Western New York can be a challenging, especially later in the year, Sunday’s game should not be impacted in any significant way. According to NFL Weather , temperatures will hover around 63 or 64°F. While the skies will be mostly cloudy, the chance of precipitation is below 50% and decreasing as the game goes on. There will be wind gusts of up 16 mph, but if they will actually impact the passing and kicking game remains to be seen. The National Weather Service shares a similar projection. According to its models, conditions will be “mostly sunny, with a high near 67” as well as a “southeast wind around 6 mph becoming southwest in the afternoon.” If the projected conditions hold, this week’s game between the two rivals will be among the warmest Patriots-Bills meetings of the last decade. Only one of them — the Week 5 showdown last season won 23-20 by the visiting New England side — had a kickoff temperature above 65°F. This week’s kickoff between the Patriots and Bills is scheduled for Sunday, Oct. 4 at 1 p.m. ET, at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, NY.

title: Patriots rooting guide for NFL Week 4
summary: The New England Patriots will attempt to get back to .500 on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against the Buffalo Bills, trying to improve to 2-2 on the year. While our focus is on this specific game, it is only one of 16 on the menu in Week 4 of the 2026 NFL regular season. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots will attempt to get back to .500 on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against the Buffalo Bills, trying to improve to 2-2 on the year. While our focus is on this specific game, it is only one of 16 on the menu in Week 4 of the 2026 NFL regular season. Here is who to root for in the other 15 not featuring the Patriots. Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) at Cleveland Browns ( 2-1 ): Go Steelers! The Patriots have already beaten the Steelers, which means they hold the head-to-head tiebreaker and a Pittsburgh win would boost their strength of schedule and victory tiebreakers. | Prime Video Sunday 9:30 a.m. ET Indianapolis Colts (1-2) at Washington Commanders ( 1-2 ) : Go Commanders! The classic case of picking the NFC team over the AFC team with no other direct ties to the Patriots. | NFL Network 1 p.m. ET Tennessee Titans (0-3) at Baltimore Ravens ( 2-1 ) : Go Titans! For the sake of the Patriots’ standing in the AFC playoff race, we will obviously go with the worse-ranked team here. | CBS New York Jets ( 1-2 ) at Chicago Bears ( 2-1 ) : Go Bears! With Patriots’ highest fifth-round pick going to Philadelphia anyway as part of the A.J. Brown trade, there are no implications should Chicago win. But even if that were not the case, we would still go NFC team over AFC team here. | FOX Jacksonville Jaguars ( 2-1 ) at Cincinnati Bengals ( 2-1 ) : Go Bengals! Somebody has to win, so it might just be the team that does not have the head-to-head advantage over the Patriots. New England needs to win more games than Jacksonville to finish ahead in the playoff standings. | CBS Dallas Cowboys ( 1-2 ) at Houston Texans ( 0-3 ) : Go Cowboys! A Cowboys win would kill two birds with one stone for the Patriots: it will keep an AFC rival down and possibly end up improving the position of the sixth-round draft pick acquired in the Marte Mapu trade. | FOX Arizona Cardinals ( 1-2 ) at New York Giants ( 2-1 ) : Go good game! Two NFC teams clashing with no impact on the Patriots. | CBS Los Angeles Rams ( 1-2 ) at Philadelphia Eagles ( 2-1 ) : Go good game! Same as above. | FOX Green Bay Packers ( 1-2 ) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers ( 0-3 ) : Go Packers! Three words: strength of schedule. | FOX 4:05 p.m. ET Miami Dolphins ( 0-3 ) at Minnesota Vikings ( 3-0 ) : Go Vikings! Strength of schedule does not matter in this game given that the Patriots play both of those teams this year. What does matter is the Dolphins dropping to 0-4 against an NFC team. | FOX 4:25 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs ( 3-0 ) at Las Vegas Raiders ( 3-0 ) : Go Raiders! Both teams are unbeaten and on New England’s schedule, with Kansas City looking like the safer bet to be a serious playoff contender in the AFC this year. In that case, a loss by them would be the preferred outcome. | CBS Los Angeles Chargers ( 0-3 ) at Seattle Seahawks ( 2-1 ) : Go Seahawks! With both teams on the Patriots’ schedule this year, we will pick the NFC team over the AFC team. Yes, it might end up hurting New England’s strength of victory, but even with the Chargers at 0-3 the season is still too young to write them off just yet. | CBS Denver Broncos ( 2-1 ) at San Francisco 49ers (3-0) : Go Niners! NFC team over AFC team, even if it ends up hurting New England’s strength of schedule. | CBS 8:20 p.m. ET Detroit Lions ( 2-1 ) at Carolina Panthers ( 1-2 ) : Go good game! Two NFC teams with no direct ties to the Patriots going at each other. Just sit back, relax, and enjoy. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Atlanta Falcons ( 1-2 ) at New Orleans Saints ( 1-2 ) : Go Falcons! The Patriots own the Saints’ sixth-round pick next year from the Ja’Lynn Polk trade, so every New Orleans loss helps boost that pick’s value. | ESPN

title: Mike Vrabel highlights ‘underrated part’ of Bills’ success ahead of Patriots game
summary: While the New England Patriots are facing questions along the offensive line heading into Week 4, their opponent has none of those issues. The Buffalo Bills have been a model of stability up front, and are set to go with the same starting five on Sunday they have used all season. The consistency in personnel […]
full_text: While the New England Patriots are facing questions along the offensive line heading into Week 4, their opponent has none of those issues. The Buffalo Bills have been a model of stability up front, and are set to go with the same starting five on Sunday they have used all season. The consistency in personnel is not the only reason why Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel highlighted the unit this week. “I think the line is a very underrated part of what they do,” Vrabel told reporters at the Gillette Stadium podium on Wednesday. “It’s been a very consistent unit, one that knows how to block for not only the running back, but also for the quarterback.” Even though the Bills changed their head coach, offensive coordinator and offensive line coach this offseason, they did not touch the O-line itself. As a result, it has remained largely in place: four of the five starters — LT Dion Dawkins, C Connor McGovern, LG O’Cyrus Torrence, RT Spencer Browns — have been brought back from last year. In fact, the quartet has started alongside one another going back to the 2023 season. The lone exception is Alec Anderson, a do-it-all backup last year who was elevated to the left guard spot after David Edwards signed a four-year, $61 million deal with the Saints in free agency. Anderson, however, has also been with Buffalo since entering the NFL in 2022. For comparison, no Patriots offensive lineman has been with the team that long. The longest-tenured member of the group is backup interior lineman Ben Brown, who joined in 2024. The longest-tenured regular starter, Mike Onwenu, went on injured reserve last week, handing over that particular title to 2025 free agency signing Morgan Moses. Moses, of course, has yet to practice this week because of a foot injury. The state of the two offensive lines is only one of the reasons why Buffalo is 3-0 entering Sunday’s game with a 1-2 Patriots team that has performed well-below expectation. “They’re really successful in a lot of things they do,” added Vrabel. “They rarely punt — five punts in three games. Josh [Allen] does a fantastic job of being able to extend plays. The linemen do a fantastic job of understanding the scheme that they want to run and creating lanes for [James] Cook, who again, once he gets cooking — no pun intended, but they’re just tough to stop, right? Because then it’s play action, it’s boots. And so, it just makes it tough to stop.”

No. 0 closed out September having had a hand in eight tackles and five passes defensed for the secondary. Three absences became four with New England’s fullback missing from practice because of a knee injury. But veterans from the offensive and defensive lines have also been out since the trip to EverBank Stadium. The 35-year-old Moses, who had been limited by a foot injury last week, did not go unaffected by it and was eventually pulled in the third quarter with 41 offensive snaps to play at right tackle. Moore (shoulder) WR Keon Coleman (ankle) DT T.J. Sanders (illness) LB Joe Andreessen (knee) S Damar Hamlin (ribs) The Patriots added Canada to the list of six limited on Thursday because of a hamstring injury. The quarterback finds himself with one touchdown and seven turnovers. And heading into the AFC East meeting, he finds himself on the official injury report for the first time this fall. The injury to Maye’s throwing shoulder did not keep the 24-year-old captain from being a full participant on Wednesday. Nor did it on Thursday. Josh McDaniels added context prior to the session. “Again, he’s always been a guy that can run and do things with his legs and all that,” the Patriots offensive coordinator told reporters. “He’s taken a few hits since he’s been in the National Football League. That’s kind of part of the process when you can make things happen with your legs. You’re going to incur some hits. They would obviously tell me obviously if there was something that we felt like we couldn’t do or he couldn’t do. That has not been the case. I know he’s a tough kid. I know that for sure. title: Josh McDaniels adds context to Drake Maye shoulder injury
summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye landed on the team’s injury report Wednesday with a right shoulder injury. Maye was a full participant in practice, and offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels provided more context on the injury Thursday. “I believe it just got dinged last week,” McDaniels said. Maye took several big hits inside the pocket […]
full_text: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye landed on the team’s injury report Wednesday with a right shoulder injury. Maye was a full participant in practice, and offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels provided more context on the injury Thursday. “I believe it just got dinged last week,” McDaniels said. Maye took several big hits inside the pocket during Sunday’s loss to the Jaguars while also running the ball four times — two scrambles, a quarterback sneak and an option run play in the red zone. McDaniels pointed to one of those runs as a potential time when Maye’s shoulder was injured. “We haven’t had a big meeting and talked about specifically, like, exactly when this or that or the other happened, but yeah, he ran the ball a few times last week,” McDaniels said. “And I think that’s what happened.” Speaking after practice on Wednesday , Maye said the injury has not affected his ability to throw the ball or his decision-making after he threw six interceptions through the Patriots’ first three games. McDaniels also said the injury has not impacted his ability to call games or execute their practice plan. “It has not,” McDaniels said. “You know, again, he’s always been a guy that can run and do things with his legs and all that. And he’s taken a few hits since he’s been in the National Football League. That’s kind of been part of the process. When you can make things happen with your legs, you’re gonna incur some hits. “They would tell me, obviously, if there was something that we felt like we couldn’t do or he couldn’t do. That has not been the case.” Maye’s struggles have been a major factor in the Patriots’ 1-2 start to the season. Despite the early turmoil, McDaniels has not seen a change in Maye’s confidence or demeanor. “I do not,” McDaniels said. “I mean, honestly, I’ve played golf with him, pickle ball with him. I’ve watched him play football, and I’m not really sure what changes that for him. He’s blessed in that regard. When I hit a T-shot in the woods, my confidence is shattered, and I’m going to do it again and again and again. He doesn’t really do that. He can do that and then the next one’s down the middle. It’s 340 [yards] and you’re sitting there going, ‘How did that happen?’ “I think his mindset is and it’s the way you have to be as a quarterback. … And yes, there are things that we can do better. Yes, there are things that we can work on to try to make some of the negative scenarios that we’ve had happen go away, and that’s what he’s focused on. But his demeanor, his countenance, his facial expressions, his ability to interject things in meetings has not changed, and I love that about the kid. I think, like I said, he’s blessed in that regard because I think there’s people that sometimes let those things weigh on them and God bless him.”
author: Brian Hines

title: Saints draft position: Entering Week 4
summary: After a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, the New Orleans Saints’ draft pick position has shifted significantly. Instead of selecting near the playoff section, they are back in the top-10, right where they selected two seasons ago. Here are two prospects that the Saints could select at pick 9: Georgia CB Ellis Robinson IV […]
full_text: ATHENS, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 26: KJ Bolden #4 of the Georgia Bulldogs rushes after an interception during the second quarter against the Oklahoma Sooners at Sanford Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Athens, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, the New Orleans Saints’ draft pick position has shifted significantly. Instead of selecting near the playoff section, they are back in the top-10, right where they selected two seasons ago. Here are two prospects that the Saints could select at pick 9: Georgia CB Ellis Robinson IV The first player we will talk about is Ellis Robinson IV. If the Saints are unable to upgrade the edge position early in the draft, CB has to be the next best option. These two position groups benefit from each other the most on defense. If the DBs cover well, it allows an average pass rush to get to the QB, but if you have a great pass rush, it stops the pass defense from getting picked apart. The Saints do not have a good pass rush or a good CB room. Kool-Aid McKinstry has played pretty well so far, and Quincy Riley has made some plays, but this team does not have a clear CB1. Robinson can be that player. He is great in both man and zone coverage, is physical, and has his eyes on the ball for a turnover. The issue is that his focus on getting an interception can cause him to get beat, which is a worry. Georgia SAF KJ Bolden Sticking with the DBs and Georgia, another player that would make sense is safety KJ Bolden, but some things need to happen first. If the Saints want to keep Jonas Sanker at slot, which hasn’t been horrible, then safety can become a major position of need. So far, since signing Justin Reid, it hasn’t been great. Not bad, but not the level of safety that I think many of us expected. His leadership has been great, and I do think that’s important, but is it crazy to say the Saints could move on from him this offseason? A post-June 1st cut would be a low dead cap hit and save some money. Even if the Saints do not move on from Reid, they will need to add a safety this season, but if they release their captain, Bolden would make a ton of sense. At Georgia, Bolden has been an incredible run defender and tackler, while also providing flexibility around the defense, and has become a leader for the Bulldogs. Bolden is a clear upgrade who could be sitting there at pick 9.

title: If Saints win/lose vs. Falcons
summary: After a gut-punching defeat to the Las Vegas Raiders at the weekend, the New Orleans Saints are gearing up to host the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football in a huge divisional matchup. Here’s what either result could mean for the black and gold. If the Saints win: All games matter, and all divisional games […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - SEPTEMBER 27: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints speaks to his teammates before kickoff against the Las Vegas Raiders during an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on September 27, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a gut-punching defeat to the Las Vegas Raiders at the weekend, the New Orleans Saints are gearing up to host the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football in a huge divisional matchup. Here’s what either result could mean for the black and gold. If the Saints win: All games matter, and all divisional games matter that little bit more. But this particular clash has all the ingredients to be particularly season-defining at an early stage. The Saints have categorically played better than their record shows. Getting back to .500 and winning their first NFC South matchup of the season is absolutely crucial, and would allow the black and gold to almost start afresh, likely atop the division, and put some of the bad luck of the opening few weeks behind them. In last week’s edition of this piece, some readers disagreed with me for labeling Week 4 a must-win in the event that New Orleans lost to Las Vegas. Unfortunately, that scenario is upon us. And it does indeed feel like must-win territory. But Kellen Moore’s squad can restore all of the feel good factor that came after the win in Baltimore by overcoming their divisional foes and improving to 2-2 on the year. If the Saints lose: A loss would be truly sickening for the black and gold. However, falling to 1-3 against the Falcons in this spot wouldn’t kill the chances of winning the division, far from it. But it would certainly nonetheless feel like a major setback. And to drop consecutive games in the Caesars Superdome to Las Vegas and Atlanta has to say something about the ceiling on this team, especially with another key injury to Travis Etienne Jr being added to the woes. Both defeats to date have felt harsh. New Orleans has good reason to feel hard done by. But losing to Atlanta on Monday night, even in its own right, would feel like a big disappointment. What are you expecting from the black and gold on primetime? How do you rate the Falcons after their surprise beatdown of Green Bay?

title: Saints announce multiple roster moves ahead of their MNF matchup against the Falcons
summary: The New Orleans Saints just wrapped up the first practice ahead of their Monday Night Football matchup against the Atlanta Falcons and wasted little time shaking up the roster in light of some recent injuries. New Orleans signed wide receiver Kevin Austin Jr. to the active roster from the practice squad, added running back Ulysses […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - SEPTEMBER 27: Travis Etienne Jr. #3 of the New Orleans Saints runs across the field during an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Cesars Superdome on September 27, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints just wrapped up the first practice ahead of their Monday Night Football matchup against the Atlanta Falcons and wasted little time shaking up the roster in light of some recent injuries. New Orleans signed wide receiver Kevin Austin Jr. to the active roster from the practice squad, added running back Ulysses Bentley IV and edge rusher David Ojabo to the practice squad and placed running back Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve. Etienne suffered a hamstring injury in Sunday’s loss to the Las Vegas Raiders and will now miss at least four games, leaving the Saints without one of their key offensive weapons. Austin is no stranger to New Orleans. He has spent the past three seasons with the Saints, bouncing between the active roster and practice squad. In 19 games with three starts, Austin has caught 25 passes for 298 yards and one touchdown. Bentley originally signed with the Colts as an undrafted free agent following the 2025 NFL Draft. He spent time on the practice squad in Indianapolis over the past two seasons and appeared in one game as a rookie. Ojabo brings some additional depth off the edge. A second-round pick by the Ravens in the 2022 NFL Draft, he appeared in 32 games with one start over four seasons in Baltimore, recording 28 tackles, 4.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and four special teams stops. The Saints will need all hands on deck as New Orleans (1-2) will welcome Atlanta (1-2) to town Monday night for their first NFC South matchup of the season. With both teams trying to climb back to .500, an early divisional win could provide some much-needed momentum.

title: NFL Picks Week 4: 20 Years in the Making
summary: The New Orleans Saints enter Week 4 with a 1-2 record as they face the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football. This is not just any other primetime matchup against the hated Falcons. This game commemorates the 20th Anniversary of the Saints’ “Domecoming” game in Week 3 of the 2006 season. That game is forever remembered for […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUSIANA - OCTOBER 7: A statue titled Rebirth featuring the likeness of former New Orleans Saints safety Steve Gleason blocking a punt by former Atlanta Falcons punter Michael Koenen on September 25, 2006 as seen outside before a game against the San Diego Chargers at the Mercedes-Benz Superdome on October 7, 2012 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick E. Hingle/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints enter Week 4 with a 1-2 record as they face the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football. This is not just any other primetime matchup against the hated Falcons. This game commemorates the 20th Anniversary of the Saints’ “Domecoming” game in Week 3 of the 2006 season. That game is forever remembered for the re-opening of the Louisiana Superdome and the Saints returning home to that building, which seemed almost impossible a year earlier. That night was the first time Sean Payton and Drew Brees took the field in the Superdome as Saints. Arguably, most famously, that was the night Steve Gleason was immortalized as a Saint and a New Orleans legend, with his punt block that created one of the most uplifting and memorable moments in the storied history of the great city of New Orleans. All that being said, that was two decades ago. These are different Falcons. These are different Saints. No players or coaches remain from that remarkable night. The anniversary was technically a week ago. This is a different time and a different era. This night will not and should not compare to that remarkable one. This game is a matter of pride, the pride in the Saints and the people of New Orleans. Many of those Saints are expected to be in attendance, and many fans will certainly be as well. Twenty years is a long time, but for some it will feel like yesterday once they enter the Caesars Superdome on Monday Night. Hopefully the 2026 New Orleans Saints will make those 2006 New Orleans Saints, and all of the fans, proud. Now let’s take a look at this and all of the games on the Week 4 NFL schedule. Last week, I went 7-9 I told you so: Ravens over Cowboys! What do I know: Panthers over Browns? *** WEEK 4 Thursday, October 1st – Thursday Night Football Steelers(2-1) at Browns(2-1) Almost like an anti-NFC South, the AFC North is currently the tightest and most hotly contested division in the NFL, and it is surprising to see these two teams in the thick of it. This will be a defensive struggle that Pittsburgh wins on the road. Pittsburgh wins 14-10. Pick: Steelers *** Sunday, October 4th – Very Early Game Colts(1-2) at* Commanders(1-2) – London, England America isn’t exactly sending its best “across the pond” in this international game, but it will be a close one between pretty even teams. Washington wins 19-13. Pick: Commanders *** Sunday, October 4th – Early Games Titans(0-3) at Ravens(2-1) Tennessee’s defense will keep the game tighter than expected, but it will be another loss despite the effort. Baltimore wins 21-14. Pick: Ravens *** Patriots(1-2) at Bills(3-0) These AFC East rivals will have a fantastic duel, but it will be the home team that remains undefeated in the end. Buffalo wins 28-27. Pick: Bills *** Jets(1-2) at Bears(2-1) The Jets certainly have some fight in them, and despite the fight they put up here, Chicago is still in another class. Chicago wins 21-14. Pick: Bears *** Jaguars(2-1) at Bengals(2-1) This should be one of the most exciting games of the week, and it will come down to late game heroics by Joe Burrow, leading the home team to a game-winning touchdown. Cincinnati wins 34-27. Pick: Bengals *** Cowboys(1-2) at Texans(0-3) This Texas showdown will be carried by the Dallas offense. Dallas wins 29-19. Pick: Cowboys *** Cardinals(1-2) at Giants(2-1) Despite a sub-.500 record, Arizona has certainly been one of the more surprising teams in the league so far, and they will show more of that fight in a nice road win over Jameis Winston and the Giants. Arizona wins 27-19. Pick: Cardinals *** Rams(1-2) at Eagles(2-1) Both of these highly-touted NFC contenders are coming off high profile losses last week, but it is Philly who gets back on track first, against a Rams team they simply have had the advantage over in recent matchups. Philadelphia wins 31-24. Pick: Eagles *** Packers(1-2) at Buccaneers(0-3) Green Bay has simply been one of the worst teams in the NFL this season, and that ineptitude will be enough to hand the Bucs their first win of the season. Tampa Bay wins 23-17. Pick: Buccaneers *** Sunday, October 4th – Late Games Dolphins(0-3) at Vikings(3-0) Minnesota is very good, and Miami is very bad. Enough said. Minnesota wins 32-14. Pick: Vikings *** Chiefs(3-0) at Raiders(3-0) Two bitter AFC West rivals, both undefeated, facing off in an early season showdown. This has all the makings of a fantastic matchup, right? Not so fast. Following their Week 3 victory, the Raiders will stumble badly at home with a turnover-riddled performance, led by a 3 INT performance by Kirk Cousins, as Patrick Mahomes hits big in Vegas. Kansas City wins 35-7. Pick: Chiefs *** Chargers(0-3) at Seahawks(2-1) The Chargers have been one of the most surprisingly bad teams to start this season, and things won’t get any easier on the road against the reigning Super Bowl Champions. This one will actually be close, but will end in another loss for the Bolts. Seattle wins 27-24. Pick: Seahawks *** Broncos(2-1) at 49ers(3-0) – Game of the Week Just when you think the Niners are going to struggle, they find a way to thrive, thanks to top-tier coaching. That has led them to a surprising undefeated start, despite offseason struggles. Now they face another team with top-tier coaching, as Denver has won consecutive games against playoff contenders. This showdown will be every bit as good as expected, but the Broncos will knock the Niners from the ranks of the unbeaten. Denver wins 29-28. Pick: Broncos *** Sunday Night Football Lions(2-1) at Panthers(1-2) Detroit may have a winning record, but they have been shaky all season, and their defense will stumble on the road in this primetime matchup in Charlotte. Carolina wins 33-31. Pick: Panthers *** Monday, October 5th – Monday Night Football Falcons(1-2) at Saints(1-2) Much has been made, and will continue to be made about what this game represents in regards to 2006, but it is 2026, and all of that is for us, not the coaches or players involved. This is ultimately a football game between bitter division rivals with identical records. This is the second-consecutive primetime game for the Falcons, while this is the first in the Kellen Moore era for the Saints. Emotions will be high in the Dome, fueled by nostalgia, but it will be the here and now that determines the winner. Bijan Robinson dominated on the ground for 194 yards at Lambeau last week, but this isn’t the porous Green Bay run defense, this is the Brandon Staley defense that held Robinson to under 100 yards combined in two meetings last season. Brock Bowers may have dominated at tight end a week ago against the Saints, but Kyle Pitts is no Bowers, no matter the draft status. The Saints have yet to play a solid full four quarters, but that changes here. The Saints will match the energy in the Superdome and channel it into victory. Saints win 28-24. Pick: Saints *** That’s how I see Week 4 playing out. Leave us your picks, insight, and comments below!

full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Oscar Delp #4 of the New Orleans Saints looks on against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints got a win, and even with some injuries in the rookie class, there were still some strong performances.
