title: Our first month with an app broke commenting records
summary: A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it.  The goal with this app was to make it easier to join […]
full_text: (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it. The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center. The results so far are encouraging. In fact, it’s helped us set a new all-time record for comments this month across all of SB Nation’s communities, and we want to thank you for that. One of the most exciting new features is the game chat. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you’re not going to find anywhere else. We also wanted to elevate the community’s contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we’ve set single-day commenting records three different times since the season started. And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there’s an option at the top to do that. So, one month in, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven’t checked it out, you can get it for iOs or Android . And if you’re not an app user, that’s OK! We’re glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.

title: Week 3 Saints Film Review: Highlights from the All 22
summary: The Saints weren’t able to secure a win vs the Raiders in a game most people had chalked up as a win on paper until the 4th quarter arrived on Sunday. Not many teams in NFL history could overcome a 4 turnover 4th quarter and the Saints were no different as they fumbled (literally) away […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - SEPTEMBER 27: New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore reacts after a replay review on a fumble during the second half of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders on September 27. 2026, at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Saints weren’t able to secure a win vs the Raiders in a game most people had chalked up as a win on paper until the 4th quarter arrived on Sunday. Not many teams in NFL history could overcome a 4 turnover 4th quarter and the Saints were no different as they fumbled (literally) away an 11 point 3rd quarter lead. While the breakdown below will not mention the referees from Sunday, I will speak on their performance briefly. They were terrible: missed holding calls, an egregious roughing the passer, the return of the “intent rule”, constant uncalled push offs – it was all there. The best way to describe this game was if the Drew Brees 5 interception game (Falcons 2012) and the No Call NFC Championship had a baby. This was a truly miserable and frustrating experience for anyone who was watching and- when fans of other teams (including the Raiders) are coming up to you expressing remorse for what just happened, you know it was exceptionally bad. As a fan of football this game left me with little hope for the future of the NFL as the league has made the refs too important and the group I affectionately call the “Theatre Kids on the Field” took every chance they had to have their “Look at me!” moment. So at last, after a few days of time away from NFL content, I am here to give you a look at what the film said about the game. Takeaways from the Film Brock Bowers is a Problem Brock Bowers is the best player I've watched this year and it was only his first game back from injury. #Raiders have a true X-Factor. Will be fun to watch how Klint Kubiak continues to utilize his unique skillset. Here he wins vs man coverage against a CB1 to convert a 3&7. pic.twitter.com/baGQmkFnHK — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 30, 2026 Brandon Staley is once again my first point of discussion this week as he had the unenviable task of trying to decipher how to stop Brock Bowers in his first game action of the 2026 season. While no one could predict the future and tell how the Raiders would be using their best player (sorry, Maxx Crosby), it was evident that Klint Kubiak had been thinking about Bowers for a long, long time. Vegas was able to stay in heavy personnel for most of the game and present looks that almost no other teams in the NFL would be capable of achieving. How Bowers was positioned all over the field while the Raiders stayed in 22 personnel (2 running backs & 2 tight ends) reminded me of how Sean Payton would use Jimmy Graham and proved to be a handful for any package the Saints threw at him. When watching the film it was hard to not keep cheering for my fantasy tight end (I drafted him and Trey McBride in the 2nd and 3rd rounds and am 3-0, no big deal) as Kubiak’s plan of using him as WR1 on their team seemed to work just as they planned. The Saints simply did not do enough to pressure Kirk Cousins (Key to Victory Number 1: X) into making mistakes and left too many yards in the flats that the veteran quarterback was able to take advantage of all day in their play action passing game which allowed Bowers and Michael Mayer to thrive. The #Raiders offense is going to be very dangerous if they can execute the run game better. With Bowers back they can stay in 22 personnel and run any scheme they want to. #Saints had the unfortunate task of trying to stop Bowers with no previous tape on him in this offense. pic.twitter.com/UbfHQR1EBW — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 30, 2026 Win the Rushing Battle The only key to victory from last week’s preview that the Saints were able to accomplish was winning the rushing battle. While the Raiders defense made their fair share of plays to stop the Saints rushing attack, the ground game seemed to be getting into a grove before Travis Eitienne went down with a hamstring injury. Las Vegas wasn’t able to do much on the ground outside of their 36 yard rushing touchdown by rookie Mike Washington Jr and the Saints held firm in the redzone as they were able to put a stop to Ashton Jeanty for most of the afternoon. Vernon Broughton and Khristian Boyd (below) were two young players that stood out with their efforts against the run game as the youth of the Saints defensive front continues to impress me. Nonetheless this will still be an area where the Saints need to improve on offense as they were clearly missing Kelvin Banks Jr. and Eitienne down the stretch in the fourth quarter and will need to rely on this aspect of the offense in games going forward. @KhristianBoyd99 was very impressive on multiple occasions vs the #Raiders . Here he makes a crucial stop in the redzone. Excited to see how he continues to develop this year in the #Saints defense. pic.twitter.com/nTYW5OALGT — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 30, 2026 Costly Mistakes #Saints were killed by 4th Quarter turnovers this weekend vs the #Raiders : This was Malcom Koonce (#51) 2nd forced turnover of the quarter. Perfect timing on the pressure for the #Raiders turned into a perfect storm type of disaster for the #Saints pic.twitter.com/FdR2o8uBtM — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 30, 2026 The 4th quarter of the game couldn’t have gone worse for the Saints as their drive chart sounded eerily similar to a Sarah McLachlan special (IYKYK) and read the following: Fumble, Interception, Fumble, Fumble. This put a king sized sharpie strike through my Key to Victory Number 3: Mistake Free Football. In his first start replacing Kelvin Banks Jr. at left tackle, Asim Richards held up well against the Raiders until the 4th quarter when he seemed to unravel in front of our very eyes and Malcom Koonce was able to make two game changing plays from the right end position. Juwan Johnson had a great game that included 2 touchdowns off of 8 receptions and 53 yards, but was unable to avoid the turnover bug that plagued the team a committed a costly fumble that ended the Saints final drive. End of the Day Despite how frustrating the Zebras were, the Saints were not able to capitalize on the many chances they had to win this game and ended the day -3 in turnover margin. A recipe for disaster. This will be a defining moment for the Saints season as the film suggests they were the better team on Sunday, but the emotional toll of a loss like this will test the moral of the team and the leadership skills of coaches and captains alike. While this team is young and the situation is much different from the last few “all in to win” years of Brees’s career (although it might feel different in some corners of the Who Dat Nation), the Saints now find themselves in a must win game to get ahead of the NFC South while they can. I will be in attendance for the game on Monday vs that team from Atlanta and hope to see a team that is hungry to right the wrongs that were on display Sunday.

title: Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona offense poses challenges for New York
summary: The New York Giants will host the 1-2 Arizona Cardinals at 1 p.m. Sunday, with Arizona favored by 2.5 points and the Over/Under set at 44.5. The Cardinals opened the season with a surprising 26-14 road victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, though Los Angeles has since shown itself to be a struggling team. Arizona […]
full_text: Jacoby Brissett has been a pleasant surprise | Getty Images The New York Giants will host the 1-2 Arizona Cardinals at 1 p.m. Sunday, with Arizona favored by 2.5 points and the Over/Under set at 44.5. The Cardinals opened the season with a surprising 26-14 road victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, though Los Angeles has since shown itself to be a struggling team. Arizona followed that win with a lopsided 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 2, but bounced back with a strong showing against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 3, falling 36-30 in a more competitive game, especially after trailing 23-6. The Giants are 2-1, coming off an uninspiring 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Jameis Winston has struggled over the past two weeks, and he’ll face an Arizona defense that surrendered 297 passing yards and four touchdowns to Brock Purdy in Week 3, following a Week 2 performance in which Drew Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns. The seat is beginning to warm up for Winston. New York traded a 2027 fifth-round pick for J.J. McCarthy, raising an obvious question: How much longer will the Giants tolerate inconsistent quarterback play? Can New York’s defense continue giving the offense enough opportunities to win close games, as it did in Week 3? Complementary football has long eluded the Giants. The special teams unit has been a bright spot, but the defense faces a major test against Arizona—especially after the injury to Brian Burns. Can New York’s defense hold up without one of its leaders against an Arizona team that’s shown more competency than many anticipated, despite their 1-2 record? Let’s look at the Cardinals’ personnel and statistics to answer that question. The Cardinals’ offense Over three games, the Cardinals rank 18th in points per game, averaging 21 points per game. The Giants are 28th in the NFL, averaging 15.3 points per game. The Cardinals rank 23rd in total yards, averaging 303 yards per game, while the Giants allow 271 yards per game, ranking 29th in the league. Arizona ranks 15th in third-down conversion rate (41%) and 20th in red-zone touchdown rate ( 55% ). The Cardinals average 210 passing yards per game ( 17th in the NFL ) and 93 rushing yards per game ( 25th ). However, running back Jeremiyah Love — who was selected in the top five — saw his role increase significantly against the 49ers. He had a 63% snap share after just 42% in Week 2. Love suffered a high-ankle sprain in preseason Week 1, leading to heavy usage for Tyler Allgeier in the first two weeks of the season. Allgeier will have a role, but Mike LaFleur seems comfortable showcasing the talents of Love, who had 26 total touches in Week 3, which is what had TOTAL in his first two games. Love has 160 yards on 41 carries (3.9 YPC), with one touchdown, 2.76 yards after contact, and five missed tackles forced. Allgeier has 24 carries for 70 yards ( 2.9 YPC ), with 2.38 yards after contact and five missed tackles forced as well. The Cardinals run a lot of DUO up front and want to displace at the point of attack in the run game. Paris Johnson Jr. starts at left tackle and Elijah Wilkinson is the starting right tackle. The latter has struggled as a run blocker, while the former continues to be one of the better young tackles in football. Isaac Seumalo and Isaiah Adams start on the interior — both bigger, more physical interior offensive linemen — and Hjalte Froholdt is their starting center. The Giants have to expect a similar DUO blocking scheme that they faced against the Rams in Week 2 — New York surrendered 163 yards on the ground against Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Expect Love’s role to be similar to Week 3, with Allgeier working in on short-yardage and to spell the talented young rookie. The wide receiver situation in Arizona is interesting, to say the least. 2024 Top-five pick Marvin Harrison Jr. looks completely disinterested and has appeared this way through two coaching staffs. The Internet believes he could be traded. Here’s Mike LaFleur responding to a question about plays being designed for the disgruntled young receiver: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur on if he has plays specifically designed for Marvin Harrison Jr. “The thing about the guys that are actually catching the football is they're in command and not in control.” Via ( @AZCardinals ) pic.twitter.com/MiMXvjnOg3 — Andrew Bernson (@andrewbernson) September 25, 2026 Harrison Jr. has four receptions on nine targets for 73 yards through three games, despite playing more than 70% of the snaps in each game. Tight end Trey McBride has been a target monster, leading the team with 31 targets and catching 26 for 211 yards and two touchdowns. Michael Wilson continues to outshine Harrison Jr. The former Stanford Cardinal has been sensational with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. Wilson averages 10.6 targets and 85.3 yards per game across the last 11 matchups; the Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase averages 10 targets and 79.7 yards per game through that same span. AZ Cardinals WR Michael Wilson cut ups from week 3 There’s just so much to love about Wilson, the elite hands, the physicality, the IQ. He rocks. Only 3 weeks of tape obviously, but I’m comfortable saying he has improved as a route runner in 2027 and looks to be ascending still pic.twitter.com/ItwkJIIqMy — Jason Lewis (@Jasonlewis54) September 28, 2026 Michael Wilson #AZCardinals Good out vs outside leverage. The head and eyes tell the story at the top of the stem and flat break. pic.twitter.com/INqKkIAgkc — Matt Waldman (@MattWaldman) September 28, 2026 Michael Wilson 4th and 2 conversion. Feet-switch and counters defender's hand which prevents any call of a push off. #AZCardinals pic.twitter.com/3pq6eChUjI — Matt Waldman (@MattWaldman) September 28, 2026 Wilson has 18 catches on 27 targets for 163 yards and a touchdown. New York will have its hands full with both Wilson and McBride. Kendrick Bourne is the third receiver, and he’s been efficient, catching 12 of 14 targets for 108 yards. The matchup Brissett is playing good football. He’s keeping the Cardinals’ offense on track with a quick, efficient passing attack that matches up well against the Giants. Brissett is completing 70% of his passes with 652 passing yards, four touchdowns, and just one interception. He has a 1.6% big-time throw rate and a 2.3% turnover-worthy play rate, and his receivers have dropped 4.7% of his passes, with 5.6 yards per attempt. Brissett’s surface-level statistics check out with the more advanced analytics. The Arizona offense ranks 11th in the NFL in EPA (Expected Points Added) per play; they’re especially efficient in short EPA (7th in the NFL), while ranking 27th in deep EPA. The Cardinals, however, are dead last in explosive-play EPA. Arizona is specifically good out of 11 and 13 personnel, recording the ninth-best EPA from the former and the third-best from the latter. Their 13 personnel package consists of McBride, Eliah Higgins, and Hunter Long. Tight end Tip Reiman is injured, which has affected the Cardinals’ ability to run effectively. The Giants may look to dial up more pressure without star pass rusher Burns, but Brissett has done well against pressure. He is sixth in EPA when pressures, but 16th in EPA against the blitz. The Cardinals have used 11 personnel at a 62% rate, 12 personnel at a 12% rate, and 13 personnel at an 18% rate. Expect the Giants to align in nickel against 11 and stay mostly in base versus heavier personnel. The addition of Jihad Ward — who is familiar with Dennard Wilson’s scheme — should lead to a different role for Kayvon Thibodeaux, who will be replacing Burns. There could be lighter fronts in passing situations with Ward, Abdul Carter, Thibodeaux, and Chauncey Golston. New York ran middle-of-the-field closed often against Cam Ward and the Titans. The Giants may align a bit more in middle-of-the-field open against Brissett. New York should be getting Tae Banks back to help the secondary. Brissett has done well against single-high…
author: Nick Falato

title: Despite McCarthy-mania, Matt Nagy reminds that Jameis Winston is the Giants’ QB
summary: During his weekly press conference on Thursday, New York Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy was peppered with questions about newly-acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Nagy answered them, but he did remind that it is important to remember that Jameis Winston, not McCarthy, is the team’s starting quarterback. “I think it’s important to say, I understand the […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Getty Images During his weekly press conference on Thursday, New York Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy was peppered with questions about newly-acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Nagy answered them, but he did remind that it is important to remember that Jameis Winston, not McCarthy, is the team’s starting quarterback. “I think it’s important to say, I understand the questions on J.J., I get it, but I also don’t want to lose sight of where we’re at with the time that we’re spending on Jameis,” Nagy said. Winston is 25 of 49 (51%) for 229 yards with no touchdowns, one interception, a passer rating of just 55.6, a league worst QBR of 22.9, and an EPA per play of -0.31, 34th of 36 graded quarterbacks. The Giants did win the game Winston started despite having to settle for four field goals in a 12-7 victory. “So, the first game with the Rams, that’s not easy. That’s a difficult situation to walk into. So, that one’s a little tough to fairly criticize, I think, in my opinion,” Nagy said. “Then the second game, there was a little bit of weather, or whether we like it or not, that’s what’s real. So, but at the same point in time, we need to score touchdowns. That’s what, it’s my job as offensive coordinator. It’s our job as players. “And so, I have a ton of trust. And I really feel great about what’s about to happen and what he can do. And I think he’s got a resume that’s shown that. And our players, our coaches, everyone here believes in Jameis, everybody. There’s no doubt. We just got to go out there and we got to do it. And scoring touchdowns will help that confidence. Scoring touchdowns will help that trust and that belief.” Malik Nabers echoed Nagy’s faith in Winston. “I think we got pretty good confidence in Jameis on his ability to throw the ball downfield, do play action, get involved with the run game. So, I feel like Jameis can do a lot in this offense,” Nabers said. “Jameis has been a part of a lot of different offense. So, this offense is probably nothing different than what he’s already seen. So, we got pretty good confidence in his ability to give us the ball and manage the offense.” McCarthy-mania No matter how many times you remind Giants fans, or most of the media, that Winston is the quarterback and will be until he plays his way out of the job, the attention is all on McCarthy and how quickly the Giants can get him ready to play. “There’s a lot involved, it takes some time, I guess is my point, what I’m saying,” Nagy said. “So, what our job is going to be is to balance it, to see what’s fair to him. What can he handle, what’s real? And then you just go from there. And I think that’s where, as long as we all have kind of the same standards and expectations as we go through this, then that’s only fair to everybody.” Nagy was non-committal about whether McCarthy would know enough to be the No. 2 quarterback vs. the Arizona Cardinals, or possibly be used in a sub-package. “What’s most realistic to get him ready to be a backup, right? That’s where you start, and that’s where we’re at, and that process takes some time,” Nagy said. “And there’s a little bit of realization in knowing it’s not going to happen in one or two days. I think that’s only fair, but we just got to see each and every day how much can he handle, and then we continue to throw more and more at him, and then we got to make our own judgment on, now, what is he doing on the field, and where does that take him as a number two or number three?”
author: Ed Valentine

title: Giants vs. Cardinals: Arizona defense presents an opportunity
summary: Can the New York Giants get their offense on track against the Arizona Cardinals? That’s one of the big questions hanging over the team as they enter Week 4. The Giants offense has been, in a word, bad since their surgical, suffocating win over the Dallas Cowboys back in week 1. Since then, they’ve scored […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Can the New York Giants get their offense on track against the Arizona Cardinals? That’s one of the big questions hanging over the team as they enter Week 4. The Giants offense has been, in a word, bad since their surgical, suffocating win over the Dallas Cowboys back in week 1. Since then, they’ve scored 6 points in a loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2 and a whopping 12 points against the Tennessee Titans in Week 3. That isn’t going to cut it going forward, and the Giants need to figure out their offense. Will that start against the Cardinals? The Cardinals’ defense The Cardinals were one of the (many) teams to hire a new head coach this offseason, hiring Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur. LaFleur made the surprising decision to retain Nick Rallis as the Cardinals defensive coordinator rather than start fresh on that side of the ball. Rallis has been the Cardinals’ defensive coordinator since 2023, which means that the decision to keep him gives the Giants much more tape to plan for his scheme and tendencies than they’d have if LeFleur hired a new coordinator. And while Rallis spent two years coaching linebackers for the Philadelphia Eagles (2021 and 2022), he isn’t the same kind of “Fangio Adjacent” defensive mind that the Giants have seen in each of the first three weeks of the season. Instead, he runs an unorthodox defensive scheme that’s built on a “three-deep” coverage shell and the versatility of safety Budda Baker. By using a three-deep coverage shell, the Cardinals look to both take away explosive plays as well as add uncertainty to quarterbacks’ pre-snap reads. They typically play with three defensive linemen, leading to light boxes that invite runs. However, Rallis makes heavy use of disguise in his scheme and led the NFL by disguising his defense on 70% of plays last year. To do that, he relies chiefly on Baker as a flex player who can either play deep or rotate down into the tackle box as a MONEY backer, or safety/linebacker hybrid. That allows the Cardinals to effectively play base 3-4 concepts against heavier personnel sets or nickel concepts against lighter sets, as well as fluidly transition between base and nickel defenses on a moment’s notice. Unfortunately for the Cardinals, they lost starting cornerback Will Johnson to a neck injury, forcing 2025 fifth- round pick Denzel Burke into the starting role. Burke started eight games for the Cardinals last year and played relatively well, though he had eight missed tackles. This year he seems to have taken a step backward and surrendered a 72.7% completion rate, two touchdowns, and 9.1 yards per target through three games (one start) It’s worth noting that none of the Cardinals’ corners are taller than 5-foot-11, which could present an opportunity for Malachi Fields and Isaiah Likely. More importantly, while the Cardinals’ defense is unorthodox and generally well-schemed… It hasn’t been very good this year. They’re bottom three in the NFL with 0.15 EPA per play added to to the opposing offense , bottom three in passing touchdowns allowed (eight), as well as giving up a league-worst 6.5 yards per play. Their run defense has been better than their pass defense, however they’re still in the bottom third of the NFL in yards and yards per carry allowed. Overall, the scheme of the Cardinals’ defense will put the onus on Matt Nagy and Jameis Winston to decipher their rotations. Once they do, however, their propensity to run zone coverages and Cover 3 offers opportunities for Malik Nabers and Darnell Mooney to pick up yards after the catch, while Fields and Likely are proving to be effective zone busters. Likewise, their tendency to play lighter packages and counter the run with scheme may be an opportunity for the run-heavy Giants. That said, the Giants may look to use pulling blockers and attack the edges of the Cardinals’ defense if they play more TITE fronts to clog interior gaps. Jameis Winston at quarterback, again Giants’ head coach John Harbaugh confirmed after the Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy that Winston would remain the starting quarterback through the foreseeable future. However, that doesn’t mean that his job is safe indefinitely. Winston has been shaky — at best — since taking over for Jaxson Dart. He hasn’t appeared sure of his reads, has held the ball at times, and has consistently thrown short of his targets. Winston, and the Giants were able to do enough to beat the Titans, but only because the defense — and elements — shut Tennessee out in the first half. The question is how much of Winston’s performance was due to a short week and the nor’easter. Can Winston settle in and finally develop a rapport with his receivers on a normal week of practice and find them on a sunny fall day? Matt Nagy and the Giants’ brain trust has generally done a decent job of creating easy answers for their quarterback. Winston’s targets were open by an average of 3.3 yards against the Titans and he only attempted a tight window throw on three passes. It seems likely at this point that the Cardinals will almost certainly use their base defense concepts to gap out the Giants’ offensive front. We’ll likely see Baker playing downhill while the Cardinals use a TITE front to try and force the Giants’ slower running backs to run laterally. The Giants want to run the ball. They have the seventh-most rushing attempts in the NFL despite having the sixth-fewest drives in the NFL. It seems likely that the Cardinals will plan to force Winston to prove that he can beat them with his arm. The Giants’ ball control offense looked suffocating in Week 1, but it needs to end in touchdowns to work. Not only do the Giants have the sixth-fewest drives in the NFL, their average drive eats up the most clock in the NFL. That means that points are at a premium, because they simply don’t get many opportunities per game to score with the style of football they want to play. New York may need Winston to prove that he’s still a productive passer in order to open things up for the run game if Arizona decides that the Giants won’t beat them on the ground. The red zone offense The Giants did a pretty good job of moving the ball between the 20’s against the Titans’ defense, particularly in the second half. The were largely able to do what they wanted and pretty easily marched down the field to get into scoring position multiple times. However, their red zone offense was both bad, weird… And utterly ineffective. It’s possible that Nagy didn’t fully trust Winston in the red zone, particularly the low red zone where the defense is the most condensed and the game is the fastest. It’s also possible that the Giants were wary of the tricky conditions brought about by the storm. Whatever the reason, they squandered every opportunity to score touchdowns and build a commanding lead over the Titans. The Giants had nine plays against the Titans in the red zone. Of them, only two were passing plays and of the seven running plays, only one (a toss to Najee Harris from the 16 yard line) got more than 10 yards. Likewise, of the Giants’ nine red zone plays, only two were vertical — a run up the middle by Cam Skattebo and a pass into the end zone from Winston. Everything else was designed to go laterally. That’s a stark contrast from what the Giants did in Week 1 against the Cowboys. They had 12 plays in the Red Zone against the Cowboys, seven of which were vertical, while five were designed to be lateral. The Giants had four red zone plays against the Rams, and only one of them (an off tackle run by Harris) began by advancing the ball toward the end zone. And even the run by Harris still had a downhill component. It’s certainly possible that Winston isn’t reading the defense quickly enough or isn’t fully comfortable with the scheme or receivers. But that shouldn’t excuse play calls and play designs that actively work against the strengths of the…

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to host the Arizona Cardinals. Giants star LB Brian Burns tore meniscus as well as ACL: Sources | The Athletic New York Giants star outside linebacker Brian Burns tore the lateral meniscus in his right knee, in addition to tearing his ACL, according to league and team sources who spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak publicly about the injury. Burns was scheduled to undergo surgery to repair both injuries Thursday at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York City. The typical timeline for recovery from ACL and meniscus surgery is 9-to-12 months. Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers suffered a similar injury on Sept. 28 last season. Even after a second “clean-up” surgery to remove scar tissue interrupted his rehabilitation, Nabers was ready for the start of the 2026 season. Sacks will come: DC Dennard Wilson "It's going to come, be patient. When it comes, it just keeps coming – just like interceptions, takeaways. Once you get one, you start to feed off it. It will come, be patient. Maybe the dam breaks this week, you don't know." – Dennard Wilson on the Giants' defense pic.twitter.com/H9cqCmt4dk — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 1, 2026 Giants’ Arvell Reese heating up with Cardinals’ Jeremiyah Love on deck | New York Daily News When Reese is running and hitting the way he did against Tennessee, it makes him that much more dangerous when the Giants use him on the edge or as a blitzer. That’s when his mindset truly stands out: When he’s running in a straight line to the ball. “Anytime we ask him to hit somebody his eyes light up,” said linebackers coach Frank Bush. “He really takes pride in the run game and being physical. It’s not just rhetoric with him. He wants to be dominating that way. So yeah, when we blitz him, his eyes light up a little bit…Because in his mind he can affect the game that way. Not a lot of thinking. It’s just a straight line, and if I whoop this guy’s ass, I got a chance.” Inside the mind of this Giants weapon and NFL’s best punter ∣ The Record There is an underlying truth with regard to Jordan Stout that only becomes more evident the longer you watch him punt for the New York Giants. Stout opens up about his goals, growing pains from rookie year to now, replacing a legend in Baltimore and making an impact. Shelby Harris calls New York Giants ideal spot for J.J. McCarthy | USAToday.com “Well, what I will say is he’s stepping into an organization that has the best coaching staff, especially on the offensive side of the ball, best coaching staff with a lot of star power on that side of the ball,” Harris said. “You gotta think the QB coach is Brian Callahan, a former head coach, literally just head coached last year. Then you have Matt Nagy at OC, you have Greg Roman as run game coordinator. “So you have these guys who have so much experience in the game that I feel like it’s truly the best situation for a young quarterback to come into, to learn from a guy who’s worked with Andy Reid. You have guys who have been around the league that have over 30 years of experience almost each.” Nabers on J.J. McCarthy Malik Nabers knew J.J. McCarthy before college Nabers on what he's seen so far: "Strong arm…he's catching on quick. He has confidence, he's targeting receivers pretty well." pic.twitter.com/IVsvtRsAWY — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 1, 2026 J.J. McCarthy introduces himself to Giants as ‘a baller and a competitor’ | NJ.com J.J. McCarthy stood on a stage in front of his new Giants teammates during Wednesday’s team meeting and started to speak. Whenever the Giants add a player, coach John Harbaugh has him address the entire team in the same way: Say your name, where you’re from and what your purpose and identity in life are. McCarthy said something else that stuck with rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields. “He’s a baller and a competitor, he said,” Fields recounted to NJ.com later Wednesday. “He’s fired up to help us out in whatever way he can. I’m excited to get to know him and see what he can do.” What Jim Harbaugh told brother John about J.J. McCarthy before Giants trade | New York Post Jim Harbaugh spoke with reporters in Los Angeles on Wednesday and said he chatted with John Harbaugh before the Giants traded a fifth-round pick to the Vikings for McCarthy on Monday. “I mean, John called me and asked me,” Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday. “I said, ‘You know, John, I love you. I love J.J. I think you guys would be — ’ so, really, I’m telling you the same thing that I told my brother.” J.J. McCarthy traded to Giants: Will he succeed in New York? | ESPN.com The Giants don’t need McCarthy to shoulder the workload. This is going to be a run-heavy team, built through their offensive line, heavy personnel groupings and a Cam Skattebo-led backfield. McCarthy can make an impact with his legs, where he ran for 181 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. The Giants can retain some of the RPOs they installed for Dart, giving McCarthy easy answers for confidence-building completions. McCarthy was at his best booting out of the pocket and getting on the run, where his QBR in 2025 was a solid 67.7 — more than 40 points better than where it landed from throws inside the pocket (27.5). In a carefully crafted offense, McCarthy can make this work. And given that the Giants are paying him less than $1 million over the rest of the season, he doesn’t have to be great for this deal to pay off. Winston hasn’t been able to move the ball, and while the weather was a real factor against the Titans, he was missing open receivers by yards against the Rams in Week 2. title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 4 preview – Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to Week 4! Another week, another spate of injuries. That’s been one of the themes this season, but honestly, it’s a theme every season in the NFL, and I don’t think 2026 is much worse than a typical year – so far. It’s a violent game, played by young men who are uncommonly big, […]
full_text: Guess who leads the NFL in passing yards? | Getty Images Welcome to Week 4! Another week, another spate of injuries. That’s been one of the themes this season, but honestly, it’s a theme every season in the NFL, and I don’t think 2026 is much worse than a typical year – so far. It’s a violent game, played by young men who are uncommonly big, fast, and strong. Another theme this season – which also happens every year – is massive early-season underperformance from players who were drafted to be starters on fantasy teams. Do you just wait it out, hoping they’ll turn it around? When do you pull the plug and play someone else? Can you drop them? The answers vary by player and obviously depend on multiple factors, including your roster, your record, and your pain tolerance. What’s worse – continuing to roll out Kyle Pitts ( three fantasy points, total , in three games in Half-PPR) – or benching him and watching him go off? These healthy players were all drafted in the Top-100 (roughly the first eight rounds of drafts in a 12-team league), and are the biggest underperformers thus far: QB: Drake Maye, Justin Herbert RB: David Montgomery (despite the 3-TD outburst in Week 1 – he’s averaged 4.6 fantasy points across the last two weeks), Rhamondre Stevenson, Jadarian Price, Kenneth Gainwell WR: George Pickens, Malik Nabers, Rome Odunze, Courtland Sutton, Carnell Tate, Marvin Harrison, Jr., Brian Thomas, Jr., Quentin Johnston TE: Colston Loveland, Tucker Kraft, Kyle Pitts, Sr. The good news is that almost all of these players were drafted outside the Top-50. Some of the players drafted in the Top-50 have disappointed as well (Saquon Barkley, Chase Brown, Omarion Hampton, Jaylen Waddle, and Ladd McConkey, to name a few), but they’ve at least mostly been playable. Of course, some of these players are worth considering as “buy-low” candidates, from managers losing patience with them. Stats of the Week : The Bucs are 0-12 against the spread (ATS) in their last 12 games. Drake Maye committed 11 turnovers in the entire 2025 regular season (he played all 17 games). In his last seven games (2025 playoffs, plus 2026 regular season), he has 15 turnovers. Nothing changes department: The two South divisions are each a cumulative 3-9 through three weeks. The Raiders have already won as many games (3) as they did all last season. The Vikings are 3-0 despite (a) not topping 250 yards of offense in any of their games, and (b) being outgained by their opponent in every game. BAL@DAL was the first game in the Super Bowl era with two field goals made in the final ten seconds. I’d give Brian Schottenheimer the 2026 Flavor Flav Clock Management Award, but Aaron Glenn (Week 2 vs. Packers) says it’s his to keep and if anyone wants it, they’ll have to pry it from his cold, dead hands. OK, Week 4, here we go! Note: The WAS@IND game is in London – set those lineups early! Bye Weeks: NONE Week 4 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Kenneth Walker . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade ,and Sleeper of the Week . The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did pretty well, for the most part. My two Sleepers of the Week, Sam Darnold and Geno Smith, both topped 25 fantasy points and finished as the QB2 and QB3 on the Week. Who was the QB1? Brock Purdy, who was my first Ride quarterback listed. Full disclosure: I whiffed on Justin Herbert. You can check my work here. *** Ride of the Week: Tetairoa McMillan (vs. DET). McMillan has been overshadowed by teammate Jalen Coker so far this season, but he hasn’t been bad, and in any case that should change on Sunday. Coker suffered a quad injury on Sunday and is questionable for this week. Meanwhile, the Lions have topped 30 points scored in every game so far, and this contest has shootout written all over it (the Vegas total is 50.5, which is the second highest on the board). Detroit’s secondary is a banged-up mess, and on the young season they’ve allowed the third most fantasy points per game (FPPG) to opposing WRs. Tet should get his on Sunday night. Fade of the Week: Emeka Egbuka (vs. GB). Baker Mayfield is going to miss this game and probably a couple more, so I’ll stick with the second-year receiver theme with my Fade. I’m not sure why Tampa went into the season with an undrafted rookie as the backup to a QB who suffered about 50 different injuries last season, but here we are. Any given week could be Todd Bowles’s last with this organization, and while the Packers’ defense is nothing special, do you really want to trust Jalon Daniels in his first NFL start? It’s unraveling fast for the Bucs, and Egbuka is a sit for me this week in what could be another very ugly offensive performance for Tampa. Sleeper of the Week: Marcus Mariota (vs. IND). Mariota drew a tough matchup in his first start (SEA) and managed to lead his team to an improbable win. It gets much easier this week, against the Colts in London. They’ve allowed the second most passing yards and fifth most FPPG to opposing QBs. Mariota is still a decent dual-threat, and with his own defense being among the league’s worst against the pass, there should be a need to put up big points this week. If you need a second QB, or even a streamer in a one-QB format, you could do worse. He’s ranked outside the Top-15 this week and I like him for a low-end QB-1 finish. I’ll give you a bonus Sleeper of the Week: Darren Waller (vs. DET). All he does is score TDs, and all the Lions do is give up TDs to his position. They’ve allowed six , to six different tight ends, in just three games! No, that’s not a typo. Like Mariota, Waller is ranked outside the Top-15 at his position, and I think that’s too low. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, and Patrick Mahomes ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Jared Goff (@CAR) should have another productive week. His team will probably need to break 30 again to win. It’s easier to run on the Panthers, but he’ll do enough with his arm. In the same matchup, give me Bryce Young (vs. DET). I’ll say it again: Detroit’s secondary is a hot mess. The Lions have allowed the second most TD passes (9) and the most FPPG to opposing QBs, and Young has put up huge numbers in two of three games on the young season. Others in the Top-15 who I think will outperform their ranking this week: Joe Burrow (vs. JAC, in what could be a high-scoring affair) and Tyler Shough (vs. ATL). Sleepers: If you need a second QB in a Superflex, there are once again some nice options, including Geno Smith (@CHI), Jacoby Brissett ( @NYG), C.J. Stroud (vs. DAL and their terrible pass defense, and especially if he gets Nico Collins back), Sam Darnold (vs. LAC), and Daniel Jones (@WAS, most TD passes (11) and second most FPPG allowed to opposing QBs). Jameis Winston (vs. ARI) hasn’t been good, but I’d write some of that off to the circumstances of his first appearance, and the horrible weather in his second. It’s a good matchup at home (Brock Purdy just lit them up for four TDs), he’s put up big numbers before, and he might feel some pressure to get it done this week after the team just acquired J.J. McCarthy. I like…

title: NFL predictions: BBV staff weighs in on Giants-Cardinals matchup
summary: Can the New York Giants make the first quarter of their 2026 season a truly good one by defeating the Arizona Cardinals to improve their record to 3-1? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the NFL Week 4 slate. Chris Pflum I think this game is […]
full_text: Can the New York Giants make the first quarter of their 2026 season a truly good one by defeating the Arizona Cardinals to improve their record to 3-1? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the NFL Week 4 slate. Chris Pflum I think this game is going to be extremely telling as to who the 2026 Giants are. This will be offense’s first game with Jameis Winston going through a normal week of practice and preparation. That’ll eliminate the excuses we’ve heard regarding the game plan against the Rams, as well as the short week and elements last week. Will the Giants trust Winston to throw the ball? And how will he execute if they do? Excuses aside, Winston hasn’t looked good since Dart went down. The Giants will need him to step up if Arizona focuses on shutting down the Giants’ run game. On the defensive side of the ball, we’ll get to see how the Giants adapt to losing their best player in Brian Burns. The Cardinals put up points against the 49ers, but was that just divisional weirdness? They only scored once against the Seahawks the week before. I’m going to pick the Giants here, and I’m doing so because of one thing that stood out from Sunday: Multiple veterans of the 2025 Giants all saying some variation of “We don’t win this game last year.” Sometimes winning isn’t pretty. Sometimes it really is just surviving and making one fewer mistake than the other guy. And understanding that they can claw their way through adversity and not collapse could be bigger than we realize for this team. I still think the Giants still have the pieces in place to be the same team we saw against Dallas — assuming Jameis Winston can step up. It might not be pretty, and special teams may be the difference in the game, but I think the Giants do enough to win and keep moving forward. Pick: Giants Tony DelGenio To me these are two evenly matched teams. I wouldn’t have said that after Game 1, but the Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns injuries lower the Giants’ level of play on both sides of the ball. The forecast for Sunday is cloudy with a chance of showers. Assuming we don’t get anything like the rain and winds of last weekend, my guess would be a high-scoring game. The Cards’ defensive line is about as good as Tennessee’s, with Zaven Collins playing great outside and Roy Lopez solid in the middle, but like the Giants, they don’t get much pass rush overall and can be run on. The secondary is nothing special either; their best-known player, Budda Baker, is not what he used to be. The bigger problem is the Cards’ offense. Jacoby Brissett is a seen by many as a quality backup-caliber QB, but he has been the starter at least part of the time for five different seasons. Last year he passed for over 3,000 yards and 23 TDs. His favorite target is All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who has had 1,000 receiving yards two years in a row, and we know the Giants never shut down good tight ends. Brissett can also go to WR Michael Wilson, who also broke 1,000 yards last season. With Brian Burns out, unless Dennard Wilson finds a way to get his rushers to the QB, the Cards can put up a lot of points – they’ve broken 30 twice, against the good defenses of the Chargers and 49ers. Rookie RB Jeremiah Love had his best game so far last week with 90 yards, more than half after contact. That said, the Giants can move the ball and put points up themselves if we get good Jameis rather than bad Jameis this week and if the rain holds off. Cam Skattebo should find room to run and the Giants’ receivers should get open enough for them to sustain drives. I can even imagine this being a breakout week for Malik Nabers in which he starts to resemble the force of nature that he was in his rookie year. Overall, I see the Cards having more firepower and coming out on top, say 31-27 if the rain is not a factor. Pick: Cards Nick Falato We are about to learn A LOT about this 2-1 Giants’ team. The Cardinals have been respectable through two weeks and sit at 1-2. They’ve run an efficient quick game, earning them the seventh-highest EPA while running the fifth-most short passes. Brissett has been pressured the sixth most in the league, but the Giants generate the LEAST amount of pressure in the league. Arizona is going to throw quickly to mitigate Abdul Carter and the Giants’ pass rush, which is now significantly worse without Brian Burns. We’ll see new looks from Dennard Wilson’s defense with the addition of Jihad Ward, but the Giants’ cornerbacks MUST make plays on the football, and the defense, overall, must rally and tackle to prevent yards after the catch. The Giants’ offense has struggled to create explosive plays, and the Cardinals’ defense has struggled to stop them. Arizona’s defense hasn’t blitz much ( 27th in blitz rate ), nor do they get much pressure ( 25th in pressure rate ), but Jameis Winston has a tendency to hold onto the football. The Giants are going to use heavier personnel, putting Arizona in a spot to use their BASE defense, which currently ranks 27th in EPA. I expect the Giants to lean on their rushing attack and attempt to run out of 11 personnel, where Arizona will match with nickel ( 27th in EPA in nickel defense ). The Giants will work the play-action and attempt to get Malik Nabers going when they do throw the football, but expect a conservative approach, again, and one that embodies what we’ve discussed since John Harbaugh took the job — physical, heavy personnel, control the clock, and don’t turn the football over. Winston must be cautious with the football. Again, I can see this going in many different ways, but I’ll project a low-scoring victory for the Giants, but we’ll see improvement in the red zone, and the Giants score two touchdowns. Pick: Giants, 20-17 David Hartman Before the season started, Arizona at home in Week 4 looked like one of the safer “wins” on the schedule for Big Blue. Well, guess what? The Cardinals are favored by 2 1/2 points on Sunday at MetLife Stadium. That’s how fast things can change in the NFL. The Giants narrowly escaped with a win over the Titans in the wind and rain last week, and this week’s injury loss for the season is another very costly one: Edge Brian Burns. New York must again regroup in the face of adversity. The 1-2 Cardinals were supposed to be among the very worst teams in the league this season, but so far, they’ve been pretty frisky, and competitive despite a really tough schedule to open the season (@LAC, SEA, @SF). They’ve got weapons on offense that could give the depleted Giants’ defense some real problems – Trey McBride is an elite talent at tight end, rookie RB Jeremiyah Love is dangerously explosive and saw his role expand last week, and WR Michael Wilson came out of nowhere last season and is a very capable receiver. Jacoby Brissett isn’t afraid to chuck the ball all over the field. I really want to take the Giants to win and get to 3-1 on Sunday, but I’m having trouble convincing myself that it’s the smart pick. I’m willing to chalk up a lot of the offensive malaise in Jameis Winston’s first two starts to the circumstances of the first one and the weather in the second one. Still, I think the Cardinals are going to give New York problems on both sides of the ball, and walk out of MetLife with the win. Pick: Arizona in a close one James Hickey The first four games of the modern NFL season is in many ways an extension of training camp. You find out what your team does well and what their issues are that need to be introduced. For the Giants going into their last game of the first quarter of the season, they are actually more unsettled then when the season started due to the losses of their two most important players on the team in consecutive weeks— first Jaxson Dart, then Brian Burns. What the Giants do best on either side of the ball is it. And with the lackluster performance of Jameis Winston necessitating the trade of J.J. McCarthy, that will be leaned on more for the rest of the season. The face an opponent…

title: ‘Disgusted’ Abdul Carter knows the Giants need more pass rush production
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — New York Giants edge defender Abdul Carter is “disgusted” by the team’s pass rush over its first three games, he told Big Blue View this week in an exclusive interview. “Honestly, seeing where we are with our pass rush, I’m honestly disgusted at it, but at the same time, we can’t […]
full_text: Abdul Carter | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — New York Giants edge defender Abdul Carter is “disgusted” by the team’s pass rush over its first three games, he told Big Blue View this week in an exclusive interview. “Honestly, seeing where we are with our pass rush, I’m honestly disgusted at it, but at the same time, we can’t let it discourage us,” Carter said. “Me and Kayvon [Thibodeaux] talked about how better we got to be and how we can be more impactful, just coming in each week, attacking each week harder, doing whatever it takes to get better. At the end of the day, we can’t get discouraged. “Obviously, teams are going to scheme against us and plan for us not to wreck the game, but we’re going to have to find a way.” The Giants will, of course have to find that way without star edge defender Brian Burns, lost for the season due to a knee injury said to include both a torn ACL and meniscus. “It hurts a lot,” Carter said. “Ever since I came in, Brian, he’s always been that guy in our defense we can look at. He does everything right. He practices hard. He plays hard. He makes sure he doesn’t miss his games. “Even when he came back, he played hurt and obviously ended up getting hurt. It shows his character and what type of man he is.” Carter has the Giants’ only sack of the season. He believes the pass rush will make its mark. “We pride ourselves on being able to get to the quarterback. That’s what we get paid to do,” he said. “I’m going to keep saying we can’t get discouraged. We can’t lose our confidence.We have to keep rushing, keep playing hard, and it’ll open up.” Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has not lost faith. “It’s there. It’s going to come. Be patient,” Wilson said. “And when it comes, it just keeps coming, okay? Just like interceptions, just like takeaways. Once you get one, you start to feed off of it. The guys start to have that feeling, and it will come. Be patient. It’s coming. And maybe the dam breaks this week. You don’t know.” Wilson said the coaching staff is tinkering with ways to find better matchups. “We’re looking at it, we have to put them in better positions for them to go ahead and take off a little bit,” he said. “Right now, obviously, the production hasn’t been there with the sack totals and everything like that, and we take full responsibility as a coaching staff to get that going. A lot of it is moving pieces around, trying to get different players in different spots so they can have more success, being able to dent the pocket in the A and B gaps. “Those are things that we’re working on and we’re still chasing it. It’s still early in the season, and early in the season it’s not where we want it, but we still have a lot of games to go to get where we want in terms of that.” Carter said players need to look in the mirror. “I think that’s where you got to start,” he said. “I think whenever you’re struggling with something, first you got to look in the mirror and look at yourself and see what you can do better first. I think you should start there and then I feel like everything else should come after that.”

title: NY Giants safety Jevon Holland named NFC Defensive Player Of the Month
summary: New York Giants safety Jevon Holland has been named the NFC Defensive Player of The Month for the month of September. Holland has been simply fantastic through the first three games of the season. He’s notched 3 interceptions and 4 passes defensed, recording an interception in each of the first three games of the year, […]
full_text: New York Giants safety Jevon Holland makes a game-winning interception against the Tennessee Titans.﻿ | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New York Giants safety Jevon Holland has been named the NFC Defensive Player of The Month for the month of September. Holland has been simply fantastic through the first three games of the season. He’s notched 3 interceptions and 4 passes defensed, recording an interception in each of the first three games of the year, and his timely interception of He’s also only been targeted in coverage 8 times, and allowed just 2 receptions for a total of 59 yards and is allowing a passer rating of 57.8, by far the best of his career. His timely interception of Cam Ward sealed the Giants’ win over the Tennessee Titans. Doug Farrar recently listed Holland as one of the NFL’s “ Secret Superstars ”, though I suspect the secret is out. Some may view Holland’s play to start 2026 as a surprise, however there were indications in 2025 that he could be on the verge of a breakout campaign. While Holland’s box score stats weren’t impressive, his advanced metrics — notably his completion percentage allowed, yards per target allowed, passer rating allowed, and missed tackle rate — were all comparable to former Giant Xavier McKinny. Also notable was that Holland wasn’t credited with a pair of interceptions (including a pick-6) that were negated by penalties elsewhere on the defense. This year, Holland seems to have put it all together and is thriving in Dennard Wilson’s more aggressive defensive scheme. Now, Holland is emerging as a key piece for the Giants’ defense and a true difference maker for the team. This was exactly what the Giants hoped for when they signed Holland away from the Miami Dolphins to a thre-year, $45.3 million contract prior to the 2025 season.

title: Joey Porter Jr. is a Cowboy, was apparently never going to be a Giant
summary: Joey Porter Jr. is now a member of the Dallas Cowboys, having been traded from the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday evening. Despite fervent fan speculation, it turns out Porter Jr. was apparently never going to be a member of the New York Giants. NFL insider Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post tweeted that the […]
full_text: Joey Porter Jr. | Getty Images Joey Porter Jr. is now a member of the Dallas Cowboys, having been traded from the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday evening. Despite fervent fan speculation, it turns out Porter Jr. was apparently never going to be a member of the New York Giants. NFL insider Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post tweeted that the Giants “ were never involved ” in trade discussions for Porter Jr. despite an apparent need at the cornerback position. Dunleavy did, though, add that the Giants “could be aggressive again here and CB is a spot to keep an eye on given injuries.” The Cowboys, 25th in the league in points and 30th in yards allowed, and with injuries to defensive backs Shavon Revel Jr., and Cobee Bryant, acquired the 27-year-old Porter in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. Porter, seeking a new mega-contract, had not played a snap for the Steelers in the first three games. Stunningly, Jerry Jones and the Cowboys agreed to the trade without signing Porter Jr. to a contract extension . The Giants had a chance to draft Porter Jr. in 2023. Instead, they traded up to select cornerback Deonte Banks 24th overall. Porter Jr. went 32nd to the Steelers. Porter was the third-ranked cornerback in the NFL last season, using Pro Football and Sports Network’s ‘ Impact Score ’. Why weren’t the Giants interested? I don’t have inside information on this, but there would seem to be two clear reasons: Draft capital — The Giants gave up a fifth-round pick this week for quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Right now, the only picks they are guaranteed are in Rounds 1, 2, 3, 6, and 7. The are projected to receive a fifth-round compensatory pick. Give up that sixth-round pick, the possibility would then exist of going from Round 3 to Round 7 before having another selection. The second-round pick in 2028 would also be difficult to recoup. Money — The market for top cornerbacks is apparently more than $30 million annually . Giving up premium draft capital AND spending that kind of money is a tough ask. The Giants’ cornerback situation There is no true shut down No. 1 cornerback on the roster. The cornerback play, though, has largely been acceptable. Greg Newsome has perhaps been better than hoped. He is currently ranked No. 13 among 106 cornerbacks by Pro Football and Sports Network . Deonte Banks has missed two games with a calf injury. Throughout the summer, Banks looked like a much-improved player. Paulson Adebo was supposed to be the team’s best cornerback. He lost his starting job, struggled in a short appearance in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys, and is now on IR. Second-round pick Colton Hood has been forced into action. He has a 144.3 passer rating against, giving up 12 completions in 15 targets. To date, PFSN ranks him 103rd out of 106 grades cornerbacks. Giants head coach John Harbaugh disputed the notion that Hood has gotten off to a rough start. “I thought he’s improved each game. And that’s really, to me, the definer,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, it’s a big stage. It’s a tough position. And I don’t know how many rookie cornerbacks out there are just dominating. So, what constitutes a rough start for a rookie corner in the National Football League? I mean, who are you comparing him against? What are the rookies you’re comparing him against? “So, I think he’s done pretty good. Has he done great? No, there’s a couple of times where coverage got a little loose. I’m quite sure that Colton Hood’s going to be a really great player for us out there. And I thought he played better this last game than he did the game before. But he’s going to play better. I’ll bet you he plays better the next game than he did the last game. And really, to me, that’s the defining trait. So, I’m not down on him at all. I’m actually kind of excited for him.”

summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Whereas I felt like the onus was on the Eagles’ defense entering Week 3 against the Chicago Bears (and Vic Fangio’s group certainly failed that test), I feel like Week 4 is on Nick Sirianni. It’s important to see how the Eagles respond to their Monday night loss. On paper, they’re not in a great spot. The Rams are a tough opponent. The Eagles are going to be missing some key players. But this is a situation where the head coach needs to get his team to rally. I’m not even suggesting that the Eagles MUST win this game. But it will be disheartening if they’re not more competitive than they were against the Bears. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Glass Half Full – Iggles Blitz The NFC East isn’t loaded right now. Dallas has a terrific offense, but their defense remains a work in progress. Trading for CB Joey Porte Jr should help, but it won’t solve all their problems. Jameis Winston has struggled since taking over for Jaxson Dart in NY. Injuries are hurting that team. Washington has played better than anyone expected, but they lack talent and you just can’t trust them. This season can get turned around if Nick Sirianni has the right messaging and can push the right buttons. I believe the biggest problems are intangibles and those can usually be fixed. I’m not ignoring the tangible issues (poor safety play for instnace), but all 32 teams have weak spots. The Eagles can turn things around quickly if Sirianni can get this team to play smarter and tougher. The Eagles don’t have to win on Sunday to give me hope. I need to see them play good football. If the Rams happen to make an extra play or two and win, so be it. I just need to see major improvement from the Birds. That would help me to believe in them going forward. Eagles-Rams Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 4 enemy – BGN After two weeks on the road, the Philadelphia Eagles are returning to Lincoln Financial Field to host a familiar enemy: the Los Angeles Rams. In order to preview this Week 4 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Turf Show Times . The excellent Evan Craig kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 194: Week 4 Preview, Cowboys get Joey Porter Jr. – NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel A new week is upon us in the NFC East and we have four games to rip through to prepare for it! The Philadelphia Eagles are set to take on the Los Angeles Rams and dropping a second straight game would certainly not be ideal. Meanwhile, the New York Giants will play the Arizona Cardinals in JJ McCarthy’s first game with the team. The Washington Commanders are across the pond in London to play the Indianapolis Colts and try to build on last week’s momentum. Stateside the Dallas Cowboys have a Texas State matchup against the Houston Texans and will take them on with a new player on the team as they just traded for Joey Porter Jr. on Wednesday night. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss it all! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! 5Qs, 5As with Bleeding Green Nation: How is Jalen Hurts faring with yet another new OC? – Turf Show Times The Los Angeles Rams take on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 for the fourth straight season. Los Angeles is searching not only for its first win over the Eagles since the 2020 campaign, but also for its first win over Philly with Nick Sirianni at the helm. Ahead of an important matchup between NFC contenders who suffered bad losses last week, I spoke with Brandon Gowton from Bleeding Green Nation to get the inside scoop on Jalen Hurts working with yet another new offensive coordinator, Vic Fangio’s defense and more. NFL Expert Picks for Week 4 – SB Nation The one game to really circle: Rams vs. Eagles. Here are two teams assumed to be the top of the NFC, but both have struggled to start the season and find themselves in need of a win. It’s seeming like one of these teams is going to miss expecations this season, and this game could definine that. If Zack Baun misses Week 4? ‘Trot was born ready’ – NBCSP With All-Pro Zack Baun likely sidelined with a concussion for Sunday’s game against the Rams, the Eagles are expected to turn to Jeremiah Trotter Jr. How ready is the young Axe Man? “Trot was born ready,” fellow linebacker Jihaad Campbell said. “Whether he’s got to play or not, at the end of the day, he always practices like a pro, he always takes notes and studies like a pro. He’ll be fine.” Trotter, 23, has technically started two NFL games before but both of those had little actual meaning. He started in Week 18 against the Giants in 2024 and Week 18 against the Commanders in 2025. This situation is a little bit different. The Eagles on Sunday afternoon are facing a desperate Rams team that has put up 480+ yards of offense in back-to-back weeks and are led by Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams, Puka Nacua and more — not to mention an offense that uses a ton of eye candy to constantly put linebackers in conflict. It’s not going to be easy on Sunday. NFL Week 4 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com Why Gennaro picked the Eagles: Last Sunday night, Los Angeles blew a 16-0 halftime lead at Denver to drop back below .500 in a season that began with the Rams as prohibitive Super Bowl favorites. One night later, Philadelphia was blown out of Chicago by a Bears team that was forced to give Case Keenum his first start in 1,009 days. So, after a pair of nationally televised debacles, who’s in better position to bounce back? Well, the expected return of star WR Puka Nacua is certainly a boon to Sean McVay’s squad. But can the Rams coach exorcise his demons against the Eagles? McVay is 1-6 vs. Philadelphia, having dropped all four matchups against Nick Sirianni. Last season’s loss at Lincoln Financial Field was particularly painful: Not only did the Rams blow a 19-point third-quarter lead, but they had two fourth-quarter field goal attempts blocked, including a would-be game-winner from 44 yards out on the last snap of the contest. In addition to swatting that final kick, hulking DT Jordan Davis memorably scooped up the ball and galloped for an exclamation-point touchdown. But the big man’s triumphant rumble was easily the Eagles’ best run of the day, as the Rams held Saquon Barkley to just 55 total yards on 22 touches. That was a huge departure from Barkley’s previous two games against L.A., when he piled up 534(!) scrimmage yards. Philly’s had trouble getting a consistent ground attack going under new OC Sean Mannion, but Barkley did enjoy success against Chicago this past Monday night before the game got out of hand, potentially signaling a schematic breakthrough. In a matchup between two established powers that have yet to play up to their talent level this season, I’m far from bullish on the Eagles. But I anticipate Sirianni will rally the troops once again versus McVay, with the Birds feeling disrespected as home underdogs. summary: The Philadelphia Eagles lost in Week 3 and now they’re dealing with some not so great injury news ahead of their Week 4 game. FIRST […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles in action against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles lost in Week 3 and now they’re dealing with some not so great injury news ahead of their Week 4 game. Leading receiver DeVonta Smith is “legitimately questionable” to play against the Los Angeles Rams this weekend due to his hamstring injury, according to a report from NFL insider Mike Garafolo . FIRST UPDATE: More reporting that suggests Smith will probably not play this weekend . There is not much optimism Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith will play Sunday against the Rams, sources tell me and @MikeGarafolo . Smith has been sidelined with a hamstring injury this week and the expectation is he won’t be able to go Sunday. — Tim McManus (@Tim_McManus) October 1, 2026 SECOND UPDATE: Speaking on the PHLY Eagles podcast on Thursday, Bo Wulf said the following: “I heard at the beginning of this week that DeVonta is likely to miss this game and maybe another one. Could be a two or three week hamstring injury.” It should be noted Garafolo calling him “legitimately questionable” isn’t necessarily the same thing as the Eagles officially listed Smith with a questionable designation on their final injury report. With the Eagles holding a walkthrough in lieu of a normal practice on Wednesday, the team issued an estimated injury report. Smith was listed under “did not participate.” Smith was also listed under DNP on Thursday ahead of their Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears. But then he was upgraded to limited on Friday and full go on Saturday. The difference from last week to this week, thus far, is that Smith also seemingly did not participate in today’s practice. If he fails to participate again on Friday, it’s hard to envision him suiting on Sunday since players who don’t practice typically don’t play in games. If Smith can’t play against the Rams, the Eagles will be without a player who has accounted for 33% of their targets, 34% of their receptions, 38% of their receiving yards, 20% of their receiving touchdowns, and 36% of their receiving first downs this season. Not ideal. Especially since they’re already down top tight end Dallas Goedert. With Hollywood Brown also missing practices this week, the Eagles could be down to these healthy receivers: Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, and Britain Covey. They also have Xavier Gipson on the practice squad. Although the Eagles might be undermanned at receiver, the Rams are dealing with injury issues of their own in their secondary. Starting cornerback Jaylen Watson is expected to miss this week’s game. We’ll continue to monitor Smith’s status leading up to Sunday’s 1:00 PM kickoff.

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Zack Baun #53 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. The Eagles listed five players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert, Hollywood Brown, and Fred Johnson. Smitty missed practice for the second day in a row due his hamstring injury. The latest reporting suggests that he is “legitimately questionable” to play on Sunday. We’ll see if he’s able to practice at all on Friday. If not, the Eagles will be without their top receiver against a tough opponent. Not great. UPDATE: DeVonta is not expected to play on Sunday. Welp. Baun has yet to reach a point in the concussion protocol where he can practice. Seems like he’s going to run out of time to be cleared to play in Sunday’s game. If Baun isn’t permitted to play, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. figures to start next to Jihaad Campbell. This will be the third career start for Trot Jr. It would also be Baun’s first missed game with the Eagles due to non-rest reasons. Jenkins as their three tight ends for the second game in a row. Brown hasn’t practiced since apparently picking up an ankle injury in practice last week. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled by Adoree' Jackson #8 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 21, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
