The excellent Evan Craig kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Evan’s questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to TST.] 1 – The Rams entered the season as Super Bowl betting favorites but they’re off to a 1-2 start. What’s gone wrong? Much of it is due to injuries and inconsistent play. The Rams began the season with a thud, largely because of a terrible travel plan where they landed in Australia about a day before the game. Sean McVay might be an offensive genius, but he should really let someone else make the travel plans from now on. Against the Giants, they looked much better, yet still weren’t overly impressive to start. Beating up on a New York team minus its starting quarterback for most of the game wasn’t overly impressive. However, a win’s a win, and with how this team’s been so far this season, they must take what they can get. Then against the Broncos, they just blew it. Special teams was part of the reason Denver managed to come back from a 16-0 first half deficit. The defense also didn’t do itself any favors. While there were some questionable calls down the stretch, it never should’ve come down to needing to hold off a miracle comeback when the Broncos were outplayed for much of the game. And the injuries have been bad too, which is a shame, considering the team was mostly healthy last season. Puka Nacua has already missed more games in the first three weeks than he did all of last season. Myles Garrett hasn’t played since the opener and is unlikely to play for a few more games. New cornerback Jaylen Watson suffered an injury in Sunday’s game but is expected to return soon. Overall, the nagging injuries have been the most frustrating part about this season. All the new pieces need time to gel, yet they haven’t been on the field long enough for that to happen. At full strength, this should be a very, very good team. I’m just unsure whether we’ll see this team reach its potential with how things are going. 2 – What’s going on with the Puka Nacua injury situation? Will he play in this game? And what’s the impact if he does or doesn’t? Puka Nacua suffered a hip injury in practice leading up to the Giants game and has missed the last two matchups. Fortunately for the Rams, it’s not a long-term injury, but enough to warrant caution. I expect Nacua won’t play again for at least this game. He could potentially be a game-time decision, but for any of you who have him in fantasy, I would hold off starting him this week. If Puka manages to play, he’ll take the load off an already thin group of pass catchers. This Rams team lacks quality depth at wide receiver, even after trading back for star Tutu Atwell (LOL). So having him back would be exactly the break the offense has needed. Now, assuming he’s out again this week, all the pressure again lies on Davante Adams, who has filled in admirably in Nacua’s absence. Adams has recorded 15 catches for 332 yards and two touchdowns against the Giants and Broncos. However, given his age and overall production since coming to LA, that’s not sustainable. Someone else needs to step up. Against New York in Week 2, tight end Terrance Ferguson also had a good game, but he might miss this week due to an ankle injury. Very slim pickings indeed, but simply put, someone other than Adams must find a way to be productive. 3 – How has Aaron Donald looked since returning? Truthfully (and I really hope he isn’t reading this), Aaron Donald should’ve stayed retired. He is clearly not the Donald of old. It’s not like he’s played poorly. He’s mostly been a non-factor and has been hovering around below-average production since his return. In his first game against the Giants, there were flashes of his former self. It was clear that whatever work he was putting in to stay in shape had paid off, since he showed his freakish speed and athleticism, despite not stuffing the stat sheet. Overall, it wasn’t the wisest move coming back, and the Denver game was a good example of that. Getting pancaked by Broncos lineman Quinn Meinerz partially proves that. Donald ranks 79th out of 91 qualified defensive linemen in pressure rate at 4.8% and has registered only two pressures out of 42 pass rush snaps. That’s not great at all and definitely not what fans were hoping to see from his second act. I’ve been iffy on Donald’s return ever since it was announced. It’s not like his legacy is on the line or anything; that has never been in question. I just found it hard to believe he could be effective after being out of the NFL for two years. So far, I’ve been proven right, though I don’t feel good about it. That’s what happens when you take too long to make a decision and skip all of training camp. Absolutely no one in their right mind expected DPOY results from him right out of the gate, and maybe he’ll improve slightly once Garrett returns, but that’s doubtful. It’s still somewhat frustrating seeing him back, as he went out on top by earning first-team All-Pro honors in what was supposed to be his final season in 2023. Sometimes when retired greats feel the itch to play again, it’s best not to scratch. With how this season’s gone, Donald would’ve been better off letting the itch nag him for a bit until it ultimately disappears. 4 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Rams’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The defensive line has been horrible and among the most unproductive in the league. Still, I like its chances against the Eagles’ offensive line on Sunday. Jalen Hurts has been sacked at least two times in every game this season. LA has just three sacks on the year, so naturally they’re due for a good game at some point. I think it happens against Philadelphia; only I’m not expecting them to be the sack masters they were against the Eagles in the playoffs a couple years ago. Matching their season sack total in this one is a very manageable goal, even if this line stinks to high heaven. As for the other side, I believe the Eagles’ secondary will have a solid day against the Rams’ wide receivers. Not that it’s a hard thing to envision, since the wideout production is generally Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and everyone else. As mentioned earlier, with Nacua likely out for this one, I don’t see Adams carrying the load for the third straight week, especially in a hostile environment. No other pass catcher should strike fear in Vic Fangio, as the one who does will be on the sideline. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Eagles currently listed as three-point home underdogs, what’s your score prediction? So far this season, I’ve correctly predicted every Rams game. Well, I likely just jinxed myself saying that. Given that the Rams are playing the second of three straight Super Bowl hopefuls, I said that between the Broncos and Eagles road games, LA would lose in Denver and beat Philly. Los Angeles is long overdue for a win over the Eagles, considering they’re 1-6 against them in the McVay era. Even though the Rams have had some injury concerns this season, I still trust them more than the Eagles right now. I also expect their defense to play much better after giving up 30 second half points to the Broncos. Plus, I feel much better about their chances after Philadelphia’s awful performance Monday night. If Case Keenum can do it, so can Matthew Stafford. Rams 24, Eagles 19.

title: Vic Fangio talks about the Eagles’ plan at safety
summary: The Eagles have a short week heading into their Week 4 matchup against the Rams, and DC Vic Fangio spoke with reporters on Wednesday about why they’re a tough team to prepare for, and also gave some insight into the current state of the secondary. Here’s what else the DC had to say: On the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Marcus Epps #29 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles have a short week heading into their Week 4 matchup against the Rams, and DC Vic Fangio spoke with reporters on Wednesday about why they’re a tough team to prepare for, and also gave some insight into the current state of the secondary. Here’s what else the DC had to say: On the lack of turnovers Fangio said that every missed opportunity for a turnover has a story, but they definitely need to get some takeaways to help the offense and to get some stops. He admitted that there were different factors leading to their low sack numbers, but the DC expects to get some eventually. “I haven’t felt like our rush has been poor. I mean, they’re throwing it rather quickly a lot of times is part of it.” He later talked about how they can try and prepare players a little more so they are better able to capitalize on potential takeaways. “Yeah, obviously you’d like to pull one or two of those in. We’ve just got to keep giving them multiple ball drills. Coaches throwing ball drills is almost a waste because they’re lollipops. We’ve got to get them on the jugs or get a real quarterback throwing them some balls that have some RPMs, maybe like a [Jhoan] Duran fastball rather than a Jamie Moyer.” On the safety position Fangio said that the plan all week was to rotate Marcus Epps and Michael Carter , and they practiced it that way. He said those two guys are going to man the position right now , although acknowledged the goal is to always have someone settle into the role. Who is on the field will be based on a rotation, not by situation. He was also asked about how newly signed DB Kenny Moore might fit into that equation. “Well, [Kenny Moore]’s a down the line possibility, maybe. He’s really never played safety in his career, so it’d be some heavy lifting for him on the immediate return.” The DC quickly dismissed the notion that Drew Mukuba was hindered by any kind of injury. Fangio also was quick with his answers about Cooper DeJean , revealing that he still plans to use DeJean in the slot when they’re in nickel, and said he thinks the DB has been “playing good”. On Jonathan Greenard’s return “About what I thought. He got, I don’t know, 18, 19 snaps, I think. Had some good rushes. Some little things were off a little bit, but about what I expected.” Fangio thinks there will be an upward trend to Greenard’s snap count, and would expect the edge rusher to get closer to 30 snaps on Sunday against the Rams. On preparing for the Rams “Yeah, they’re really good. Not counting their San Francisco game in Australia, their last three games going back to the NFC championship game, they’ve gotten 500 yards in all three games against Seattle, the Giants and Denver. Three good defenses. That in and of itself explains to you what the chore is we have. They run it very well. They stay committed to the run and they’ve got a really good play action game off of it that they marry very well to the run game.” Fangio went on to point out that they’ve got QB Matthew Stafford, who he says is a first-ballot Hall of Famer, and has weapons at receiver and tight end, including Puke Macua who is expected to be back. The DC also had a lot of compliments for WR Davante Adams. “[Davante Adam]’s got size, number one. He’s quick and a really good releaser off the ball. He knows how to body up DBs and get himself an advantage one way or the other. With a quarterback like Stafford, that’s all you need.” He also disproved the notion that Sean McVay has really change his run scheme the past few years, explaining that he’s really just changed the personnel he’s using in that run scheme – utilizing more three tight ends. “Yeah, their tight ends are versatile. They’re pretty good receivers, and obviously the blocking and they create extra gaps in there. They’re committed to it and they’re good at it.” Other notables Fangio said that Jalen Carter’s wrist injury hurts his performance, admitting there’s no way playing with a cast won’t hinder a player, but says Carter has done better than the DC thought he would with it. He said that it’s possible they could look at rotating LB Jeremiah Trotter Jr. in and getting him so reps, but Fangio didn’t feel like they needed to against the Bears. The DC thought the guys were ready to play mentally and physically, but felt the details were off a little and they weren’t prepared enough for Case Keenum throwing so quickly. Fangio admitted that there was a miscommunication between Cooper DeJean and Riq Woolen on the 41-yard TD against the Bears, but didn’t want to blame either of them – at least publicly – and suggested that the two sort it out so it doesn’t happen again. When asked if he was happy with the call on that play, the DC quipped, “No, the result was sh*tty.”

title: Eagles make some practice squad moves
summary: The Eagles are still tinkering with their roster, and as we head into October, the team made some practice squad moves. Here’s an overview: Hall’s return gives the Eagles more defensive tackle depth. The Eagles have been going five DTs deep during games while Jalen Carter is playing through a hairline fracture in his wrist. […]
full_text: Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles are still tinkering with their roster, and as we head into October, the team made some practice squad moves. Here’s an overview: DT Gabe Hall was re-signed to the practice squad after being cut last week. LB Chance Campbell was placed on the practice squad injured list. LB Anfernee Orji was signed to the practice squad. Hall’s return gives the Eagles more defensive tackle depth. The Eagles have been going five DTs deep during games while Jalen Carter is playing through a hairline fracture in his wrist. Campbell was temporarily elevated from the practice squad in Week 3 to give the Eagles another special teams contributor. It was his Eagles debut and his first regular season game action since 2023. Bummer for him that he got hurt. Orji signed with the Saints after a college career at Vanderbilt. He spent his entire rookie season in 2023 on the team’s practice squad, but played in 16 games for New Orleans in 2024. He played most of his snaps on special teams, but did record 146 defensive snaps and was even a starter for two games. Overall, he notched 30 total tackles, but was waived in May 2025. The Titans swooped in and claimed Orji off waivers, but ended up on IR during training camp and was ultimately waived. He cleared waivers and defaulted to Tennessee’s injured reserve for the season. The LB then spent most of his summer with the Giants, before being released as part of the final 53-man roster cuts.

title: Eagles News: Jalen Carter is playing through a hairline fracture in his wrist
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Carter playing through this injury doesn’t really seem tenable? Shutting him down sure wouldn’t be ideal, especially in the short-term. But they really need the healthy version of him for this team to reach their ceiling. And so they might […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Carter playing through this injury doesn’t really seem tenable? Shutting him down sure wouldn’t be ideal, especially in the short-term. But they really need the healthy version of him for this team to reach their ceiling. And so they might need to bite the bullet at some point. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter playing with hairline fracture in his wrist – Inquirer Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter has a hairline fracture in his right wrist, NFL sources told The Inquirer. Carter suffered the injury in the Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders and has played with a soft cast in the last two games. He was an estimated full participant in Wednesday’s walkthrough ahead of Sunday’s game vs. the Rams. Carter’s playing time has decreased since the injury. He played 66 snaps in the opener (94%), 41 snaps vs. the Titans in Week 2 (77%), and 51 snaps (71%) in Monday night’s 27-7 loss at the Bears. […] “It’s a negative,” Fangio said. “There’s no way it can’t be, but to be honest with you, he’s done better than I thought he would with it.” Eagles-Bears Film Review: Rough game for Vic Fangio – BGN I criticized the lack of fight earlier, so I should also mention the first-half goal-line stand. The Eagles made several big plays with their backs against the wall. Jalen Carter made this one without using his right hand. That is impressive, but it also shows the problem. He clearly can’t play right now, and the Eagles desperately need him to be a disruptive player again. He recorded no pressures on 33 pass-rush snaps. The Eagles are paying him a lot of money and can’t rush the quarterback. It’s a big issue. Eagles-Rams preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice 5) The Eagles’ receivers vs. the Rams’ banged-up secondary. The Rams’ secondary is a little banged up heading into this matchup. Their normal configuration looks like so: CB: Trent McDuffie, S: Kamren Curl, S: Kam Kinchens, SCB: Quentin Lake, CB: Jaylen Watson. Kinchens has missed each of the last two games with a hamstring injury. He did practice on Wednesday, but was limited. When he got hurt, Lake moved to safety, and Josh Wallace filled in at the slot. Watson was carted off the field with a shoulder injury during the Rams’ loss to the Broncos Week 3. When he got hurt, Wallace played outside corner, and moved into the slot in nickel, with Emmanuel Forbes playing on the outside. Of course, Forbes was a player who A.J. Brown reliably dominated during Brown’s time with the Eagles, because he outweighed Forbes by like 40 pounds. That won’t be as big of a mismatch this time around, but certainly the Eagles have prioritized attacking Forbes in the past. Wallace is now also on the injury report. He was limited on Wednesday with a shoulder injury. In other words, the Rams have had to do some juggling in their secondary. To be determined who will be available on Sunday, and who won’t. So far, one of the bright spots for the Eagles has been the play of DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. We also saw a glimpse of progress (baby steps, for sure) from Makai Lemon on Monday night, both as a receiver and blocker. Game Review – CHI 27, PHI 7 – Iggles Blitz The Bears were embarrassed by their 9-3 loss to the Vikings in Week 2. Johnson had them fired up and ready to play. Sirianni clearly did not have the Eagles at the same level. The biggest strategic mistake came when Sirianni decided to punt on 4th down in the second half. He admitted after the game that he should have gone for it. Some think he should have called timeout when Hurts was being checked for a concussion. I don’t think you can fault him for that. Too many unknowns in that situation. Sean Mannion had a good plan in the first half. The Eagles out-gained the Bears 186 to 176 and only trailed 10-7. The Eagles ran a WR screen with 19 seconds left in the first half. Hurts was able to then get the team lined up and the ball snapped with one second left. He pushed his way in for a TD. The result was good, but that was a highly risky call with no timeouts. The second half was terrible. Before he called plays for the Eagles, Sean Mannion was the Rams’ ‘Big Shooter’ – The Athletic They called him Big Shooter. Sean Mannion, 6 feet 6 and 230 pounds, was the most imposing Los Angeles Rams quarterback in the summer of 2017. Starter Jared Goff was a lean, lanky 22-year-old then. Dan Orlovsky, then a 6-foot-5 veteran, coined Mannion’s nickname. Orlovsky said he and Goff would watch “this mountain of a man” break huddles in training camp, lumber toward the line of scrimmage, then “fudging rip these throws.” “Every ball was like a fastball,” said Orlovsky, now an ESPN analyst. “Sean would get in there and hand-missile this 20-yard in route, and I’d be in the back yelling, ‘BIG SHOOTER!’” […] Orlovsky described Mannion as a “very serious,” “very intense guy” who “always wanted to do well.” “Jared would throw an interception, and it would almost be like it never happened,” Orlovsky said. “Sean would throw an incompletion, and he’d be like he just lost the Super Bowl.” In 2017, first-year Rams coach Sean McVay brought Orlovsky aboard to mentor both quarterbacks until final roster cuts. Orlovsky took no practice reps, instead offering advice and sharing his process for studying playbooks and film. Orlovsky was yet again counseling a future Eagles offensive coordinator. The never-ending safety competition that has turned into a rotation – NBCSP Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II battled all training camp for the same starting safety position. And now we’re four weeks into the season and that competition still isn’t over. Now it’s a rotation. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio used both Epps and Carter against the Bears in Week 3 — Epps played 27 snaps, Carter played 20. And on Wednesday, the longtime DC said that rotation is going to continue. “Those two guys are still going to man it,” Fangio said. Of course, you can argue that if you have two safeties at one spot, it’s because you don’t really have one. So when asked if he’d like either Epps or Carter to eventually settle into that role, Fangio said, “That’s always your goal.” So how did we get here? That unit is tied for 26th among D/STs, has the league’s fifth-lowest sack rate and would be an iffy start in an average matchup. The Rams are not an average matchup after dropping 54 points over the last two games without Puka Nacua. Even if Matthew Stafford throws another pick (he already has four), Philly’s defense has not shown enough to be trusted in starting lineups. title: Our first month with an app broke our commenting records
summary: A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it.  The goal with this app was to make it easier to join […]
full_text: (Photo by Brett Carlsen/Getty Images) | Getty Images A month ago we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past month and have been using it. The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center. The results so far are encouraging. In fact, it’s helped us set a new all-time record for comments this month across all of SB Nation’s communities, and I want to thank you for that. One of the most exciting new features is the game chat. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you’re not going to find anywhere else. We also wanted to elevate the community’s contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we’ve set single-day commenting records three different times since the season started. And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there’s an option at the top to do that. So, one month in, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven’t checked it out, you can get it for iOs or Android . And if you’re not an app user, that’s OK! We’re glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.

title: The Steelers is the Steelers, and this is their new normal
summary: Trade Joey Porter Jr. and lose to the Cleveland Browns in a 24-hour span. This is the new normal for the Pittsburgh Steelers. And I say “new normal,” but it’s not exactly new, is it? The Steelers haven’t beaten the Browns in Cleveland since Ben Roethlisberger’s final season in the NFL back in 2021, and […]
full_text: (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Trade Joey Porter Jr. and lose to the Cleveland Browns in a 24-hour span. This is the new normal for the Pittsburgh Steelers. And I say “new normal,” but it’s not exactly new, is it? The Steelers haven’t beaten the Browns in Cleveland since Ben Roethlisberger’s final season in the NFL back in 2021, and they’ve made a habit of trading top players at key positions without any sort of backup plan in place. They did it with Diontae Johnson in 2023 and didn’t find an adequate No. 2 for George Pickens. They then traded Pickens in 2025, didn’t find a good No. 2 to put opposite DK Metcalf, and Pickens went on to be an All-Pro. Now, they’ve dealt Porter and their secondary was immediately exposed by Deshaun Watson and the Browns. This isn’t the team from the 2000s where their defense was the best in the league for a six-year span and the offense was being led by a young star at the position. At some point, they stopped being the big brother that would give the Browns a noogie twice a year. Instead, they are the brother that is past their prime and still clinging to his glory days at a high school reunion. At some point, it’s time to take off the letterman jacket and class ring and leave your hometown. The Steelers haven’t done that, though, and it doesn’t feel like they ever will. Not with this owner, at least. Rather than being a team that consistently competes for Super Bowls like they did 15-20 years ago, now they trade players they don’t want to pay and lose to the Browns every year. Because that’s who they are now. Draft a good player, player showcases high-end talent, trade player away, try trading for another player to replace the player you just traded. The whole “Browns is the Browns” joke is certainly rich coming from any Steelers fan who still says it, because at this point, the Steelers is the Steelers, and this is their identity. But hey, that 2008 season was special, wasn’t it? It’s the morning after game day, and it’s time for the Steelers to change how they do business. Aaron Rodgers miscues Aaron Rodgers had several misses that severely impacted the outcome. In the third quarter, he had DK Metcalf wide open for what would have been the easiest deep touchdown pass of his career. He didn’t see it and instead checked it down to Ben Skowronek. Aaron Rodgers didnt see a wide open DK metcalf pic.twitter.com/Xwm9ktR19K — Tanner Phifer (@TannerPhifer) October 2, 2026 On the final play of the game for the Steelers, Rodgers had Metcalf open again. This time, it would have been an easy completion to put the Steelers at the 35-yard line for what would have been a 52-yard field goal for Chris Boswell to try and send the game into overtime. Instead, he forces a ball to Roman Wilson that gets picked off and seals the game. DK Metcalf was WIDE OPEN Aaron Rodgers blew it pic.twitter.com/AC7mUWR8Qh — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 2, 2026 Pressure on Rodgers puts hard cap on Steelers offense The Browns found a specific defense that worked and just ran it into the ground all night. Per Sumer Sports, Cleveland played one-high safety on 80 percent of looks, which usually coincided with pressure getting to Rodgers. They rushed five on roughly one third of snaps, and the Steelers couldn’t figure out a counter for what the Browns were doing for most of the night. There were sacks where Rodgers held the ball for quite a bit, but that had a lot to do with the Steelers’ receivers complete inability to generate separation against man coverage. The Steelers don’t have consistent man-beaters, and that’s something that defenses can certainly hone in on throughout the year. Atrocious tackling and coverage The lack of ability to take down a ball carrier was abhorrent. Cole Holcomb and Rayshawn Jenkins both riffed on bringing down Jaleel McLaughlin on the Browns’ first touchdown of the night. Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen both had dreadful nights when it came to bringing down ball carriers, and there were whiffs on potential sacks. It was a largely bad game from the defense, especially in the first half when the Browns scored 21 unanswered points. Additionally, coverage was terrible. Daylen Everette was torched multiple times, including a 60-yard bomb to Denzel Boston that set up a Browns touchdown, and a slant while playing outside leverage while Cleveland was deep in its own territory. If only they had a high-quality young cornerback on their roster. Other notes T.J. Watt continues looking like his old self. He finished with a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and a sack. Jalen Ramsey needs moved to safety permanently and Brandin Echols should take the nickel spot. The current safety rotation just isn’t getting it done. The offense needs to run through Jaylen Warren. On money downs, and short yardage situations, he needs to be the guy. I’m officially at Defcon 3 with Chris Boswell. If he makes his first kick of the night, we are having a very different conversation right now. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! Steelers allow five sacks on Aaron Rodgers, fall to Browns 27-24 Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr to Cowboys Browns HC Todd Monken jokes that T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward should retire Jerry Jones hints that Cowboys have interest in Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. Steelers CB Brandin Echols in concussion protocol
author: Jarrett Bailey

title: Steelers stock report after Thursday night loss to Browns
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers lost in a heartbreak on Thursday in Cleveland 27-24. After tying the game with just over a minute to play, the Steelers came up just short once again against the Browns on Thursday Night Football. As always, here is our weekly stock report after the Steelers fell to 2-2 on the season. […]
full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers lost in a heartbreak on Thursday in Cleveland 27-24. After tying the game with just over a minute to play, the Steelers came up just short once again against the Browns on Thursday Night Football. As always, here is our weekly stock report after the Steelers fell to 2-2 on the season. Stock Up WR Roman Wilson Why not Roman Wilson? After catching a 38-yard touchdown pass last weekend against Cincinnati, Wilson was on the bench for most of the second half after letting a pass bounce off his hands that resulted in an interception. The Steelers did not shy away from going to Wilson in this one. He took a touch pass 12 yards to the end zone for the game’s first score. Later in the contest, Rodgers found Wilson streaking up the seam for a huge chunk gain of 49. The inconsistencies continue to haunt Wilson, but tonight was a bright spot as Wilson has now scored in consecutive games for Pittsburgh. TE Darnell Washington Washington continues to be one of the most impactful players on the Steelers offense. His biggest and most notable play of the night came on his 21-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter. Washington became the target of choice for Rodgers on the game-tying drive, as he was the target on three straight plays. The defensive pass interference that the tight end drew in the end zone set the Steelers up to eventually tie the game. Washington is a matchup nightmare that continues to see more work in the Steelers offense. QB Aaron Rodgers Unc still got it. What a gutsy fourth quarter from the veteran quarterback. The Steelers seemed all but dead and buried down 24-10 well into the fourth quarter, but Aaron Rodgers kept them alive. For as much as his age showed up in the pocket in this game, Rodger rolled out and delivered a strike to Washington in the end zone to kick off the fourth quarter. The veteran quarterback then led another drive downfield and tossed a touchdown on a bootleg to Pat Freiermuth. We have to give some credit to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy for the playcall on the 2-point conversion after the penalty from Cleveland. Rodgers did not get much of a push from the offensive line, but he found enough room to sneak in. The Steelers do not come back and tie this game if not for Rodgers, who took a serious beating tonight. Stock Down Offensive Line It was just a messy game from the offensive line as a whole. Rodgers was sacked five times in the game and took a serious beating with 10 quarterback hits. Jaylen Warren ran the ball incredibly well once again as he averaged 5.5 yards per carry, so the line does deserve some credit for that. However, Rodgers was pressured and hit a ton, and that really put them in a hole that proved to be too much. K Chris Boswell Boswell missed his third field goal of the season in Week 4, as the 48-yard attempt went wide left. It’s nowhere near time to panic or sell your stock in Boswell, but this inconsistency is something to monitor. Secondary Joey Porter Jr. was almost certainly watching this game with a smile on his face from his new apartment in Dallas. Deshaun Watson has a 94.0 passer rating to the tune of 268 yards and a touchdown. The Steelers continued to play a lot of zone coverage, which is going to continue to be a hot topic of conversation as opposing quarterbacks carve up the Steelers secondary. Watson did plenty with his legs tonight, but it was obvious that the Steelers’ secondary is in major need of help. Jamel Dean left the game with an ankle injury and did not return, so an already thin secondary could be without their now-top corner. Deshon Elliott is eligible to come off injured reserve as early as needed this week, which should provide a boost, but this secondary needs major help and fast. title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns
summary: Another Thursday Night Football game in Cleveland. Another loss for the Steelers. Some things change. Some things don’t. But there are always some takeaways to be had: 1. Old habits die hard A brand new coaching staff. Fresh momentum following an exciting win over Cincinnati. A Browns team without Myles Garrett and two starting offensive […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 01: Head coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 01, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another Thursday Night Football game in Cleveland. Another loss for the Steelers. Some things change. Some things don’t. But there are always some takeaways to be had: 1. Old habits die hard A brand new coaching staff. Fresh momentum following an exciting win over Cincinnati. A Browns team without Myles Garrett and two starting offensive linemen. You’d think that might be enough to break Pittsburgh’s surprisingly long-running losing streak in Cleveland — but instead, history repeated on Thursday Night Football. The Steelers jumped out to an early 7-0 lead, but quickly fell apart. The black and gold drew even in a nail-biting fourth quarter, but the optimism was short-lived, with the Pittsburgh defense giving up a game-winning field goal drive orchestrated by Deshaun Watson. Despite looking like a new, exciting team under Mike McCarthy at points over the summer and even in last week’s win over the Bengals, the bulk of the season has shown the team still looking like the same, old Steelers: familiar highs and and lows, and a number of issues we’ve seen before, from an offense that seems low on talent to a secondary that can’t seem to get a consistent stop. The good news for Pittsburgh is Cleveland did most of its damage in one quarter — 21 of the Browns’ 27 points came in the second — and the Steelers showed some grit rallying back in the fourth on the road. But the bad was ugly, and the late-game explosion from Aaron Rodgers and DK Metcalf felt more like a rerun of Ben Roethlisberger’s last gasps at brilliance in 2020 and 2021 than anything resembling an offense that’s finally made the jump to the modern era. It’s not that the Steelers aren’t expected to lose games. The worrying part is that four games into the season — well after the worst of the preseason rust should’ve worn off — I can’t get a solid read on what this team truly is once again. 2. Aaron Rodgers can’t consistently lead an offense Some truly incredible throws from Aaron Rodgers saved this game from being one of the worst I’ve ever seen him play, but it was close. And while the veteran passer still seems to uncork a handful of perfect deep passes every few games to throw internet doubters off the scent of his regression (the touchdown pass to Darnell Washington was a thing of beauty), it’s beyond clear that the overall product Thursday night was not what you want from an NFL quarterback. Sure, Rodgers was sacked five times versus Cleveland and dealt with consistent pressure. As the broadcast almost turned into a broken record repeating, Steelers receivers were not gaining enough separation against the Browns’ man coverage. But Rodgers still shoulders plenty of blame on a number of those sacks and incompletions. Per @NextGenStats , the Browns have played 73 percent man coverage in this game. Crazy disrespectful — and rightly so. — Robert Mays (@robertmays) October 2, 2026 Now 42, Rodgers looks unsettled in the face of pressure. His reactions in the pocket are always a tick or two late, and he repeatedly moves into rushers. And the future Hall of Famer, once praised for unreal accuracy and football IQ, threw several passes into questionable coverage, didn’t always see when receivers were open, and missed high and low. I don’t doubt that having a player of Rodgers’ vast experience has been a boon to many of the younger players on the Steelers’ roster. But at the same time, having a quarterback with his mobility limitations hasn’t been the best fit for a young offensive line that’s finally showing signs of real progress. I’m not advocating to bench Rodgers, to be clear. But two things can be true: Rodgers might’ve been the best option the Steelers had at quarterback this year, but that doesn’t mean that he isn’t capping the potential of the offense. 3. Defense disappoints, but the sky isn’t falling Hear it from Cam Heyward. It wasn’t all bad on Thursday for the Steelers defense, but giving up 27 points for a second straight game is not exactly something to hang your hat on. “27 points? These last two games have been not good on defense.” —Cam Heyward pic.twitter.com/F18vjQuemX — Chris Adamski (@C_AdamskiTrib) October 2, 2026 In fairness to new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, losing Jamel Dean to injury and the now-guaranteed lack of Joey Porter Jr. this season has rookie corner Daylen Everette in the starting lineup at least a year earlier than he should be. While it was tough to see what was supposed to be a strong secondary this year continually lose to a (admittedly good) rookie wide receiver duo, at this point it’s fair to say Pittsburgh just doesn’t have enough talent in the secondary. Even then, Graham managed to batten the hatches in the second half, forcing a pair each of punts and turnovers (not to gloss over two field goals including the game winner). Yes, the Browns’ Todd Monken perfectly countered Graham’s blitzes throughout the game, and Pittsburgh’s tackling, which was frankly embarrassing at times, was a poor reflection of its coaching staff. Still, I’m not ready to give up on the Steelers’ new coordinator in his fourth game with the team just yet. Still, the roster construction of the defense is looking suspect. The Porter trade is something that the front office clearly wasn’t planning for entering the season. The decision might be defendable depending on what exactly the young cornerback was hoping for contract-wise, but it’s still a tough look when you see the Steelers, who were willing to pay and trade for the-now 31-year-old Jalen Ramsey last year, clearly still in need of a CB1. Plus, it was clear heading into the summer that the Steelers’ depth at safety was a glaring weak link on the defense well before DeShon Elliott landed on injured reserve. Now it’s even worse, with Jaquan Brisker struggling to make tackles in the open field on Thursday, and Rayshawn Jenkins getting benched for seventh-round rookie Robert Spears-Jennings (also starting far earlier than anticipated), who logged a game of dizzying highs and lows. I had reasonably high expectations for this defense entering the season. I still do. But if the Steelers continue to be this undermanned on the back end of things, consistent success will be hard to come by. 4. At least DK Metcalf is back, maybe The Steelers took several steps forward on offense last week, and retraced many of them in the loss to the Browns. But WR1 DK Metcalf is still on an upward trajectory, at least. Metcalf recorded by far his best game of the season on Thursday night, with five receptions for 115 yards on a wide variety of plays — a sideline contested catch, a 43-yard post, and a wide receiver screen that went for big yards-after-catch on a third down, to name a few. Metcalf could’ve garnered an even stronger stat line as well if Rodgers had seen him breaking open during a few key moments later in the game. Aaron Rodgers didnt see a wide open DK metcalf pic.twitter.com/Xwm9ktR19K — Tanner Phifer (@TannerPhifer) October 2, 2026 A 15-yard taunting penalty in the first quarter showed that the Metcalf of old is still very much there, but after an incredibly rough start to the season overall, the Steelers’ top receiver is finally looking the part. He even heated up in the fourth quarter, with a few of his grabs coming on clutch connections with Rodgers to tie up the game late. Even when the Steelers offense has looked good in past games this season, it’s been with Metcalf underperforming compared to the role Pittsburgh is paying him to fill. If Thursday’s game can be a sign of things to come, it should greatly add to the Steelers’ underneath passing game as well as Rodgers’ options downfield. I was similarly encouraged by the play of Roman Wilson on Thursday…
author: Ryland Bickley

title: Steelers allow five sacks on Aaron Rodgers, fall to Browns 27-24
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers nearly completed an 11-point fourth-quarter comeback against the Cleveland Browns, but a last-minute field goal from Andre Szmyt allowed the Browns to escape with a victory and get to 3-1 on the season. The Steelers had a dream start to the game. They forced the Browns to go three-and-out, and then embarked […]
full_text: (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers nearly completed an 11-point fourth-quarter comeback against the Cleveland Browns, but a last-minute field goal from Andre Szmyt allowed the Browns to escape with a victory and get to 3-1 on the season. The Steelers had a dream start to the game. They forced the Browns to go three-and-out, and then embarked on a 17-play drive that took nearly 10 minutes off the clock and culminated with a Roman Wilson touchdown on a jet touch pass. However, the offense would stall out and the Browns would take advantage. After an interception thrown by Rodgers to Denzel Ward, the Browns turned it into points with a 28-yard touchdown run by Jaleel McLaughlin. The Steelers then went three-and-out, and the Browns marched down the field in just four plays and Quinshon Judkins ran it in from two yards out to make it 14-7. The Steelers then put a drive together and got into field goal range, but Chris Boswell was unable to make a 48-yard field goal. The Browns then drove down the field and scored another touchdown to make it 21 unanswered points, with Harold Fannin scoring on a two-yard touchdown pass to make it 21-7. Boswell did connect on a field goal at the end of the half to make it 21-10 at halftime. In the second half, the Steelers’ defense turned things around. After allowing 21 points in the first two quarters, Pittsburgh allowed just three in the second half and had two takeaways. T.J. Watt forced a fumble on Deshaun Watson, recovering it to give Pittsburgh the ball. They would then punt after five plays. On the ensuing Browns drive, Robert Spears-Jennings picked off Watson after Jack Sawyer tipped the pass. The Steelers then turned that into a touchdown on a vintage Rodgers throw. Scrambling to his right Rodgers flung the ball 21 yards to Darnell Washington. The Steelers went for two and were held out of the end zone, so the game remained 21-16. Cleveland answered with a field goal to make it a 24-16 game. Rodgers then led an eight-play, 80-yard drive, finishing with a Pat Freiermuth touchdown reception, but Pittsburgh still trailed by two. After a Jared Verse penalty, the ball moved to the one yard-line, where Mike McCarthy dialed up an Aaron Rodgers sneak to tie the game up. Unfortunately for the offense, the defense then allowed the Browns to march down the field and get into field goal range, going 36 yards on seven plays and setting up Andre Szmyt for the game-winning 56-yard field goal. Rodgers had one last heave that was picked off by Grant Delpit to seal the 27-24 win for the Browns. Rodgers finished the game 22-of-40 for 299 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. He and DK Metcalf had their best game, collectively of the season, connecting five times for 115 yards. Ultimately, though, a missed kick from Boswell, a brutal showing from the offensive line (five sacks on Rodgers), and a defense that couldn’t tackle or shut the door in the biggest moments leads to the Steelers falling to 2-2. title: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 4 predictions for Pittsburgh
summary: It’s a battle for sole possession of first place in the AFC North as the 2-1 Steelers take on the 2-1 Browns at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Pittsburgh is coming off of a massive victory over the Cincinnati Bengals last week, where its offense came to life in a thrilling […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers throws the ball while being tackled by Alex Wright #91 of the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a battle for sole possession of first place in the AFC North as the 2-1 Steelers take on the 2-1 Browns at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Pittsburgh is coming off of a massive victory over the Cincinnati Bengals last week, where its offense came to life in a thrilling 30-27 victory. However, Cleveland is coming off of a Week 3 victory of its own after defeating the Carolina Panthers by a score of 21-18. With both teams coming off major wins, FanDuel Sportsbook has the Steelers as 2.5-point favorites over the Browns. An early-season road divisional matchup can be hard to predict, especially given the Steelers’ history in Cleveland on Thursday night. With that being said, here are three predictions for the Week 4 matchup: Jaylen Warren goes for 100+ rushing yards again ​ Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is coming off one of the best games of his entire career, as he averaged 7.5 yards per carry to the tune of 127 rushing yards against the Bengals. With fellow starting running back Rico Dowdle out for the second straight week, the Browns provide a good matchup for Warren to repeat the same success he saw last week. The Browns defense has overall been a solid unit this season, but they have given up 4.5 yards per carry through three contests this season. Warren is also the best running back that the Browns have faced so far this season in terms of yards and overall efficiency. Warren is currently averaging 5.7 yards per carry through three games, and while that number is unlikely to hold all season long, this feels like a perfect spot for Warren to continue his red-hot streak as the most featured player in the Steelers’ offense. Steelers edge rushers sack Deshaun Watson multiple times After TJ Watt set a blazing pace with 3.5 sacks through the team’s first two contests, the star edge rusher was quiet in the Steelers Week 3 victory. In fact, Pittsburgh edge rushers did not record a single sack in the win over Cincinnati. This game against Cleveland is the perfect get-right spot for the group, which remains the strongest and deepest position on the Steelers roster. They will face a quarterback in Deshaun Watson who has been sacked nine times through three games this season. I’ll be looking at Nick Herbig as the one who needs a sack the most, as he has had a quiet season on the stat sheet so far after a breakout 2025 campaign. It’s tough to imagine the Steelers edge rusher group not getting home and sacking the quarterback for two straight contests, especially considering the number of sacks Watson is taking so far this season. Roman Wilson catches another deep shot Through three weeks of the 2026 NFL season, nobody plays more man coverage than the Cleveland Browns. Mike Rutenberg’s defense plays man at a 41.7% rate , with the next closest team playing man just 34.4% of the time. Interestingly enough, the Steelers have a receiver who they love to target when a team is in man coverage. In fact, Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson has a 21.56-yard average depth of target against man this season, the highest of any receiver in the league. That number comes on nine targets, meaning it’s no fluke. Coming off a game where Wilson caught a 38-yard touchdown, this could be a spot for Wilson to repeat some of that downfield magic. What are your predictions for Steelers vs. Browns? Join the BTSC comment section and let us know!

title: 5 questions about the Browns ahead of Steelers matchup
summary: The NFL’s Week 4 kicks off with a big AFC North matchup on Thursday Night Football as the Cleveland Browns (2-1) host the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1). Ahead of the game, I chatted with Chris Pokorny of Dawgs by Nature, SB Nation’s Browns site, to learn more about Cleveland ahead of the game. You can read […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns looks on against the Carolina Panthers during the third quarter at Huntington Bank Field on September 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s Week 4 kicks off with a big AFC North matchup on Thursday Night Football as the Cleveland Browns (2-1) host the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1). Ahead of the game, I chatted with Chris Pokorny of Dawgs by Nature , SB Nation’s Browns site, to learn more about Cleveland ahead of the game. You can read my questions and his answers below: 1. The Browns defense is hovering around the middle of the pack when it comes to defensive metrics. How does this group look without Myles Garrett? And what are your thoughts on the trade a few games into the season? Week 1 was a disaster against the Jaguars. Mistakes were being made left and right, there was no pressure to be found, and man coverage seemed to take a backseat to zone coverage. Right away, fans were thinking, “Oh, boy — it looks like we can’t do anything without Myles Garrett.” The last two weeks have painted a far different picture. The defense is bringing more creative blitzes than the previous coaching staff, and they’ve generated enough pressures to where fans aren’t even noticing that Myles Garrett is missing now. Instead of it being a one-man show with Garrett, everyone on the defensive line seems to be taking their turn with generating pressure. Jared Verse has played the selfless role of helping draw more eyes to free up other people, and defensive tackle Mason Graham has taken a huge step forward in year two. He was the No. 5 overall pick last year, and he looks dominant against the run and at rushing the passer. He has a sack in each of his first three games and four sacks total. As far as my thoughts on the trade go, I liked Garrett, but he had spent enough years here to where I think it was fair for him to try finding a winning opportunity elsewhere. And in return, the Browns got a stellar pass-rusher, a first round pick in 2027, and other draft assets to where they’ll have some leverage to trade up for their quarterback of the future. Right now, I’m not even thinking about the trade. In hindsight, it probably also makes it easier to digest when you see that Garrett is having knee issues. 2. NFL fans wanted to proclaim the Browns’ season as over following a big Week 1 loss. Now, Cleveland is 2-1. How expected/unexpected has the recent winning streak been for those who follow the Browns? It’s not unexpected that the defense turned things around. Also, with the sad state that the NFC South was last year, it’s not lost on me that both of the Browns’ victories came against that division. Nonetheless, the surprising factor that has shocked everyone is that for the first time in a Browns uniform, Deshaun Watson looks competent. I don’t want to delve too much into Watson yet, since I see your next question focuses on his play, but no one really saw his improved play coming. It was a foregone conclusion that, ‘Yeah, Watson will struggle in Week 2 again, and then Shedeur Sanders will start the home opener so we don’t have to deal with fans booing the hell out of Watson the whole game.’ With Cleveland having one of the easiest schedules in the NFL, fans are back on board with being optimistic for contending this season, and having those assets to continue improving in 2027 and beyond. 3. On a similar note, not many expected Deshaun Watson to start the entire season, but he currently has a 4-0 touchdown-interception ratio over the last two weeks. How has he been playing? Deshaun Watson was really sharp in Week 2 against the Buccaneers. In Week 3, he faced accuracy issues and definitely could have been better, but he still played well in the elements of his game beyond that. When we talk about Watson, we have to understand how awful he’s been during his time in Cleveland, up until this year. Ever since the off-the-field issues, it looked like he was always ‘off.’ I don’t think he could shake the mental hurdle of that, and nothing came off natural with him. As soon as I saw Watson play a little bit this preseason, I immediately went, “Hmm, that’s interesting.” And it was because I could tell that he seemed to be completely immersed in the game, as if he had let loose. It’s hard to put into words, but it’s something the eye test of watching him these past few years can pick up on right away. Now, in training camp and the first game (where he threw an interception), he would still struggle with reading a defender who dropped underneath a deeper route, but even getting to that decision was honestly a step beyond what he was delivering in the past. The most impressive element of Watson’s game these past two weeks is how effective he has been when running the ball, recognizing when to step up. In the red zone, he’s also done a good job coming off of his first read, buying time, and finding the eventual open man for a touchdown. The Watson we’re seeing right now is playing very much like a game manager. He’s not yet slinging it all over the field. But with the confidence we’ve seen grow over the past couple weeks, maybe he’ll continue to play well and get back to the player he used to be. 4. It’s the first year for Todd Monken as the Browns’ head coach. How has his leadership and scheme differed from the Kevin Stefanski era? There have been a few things that Todd Monken has done to turn heads in a bad way, like the handling of the quarterback competition in training camp, how unprepared the team looked in Week 1, and some questionable short-yardage situations where he has gone for it on fourth down already (and of course, the two questionable calls did not get converted). However, one of my favorite things from any head coach that I look for is, ‘How many adjustments is a coaching staff willing to make, or are they doing to be so darn stubborn?’ With Kevin Stefanski, he was a good guy, but I thought he was horrible at week-to-week and in-game adjustments. Former defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz — I loved the guy and think he did great, but the one element I disliked was that I thought he refused to pivot from his bread-and-butter philosophy against teams that might have been more equipped to beat it. There were no adjustments. Under Monken, I saw the team get their butts whooped in Week 1, with a lot of pre-snap penalties or timeouts related to delay of games. Prior to Week 2, we heard the offensive coordinator mention that they adjusted things in practice by shortening the play clock to 35 seconds, and focusing on how to make offensive substitutions quicker. While the offensive line has still been plagued by a ridiculous number of false starts, all of the procedure penalties that could contribute to a delay of game seem to have been cleaned up quickly. Defensively, we’ve seen the Browns go back to man coverage in some situations, but also utilizes blitzes from a variety of directions. I get the feeling that our new defensive coordinator, Mike Rutenberg, wants to actually devise a strategy each week based on his opponent, as opposed to just calling it the same way each week. So those are some encouraging things thus far. 5. The Browns are currently slim underdogs against the Steelers. What’s your final score prediction, and why? Does Cleveland earn another Thursday Night Football win over the Steelers? While the offense has gained traction, they are methodical in what they do. They aren’t yet built to run-and-gun up and down the field. I’m still a bit caught off guard on how the Steelers exploded offensively last week, but overall, I don’t perceive them to be a juggernaut. The Steelers have been terrible on Thursday Night Football over the years, for whatever reason. I know much of that was under Mike Tomlin’s watch, but that tips the scale to Cleveland’s favor here. I’ll take the Browns to win and cover by a score of 20-17.

full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been quite an eventful week for the Pittsburgh Steelers. They defeated the Cincinnati Bengals 30-27, and enter tonight’s matchup with the Cleveland Browns as 2.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Despite the big win, though, fans don’t seem to be excited about what the Steelers’ future holds. We ran a survey here at SB Nation over the last week asking fans if they have faith in the direction the Steelers are going in, to which only seven percent of people voted yes. A win on Thursday night slots Pittsburgh in sole possession of first place (3-1) in the AFC North entering the weekend. Despite this, many long-term questions marks remain with the offensive line and how to replace star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The Steelers traded Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys late Wednesday night for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. A secondary still missing DeShon Elliott and dealing with Jalen Ramsey’s broken wrist faces additional question marks with Porter Jr. officially off the team. Led by Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers, the Steelers offense ranks 17th in total offense (329 yards per game) but 26th in scoring (17.7). They are a bottom-five offense on third down (32.4%) and still don’t have an identified franchise quarterback waiting in the wings, unless Drew Allar takes the next step. Much pessimism likely stems from a nine-year drought without a playoff win and a roster similar to that of a year ago. General Manager Omar Khan hasn’t guided the Steelers to much success, and the confidence index for Steelers fans continues to waver around the nation. Let us know what you think in the comments . On the other side, the Los Angeles Chargers are still winless in 2026. They lost to the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas Raiders, and Buffalo Bills, but the Chargers were […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 10: George Holani #36 of the Seattle Seahawks scores a touchdown against the Los Angeles Chargers in the first half before a preseason game at SoFi Stadium on August 10, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images After opening the season with two wins, the Seattle Seahawks enter Week 4 looking to bounce back from an unexpected 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders. On the other side, the Los Angeles Chargers are still winless in 2026. They lost to the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas Raiders, and Buffalo Bills, but the Chargers were in position to win their latest game after taking a 10-0 lead over Buffalo before eventually falling 24-16, despite forcing five turnovers. The matchup will be played at Lumen Field in Seattle on Sunday, October 4, at 1:25 p.m. local time. It will be the first regular-season meeting between these teams since 2022, when the Seahawks defeated the Chargers 37-23 in Los Angeles. For Seattle, this game is also an opportunity to prevent the loss in Washington from becoming the start of a negative stretch. The Seahawks committed three turnovers against the Commanders, and all three resulted in touchdowns, accounting for 20 of Washington’s 33 points. Seattle gained 437 yards compared to just 229 for Washington, but ultimately lost because it could not protect the football in the most important moments. Can the Seahawks’ run game get back on track? Perhaps the biggest question for Seattle entering this game is the running game. The Seahawks managed just 44 rushing yards against Washington after producing much better numbers during the first two weeks. The challenge now comes against a Chargers defense that has produced very different results from week to week. Los Angeles allowed 116 rushing yards to Arizona in Week 1, then held Las Vegas to just 57 yards in Week 2 and Buffalo ran for 176 yards in Week 3, with James Cook accounting for 154 of them. Through three games, the Chargers are allowing about 116 rushing yards per game. That means there is an opportunity for Seattle to try to re-establish its identity on the ground, but the matchup is not necessarily a simple one. Dalvin Tomlinson is an important piece of the interior defensive line, with Teair Tart and Jamaree Caldwell also there. Tomlinson might miss the game due to injury. For Seattle, the goal will be to find a way to consistently gain yards without turning every run into a second- or third-and-long situation. After the struggles against Washington, establishing some offensive balance could also help take pressure off Sam Darnold. The offensive line vs. the Chargers pass rush The other major test for Seattle’s offense will come in pass protection. The Chargers have one of the more interesting pass-rush groups in the league, with Khalil Mack, Tuli Tuipulotu, and first-round rookie Akheem Mesidor giving them three players who can win from the edge. Mesidor gets a hard set where defender is low on him, defeats the hands with double swipe, clears defender with rip pic.twitter.com/d21FxAzVRj — betz (@adaptskill) September 30, 2026 Tuipulotu has already generated 12 pressures and two sacks through three games, while Mesidor has added five pressures and 1.5 sacks despite playing just 66 defensive snaps. Mack has also recorded two sacks this season. The Chargers showed against Buffalo that they can create pressure without constantly sending extra rushers. Tuipulotu, in particular, was a problem for the Bills, finishing the game with 1.5 sacks and two quarterback hits. Abe Lucas struggling in 2026… — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-10-01T00:02:09.155Z That will be a major test for Seattle’s offensive line. Abe Lucas has been almost unrecognizable compared to the level we are accustomed to seeing from him this season, and this would be a good opportunity for him to get back to his usual level. Grey Zabel was listed on the injury report (groin), which could help explain some of his struggles over the past two games. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-30T23:46:22.358Z Grey Zabel will also need to rebound after a down game against Washington. The Seahawks cannot afford to let the Chargers’ edge rushers consistently win early in the down. If Mack, Tuipulotu and Mesidor can create pressure without requiring additional help, Los Angeles can make life difficult for Darnold and limit the time available for Seattle’s deeper passing concepts. Turnovers: the Chargers can take the ball away There is an important similarity between these two teams entering this matchup: turnovers have already played a major role in their seasons. Seattle turned the ball over three times against Washington, and all three turnovers became touchdowns. The Chargers, meanwhile, just experienced almost the exact opposite situation. Against Buffalo, Los Angeles forced five turnovers — two interceptions and three fumble recoveries — but still lost. That makes protecting the football particularly important for Seattle, especially for rookie running back Jadarian Price ( assuming he plays after not practicing on Thursday ). The Chargers have shown that their defense can create opportunities, and another game with multiple takeaways could give Los Angeles a path to victory even if the offense does not have a dominant performance. Justin Herbert has given defenses opportunities Justin Herbert remains the central figure of the Chargers’ offense, but there have been opportunities for opposing defenses to make plays against him this season. Justin Herbert was really fortunate to get out of that Bills game with only one turnover. First clip is the literal first pass he threw. pic.twitter.com/aUrPeUWybE — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) September 30, 2026 Through three games, Herbert has thrown for 627 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions, while taking eight sacks. More importantly for Seattle, his four interceptions do not tell the entire story. PFF has charted Herbert with seven turnover-worthy plays through his first three games. That creates an interesting opportunity for Seattle’s defense. Herbert has already put the ball in harm’s way more often than his interception total suggests, and the Seahawks’ defense could be looking to turn those opportunities into actual takeaways. Against Buffalo, Herbert finished with 226 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception. His interception came in the fourth quarter, when C.J. Gardner-Johnson undercut a throw intended for Marquez Valdes-Scantling near the goal line and returned it 41 yards. Seattle’s pass rush vs. the Chargers offensive line This matchup goes both ways. While the Chargers’ pass rush will test Seattle’s offensive line, the Seahawks’ front has a favorable opportunity against an offensive line that has had its share of problems through three weeks. The Chargers’ interior has been particularly inconsistent. Cole Strange has allowed seven pressures through three games, while his PFF pass-blocking grade sits at just 25.6. The unit has also struggled with penalties. Joe Alt was flagged four times against the Raiders in Week 2, and he was penalized again against Buffalo. That brought his season total to six penalties through three games, the most in the NFL . That said, Alt’s season should not be reduced to those penalties. He had a strong performance against Buffalo and finished Week 3 with an 83.6 PFF grade, according to Chargers-focused reporting. Still, the penalties are something Seattle can try to exploit. The Seahawks have the defensive line talent to make the Chargers play behind the chains, and the interior matchup against Strange could be particularly interesting. Seattle’s pass rush will be particularly important here. Through three games, the Seahawks have generated seven sacks and 21 quarterback hits, with Leonard Williams and DeMarcus Lawrence leading the pressure production against Washington. If Seattle can create pressure while maintaining its coverage…

title: NFL predictions: What’s going to happen in Seahawks vs. Chargers
summary: After a disappointing loss versus the Washington Commanders, the Seattle Seahawks look to get back on track at home versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Per FanDuel Sportsbook, they look to be seven-point favorites at the time of writing this. How will this get accomplished? Let’s take a look. 1. Aerial attack against Chargers secondary The […]
full_text: After a disappointing loss versus the Washington Commanders, the Seattle Seahawks look to get back on track at home versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , they look to be seven-point favorites at the time of writing this. How will this get accomplished? Let’s take a look. 1. Aerial attack against Chargers secondary The Seahawks are averaging 266 passing yards a game so far this season, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, averaging 135 of those yards. The Chargers are allowing opponents to throw for 233 yards per game. The Seahawks have had eight passing touchdowns so far this season, while the Chargers have allowed four. Expect Jaxon to have another 100+ yard receiving game, with one to two more touchdowns to add to his six current touchdowns. He is on a historic pace right now . Prediction: Jaxon Smith-Njigba 125 yards and 2 Touchdowns Elite company. pic.twitter.com/ePvBRiOLja — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 29, 2026 2. The Dark Side to stop the run The Chargers offense has averaged 113 yards rushing per game, but I do not expect that to continue. The Seahawks defense is allowing only 87 yards of rushing per game and 3.3 yards per attempt, and they haven’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in almost two full seasons. Even with getting 113 yards per game, the Chargers are only averaging 4.2 yards per attempt. I expect that to continue as the Seahawks defense is still ranked third per DVOA. Meanwhile, the Chargers have the 26th ranked offense per DVOA. Not a favorable matchup for them. Prediction: Hold the Chargers to 90 rushing yards, no rushing TD’s 3. Expect the Seahawks to cover The Seahawks are the seven-point favorite, and I expect them to cover that. With the bad weather and Sam Darnold’s first game back, I believe the loss to the Commanders was an anomaly. I have full faith that Mike Macdonald with get the team back on track and with the help of the fans cheering the team on at home, win this game. The Seahawks have been outscoring their opponents by 8.3 points and are ranked seventh in point differential across the league. Meanwhile, the Chargers are ranked 30th in point differential and allow opponents to outscore them by an average of 10.6 points. Prediction: Seahawks cover the seven points 4. Under the 43.5 Points FanDuel has the game at 43.5 points. The average Seahawks came is currently around 41.7 points, while for the Chargers their games are averaging 40 points total on the dot. Averaging those totals together comes to 40.85, just under three points from the Fan Duel prediction. The Seahawks are averaging 25 points per game while the Chargers are allowing opponents an average of 25.3. On the other side, the Chargers are averaging 14.7 points per game while the Seahawks are allowing opponents and average of 16.7 points per game. Prediction: 25-15 Seahawks victory , total points 40. Concluding Points The Seahawks generally do not lose back-to-back games. The last time it happened was in 2024 when they lost to both the Packers and Vikings in Weeks 15 and 16 during Macdonald’s first season. After that season, Macdonald was able to make the team more in his image, and has not lost back to back games sense, and just finished a 12 game winning streak (stopping there in respect to the 12’s). I expect the Seahawks to continue to try to run the back with the committee of Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani to set up the passing game. Will this be the game where Price gets his first rushing touchdown? That will depend on the offensive line that has had its struggles with opening up running lanes in the red zone. With John Benton coaching up the offensive line, I foresee the offensive line getting back on track, opening up running lanes for the running back stable, and Price getting his first touchdown of the season. Starting safety Ty Okada is finally back at practice in a limited manner. This is the first time Okada has practiced all season. It will be […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 28: Ty Okada #39 of the Seattle Seahawks tackles Rico Dowdle #5 of the Carolina Panthers during the third quarter at Bank of America Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Thursday injury report entering Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers has come out. There are some major updates with this report. Let’s start with the good news. Starting safety Ty Okada is finally back at practice in a limited manner. This is the first time Okada has practiced all season. It will be fascinating to see whether he is able to practice again tomorrow and potentially even suit up on Sunday. The other starting safety, Julian Love, was limited in practice again on Thursday with a calf injury. However, when asked whether he plans to play Sunday against the Chargers, Love responded, “ Yeah, I feel good .” Usually having media availability is a sign that a player will play. The other good news out of Thursday’s practice is that running back Zach Charbonnet has officially returned to practice on a limited basis. Since Charbonnet is on the PUP list, he has to sit out four total games, meaning he will not be able to play Sunday against the Chargers. However, Charbonnet returning also means that he has to be activated off of the PUP list within 21 days, or his season is over. That timeline shows that Charbonnet could be back as early as Week 5 against the San Francisco 49ers, while the latest he could return is ahead of the Week 7 matchup against Kenneth Walker III and the Kansas City Chiefs. It wasn’t all good news for the Seahawks. Running back Jadarian Price went from a limited participant in practice yesterday, to a “did not participate” in today’s practice due to a chest injury. If Price cannot go Sunday, then that likely means a heavy dose of George Holani and Emanuel Wilson at running back (and perhaps even a Velus Jones Jr. or Jacardia Wright off the practice squad). Although it should be noted that for the second straight day, Holani was limited in practice with a rib injury. Defensive tackle Brandon Pili (neck), safety Nick Emmanwori (ankle), and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (hip) were all full participants for the second day in a row. Meanwhile left guard Grey Zabel (groin), and defensive tackles Jarran Reed (foot) and Leonard Wiliams (veteran rest day) all went from limited participants yesterday to full participants today.

summary: After being sidelined for the past eight months while recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in the 2026 Divisional Round, Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet is one step closer to returning to game action. The Seahawks designated Charbonnet to return to practice on Thursday morning, meaning they’ll have a 21-day window to activate […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Zach Charbonnet #26 of the Seattle Seahawks runs the ball in the first quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images After being sidelined for the past eight months while recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in the 2026 Divisional Round , Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet is one step closer to returning to game action. The Seahawks designated Charbonnet to return to practice on Thursday morning, meaning they’ll have a 21-day window to activate him to their active roster. The fourth-year running back is required to miss a minimum of four games after he opened the season on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, but becomes eligible to return in Week 5 against the San Francisco 49ers. Should the team opt not to activate him, he will remain on the physically unable to perform list for the remainder of the year. Given he hasn’t fully participated in a practice in nearly nine months, it wouldn’t be surprising for the Seahawks to give Charbonnet the full 21 days to ramp up. Should that be the case, he would likely be slated to return to action against the Denver Broncos in Week 6 (exactly two weeks from today) or the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7. Charbonnet totaled a career-best 730 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns across 16 games last season while splitting work with Kenneth Walker III, and figures to re-emerge as the go-to back in short yardage and goal line situations. Upon his return, he’s set to split carries with rookie Jadarian Price, who has yet to carve out a feature role for himself. Seattle also has Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, whom they’ve utilized alongside Price in Charbonnet’s absence.
